### `PR.0/p-local-integer-initial` — Initiality of the p-local integer δ-ring

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-local-integer-initial` · theorem · part PR.0.

For every commutative δ-ring B in which the image of every integer not divisible by p is a unit, there exists exactly one unital ring map Z_(p)→B commuting with δ. B may have nonzero p-torsion or be the zero ring.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; the coefficient condition is explicit: for every integer n with p not dividing n, the cast of n is a unit of B.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The integer-cast-delta lemma shows that Int.castRingHom B commutes with δ. This uses the integer recurrence, not cancellation of p in B.
2. Membership outside the principal ideal (p) is precisely nondivisibility by p. The coefficient condition therefore supplies unit images of all denominators.
3. Use the existing delta-localization-universal theorem with the actual intAtPrime operation, whose compatibility on Z is supplied by p-local-integer-delta-base.
4. Any unital ring map Z_(p)→B restricts to the integer cast. Localization ringHom_ext therefore proves uniqueness even before imposing δ-compatibility.

*Uses.*
- PR.0 coefficient and localization inputs to local distinguished generators: Supplies the actual p-local δ-structure or its target unit condition without p-cancellation.

*Acceptance.*
- Specialize to B=Z_(p) to recover the identity.
- The zero target is allowed; no nontriviality premise is introduced.
- The target can have p-torsion; equality of Frobenius maps is not used to infer equality of δ-maps.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-local-integer-delta-base`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-localization-universal`, `mathlib:IsLocalization.lift`, `mathlib:IsLocalization.lift_eq`, `mathlib:IsLocalization.ringHom_ext`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-FRESH-LOCAL, Example 2.6, printed p.14: “In fact, this is the initial object in the category of” (Gives an explicit localization proof of source initiality, retaining the target p-local condition and allowing torsion.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Localization`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`. Declaration: `TauCeti.Delta.intAtPrime_initial`.

### `PR.0/delta-span-stability` — δ stability from ideal generators

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-span-stability` · lemma · part PR.0.

For a subset S of A, the ordinary ideal J generated by S is δ-stable if and only if δ(s) belongs to J for every s in S.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The forward implication is restriction along the inclusion of S in its ideal span.
2. For the converse apply span induction to the predicate δ(x) belongs to J, keeping x in J as the induction membership. Zero follows from δ(0)=0.
3. For a sum, use the δ addition identity and delta-adic-correction with J: the correction term is in J because the second summand is in J.
4. For a scalar multiple ax, use δ(ax)=a^p δ(x)+x^p δ(a)+p δ(a)δ(x). The first and third terms lie in J by the inductive hypothesis, and the second because x lies in J and p is positive. This argument never assumes δ is additive.

*Acceptance.*
- The empty generating set gives the stable zero ideal. For p=2 on the integers, the generator 2 fails the criterion because δ(2)=-1 is not in (2).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-adic-correction`, `mathlib:Ideal.subset_span`, `mathlib:Submodule.span_induction`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-stable`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-DELTA-QUOTIENT, Section 2 opening convention and Definition 2.1, p.13; Lemma 2.9 and Example 2.10, p.15: “but this follows immediately from the additivity formula” (Declaration-sized refinement of the source universal delta quotient. The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`. Declaration: `TauCeti.Delta.span_delta_stable_iff`.

### `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure` — δ-stabilization of an ideal

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure` · definition · part PR.0.

For an ideal I of A, define its δ-stabilization C_d(I) to be the ordinary ideal generated by all δ^n(a), for n a nonnegative integer and a in I. The exponent means iteration of δ, with δ^0 the identity; it is not a ring power or a Witt-coordinate operation.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Use the existing ideal span of the set of all iterated δ images. The index n=0 includes the original ideal.
2. Stability and the least-stable-ideal characterization are separate lemma nodes. Idempotence and monotonicity follow from those lemmas, giving the usual closure-operator laws without introducing another ideal type.
3. For the prime-ideal acceptance test, use integer-cast-delta: δ(p)=1-p^(p-1). The zeroth and first iterates place p and δ(p) in the closure; p is at least two, so their ideal combination is 1.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Example 2.10 and Notation 2.8; PrismaticCohomology:PR.0: Supplies the concrete universal quotient that kills prescribed relations and all their δ iterates. It is an algebraic ingredient for δ-algebra presentations; no derived or prism-envelope universal property is asserted.

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_eq_span` (characterisation): C_d(I) is exactly the ideal span of the set of all δ^n(a) with n nonnegative and a in I.
- `TauCeti.Delta.le_idealClosure` (constructor): I is contained in C_d(I), by the zeroth iterate.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_stable` (structure): For x in C_d(I), δ(x) is in C_d(I); the separate stability lemma supplies this API.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_le` (universal-property): For a δ-stable ideal J, C_d(I) is contained in J if and only if I is contained in J; the separate minimality lemma supplies this API.
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_idem` (simp): C_d(C_d(I))=C_d(I).
- `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure_mono` (functoriality): If I is contained in J, then C_d(I) is contained in C_d(J).

*Unit tests.*
- `ideal_closure_zero` (degenerate): The δ-stabilization of the zero ideal is the zero ideal.
- `ideal_closure_stable_fixed` (characterisation): If I is already δ-stable, then C_d(I)=I.
- `ideal_closure_prime_is_top` (computation): In every δ-ring A, C_d((p)) is the unit ideal: both p and δ(p)=1-p^(p-1) belong to it, so 1 does too.
- `ideal_closure_not_ordinary_span` (non-example): For the canonical 2-δ-structure on the integers, C_d((2)) differs from the ordinary ideal (2), since δ(2)=-1.

*Acceptance.*
- Check the zero ideal and the ideal generated by p; δ-stabilization of the latter is the unit ideal.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `mathlib:Ideal.span`, `mathlib:Function.iterate_zero_apply`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-cast-delta`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-stable`, `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-minimal`, `PR.0/delta-universal-quotient`.

*Sources.*

The source uses p-local rings; the displayed proof uses only the integral delta identities and establishes this explicitly broader elementary statement.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Ideal`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`. Declaration: `TauCeti.Delta.idealClosure`.

### `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-stable` — Stability of δ-stabilization

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-stable` · lemma · part PR.0.

For every ideal I, δ carries C_d(I) into C_d(I).

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. For a generating element δ^n(a), its δ is δ^(n+1)(a), another generator.
2. Apply delta-span-stability to these generators. Their ideal span is C_d(I) by definition; no assumption that I itself is stable is used.

*Acceptance.*
- At p=2 on the integers, stabilization of (2) contains -1 and hence is the stable unit ideal, not the original ideal.

### `PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-minimal` — Minimality of δ-stabilization

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ideal-closure-minimal` · lemma · part PR.0.

For any δ-stable ideal J, C_d(I) is contained in J if and only if I is contained in J.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The forward direction uses the zeroth iterate in the generating set.
2. Conversely, if I is contained in J, induction on n shows δ^n(a) belongs to J for every a in I. Use stability of J in the successor step, then the universal property of ideal span.

*Acceptance.*
- If I is already δ-stable, use J=I to obtain C_d(I)=I; with J=C_d(I), the same criterion gives idempotence.

*Hypotheses.*

*Proof or construction outline.*

### `PR.0/delta-universal-quotient` — Universal δ quotient by an ideal

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient` · construction · part PR.0.

On the existing quotient ring Q=A/C_d(I), construct the unique δ-structure for which the ordinary quotient map q:A to Q commutes with δ. This is the universal δ A-algebra annihilating I, as proved by the separate universal-property theorem.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Apply delta-stable-quotient to the ideal C_d(I), using delta-ideal-closure-stable. Select the unique compatible δ-structure on the existing quotient carrier.
2. Its evaluation on q(a) is q(δ(a)). The map kills I since I is contained in its closure. The universal mapping property is proved separately through the existing ring quotient lift.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Example 2.10 and Notation 2.8; PrismaticCohomology:PR.0: Supplies the concrete universal quotient that kills prescribed relations and all their δ iterates. It is an algebraic ingredient for δ-algebra presentations; no derived or prism-envelope universal property is asserted.

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_mk` (simp): The quotient δ-operation sends q(a) to q(δ(a)); this is also a separate projection lemma.
- `TauCeti.Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_unique` (characterisation): Every δ-structure on A/C_d(I) compatible with q equals the constructed one.
- `TauCeti.Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_kills` (compatibility): For a in I, the existing quotient projection q sends a to zero.

*Unit tests.*

- `universal_quotient_prime_collapses` (degenerate): For I=(p), the quotient A/C_d(I) is the zero ring, expressed by its carrier being a subsingleton.

*Acceptance.*
- Retain the stated δ-compatibility and all ideal-membership hypotheses.

### `PR.0/delta-universal-quotient-lift` — Universal property of the δ quotient

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-universal-quotient-lift` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let B be a δ-ring and f:A to B a unital ring map commuting with δ and annihilating I. There exists a unique ring map g:A/C_d(I) to B extending f and commuting with the quotient δ-operation. Its underlying map is the existing ordinary quotient lift.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified δ-structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. δ-kernel-stability makes the ordinary kernel of f δ-stable. Minimality of C_d(I), with I contained in that kernel, shows f annihilates the closure.
2. Construct g by the existing Ideal.Quotient.lift and use its evaluation theorem to prove g(q(a))=f(a).
3. For an arbitrary quotient element choose a representative using surjectivity of q. Evaluate the quotient δ via delta-universal-quotient-projection and use compatibility of f to prove compatibility of g.
4. Any competing map agrees after precomposition with the surjective q, hence agrees everywhere. This proves initiality among the stated δ-compatible maps, without building an unrelated category or assuming an adjunction.

*Acceptance.*
- With target Q=A/C_d(I) and f=q, the unique factor is the identity. With the zero target, the unique zero-ring map is allowed and δ-compatible.

### `PR.0/free-delta-ring` — Free δ-rings ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Free δ-rings**.

For a set S, the free δ-ring Z{S} on S is the polynomial ring Z[x_{s,n} : s ∈ S, n ≥ 0] with the unique δ-structure such that δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}; its Frobenius is φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. For every δ-ring R and every family (f_s) in R there is a unique map of δ-rings Z{S} → R with x_{s,0} ↦ f_s; it sends x_{s,n} to δ^n(f_s). The Frobenius endomorphism of Z{S} is faithfully flat. After inverting p, Z{S}[1/p] is also the polynomial ring on the elements φ^n(x_{s,0}). The source works over Z_(p); Z_(p){S} = Z{S} ⊗_Z Z_(p), and all statements base-change.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; S is any set.
- The source states the one-generator case over Z_(p) (all rings there are Z_(p)-algebras); the statement over Z has the same proof, since Z[x_{s,n}] is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, and it base-changes to the source statement.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. On A = Z[x_{s,n}] define the ring endomorphism φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. It lifts Frobenius modulo p, and A is p-torsion-free, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives the unique δ-structure with φ as its Frobenius; it satisfies δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}.
2. Universal property: the ring map η with η(x_{s,n}) = δ^n(f_s) exists and is unique by the universal property of the polynomial ring; it commutes with δ on the generators, hence everywhere because the two δ-identities determine δ on the subring generated by the x_{s,n} (BS22, proof of Lemma 2.11).
3. Faithful flatness: write φ as the filtered colimit of the maps Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i] → Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i+1]. By the fibrewise criterion it suffices to treat [1/p], where the map shifts the polynomial generators φ^j(x), and the reduction modulo p, where it is Frobenius followed by a polynomial inclusion; both are faithfully flat.
4. Corollary 2.12: for a δ-ring A and x ∈ A, the pushout B of Z{s} ← Z{t} → A (t ↦ φ(s), t ↦ x), computed on underlying rings by delta-ring-category, is faithfully flat over A and x becomes φ(s) in B.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 2.15, proof: a δ-ring is a quotient of a free δ-ring, which is p-torsion-free; this reduces localization to the torsion-free case
- BS22 Corollary 2.12 and Construction 4.17: faithful flatness of φ gives fpqc-local surjectivity of Frobenius; free δ-A-algebras surjecting onto R are the weakly initial objects of the prismatic site (PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex)
- BS22 Lemma 2.36, Corollary 2.39, Proposition 3.13: the pushouts defining A{φ(f)/p} and prismatic envelopes are taken along maps out of free δ-rings

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free` (data): The carrier Z[x_{s,n}] of the free δ-ring on S, a polynomial ring on S × N.
- `TauCeti.Delta.freeDelta` (structure): The δ-structure on Free S.
- `TauCeti.Delta.freeDelta_X` (simp): δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.lift` (universal-property): For a δ-ring R and f : S → R, the ring map Free S → R with x_{s,n} ↦ δ^n(f s).
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.lift_isDeltaHom` (universal-property): lift f commutes with δ, and it is the unique δ-map sending x_{s,0} to f s.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Free.frobenius_faithfullyFlat` (other): Free S is faithfully flat over itself along its Frobenius.

*Unit tests.*
- `free_delta_frobenius_X` (computation): φ(x_{s,0}) = x_{s,0}^p + p·x_{s,1} in Free S.
- `free_delta_lift_int_two` (computation): For p = 2 the δ-map Free(point) → Z with x_0 ↦ 2 sends x_1 to −1.
- `free_delta_empty` (degenerate): The free δ-ring on the empty set is Z with its canonical δ-structure: the structure map Z → Free(∅) is bijective.
- `free_delta_not_free_ring` (non-example): The ring map Z[x] → Free(point), x ↦ x_0, is not surjective: x_1 = δ(x_0) is not in its image, so the free δ-ring is strictly bigger than the free ring.

*Acceptance.*

- The universal map to (Z, canonical δ) sending x_0 to 2 for p = 2 sends x_1 to δ(2) = −1.

### `PR.0/delta-ring-category` — Limits, colimits and Witt vectors of δ-rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category` · construction · part PR.0.

The category of δ-rings (objects: commutative rings with a δ-structure; morphisms: ring maps commuting with δ) has all limits and colimits, and the forgetful functor to commutative rings preserves both. In particular products, equalizers, tensor products A ⊗_C B along δ-maps and filtered colimits of δ-rings carry unique δ-structures making the structure maps δ-maps. The forgetful functor has a left adjoint (free δ-rings) and a right adjoint, the p-typical Witt vector functor W: for a ring R, W(R) carries the δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius, and for a δ-ring A there is a natural δ-map w_A : A → W(A), the unit, whose first two Witt coordinates are (x, δ(x)).

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; rings are commutative.
- The δ-structure on W(R) for R with p-torsion is defined by cofreeness, not by dividing F(x) − x^p by p.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Limits: δ is defined coordinatewise on a product and restricts to an equalizer of δ-maps, since the axioms are equational.
2. Colimits: by delta-witt-section-equivalence a δ-structure on R is a ring section of W_2(R) → R; the natural map colim_i W_2(R_i) → W_2(colim_i R_i) turns the sections of the R_i into a section for the colimit of underlying rings (BS22 Remark 2.7).
3. Adjoints: the forgetful functor commutes with limits and colimits and the categories are presentable, giving both adjoints; the right adjoint is W by Joyal's theorem (cited in Remark 2.7). Concretely the Witt vector Frobenius F on W(R) satisfies F(x) ≡ x^p mod p and W(R) is the universal δ-ring over R; when R is p-torsion-free so is W(R) and the structure is δ(x) = (F(x) − x^p)/p.
4. The unit w_A is determined by the ghost identities φ^n(x) = δ_0(x)^{p^n} + p δ_1(x)^{p^{n−1}} + … + p^n δ_n(x) (Remark 2.13); its truncation to W_2 is the section of delta-witt-section-equivalence.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Corollary 2.12, Lemma 2.15, Lemma 2.36, Proposition 3.13: pushouts of δ-rings are computed on underlying rings, which is what makes A{J/I} computable
- BS22 Remark 2.22 and Lemma 3.8: the composite A → W(A) → W(A/d) maps a distinguished element to p times a unit
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: Cartier–Witt divisors live on W(R) with its δ-structure

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDeltaHom` (characterisation): For δ-structures d on A and e on B, a ring map f : A → B is a map of δ-rings when f(d(x)) = e(f(x)) for all x; the identity is one, composites of such maps are such maps, and such a map commutes with the associated Frobenius endomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.prod` (constructor): The coordinatewise δ-structure on A × B.
- `TauCeti.Delta.Structure.tensorProduct` (constructor): For δ-maps C → A and C → B, the unique δ-structure on A ⊗_C B for which both inclusions are δ-maps.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt` (structure): The δ-structure on W(R) whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Delta.witt_frobenius` (compatibility): The Frobenius of the δ-structure on W(R) equals WittVector.frobenius.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit` (universal-property): For a δ-ring A, the δ-map w_A : A → W(A).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_coeff_zero` (simp): The 0-th Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is x.
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_coeff_one` (simp): The first Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is δ(x).
- `TauCeti.Delta.wittUnit_ghost` (characterisation): The n-th ghost component of w_A(x) is φ^n(x).

*Unit tests.*
- `witt_unit_int_ghost` (computation): For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure, every ghost component of w_Z(n) equals n.
- `delta_prod_fst` (compatibility): The first projection A × B → A commutes with δ for the product structure.
- `witt_delta_torsionfree` (compatibility): On W(Z) the δ-structure satisfies p·δ(x) = F(x) − x^p.
- `witt_unit_not_teichmuller` (non-example): For A = Z and p = 2, w_Z(2) is not the Teichmüller representative [2]: its first Witt coordinate is δ(2) = −1, not 0.

*Acceptance.*

- The pushout of Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ φ(s)) and Z{t} → A (t ↦ x) is A ⊗_{Z{t}} Z{s} as a ring.

### `PR.0/animated-delta-rings` — Simplicial commutative δ-rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings` · construction · part PR.0.

A simplicial commutative δ-ring is a simplicial object in the category of δ-rings; the ∞-category of animated δ-rings is obtained from these by inverting weak equivalences of underlying simplicial sets, equivalently it is the animation (sifted-colimit completion) of the category of free δ-rings on finite sets. The forgetful functor to animated commutative rings preserves all limits and colimits; in particular a derived pushout of animated δ-rings is computed as the derived pushout of the underlying animated rings. Free adjunction: for an animated δ-ring A and x ∈ π_0(A), the animated δ-A-algebra A{x/p} is the derived pushout of A ← Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ x, t ↦ p·s); similarly A{J/I} for I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) is the derived pushout of A ← A{t_1,…,t_r} → A{s_1,…,s_r} (free δ-A-algebras) along t_i ↦ x_i and t_i ↦ d·s_i. For a finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p the derived I-complete animated δ-rings form a full subcategory, with derived I-completion left adjoint to the inclusion.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime.
- Animated commutative rings, sifted left Kan extension and derived pushouts are supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation; derived completion by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
- The source uses this ∞-category without defining it (Corollary 2.39, Corollary 2.44, the proof of Proposition 3.13, Construction 6.1); the node supplies the definition those uses need.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Define the 1-category of simplicial δ-rings levelwise. Because the free δ-ring functor is a polynomial ring functor on underlying rings (free-delta-ring), free δ-rings on finite sets are compact projective generators and the category of δ-rings is the category of product-preserving presheaves on them; apply animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
2. The forgetful functor is induced by the functor on compact projective generators sending Z{S} to the polynomial ring Z[S × N], a filtered colimit of finitely generated polynomial rings, so it preserves sifted colimits; with preservation of finite coproducts (delta-ring-category: coproducts of δ-rings are tensor products of underlying rings) it preserves all colimits. Limits are computed levelwise.
3. Define A{x/p} and A{J/I} by the displayed pushouts; by the previous step their underlying animated rings are the corresponding derived tensor products, which is how Lemma 2.38 enters the proof of Corollary 2.39.
4. Derived completion of an animated δ-ring along a finitely generated ideal containing p carries a unique compatible δ-structure: apply δ-etale-extension's argument levelwise in the W_2-description, since W_2 commutes with the relevant limits.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Corollary 2.39: δ-pushouts must be pushouts of simplicial commutative rings in order to apply Lemma 2.38
- BS22 Proposition 3.13, proof: the prismatic envelope is first built as a derived (p,I)-complete animated δ-ring and then shown to be discrete
- BS22 Construction 6.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology: the universal oriented prism maps to a crystalline one through an animated δ-ring; derived prismatic cohomology is valued in animated objects

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing` (structure): A simplicial commutative ring with a δ-structure in each degree, compatible with all simplicial operators.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.const` (constructor): The constant simplicial δ-ring on a δ-ring.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius` (data): The levelwise Frobenius φ, an endomorphism of the underlying simplicial ring.
- `TauCeti.Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius_app` (simp): In each degree n the Frobenius is x ↦ x^p + p·δ_n(x).

*Unit tests.*
- `simplicial_delta_const_obj` (degenerate): The constant simplicial δ-ring on A has the ring A in every degree.
- `simplicial_delta_const_frobenius` (compatibility): The levelwise Frobenius of the constant simplicial δ-ring on A is the Frobenius of A in every degree.
- `simplicial_delta_face_commutes` (characterisation): Every simplicial operator of a simplicial δ-ring commutes with the levelwise Frobenius.
- `simplicial_delta_frobenius_mod_p` (characterisation): In each degree the Frobenius of a simplicial δ-ring is congruent to the p-th power map modulo p; a simplicial ring with an arbitrary levelwise endomorphism is not a simplicial δ-ring.

*Acceptance.*
- A discrete δ-ring, viewed as a constant simplicial δ-ring, has π_0 the original δ-ring and no higher homotopy.
- For A = Z_(p){x}, the animated δ-ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p is discrete (BS22 Remark 2.37); and A{x/p} is Z_(p){s} with x = p·s, a pushout along an isomorphism.

### `PR.0/delta-radical-localization` — p-local localization of a δ-ring

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-radical-localization` · construction · part PR.0.

Let A be a δ-ring and S ⊂ A a multiplicative subset. Let T be the multiplicative subset generated by S, φ(S), φ^2(S), …. Then (S^{-1}A)_(p) := the localization of S^{-1}A along V(p) (inverting 1 + p·a for all a) coincides with (T^{-1}A)_(p); it carries a unique δ-structure compatible with the one on A, has p in its Jacobson radical, and A → (S^{-1}A)_(p) is the initial δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) in which every element of S is invertible. The same holds for the localization along V(p, I) for an ideal I, which is the form used for prisms.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a δ-ring; S is a submonoid of A.
- An arbitrary localization S^{-1}A need not carry a compatible δ-structure; the statement concerns its p-localization.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. If p ∈ rad(B) and f ∈ B is a unit then φ(f) = f^p + p·δ(f) is a unit (frobenius-image-unit-jacobson). Hence in any δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) where S is invertible, all of T is invertible.
2. T is φ-stable, so delta-localization-phi-stable gives the unique compatible δ-structure on T^{-1}A, initial among δ-A-algebras inverting T.
3. The submonoid 1 + p·T^{-1}A is φ-stable because φ is a ring map: φ(1 + p·a) = 1 + p·φ(a); localize again by delta-localization-phi-stable. The result has p in its radical and, by step 1, the stated initial property; the comparison with (S^{-1}A)_(p) follows because both are initial for the same property among rings with p in the radical (BS22 Remark 2.16).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 3.1, proof: the localizations A[1/g_i] along V(p, I) carry unique δ-structures; their product is the ind-Zariski cover on which I is generated by a distinguished element
- BS22 Example 2.21 and Example 3.4: the universal distinguished element lives in the localization of Z_(p){d} at δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates
- BS22 Lemma 3.7(4): bounded prisms are locally orientable through the completion of such a localization

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusSaturation` (data): The submonoid T generated by all φ^n(s), s ∈ S, n ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Delta.frobeniusSaturation_stable` (characterisation): φ maps T into T, and S ≤ T.
- `TauCeti.Delta.radicalSaturation` (data): The submonoid of elements of A that become units modulo p in T^{-1}A; the localization of A at it is (S^{-1}A)_(p).
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical_p_mem_jacobson` (characterisation): In the localization B of A at the radical saturation, p lies in the Jacobson radical and every element of S is a unit.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical` (constructor): The unique δ-structure on the localization B of A at the radical saturation that is compatible with A → B.
- `TauCeti.Delta.localizeRadical_unique` (universal-property): Any δ-A-algebra C with p ∈ rad(C) in which S is invertible receives a unique δ-A-algebra map from B.

*Unit tests.*
- `frobenius_saturation_phi_stable_already` (degenerate): If φ(S) ⊂ S then the Frobenius saturation of S is S.
- `frobenius_saturation_int` (computation): For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure (φ = id) the Frobenius saturation of any submonoid is itself.
- `frobenius_saturation_free_strict` (non-example): In the free δ-ring on one generator x_0, the Frobenius saturation of the powers of x_0 contains x_0^p + p·x_1, which is not a power of x_0.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = Z and S generated by 3 with p = 2: the result is Z_(2) with its canonical δ-structure.
- For A = Z{x} and S = {x^n}: T contains φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x), which is not a unit of Z{x}[1/x] but is a unit of its p-localization.

### `PR.0/witt2-derived-pullback-square` — The pullback square for W_2 of a simplicial commutative ring

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-derived-pullback-square` · lemma · part PR.0 · added by REV-PrismaticCohomology--PR.0.

(1) For a p-torsion-free ring R the square of rings formed by the restriction W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x, the Witt vector Frobenius F : W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x^p + p·y, the projection R → R/p and the composite R → R/p → R/p of the projection with the Frobenius of R/p is a pullback square: W_2(R) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ R × R : b ≡ a^p modulo p}. (2) For every simplicial commutative ring B there is a pullback square of simplicial commutative rings, functorial in B, with the same two maps out of W_2(B) (W_2 applied levelwise) and with R/p replaced by B ⊗^L_Z F_p. In particular, for a cosimplicial simplicial ring B^• with discrete colim lim, colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ W_2(B^•) is W_2 of colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ B^•.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime. In (1) R is p-torsion-free; in (2) B is any simplicial commutative ring (an animated ring, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
- W_2 is the ring of length-two p-typical Witt vectors with the addition and multiplication of PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate and PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate.
- Only the square is planned here. The reformulation of δ-structures as derived Frobenius lifts (the rest of BS22 Remark 2.5) is not: no target needs it.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) The map W_2(R) → R × R, (x, y) ↦ (x, x^p + p·y), is a ring homomorphism by the coordinate formulas (PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate, PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate); it is injective because p is a nonzerodivisor of R, and its image is the set of pairs (a, b) with b ≡ a^p modulo p.
2. (2) Both W_2 (whose underlying set-valued functor is R ↦ R × R) and R ↦ R ×_{R/p} R, restricted to polynomial rings over Z, extend to sifted-colimit-preserving functors on animated rings; a finitely generated polynomial ring is p-torsion-free, so (1) identifies the two functors there, and the identification extends (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation). The extension of R ↦ R/p is B ↦ B ⊗^L_Z F_p (BS22 Remark 2.5: "Passing to simplicial resolutions").
3. The last sentence: regard the square as a pullback square of E_∞-rings; on underlying spectra a pullback square is preserved by limits and by colimits, and the totalisation and the realisation are computed levelwise in the three other corners. Discreteness of colim lim B^• is what identifies the result with W_2 of a ring.

*Acceptance.*
- R = Z: W_2(Z) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ Z × Z : b ≡ a^p mod p}; the pair (p, 0) is the image of the Witt vector (p, −p^{p−1}), and (1, 0) is not in the image.
- R = F_p (not p-torsion-free): the underived square fails, W_2(F_p) = Z/p² is not F_p ×_{F_p} F_p = F_p; the derived square holds with F_p ⊗^L_Z F_p in the corner.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`, `mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`.

### `PR.0/delta-etale-extension` — δ-structures on completely étale algebras and derived completions

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let A be a δ-ring and I ⊂ A a finitely generated ideal containing p. If B is a derived I-complete and I-completely étale A-algebra, then B admits a unique δ-structure compatible with the one on A. In particular the δ-structure of A extends uniquely to the derived I-completion of A, for every finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p.

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring; I is finitely generated and contains p (for the last sentence: a power of p).
- Derived I-completeness and I-complete étaleness are the notions of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the classical completion statement is delta-classical-completion, which this node does not replace.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Use delta-witt-section-equivalence: a compatible δ-structure on B is a ring map w_B : B → W_2(B) over w_A lifting the identity of B.
2. By Elkik's algebraization theorem (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1) B is the derived I-completion of an étale A-algebra B′. By van der Kallen's theorem W_2(A) → W_2(B′) is étale; from 0 → φ_*B′ → W_2(B′) → B′ → 0 and the equality of derived I- and φ(I)-completion (p ∈ I), W_2(B) is the derived I-completion of W_2(B′).
3. Since A → B′ is étale and W_2(B) → B is a pro-infinitesimal thickening, there is a unique lift B′ → W_2(B) of B′ → B over A → W_2(B); it extends uniquely to B because W_2(B) is derived I-complete.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = Z_(p) and I = (p): the derived p-completion Z_p carries the unique δ-structure with φ = id.
- For A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p and B the p-completion of A[1/x]: the δ-structure extends with φ(1/x) = 1/x^p.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-witt-section-equivalence`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-classical-completion`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/animated-delta-rings`, `PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`, `PR.1/prismatic-to-etale-morphism`, `PR.1/etale-localization`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 2.18 (Étale maps) and its proof: “is a pro-infinitesimal thickening, we see that there is a unique lift” (The node is the lemma with the consequence stated after it; the proof imports Elkik algebraization and van der Kallen's theorem.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Etale`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`.

### `PR.0/distinguished-element` — Distinguished elements ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element` · definition · part PR.0 · planet **Distinguished elements**.

An element d of a δ-ring A is distinguished if δ(d) is a unit of A. Every map of δ-rings preserves distinguished elements. Examples: p ∈ Z_p (δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}); [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) ∈ Z_p[[q−1]] with φ(q) = q^p; any generator ξ of the kernel of θ : A_inf(O_C) → O_C; any generator of the kernel of W[[u]] → O_K, u ↦ π, with φ(u) = u^p.

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring for the prime p.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition. Preservation under δ-maps: f(δ(d)) = δ(f(d)) and ring maps preserve units.
2. δ(p) = (p − p^p)/p = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit of Z_(p). For [p]_q: δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1), and (q − 1)-adic completeness lifts units. For ξ and for the Breuil–Kisin generator: specialise along the δ-maps A_inf → W(k) and W[[u]] → W, u ↦ 0, under which the element maps to p times a unit (BS22 Example 2.20).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 2.25 and Lemma 3.1: a locally principal ideal I with p, I in the radical satisfies p ∈ I + φ(I)A exactly when it is locally generated by a distinguished element
- BS22 Definition 3.2 and Lemma 3.8: the ideal of an orientable prism is generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: the condition on δ of a generator is the Cartier–Witt condition on W(R)

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished` (data): The predicate: δ(d) is a unit.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished.map` (functoriality): A δ-map sends distinguished elements to distinguished elements.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.isDistinguished_p_int` (example): p is distinguished in Z_(p) with its canonical δ-structure.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsDistinguished.p_mem_span` (relation): If d is distinguished then p ∈ (d, φ(d)): indeed p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p.

*Unit tests.*
- `distinguished_p_value` (computation): In Z_(p) with its canonical δ-structure, δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}.
- `distinguished_p_squared_fails` (non-example): p^2 is not distinguished in Z_(p).
- `distinguished_zero_ring` (degenerate): In the zero ring every element is distinguished.
- `distinguished_unit_times_p` (compatibility): For a unit u of Z_(p), u·p is distinguished (distinguished-factor-rigidity applied to Z_(p)).

*Acceptance.*
- δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} in Z_(p); for p = 2 this is −1.
- p^2 is not distinguished in Z_p: δ(p^2) = p − p^{2p−1} is divisible by p.
- In the free δ-ring on d, the generator d is not distinguished; it becomes distinguished after inverting δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates (BS22 Example 2.21).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/integer-delta`.

*Sources.*

### `PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity` — Factors of distinguished elements

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let A be a δ-ring. (1) If d ∈ A is distinguished, u ∈ A is a unit and d, p ∈ rad(A), then u·d is distinguished. (2) If d = f·h is distinguished with f, p ∈ rad(A), then f is distinguished and h is a unit.

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring; rad(A) is the Jacobson radical.
- For (1): d, p ∈ rad(A). For (2): f, p ∈ rad(A).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) δ(u d) = u^p δ(d) + d^p δ(u) + p δ(u) δ(d); the first term is a unit and the other two lie in rad(A).
2. (2) δ(f h) = f^p δ(h) + h^p δ(f) + p δ(f) δ(h) is a unit and the first and third terms lie in rad(A), so h^p δ(f) is a unit; hence h and δ(f) are units.

*Acceptance.*
- In Z_(p): p = p·1 and (−p) = (−1)·p are distinguished.
- The hypothesis f ∈ rad(A) in (2) is needed: in Z_(p), p = 1·p with f = 1 ∉ rad; f is not distinguished (δ(1) = 0) and h = p is not a unit.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`, `mathlib:Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot`.

### `PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators` — Local distinguished generators of a prism ideal

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let A be a δ-ring. (a) (Lemma 2.25) If d, p ∈ rad(A), then d is distinguished if and only if p ∈ (d, φ(d)); in particular distinguishedness depends only on the ideal (d). (b) (Lemma 3.1) Let I ⊂ A be a locally principal ideal with p, I ⊂ rad(A). The following are equivalent: (1) p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A; (2) p ∈ I + φ(I)A; (3) there is a faithfully flat map A → A′ of δ-rings that is an ind-(Zariski localization) such that IA′ is generated by a distinguished element d with d, p ∈ rad(A′).

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring; in (a) d, p ∈ rad(A); in (b) I is locally principal and p, I ⊂ rad(A).
- No global generator of I is assumed in (b).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a) If δ(d) is a unit then p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p shows p ∈ (d, φ(d)). Conversely let p = a d + b φ(d). As d, p ∈ rad(A) it suffices to show A/(p, d, δ(d)) = 0; after a suitable ind-Zariski localization one may assume p, d, δ(d) ∈ rad(A). Substituting φ(d) = d^p + p δ(d) gives p(1 − b δ(d)) = c d; the left side is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (1), so d is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (2), and then δ(d) is a unit lying in the radical, forcing the localized ring to vanish (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.25).
2. (b) (1) ⇒ (2) is clear. (2) ⇒ (3): choose g_1,…,g_n generating the unit ideal with IA[1/g_i] principal; localize each A[1/g_i] along V(p, I) using delta-radical-localization, and let A′ be the product; on each factor apply (a).
3. (3) ⇒ (1): on A′, p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p gives p ∈ I^p A′ + φ(I)A′; descend the containment along the faithfully flat map A → A′.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = Z_p[[q − 1]] and I = ([p]_q): p ∈ (I, φ(I)) because φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q.
- For I = (p^2) ⊂ Z_p: p ∉ I + φ(I)A, consistent with p^2 not being distinguished.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-radical-localization`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`.

### `PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria` — p-torsion in δ-rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria` · lemma · part PR.0.

A δ-ring A is p-torsion-free if its Frobenius φ is injective (for instance if A is perfect), and also if A is reduced. Neither hypothesis implies the other: A = Z_p[x]/(x^p − 1) with φ(x) = x^p is reduced and φ(x − 1) = 0; B = Z_p[x]/(x^2) with φ(x) = p·x is not reduced and φ is injective.

*Hypotheses.*
- A is any δ-ring. (The source assumes Z_(p)-algebras and uses that δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit; this is not needed, because p·x = 0 gives p^{p−1}φ(x) = φ(p^{p−1}x) = 0 and δ(p)φ(x) = 0, hence φ(x) = 0.)

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Stronger claim: if p x = 0 then φ(x) = 0. Apply δ to p x = 0: 0 = p^p δ(x) + x^p δ(p) + p δ(x) δ(p) = p^p δ(x) + φ(x) δ(p). Since δ(p) is a unit (the rings are Z_(p)-algebras) it suffices that p^p δ(x) = 0; but p^p δ(x) = p^{p−1}(φ(x) − x^p) = φ(p^{p−1} x) − p^{p−1} x^p = 0 because p x = 0 and p ≥ 2. If φ is injective, x = 0.
2. If A is reduced and p x = 0: p^p δ(x) = 0 gives p δ(x) = 0 by reducedness; φ(x) = 0 gives x^p = −p δ(x) = 0, so x = 0 (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.28).

*Acceptance.*
- Z ⊕ F_2·ε with the λ = 1 structure of square-zero-delta-family has 2-torsion and is neither reduced nor has injective Frobenius.
- The two examples of Remark 2.29.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`, `mathlib:IsReduced`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`, `PR.0/perfect-prism-properties`, `PR.0/prism-perfection`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 2.28 (p-torsion in δ-rings) with proof; Remark 2.29: “if at least one of the following holds true” (Lemma and the two examples showing the criteria are not comparable.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`.

### `PR.0/perfect-delta-rings` — Perfect δ-rings and Witt vectors of perfect rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings` · theorem · part PR.0.

A δ-ring A is perfect if φ is an isomorphism. The following categories are equivalent: (1) perfect p-complete δ-rings; (2) p-adically complete, p-torsion-free rings A with A/p perfect; (3) perfect F_p-algebras. The functor (1) → (2) forgets δ; in particular every ring map between perfect p-complete δ-rings is a δ-map. The functors between (2) and (3) are A ↦ A/p and R ↦ W(R); in particular W(R) has exactly one δ-structure for R perfect of characteristic p. The inclusion of perfect δ-rings into δ-rings has the left adjoint A ↦ colim_φ A and the right adjoint A ↦ lim_φ A.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime. "p-complete" in (1) and (2) is classical p-adic completeness; for perfect δ-rings it agrees with derived p-completeness because they are p-torsion-free.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. A perfect δ-ring is p-torsion-free by p-torsion-freeness-criteria, and φ reduces to the Frobenius of A/p, which is therefore bijective; this gives (1) → (2), fully faithful by torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence once ring maps are shown to commute with the unique Frobenius lifts.
2. (2) ≃ (3): for R perfect, W(R) is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with W(R)/p = R (Mathlib: WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP and the p-torsion-freeness in the same file); conversely a p-complete p-torsion-free A with A/p perfect is W(A/p) by the uniqueness of deformations of perfect F_p-algebras (vanishing cotangent complex, BS22 proof of Corollary 2.31).
3. On W(R) the Witt vector Frobenius is bijective for R perfect (WittVector.frobenius_bijective) and is the unique lift of Frobenius, giving (2) → (1).
4. The adjoints: colim_φ A and lim_φ A are computed on underlying rings by delta-ring-category and φ becomes bijective on them (Remark 2.27).

*Acceptance.*
- W(F_p) = Z_p with φ = id is perfect; Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p is not (x is not in the image of φ).
- For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], W(R) is the p-completion of Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/p-torsion-freeness-criteria`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_bijective`, `mathlib:WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`, `mathlib:WittVector`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`, `PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `PR.0/ainf-prism`, `PR.0/prism-frobenius-ideal-principal`, `PR.0/prism-perfection`, `PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `PR.0/perfectoid-tor-independence`, `PR.1/perfect-prism-initial`, `PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys`, `PR.2/derived-crystalline-comparison`, `PR.2/perfection-comparison`, `PR.2/perfectoidization-coconnective`, `PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid`, `PR.6/comparison-uniqueness`.

*Sources.*

### `PR.0/rank-one-elements` — Perfect elements have rank one

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rank-one-elements` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let A be a δ-ring and x ∈ A. Then δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A for all n ≥ 0. In particular, if A is p-adically separated and y ∈ A admits a p^n-th root for every n, then δ(y) = 0 (y has rank 1); in particular φ(y) = y^p (the converse needs A p-torsion-free).

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring; for the second statement A is p-adically separated.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reduce to the universal case x = x_0 in the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), which is p-torsion-free. There δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A is equivalent to φ(x^{p^n}) ≡ x^{p^{n+1}} modulo p^{n+1}. For n = 0 this is the definition of φ; inductively, a ≡ b modulo p^k implies a^p ≡ b^p modulo p^{k+1} by the binomial theorem, applied to φ(x) ≡ x^p modulo p (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.32).
2. If y = z_n^{p^n} for every n then δ(y) ∈ ∩_n p^n A = 0. The separatedness hypothesis is needed: on Q[x^{1/p^∞}] the identity is a Frobenius lift and δ(x) = (x − x^p)/p ≠ 0.

*Acceptance.*
- In W(R) for R perfect, the Teichmüller representatives [a] have rank 1: φ([a]) = [a]^p.
- q ∈ Z_p[[q − 1]] with δ(q) = 0 has rank 1 without having p-power roots: the converse of the lemma fails.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`, `PR.0/prismatic-envelope-rank-one-presentation`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 2.32 (Perfect elements have rank 1) with proof: “Perfect elements have rank” (Statement and proof.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Delta/Perfect`, namespace `TauCeti.Delta`.

### `PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings` — Distinguished elements of perfect δ-rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let A be a perfect p-complete δ-ring, so A = W(R) with R = A/p perfect, and let d = Σ_{i≥0} [a_i] p^i be the Teichmüller expansion of d ∈ A. Then d is distinguished if and only if a_1 is a unit of R. Moreover (Lemma 2.34) if A is a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with A/p reduced and d ∈ A is distinguished, then d is a nonzerodivisor and R = A/d satisfies R[p^∞] = R[p].

*Hypotheses.*
- First statement: A perfect and p-complete. Second statement: A p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, A/p reduced (for example A perfect and p-complete); d distinguished.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. With A = W(R) by perfect-delta-rings, δ(d) = (1/p)(Σ [a_i^p] p^i − (Σ [a_i] p^i)^p), so δ(d) ≡ a_1^p modulo p; by p-completeness d is distinguished exactly when a_1 is a unit of R (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.33).
2. Nonzerodivisor: if f d = 0 with f ≠ 0, divide f by a power of p to assume p ∤ f. Applying δ to f d = 0 gives f^p δ(d) + δ(f) φ(d) = 0; multiplying by φ(f) and using φ(f d) = 0 gives f^p φ(f) δ(d) = 0, so f^p φ(f) = 0, hence f^{2p} ≡ 0 modulo p and f ∈ pA because Frobenius is injective on the reduced ring A/p: a contradiction (proof of Lemma 2.34(1)).
3. Bounded torsion: it suffices that R[p] = R[p^2]. If p^2 f = g d then δ(d) g^p + δ(g) φ(d) ∈ pA; multiplying by φ(g) and using φ(d g) ∈ pA gives δ(d) g^p φ(g) ∈ pA, so g^{2p} ∈ pA and g ∈ pA; hence p f ∈ dA (proof of Lemma 2.34(2)).

*Acceptance.*
- In W(F_p) = Z_p: d = p has a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1; d = p^2 has a_1 = 0 and is not distinguished.
- ξ = p − [p^♭] ∈ A_inf(O_C) has unit coefficient of p in its Teichmüller expansion and is distinguished; A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/rank-one-elements`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:IsReduced`, `mathlib:nonZeroDivisors`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/ainf-prism`, `PR.0/prism-frobenius-ideal-principal`, `PR.0/perfect-prism-properties`, `PR.0/prism-perfection`, `PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `PR.0/perfectoid-tor-independence`, `PR.2/perfectoidization-coconnective`.

### `PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope` — The PD envelope of the free δ-ring as a δ-pushout

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) (Lemma 2.35) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-ring and z ∈ A with γ_p(z) = z^p/p! ∈ A. Then γ_n(z) = z^n/n! ∈ A for all n ≥ 0. (2) (Lemma 2.36) The δ-ring C = Z_(p){x, φ(x)/p}, defined as the pushout of Z_(p){z} ← Z_(p){y} → Z_(p){x} along y ↦ p·z and y ↦ φ(x), is identified with the PD envelope D = D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); both are the smallest δ-subring of Z_(p){x}[1/p] containing Z_(p){x} and x^p/p. (3) (Remark 2.37) The same square is a pushout of simplicial commutative rings: the animated ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p to Z_(p){x} is discrete.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; divided powers γ_n(z) = z^n/n! are computed in A[1/p], A being p-torsion-free.
- The printed Remark 2.37 writes D_(x)(Z_(p)) for D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); the corrected form is used (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E3).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) First γ_{p^2}(z) ∈ A: δ(z^p/p) = (z^p + pδ(z))^p/p^2 − z^{p^2}/p^{p+1} ∈ A, and the first term equals p^{p−2}((z^p + pδ(z))/p)^p ∈ A. Then induct on n using γ_{kp} = u·γ_k∘γ_p with u a unit of Z_(p): γ_p(z) is again admissible.
2. (2) The left vertical map of the pushout square is φ on Z_(p){x}, faithfully flat by free-delta-ring, so C is p-torsion-free and embeds in Z_(p){x}[1/p]. D ⊂ C by (1). For C ⊂ D show that φ preserves D and reduces to Frobenius modulo p: φ(x^n/n!) expands with coefficients ((pi)!/i!)·(p^{n−i}/(n−i)!) ∈ Z_(p), divisible by p for 0 < i or i < n, and (x^n/n!)^p = p!·γ_p(x^n/n!) ≡ 0 modulo p.
3. (3) The pushout of animated rings is computed by the derived tensor product; flatness of φ (free-delta-ring) makes it discrete.

*Acceptance.*
- For p = 2 and z = x: δ(x^2/2) = x^4/8 + x^2·δ(x) + δ(x)^2, which exhibits x^4/8 = 3·γ_4(x) as an element of C.
- C ≠ Z_(p){x}[1/p]: 1/p ∉ C.

### `PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope` — PD envelopes of regular sequences are δ-envelopes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) (Lemma 2.38) Let B be a p-torsion-free ring and f_1,…,f_r ∈ B a Koszul-regular sequence on B/p. The derived pushout D′ of D_(x)(Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r]) ← Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r] → B (x_i ↦ f_i) in animated rings is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to the PD envelope D_(f_1,…,f_r)(B); its formation commutes with base change B → B′ to p-torsion-free rings in which the f_i stay Koszul-regular modulo p. (2) (Corollary 2.39) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-ring and f_1,…,f_r ∈ A a regular sequence in A/p. The animated δ-ring A{φ(f_1)/p,…,φ(f_r)/p} (animated-delta-rings) is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to D_I(A), I = (f_1,…,f_r); so D_I(A) is a δ-ring, finitely presented as a δ-A-algebra. (3) (Remark 2.40) D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f_1/p,…,f_r/p}, which depends only on I and is the universal p-torsion-free δ-A-algebra in which p divides I. (4) (Warning 2.41) The Frobenius twist cannot be removed: for A = Z_(p)[x], f = x, the subrings A{x/p} ⊂ A[1/p] for the δ-structures with φ(x) = x^p and φ(x) = x^p + p are not comparable.

*Hypotheses.*
- B, A p-torsion-free; the f_i Koszul-regular on B/p (resp. regular in A/p).
- PD envelopes and their universal property are supplied by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0.
- The misprints in the printed proofs (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E9) do not affect the statements.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) Modulo p, F_p[x] → D_(x)(F_p[x]) is free over F_p[x]/(x_i^p) = Kos(F_p[x]; x_i^p); so D′ ⊗^L F_p is free over Kos(B/p; f_i^p), which is discrete because Kos(B/p; f_i^{n_i}) is discrete for all n_i by induction. Hence D′ is discrete and p-torsion-free. The maps a : D_(f)(B) → D′ (universal property) and b : D′ → D_(f)(B) (pushout) are mutually inverse: check after inverting p and on PD generators.
2. (2) Factor the pushout square as two squares; by free-delta-pd-envelope the middle row is Z_(p){x_i} → D_(x)(Z_(p){x_i}); apply (1) with flat base change Z_(p)[x] → Z_(p){x}.
3. (3), (4) as in the source: A{f_i/p} is characterised by its universal property; the explicit elements δ_1(x/p) and δ_2(x/p) differ by 1/p.

*Acceptance.*
- A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p, f = x: A{x^p/p} is the divided power polynomial algebra on x over Z_p.
- Warning 2.41: δ_1(x/p) = (x^p/p^{p+1})(p^{p−1} − 1) and δ_2(x/p) = δ_1(x/p) + 1/p.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, `mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, `mathlib:DividedPowers`.

### `PR.0/complete-regular-sequence` — Completely regular sequences relative to a base

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/complete-regular-sequence` · definition · part PR.0.

Let A be an animated commutative ring and I = (f_1,…,f_n) ⊂ π_0(A) a finitely generated ideal. Let B be a derived I-complete animated A-algebra. A sequence x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) is I-completely regular relative to A if the map Kos(A; f_1,…,f_n) → Kos(B; f_1,…,f_n, x_1,…,x_r) is a flat map of animated rings. For discrete A and B and I = 0 this says that (x_1,…,x_r) is Koszul-regular on B and B/(x) is flat over A.

*Hypotheses.*
- A animated; I finitely generated; B derived I-complete.
- Kos(A; f) is the derived quotient A ⊗^L_{Z[t_1..t_n]} Z; flatness of a map of animated rings is the notion of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation / DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
- The definition does not depend on the choice of generators of I.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition (BS22 Definition 2.42).
2. Independence of the generators of I: Kos(B; f, x) ≃ Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A Kos(A; f) and π_0(Kos(A; f)) = π_0(A)/I, so flatness of Kos(A; f) → Kos(B; f, x) says exactly that Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A π_0(A)/I is discrete and flat over π_0(A)/I (that is, Kos(B; x) is I-completely flat over A); this does not mention the generators. The source uses this independence without comment.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 2.43, Corollary 2.44: the hypothesis under which PD envelopes and δ-envelopes are completely flat
- BS22 Proposition 3.13 and Example 3.14: the ideals J admitting prismatic envelopes are those locally generated by I and a sequence (p,I)-completely regular relative to A; kernels of surjections from completely smooth algebras onto completely smooth R are of this form
- Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8: the crystalline comparison extends to syntomic algebras because the Čech–Alexander kernels are generated by such sequences

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular` (data): For discrete rings: A → B, an ideal I of A and a sequence x_1,…,x_r in B; the predicate that x is weakly regular on B/IB and that B/(IB + (x_1,…,x_k)) is flat over A/I for every k ≤ r. This discrete condition implies the definition whenever the chosen generators of I form a regular sequence on A and on B; it is the form in which the definition is tested.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.nil` (example): The empty sequence is relatively regular exactly when B/IB is flat over A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.polynomial` (example): The variables x_1,…,x_r of A[x_1,…,x_r] are relatively regular for every ideal I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular.baseChange` (functoriality): Relative regularity is preserved by base change along A → A′.

*Unit tests.*
- `relatively_regular_variable` (computation): In Z[x] over Z with I = (p), the sequence [x] is relatively regular.
- `relatively_regular_empty_self` (degenerate): For B = A the empty sequence is relatively regular for every I.
- `relatively_regular_p_fails` (non-example): In Z over Z with I = (p), the sequence [p] is not relatively regular: it is zero on Z/p, hence not regular there.
- `relatively_regular_non_flat_quotient` (non-example): In Z[x] over Z with I = (0), the sequence [p·x] is regular but not relatively regular: Z[x]/(p·x) is not flat over Z.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p⟨x⟩: the sequence (x) is p-completely regular relative to A.
- For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p: the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A, since Kos(Z_p; p) → Kos(Z_p; p, p) is not flat.

*Depends on:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, `mathlib:RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/pd-envelope-complete-flatness`, `PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Definition 2.42: “is a flat map of simplicial commutative rings” (Definition as printed.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic`.

### `PR.0/pd-envelope-complete-flatness` — Complete flatness of PD envelopes and of p-adic δ-envelopes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-complete-flatness` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) (Lemma 2.43) Let A be an animated ring and B a p-complete animated A-algebra with x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) such that x_1^p,…,x_r^p is p-completely regular relative to A. Let D be the pushout of D_(y)(Z_p[y_1,…,y_r])^∧ ← Z_p[y_1,…,y_r]^∧ → B (y_i ↦ x_i) in derived p-complete animated rings. Then A → D is p-completely flat. (2) (Corollary 2.44) Let A be a p-complete animated δ-ring, B a p-complete animated δ-A-algebra and x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) p-completely regular relative to A. Then C = B{x_1/p,…,x_r/p}^∧, the pushout of Z_p{z_i}^∧ ← Z_p{x_i}^∧ → B (x_i ↦ p·z_i), is p-completely flat over A.

*Hypotheses.*
- Derived p-completion and p-complete flatness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
- In (1) the hypothesis is on the p-th powers x_i^p; in (2) on the x_i themselves.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) Reduce modulo p: D_(y)(F_p[y]) is free over F_p[y]/(y_i^p), so D ⊗^L F_p is a free module over Kos(B ⊗^L F_p; x_i^p), which is flat over A ⊗^L F_p by hypothesis.
2. (2) Apply Frobenius: by pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Remark 2.40) the φ-pullback of B{x_i/p} is the PD envelope of (x_i), to which (1) applies after noting that φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p; then descend complete flatness along the p-completely faithfully flat Frobenius of the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), as in the source.

*Acceptance.*
- A = Z_p, B = Z_p⟨x⟩: C = Z_p{x, x/p}^∧ is p-completely flat over Z_p.
- The hypothesis is not automatic: for B = A = Z_p the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A (complete-regular-sequence), and the corollary does not apply to B{p/p}^∧.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/complete-regular-sequence`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`.

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Envelope`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic`.

### `PR.0/prism` — Prisms ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism` · definition · part PR.0 · planet **Prisms**.

A δ-pair is a δ-ring A with an ideal I ⊂ A. A prism is a δ-pair (A, I) such that (i) I defines a Cartier divisor on Spec(A), that is, I is an invertible A-module (locally generated by a nonzerodivisor); (ii) A is derived (p, I)-complete; (iii) p ∈ I + φ(I)A. Consequences: p and I lie in the Jacobson radical of A; φ(I)A is principal, generated by a distinguished element; I is ind-Zariski locally generated by a distinguished element (local-distinguished-prism-generators).

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime; A is a δ-ring.
- Derived (p, I)-completeness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; it implies p, I ⊂ rad(A).
- A prism is not a δ-ring alone, and no generator of I is part of the data.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition (BS22 Definition 3.2(1)).
2. p, I ⊂ rad(A): for f in an ideal along which A is derived complete, 1 + f·a is a unit (DD.1).
3. The equivalent forms of (iii) are local-distinguished-prism-generators.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 3.5: maps of prisms are rigid: the ideal of the target is generated by the ideal of the source
- BS22 Definition 4.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site: objects of the prismatic site are prisms over a base prism with a map to the formal scheme
- BS22 Theorem 3.10: perfect prisms are equivalent to perfectoid rings
- Bhatt–Lurie Definition 3.1.4 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor: a prism gives a point of the Cartier–Witt stack through A → W(A)

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism` (structure): The structure: a δ-structure on A, an ideal I that is an invertible module, and p ∈ I + φ(I)A (derived completeness is the field supplied by DD.1).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.φ` (projection): The Frobenius lift φ(x) = x^p + p·δ(x) of the prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.bar` (projection): The reduction A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.p_mem_pow` (characterisation): p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.exists_distinguished_generator_map` (characterisation): φ(I)A is a principal ideal generated by a distinguished element.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ext` (extensionality): Two prisms on the same ring with equal δ and equal ideals are equal.

*Unit tests.*
- `prism_ideal_ne_bot` (characterisation): If A is nonzero then the ideal of a prism on A is nonzero.
- `prism_p_squared_fails` (non-example): There is no prism structure on the ring Z_p with ideal (p^2).
- `prism_zero_ring` (degenerate): On the zero ring there is exactly one prism.
- `prism_ideal_p_implies_torsionfree` (characterisation): If the ideal of a prism is (p) then p is a nonzerodivisor of A.

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p, (p)), (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), (A_inf, ker θ) and (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) are prisms.
- (Z_p, (p^2)) is not a prism: p ∉ (p^2) + φ(p^2)Z_p. (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is not a prism: p ∉ (q−1, q^p−1). (Z, (p)) is not a prism: Z is not derived p-complete.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-frobenius-dictionary`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/associated-frobenius`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `mathlib:Module.Invertible`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`.

### `PR.0/prism-category` — Maps of prisms; perfect, bounded, orientable and crystalline prisms

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category` · definition · part PR.0.

A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of δ-rings A → B carrying I into J; prisms form a full subcategory of δ-pairs. A prism (A, I) is perfect if φ is an isomorphism; bounded if A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, that is, (A/I)[p^∞] = (A/I)[p^n] for some n; orientable if I is principal, an orientation being a choice of generator; crystalline if I = (p). A crystalline prism is bounded and orientable. A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is (faithfully) flat if A → B is (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I), (B, J) prisms.
- (p, I)-complete (faithful) flatness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definitions (BS22 Definition 3.2).
2. Crystalline ⇒ bounded and orientable: A is p-torsion-free because I = (p) is invertible, and A/p is killed by p.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 3.7 and Corollary 3.12: bounded prisms with faithfully flat maps form the site on which the structure sheaves are sheaves
- BS22 Theorem 1.8 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site: the comparison theorems are stated over a bounded base prism
- BS22 Theorem 5.2: the crystalline comparison is stated for crystalline prisms
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison: the étale comparison is stated over a perfect prism

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom` (structure): A map of prisms: a ring map commuting with δ and carrying I into J.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom.id` (constructor): The identity map of a prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.Hom.comp` (functoriality): Composition of maps of prisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsBounded` (data): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsPerfect` (data): φ is bijective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsOrientable` (data): I is principal.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline` (data): I = (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline.isBounded` (relation): A crystalline prism is bounded.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.IsCrystalline.isOrientable` (relation): A crystalline prism is orientable.

*Unit tests.*
- `prism_hom_id_toRingHom` (degenerate): The underlying ring map of the identity map of a prism is the identity.
- `prism_hom_map_phi` (compatibility): A map of prisms commutes with the Frobenius lifts.
- `prism_bounded_of_torsionfree_quotient` (characterisation): If p is a nonzerodivisor on A/I then the prism is bounded.
- `prism_perfect_frobenius_injective` (characterisation): A perfect prism has injective Frobenius; a prism with non-injective Frobenius is not perfect.

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p, (p)) is perfect, bounded, oriented by p and crystalline; (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is bounded and orientable, not perfect, not crystalline.
- A δ-map is a map of prisms only if it carries I into J: the map Z_p[[q−1]] → Z_p, q ↦ 1, is a map of prisms ([p]_q) → (p), and there is no map of prisms in the other direction because p is not sent into ([p]_q) by the structure map Z_p → Z_p[[q−1]].

### `PR.0/crystalline-prism` — Crystalline prisms

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism` · construction · part PR.0.

For every p-torsion-free, p-adically complete δ-ring A, the pair (A, (p)) is a crystalline prism, and every crystalline prism is of this form. Examples: (Z_p, (p)) with φ = id; (W(k), (p)) for a perfect field (or perfect F_p-algebra) k with the Witt vector Frobenius; (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with φ(x) = x^p.

*Hypotheses.*
- A is a δ-ring, p-torsion-free and classically p-adically complete.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (p) is invertible because p is a nonzerodivisor; A is derived p-complete because it is classically complete and p-torsion-free (DD.1); p ∈ (p).
2. Conversely if (A, (p)) is a prism then (p) invertible forces p to be a nonzerodivisor, and derived p-completeness with p-torsion-freeness gives classical completeness.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 5.2 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison: the base of the crystalline comparison
- BS22 Construction 6.1: the universal oriented prism maps to a crystalline prism, reducing the Hodge–Tate comparison to characteristic p
- BS22 Theorem 3.10 for R of characteristic p: perfect crystalline prisms (W(R), (p)) correspond to perfect F_p-algebras R

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline` (constructor): The prism (A, (p)) of a δ-ring A in which p is a nonzerodivisor (and which is p-adically complete).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_I` (simp): Its ideal is (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_isCrystalline` (characterisation): It is crystalline.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.padicInt` (example): The prism (Z_p, (p)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.witt` (example): The prism (W(k), (p)) of a perfect ring k of characteristic p.

*Unit tests.*
- `crystalline_prism_padic_phi` (computation): The Frobenius of the prism (Z_p, (p)) is the identity.
- `crystalline_prism_padic_perfect` (characterisation): The prism (Z_p, (p)) is perfect and bounded.
- `crystalline_prism_witt_phi` (compatibility): The Frobenius of the prism (W(k), (p)) is the Witt vector Frobenius.
- `crystalline_prism_bar` (computation): The reduction of (Z_p, (p)) has p = 0 and exactly p elements.

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p, (p)): δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}, a unit, so p is distinguished.
- (F_p, (0)) is not a prism: (0) is not invertible; (Z/p^2, (p)) is not a prism: p is a zero divisor.

### `PR.0/ainf-prism` — The perfect prism of a perfectoid ring

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism` · construction · part PR.0.

Let R be an integral perfectoid ring (in the sense of BMS1 §3, supplied by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra), R^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R/p its tilt, A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and θ : A_inf(R) → R Fontaine's map. Then A_inf(R) with the Witt vector Frobenius and I = ker θ is a perfect prism with A_inf(R)/I = R: ker θ is generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor ξ, and A_inf(R) is classically (p, ξ)-complete. For R = O_C with C a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing a compatible system p^♭ of p-power roots of p (for instance C algebraically closed), one may take ξ = p − [p^♭].

*Hypotheses.*
- R is integral perfectoid: π-adically complete for some π with π^p dividing p (equivalently p-adically complete with π^p = p·unit for some π), Frobenius on R/p surjective and ker θ principal (BMS1 Definition 3.5; BMS2 Definition 4.18).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. W(R^♭) is a perfect p-complete δ-ring by perfect-delta-rings. θ is surjective (Mathlib: surjective_fontaineTheta) and ker θ = (ξ) with ξ having unit first Teichmüller coefficient (BMS1 Remark 3.11, supplied by Q0:integral-algebra), so ξ is distinguished by distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings and a nonzerodivisor by the same node.
2. Completeness: W(R^♭) is p-adically complete and R^♭ is complete for the image of ξ; this gives classical, hence derived, (p, ξ)-completeness. p ∈ (ξ, φ(ξ)) by local-distinguished-prism-generators (a).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 3.10: one of the two functors of the equivalence between perfectoid rings and perfect prisms
- BS22 Theorem 17.2 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison: AΩ is compared with prismatic cohomology over (A_inf, ker θ)
- BS22 Theorem 9.1 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison: the base prism of the étale comparison

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf` (constructor): For a p-adically complete ring O with p not a unit, Frobenius surjective on O/p and ker θ generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor: the prism (W(O^♭), ker θ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_I` (simp): Its ideal is the kernel of Fontaine's θ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_phi` (compatibility): Its Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius of W(O^♭).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_isPerfect` (characterisation): It is a perfect prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.ainf_bar_equiv` (equivalence): θ induces an isomorphism W(O^♭)/ker θ ≅ O.

*Unit tests.*
- `ainf_prism_theta_teichmuller` (computation): θ sends the Teichmüller lift [x] to the untilt of x (Mathlib: fontaineTheta_teichmuller).
- `ainf_prism_kernel_not_p` (non-example): If p ≠ 0 in O then ker θ ≠ (p): p is not in the kernel.
- `ainf_prism_perfect_bounded` (characterisation): The prism (W(O^♭), ker θ) is bounded.

*Acceptance.*
- R = Z_p^cycl-completion, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …): ξ = [p]_q at q = [ε^{1/p}], that is ξ = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}], and θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0.
- R perfect of characteristic p: A_inf(R) = W(R), ker θ = (p), and the prism is the crystalline prism (W(R), (p)).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/theta-naturality`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:PreTilt`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_bijective`.

### `PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism` — The Breuil–Kisin prism

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism` · construction · part PR.0.

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, W = W(k), π a uniformizer of O_K and E(u) ∈ W[u] its Eisenstein minimal polynomial over W[1/p]. Then A = W[[u]] with the δ-structure extending the canonical one on W and satisfying φ(u) = u^p, and I = (E(u)), is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I ≅ O_K via u ↦ π. Every generator of the kernel of A → O_K is distinguished.

*Hypotheses.*
- k perfect of characteristic p; K finite totally ramified over W[1/p]; E Eisenstein of degree e = [K : W[1/p]].
- The source says "discretely valued extension K/Q_p" and "maximal unramified subring"; the perfect residue field hypothesis makes W = W(k) (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E8 records the imprecision).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. A is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ. A is (p, u)-adically complete, hence (p, E)-adically complete since E ≡ u^e modulo p.
2. E is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A. Under the δ-map A → W, u ↦ 0, E maps to E(0) = p·(unit), which is distinguished in W; since units and δ are detected modulo u in the u-complete ring A, δ(E) is a unit.
3. A/E ≅ O_K is p-torsion-free, so the prism is bounded; φ is not surjective (u is not in its image).

*Uses.*
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7/breuil-kisin-evaluation: evaluating a prismatic F-crystal on this prism gives a Breuil–Kisin module
- BS22 §15.2 and AInfCohomology:AI.7: Breuil–Kisin cohomology is prismatic cohomology over this prism
- BS22 Remark 3.11: the analogous prism structure on W[[x_1,…,x_d]] gives perfectoid covers of regular local rings

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin` (constructor): For a power-series δ-ring W[[u]] with φ(u) = u^p over a crystalline base and E ∈ W[u] Eisenstein at p: the prism (W[[u]], (E)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_I` (simp): Its ideal is generated by E(u).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_phi_X` (simp): φ(u) = u^p.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_isBounded` (characterisation): It is a bounded, orientable prism.

*Unit tests.*
- `breuil_kisin_not_perfect` (non-example): The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect: u is not in the image of φ.
- `breuil_kisin_not_crystalline` (non-example): For E = u − p over Z_p the ideal (E) is not (p).
- `breuil_kisin_linear_reduction` (computation): For E = u − p over Z_p, the quotient Z_p[[u]]/(u − p) is Z_p via u ↦ p.

*Acceptance.*
- K = Q_p, π = p: A = Z_p[[u]], E = u − p, δ(u − p) = δ(−p) + (correction) is a unit congruent to δ(−p) modulo u.
- K = Q_p(p^{1/2}), p odd: E = u^2 − p.

### `PR.0/q-de-rham-prism` — The q-de Rham prism

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism` · construction · part PR.0.

A = Z_p[[q − 1]] with the δ-structure determined by φ(q) = q^p (equivalently δ(q) = 0), and I = ([p]_q), where [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at q. Then (A, I) is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I = Z_p[ζ_p]. The ideal of the prism is ([p]_q), not (q − 1): (A, (q − 1)) is not a prism.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is prime.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. A is p-torsion-free and φ(q) = q^p extends uniquely to a continuous ring endomorphism lifting Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ with δ(q) = 0. A is (p, q − 1)-complete, hence (p, [p]_q)-complete because [p]_q ≡ (q − 1)^{p−1} modulo p.
2. [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q − 1), so δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1); δ(p) is a unit and A is (q − 1)-adically complete, so δ([p]_q) is a unit. [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A.
3. A/[p]_q = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free: bounded. For (q − 1): p ∉ (q − 1, q^p − 1) = (q − 1).

*Uses.*
- BS22 §16 and PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair: the base of q-crystalline and q-de Rham cohomology
- BS22 §12.2: the key case of the Nygaard filtration is computed over this prism
- HabiroRings:HR.1 and HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.8: the p-adic chart of the Habiro ring; the identity q^p − 1 = (q − 1)[p]_q relates the two completion ideals

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog` (data): The q-analogue [n]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{n−1} in a ring with a chosen element q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog_mul_sub_one` (relation): (q − 1)·[n]_q = q^n − 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.qAnalog_one_eq` (simp): At q = 1, [n]_q = n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham` (constructor): The prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_I` (simp): Its ideal is generated by [p]_q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_phi_q` (simp): φ(q) = q^p.

*Unit tests.*
- `q_analog_two` (computation): [2]_q = 1 + q.
- `q_analog_prime_cyclotomic` (compatibility): In Z[X] with q = X, [p]_q is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial.
- `q_de_rham_ideal_not_q_minus_one` (non-example): In Z_p[[q − 1]] the ideals ([p]_q) and (q − 1) are different.
- `q_de_rham_p_mem` (characterisation): p ∈ ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) in Z_p[[q − 1]].

*Acceptance.*
- [p]_q evaluated at q = 1 is p; φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q.
- p = 2: [2]_q = 1 + q, δ(1 + q) = δ(1) + δ(q) − q = −q, a unit.
