### `PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology` — Čech–Alexander complexes compute prismatic cohomology; independence of the presentation

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R. Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^•/IC^• are isomorphisms in D(A) (of E_∞-A-algebras), so Δ_{R/A} is computed by the cochain complex of C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} by that of C^•/IC^•. For two presentations B_0 → R and B_0′ → R the presentation B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0′ → R receives maps from both, and the induced maps of cosimplicial rings are compatible with the identifications with Δ_{R/A}; hence the isomorphism class and the comparison isomorphisms do not depend on the presentation (the category of presentations is sifted). In particular the strictly functorial complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) represents the functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) bounded; R p-completely smooth over A/I (or p-completely syntomic, with the same proof).
- The statement uses the general fact: for a topos 𝒳, an abelian sheaf F and a weakly final object X_0 with Čech nerve X_0^•, RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim RΓ(X_0^•,F); if F is acyclic on each X_0^n this is the complex F(X_0^•) (Bhatt–Scholze, footnote to Construction 4.18).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Čech descent: the map from the weakly final object X_0 to the final object of the topos is an epimorphism, so RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim_Δ RΓ(X_0^•,F) by cohomological descent along its Čech nerve (requested from E2; the source adapts Stacks, Tag 07JM).
2. Acyclicity: each (C^n, IC^n) is an object of the site of bounded prisms and O, Ō have no higher cohomology on any object (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3)), so RΓ(X_0^n, O_Δ) = C^n and RΓ(X_0^n, Ō_Δ) = C^n/IC^n.
3. Independence: products of presentations exist, so the category of presentations is sifted (non-empty with binary coproducts); a map of presentations induces a map of Čech nerves of weakly final objects over the final object, hence the identity on RΓ.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = A/I the theorem gives Δ_{R/A} = A.
- Two presentations of A/I⟨X⟩, by A⟨X⟩ and by A⟨X,Y⟩ with Y ↦ 0, give quasi-isomorphic complexes through the presentation A⟨X,Y,X′⟩.
- H^0(Δ_{R/A}) is the equaliser of the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`, `PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`, `PR.1/etale-localization`, `PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line`, `PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Construction 4.18 and its footnote: “it follows from the vanishing assertion” (The theorem is the conclusion of Construction 4.18, with the topos-theoretic lemma of the footnote.)
- BS22-v4, Theorem 5.2, proof (the same argument on the crystalline side): “this recipe is independent of the choice of” (Independence of the presentation by siftedness is stated there for the parallel crystalline construction.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site`.

### `PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology` — The Frobenius of prismatic cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology` · construction · part PR.0.

The structure sheaf O_Δ of (X/A)_Δ is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras: on each object (B,g,f) the ring B carries its δ-structure, with Frobenius lift φ_B(x) = x^p + pδ(x), and maps of prisms commute with δ. Hence φ : O_Δ → O_Δ is an endomorphism of sheaves of rings which is φ_A-semilinear, that is A-linear as a map O_Δ → φ_{A,*}O_Δ. It induces φ_X : Δ_{X/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) and φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A} in D(A), maps of commutative algebra objects, natural in X (or R) and compatible with base change of the prism. By adjunction φ_R is the same as its linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, where φ_A^* = − ⊗^L_{A,φ_A} A (derived (p,I)-completed where stated). On a Čech–Alexander model, φ_R is induced by the termwise Frobenius lifts of the cosimplicial δ-ring C^•.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) bounded prism, X a p-adic formal scheme over A/I (smooth where comparison theorems are used).
- φ_A need not be flat or an isomorphism; φ_A^* is a derived functor and is not assumed to commute with totalisations unless proved (Theorem 5.2, proof).
- φ carries I into φ(I)A, which is contained in I only for crystalline prisms; so in general Ō_Δ has no induced endomorphism (for I = (p) it has the Frobenius); reduction modulo I after φ gives the maps used in the de Rham comparison.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Maps of prisms are maps of δ-rings (PR.0/prism-category), so the Frobenius lifts φ_B are natural in the object: φ is an endomorphism of the presheaf O_Δ, semilinear over φ_A because g is a δ-map.
2. Apply Rν_* and RΓ: restriction of scalars along φ_A is exact, so R ν_*(φ_{A,*}O_Δ) = φ_{A,*}Rν_*O_Δ, giving φ_X and φ_R as maps of commutative algebra objects.
3. The linearisation is the adjoint map under the adjunction between derived extension of scalars along φ_A and restriction of scalars (requested from DD.1 with its completed form).
4. On C^•: each C^n is a δ-A-algebra and cofaces and codegeneracies are δ-maps, so φ is a map of cosimplicial rings over φ_A; under PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology it induces φ_R.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 5.2: the crystalline comparison is Frobenius-equivariant
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 6.4: the de Rham comparison is the reduction of the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ modulo I
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (Theorem 15.3, Corollary 15.5): the linearised Frobenius factors through Lη_I and is an isogeny
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (Theorem 9.1): étale cohomology is the fibre of φ − 1 after inverting I

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius` (data): The endomorphism φ of the presheaf of rings O_Δ, with component φ_B on the object (B,g,f).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius_structureMap` (compatibility): φ_B(g(a)) = g(φ_A(a)) for a ∈ A: the Frobenius of O_Δ is φ_A-semilinear.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.frobenius_naturality` (functoriality): For a map R → S of A/I-algebras the square formed by φ_R, φ_S and the induced maps Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} commutes.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site.frobeniusLinearization` (data): The linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the adjoint of φ_R under φ_A^* ⊣ φ_{A,*}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr1_frobenius_sheaf_component` (computation): On an object (B,g,f) the Frobenius of O_Δ is x ↦ x^p + pδ(x).
- `pr1_frobenius_trivial_base` (degenerate): If φ_A is the identity (for instance A = Z_p) then φ_{A,*} is isomorphic to the identity functor of D(A), so φ_R is an A-linear endomorphism of Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr1_frobenius_not_linear` (non-example): If φ_A(a) ≠ a and g : A → B is injective then φ_B(g(a)) ≠ g(a): the Frobenius is not A-linear, so it is not an endomorphism of Δ_{R/A} in D(A).

*Acceptance.*
- On Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A the Frobenius is φ_A.
- For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) the Frobenius of Δ_{R/Z_p} is Z_p-linear.
- For a crystalline prism, φ corresponds under the crystalline comparison to the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology (PR.1/crystalline-comparison).

### `PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude` — Base change along maps of finite complete Tor amplitude

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) → (A′,IA′) be a map of bounded prisms such that A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude, let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and R′ := R ⊗̂_A A′ its p-completed base change (a p-completely smooth A′/IA′-algebra). Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ → Δ_{R′/A′} and Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} A′/IA′ → Δ̄_{R′/A′} are isomorphisms, the completions being derived (p,I)-adic and p-adic. More precisely, for every map of bounded prisms the termwise completed base change C^• ⊗̂_A A′ of the functorial Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of R computes Δ_{R′/A′}, and the Tor amplitude hypothesis is used only to commute the completed base change with the totalisation.

*Hypotheses.*
- Both prisms are bounded; A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude: A′ ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) has finite Tor amplitude over A/(p,I).
- R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
- The Tor amplitude hypothesis is removed by PR.1/prismatic-base-change, which uses the Hodge–Tate comparison; the present statement is an input of that comparison and cannot be replaced by it.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Termwise statement (Lemma 4.20, proof): C^n is the prismatic envelope of a completed free δ-A-algebra; by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (2) envelopes commute with base change along every map of bounded prisms, and the base change of a weakly initial object and of its Čech nerve is again one for R′. So C^• ⊗̂_A A′ computes Δ_{R′/A′} by PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology.
2. Lemma 4.22: for a ring C with a finitely generated ideal J and a map C → C′ of finite J-complete Tor amplitude, the J-completed base change commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial objects of D^{≥0}. Proof in the source: finite skeleta commute, and the functor K ↦ (K ⊗^L_C C′) ⊗^L Kos(C′;x_1^m,…,x_r^m) lowers the degree of coconnectivity by a constant independent of m. Requested from DD.1.
3. Apply Lemma 4.22 to C^• over (A,(p,I)), and reduce modulo I for Δ̄.

*Acceptance.*
- A completely flat map of bounded prisms satisfies the hypothesis with amplitude 0.
- The map α of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism satisfies the hypothesis.
- For A → A′ with infinite complete Tor dimension the statement is not available at this point of the theory.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`, `PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 4.20, Lemma 4.22 and their proofs: “Tor amplitude assumption above can be dropped” (The node is Lemma 4.20 together with the algebraic Lemma 4.22 used in its proof.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site`.

### `PR.1/etale-localization` — Étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R → S a p-completely étale map of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Then the natural map Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an isomorphism (derived p-completed tensor product). The restriction functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ has, in the algebraic language, a left adjoint F : (R/A)_Δ → (S/A)_Δ sending (B → B/IB ← R) to (B_S → B_S/IB_S ← S), where B_S is the unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra with B_S/IB_S = B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S; F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is bounded; R and S are p-completely smooth over A/I and R → S is p-completely étale: S is derived p-complete and S ⊗^L_R R/p is étale over R/p.
- The statement is for Δ̄; the corresponding statement for Δ follows only after completion along I and is not an S-linear statement, since Δ_{R/A} is not an R-module.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Construction of F (Lemma 4.21, proof): for an object (B → B/IB ← R) the map B/IB → B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S is p-completely étale; by Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 with Elkik algebraization (stage PR.0, DD.1) it deforms uniquely to a (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra B_S, and (B_S, IB_S) is a bounded prism by PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness. Adjointness follows from the uniqueness of étale lifts.
2. As a left adjoint F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects. Apply it to the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object C^• of R: D^• := F(C^•) is the Čech nerve of a weakly initial object of (S/A)_Δ, so D^•/ID^• computes Δ̄_{S/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, whose proof only needs a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve).
3. Termwise C^n/IC^n ⊗̂^L_R S ≅ D^n/ID^n by the definition of F; the p-completed base change along the p-completely flat map R → S commutes with the totalisation by Lemma 4.22 (DD.1).

*Acceptance.*
- For a p-completed localisation S = R⟨1/f⟩: Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R⟨1/f⟩.
- Étale chart: for a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S; with the Hodge–Tate comparison for the polynomial ring this gives H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^i_{S/(A/I)}{−i}.
- For R = S the functor F is the identity.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-etale-extension`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`, `PR.1/acceptance-computations`, `PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `PR.6/nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 4.21 and its proof: “it preserves coproducts and carries weakly initial objects to weakly initial objects” (The node is Lemma 4.21 with the adjoint functor of its proof.)

### `PR.1/bockstein-differential` — The Bockstein differential on twisted Hodge–Tate cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra (or X smooth over A/I, with sheaves on X_ét). For i ≥ 0 the connecting map of the triangle Δ̄_{R/A}{i+1} → Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{R/A}{i} is the Bockstein differential β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}. With the cup product of the commutative algebra object Δ̄_{R/A}, the graded group H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} = ⊕_i H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is a graded-commutative differential graded A/I-algebra: β_I is A/I-linear, β_I ∘ β_I = 0 and β_I(xy) = β_I(x)y + (−1)^{deg x} x β_I(y). Its degree-0 part is an R-algebra through η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}), and β_I ∘ η^0_R : R → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} is an A/I-linear derivation into a derived p-complete R-module. It therefore induces the R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1}, f dg ↦ f·β_I(η^0_R(g)), where Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} is the p-completed module of differentials, finite projective over R.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
- β_I is A/I-linear but not R-linear.
- Graded commutativity is xy = (−1)^{deg x · deg y} yx. The vanishing of squares of odd elements is not part of this node; for elements β_I(f), f ∈ R, it is Lemma 4.10 and is proved in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line.
- When I = (d) the twists are trivialised by d and β_I is the Bockstein of the triangle Δ → Δ → Δ̄ given by multiplication by d (the convention of the source for d = p).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Construction 4.9: the triangle is that of PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology; its connecting map Δ̄{i} → Δ̄{i+1}[1] induces β_I on cohomology.
2. β_I ∘ β_I = 0: the two triangles for i and i+1 come from the filtration of Δ ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+3} by powers of I, and a composite of consecutive connecting maps of a three-step filtration vanishes on cohomology.
3. Leibniz rule: the I-adic filtration of the commutative algebra object Δ_{R/A} is multiplicative, so the connecting maps of its graded pieces form a derivation on ⊕_i H^*(gr^i) (the standard multiplicativity of the Bockstein spectral sequence of a filtered commutative algebra object; requested from DD.1 as the multiplicative I-adic filtration).
4. η^0 is H^0 of the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}. The derivation β_I η^0 factors through the completed differentials because its target is derived p-complete (universal property of Ω^1, completed form requested from DD.2).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9: the target of the Hodge–Tate comparison map is this dg algebra
- Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2: η^0 and η^1 are proved to be isomorphisms for the affine line before η^* is available in general
- Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 4.15: the extension class of τ^{≤1}Δ̄ is the Bockstein; it is the cotangent complex L_{X/A}
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (Theorem 15.3): Lη_I of Δ has terms H^i(Δ̄){i} and differential β_I

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistedCohomology` (data): The R-module H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) ⊗_R R{i}, for i ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein` (data): The additive map β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}; it is A/I-linear.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_comp_bockstein` (relation): β_I ∘ β_I = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.cup` (structure): The cup product H^i{i} × H^j{j} → H^{i+j}{i+j}, R-bilinear, associative, unital and graded-commutative.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_cup` (relation): β_I(x ∪ y) = β_I(x) ∪ y + (−1)^i x ∪ β_I(y) for x of degree i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta0` (data): The R-linear map η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}){0}, a ring map for the cup product.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta1` (universal-property): The R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} with η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)).

*Unit tests.*
- `pr1_bockstein_eta1_d` (computation): η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)) for every g ∈ R; hence η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `pr1_bockstein_base_zero` (degenerate): For R = A/I, β_I vanishes on H^0(Δ̄_{(A/I)/A}) = A/I.
- `pr1_bockstein_not_linear` (non-example): If dg ≠ 0 in Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} for a p-completely smooth R, then β_I(η^0_R(g)) ≠ 0 although β_I(η^0_R(1)) = 0: β_I is not R-linear.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = A/I the cohomology is A/I in degree 0 and β_I = 0.
- For R = A/I⟨X⟩, β_I(X) is a generator of H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line).
- For a crystalline prism and I = (p), β_p is the Bockstein of crystalline cohomology modulo p², which on the de Rham complex of a lift sends the class of x^p to the class of x^{p−1}dx.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`, `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential.D`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line`, `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`, `PR.1/acceptance-computations`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Construction 4.9: “we have a Bockstein differential” (The node is the Bockstein differential, the dg-algebra structure and the maps η^0, η^1 of Construction 4.9.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/HodgeTate/Comparison`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate`.

### `PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma` — The relative Frobenius of a polynomial Čech nerve is a cosimplicial quasi-isomorphism on modules

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let k be a commutative ring of characteristic p, B a polynomial k-algebra (in any set of variables), B^• the Čech nerve of k → B (B^n = B^{⊗_k (n+1)}), and B^{•,(1)} := B^• ⊗_{k,Frob} k its Frobenius twist, with the relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•, a map of cosimplicial k-algebras. For every cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module N the natural map N → N ⊗_{B^{•,(1)}} B^• induces a quasi-isomorphism on the associated unnormalised cochain complexes of k-modules.

*Hypotheses.*
- k is a ring with p = 0; B is a polynomial k-algebra; no finiteness on the number of variables.
- N is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial ring B^{•,(1)}; the tensor product is termwise.
- In the proof the displayed decomposition of the monoid M = N^r reads ⊔_{s ∈ S} (pM + s) = M with S = {0,…,p−1}^r; the printed index set is M (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E11).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Filtered colimits reduce to finitely many variables: B = k[M], M = N^r. The Čech nerve is k[EM] for the cosimplicial monoid EM, [n] ↦ M^{[n]}, and B^{•,(1)} → B^• is k[E(pM)] → k[EM].
2. With S = {0,…,p−1}^r, the subsets S^{[n]} ⊂ M^{[n]} are preserved by the coface maps (they only insert 0), so ES ⊂ EM is a semi-cosimplicial subset and k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] as semi-cosimplicial k[E(pM)]-modules; the unit corresponds to id ⊗ η with η : k → k[ES] induced by 0 ∈ S.
3. The unnormalised complex depends only on the semi-cosimplicial structure, so it suffices that id_N ⊗ η : N → N ⊗_k k[ES] is a quasi-isomorphism.
4. k[ES] is the semi-cosimplicial module underlying the Čech nerve C^• of k → k[M^{grp}/pM^{grp}], and η underlies its unit, which is a cosimplicial homotopy equivalence because the algebra map has a section; homotopy equivalences of cosimplicial k-modules are preserved by N ⊗_k −.

*Acceptance.*
- For B = k (no variables) the map is the identity.
- For B = k[x] and N = B^{•,(1)} the lemma says that k[x^p]-type Čech complex and the Čech complex of k → k[x] are quasi-isomorphic; both are resolutions of k.
- The decomposition k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] is an isomorphism of semi-cosimplicial modules only: codegeneracies do not preserve S (p = 2, r = 1: (1,1) ↦ 2 ∉ S).

*Depends on:* `mathlib:AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex`, `mathlib:MvPolynomial`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 5.4 and its proof: “gives a quasi-isomorphism on associated unnormalized chain complexes of” (The node is Lemma 5.4.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Crystalline/Comparison`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline`.

### `PR.1/crystalline-comparison` — The crystalline comparison ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Crystalline comparison**.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism (A is a p-torsion-free, p-complete δ-ring) and let I ⊂ A be an ideal with divided powers and p ∈ I. The Frobenius of A/p kills I/pA, so it induces ψ : A/I → A/p. Let R be a smooth A/I-algebra and R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/I,ψ} A/p, a smooth A/p-algebra. Let RΓ_crys(R/A) be the crystalline cohomology of Spec(R) relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/I) ⊂ Spf(A) (p-adically: the derived limit over n of the crystalline cohomology over A/p^n). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) of E_∞-A-algebras, compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms (the Frobenius of prismatic cohomology on the left, the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology induced by the Frobenius of Spec(R) and φ_A on the right). In the case I = (p), with C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R and D^• the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of the same presentation, the isomorphism is induced by a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras φ_A^*C^• → D^•, where φ_A^*C^• (termwise base change along φ_A) computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism, hence bounded; I is a PD ideal containing p (its divided powers are unique since A is p-torsion-free, and they are compatible with the canonical ones on (p)).
- R is a smooth A/I-algebra in the usual sense (A/I has characteristic p).
- The Frobenius twist is on the prismatic side: it is R^{(1)}, not R, whose prismatic cohomology is the crystalline cohomology of R. For I = (p) and with base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) this reads φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A); the untwisted statement Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) is false in general.
- The statement φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is termwise; it is not claimed here that φ_A^* commutes with the totalisation of C^•.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Crystalline side, I = (p) (requested from CR.1 and CR.2). For a presentation B_0 → R with kernel J_0, B := Free_δ(B_0)^∧ and R′ := B/J_0B, let D_0, D be the p-completed PD envelopes of J_0 ⊂ B_0 and J_0B ⊂ B; they are p-torsion-free (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, Lemma 2.38), and the pro-object {(D/p^n → R′ ← R)}_n of the big crystalline site is weakly initial and compatible with coproducts. Hence RΓ_crys(R/A) ≃ lim D^•, D^• the envelope of the Čech nerve, independently of the presentation; big and small sites agree (Berthelot, III.4.1.4).
2. Prismatic side. C^• = B^•{J_0^•B^•/p}^∧ computes Δ_{R/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), and its termwise base change φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude, termwise part). By PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39), D^• = B^•{φ(J_0^•)B^•/p}^∧. The relative Frobenius of A → B^• therefore induces η : φ_A^*C^• → D^•, and D^• is the pullback of the cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module φ_A^*C^• along the flat relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•.
3. Both sides of η are p-torsion-free. By PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma applied to N = φ_A^*C^•/p, η is a quasi-isomorphism modulo p, hence a quasi-isomorphism by derived Nakayama (DD.1).
4. Frobenius. η is a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras; the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology corresponds to the δ-Frobenius of D^• under RΓ_crys ≃ lim D^•, by functoriality of crystalline cohomology for the Frobenius endomorphism of the simplicial PD thickening (requested from CR.3).
5. General I. The map A/p → A/I is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel, so R lifts to a smooth A/p-algebra R̃, and R̃ ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}; the case I = (p) for R̃ and the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base give the isomorphism. It is canonical: for a presentation B_0 → R with B_0 a δ-A-algebra, the PD envelope D^• of the Čech nerve has φ_{D^•}(ker(D^• → R)) ⊂ pD^•, giving a cosimplicial object (D^• → D^•/p ← R^{(1)}) of (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ and hence a map Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} → lim D^• independent of choices; it agrees with the previous map because η is a morphism of cosimplicial objects of the site (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ (the source leaves this compatibility to the reader).

*Acceptance.*
- A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[x]: Δ_{F_p[x]/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[x]/Z_p), the de Rham complex of Z_p⟨x⟩; here R^{(1)} = R.
- A = W(k) with k perfect and R̃ smooth over k: Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)); the twist is by the Frobenius of k.
- A = A_crys(O_C/p) and I = ker(A_crys → O_C/p), a PD ideal strictly containing (p): for R smooth over O_C/p, Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_crys} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A_crys), with ψ : O_C/p → A_crys/p induced by the Frobenius.

### `PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic` — The crystalline comparison for syntomic algebras

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism, J ⊂ A a PD ideal with p ∈ J, and R a syntomic A/J-algebra (flat, of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres). Put R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/J,ψ} A/p. Then there is a canonical Frobenius-compatible isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras RΓ((R^{(1)}/A)_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), where the left side is the cohomology of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} and the right side is crystalline cohomology relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/J) ⊂ Spf(A). For R smooth this is PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,(p)) crystalline; J a PD ideal containing p; R syntomic over A/J.
- The left side is site cohomology. Its identification with derived prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)}, and the extension of the comparison from quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras by descent, belong to PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (nodes derived-agrees-with-site, qrsp-prism and quasisyntomic-descent) and consume this node; they are not asserted here.
- For J ≠ (p) the reduction to J = (p) uses a syntomic lift of R to A/p, which exists Zariski-locally (a relative global complete intersection lifts by lifting its equations, and flatness is checked on the unchanged fibres); the canonical map of the smooth case glues the local isomorphisms.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Presentation: choose B_0 → R̃ with B_0 a p-completed polynomial A-algebra and R̃ a (local) syntomic lift over A/p. In each cosimplicial degree the kernel of B^n → R̃ is the filtered union of ideals (p, x_1,…,x_r) with (x_1,…,x_r) p-completely regular relative to A (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8). Hence PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes applies along the colimit: the envelopes C^n exist, are p-completely flat over A and form a weakly initial Čech nerve, exactly as in PR.1/cech-alexander-complex.
2. The cohomology of the site (R̃/A)_Δ is lim C^• by the argument of PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, which only uses a weakly initial object and the acyclicity of O_Δ on objects; termwise base change gives φ_A^*C^• for R^{(1)}.
3. The crystalline side is computed by the cosimplicial PD envelope D^• for any R (CR.2), and D^• = B^•{φ(J^•)/p}^∧ by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, since the kernels are ind-regular modulo p.
4. The comparison map φ_A^*C^• → D^• and the proof that it is a quasi-isomorphism (PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma, which concerns only the polynomial Čech nerve, then derived Nakayama) and Frobenius-compatible are those of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

*Acceptance.*
- R = F_p[x]/(x^n) over (Z_p,(p)): the prismatic site cohomology of R^{(1)} = R is RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), computed by the PD envelope of (x^n) in Z_p⟨x⟩ with its de Rham complex.
- R = k[x,y]/(xy) over W(k): a syntomic, non-smooth example.
- For R smooth the statement and the map coincide with PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

- ALB23, Remark 3.1.8 (2), last sentence: “The statement extends by descent from the quasi-regular semiperfect case to all quasi-syntomic rings over” (The descent extension named there is the part consumed by PR.2; the node records the dependency and does not assert it.)

### `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p` — The Hodge–Tate comparison in characteristic p

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism and S a smooth A/p-algebra. (1) For every f ∈ S the class β_p(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) has square zero, so the maps η^0_S, η^1_S of PR.1/bockstein-differential extend uniquely to a map of commutative differential graded A/p-algebras η^*_S : (Ω^*_{S/(A/p)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{S/A}), β_p), the twists being trivialised by the generator p of I. (2) η^*_S is an isomorphism: H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/p)}{−i} for all i. (3) The functor S ↦ Δ_{S/A} commutes with p-completed base change along every map of crystalline prisms (A,(p)) → (A′,(p)): Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{S ⊗_A A′/A′}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism; S is smooth over A/p.
- The source states (2) for 'the comparison map from Theorem 4.11', whose construction for p = 2 rests on Lemma 4.10, itself deduced from Proposition 6.2, whose proof uses this corollary. The order adopted here removes the circle: (1) is proved together with (2) from the Cartier isomorphism, and Proposition 6.2 then only uses the statement for η^0 and η^1 of the affine line.
- The Cartier isomorphism is imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/26).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reductions. By PR.1/etale-localization and the local structure of smooth algebras (Zariski-locally étale over a polynomial algebra) both sides localise, so S = A/p[X_1,…,X_n]. A is p-torsion-free, so Z_p → A is p-completely flat and PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude reduces to A = Z_p, S = F_p[X_1,…,X_n].
2. S = R^{(1)} for R = F_p[X_1,…,X_n], and PR.1/crystalline-comparison gives Δ_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), hence Δ̄_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) ⊗^L F_p ≃ Ω^•_{R/F_p}, the de Rham complex of R (crystalline cohomology of R is the de Rham complex of the lift Z_p⟨X⟩; requested from CR.2). The S-algebra structure of H^0 corresponds to the relative Frobenius S = R^{(1)} → H^0(Ω^•_{R/F_p}).
3. Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map): C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R^{(1)}/F_p} ≅ H^i(Ω^•_{R/F_p}) is an isomorphism of graded R^{(1)}-algebras. So H^*(Δ̄_{S/Z_p}) ≅ Ω^*_S as graded S-algebras; this algebra is strictly graded-commutative, which gives (1).
4. Identification with η^*. On the lift Z_p⟨X⟩ with φ(X_j) = X_j^p, the Bockstein of the class of x^p is the class of d(φ(x̃))/p = x^{p−1}dx + dδ(x̃), which is C^{−1}(dx). So η^1_S = C^{−1} on generators, and η^*_S = C^{−1} by multiplicativity; this proves (2).
5. (3): by derived Nakayama it suffices to compare modulo p, where both sides have cohomology Ω^i, which commutes with base change.

*Acceptance.*
- S = F_p[X] over Z_p: H^0(Δ̄) = F_p[X], H^1(Δ̄) = F_p[X]·β_p(X), H^i = 0 for i ≥ 2; under the crystalline comparison β_p(X) is the class of X^{p−1}dX.
- S = F_2[X] (p = 2): β_2(X)² = 0.
- Base change: for a map of crystalline prisms Z_p → W(k), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

### `PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism` — Mapping an oriented prism to a crystalline one

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (A,(d)) be an oriented prism such that A/(d) is p-torsion-free and the Frobenius A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p), x ↦ x^p, is flat (for example the universal oriented prism, the (p,d)-completion of Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{−1}}). Let B := A{φ(d)/p}^∧ be the p-complete animated δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining φ(d)/p. Then: (a) B is discrete and p-torsion-free, it is the p-completed PD envelope of (d) ⊂ A, and φ(d) = p·u in B with u a unit; B is (p,d)-complete. (b) The composite α : A → B of φ_A : A → A with the canonical map A → B satisfies α(d) ∈ pB, so α is a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)) and (B,(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism. (c) Modulo p, α factors as A/p → A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) → B/p = D_{(d)}(A/p), where the first map has finite Tor amplitude, the second is the Frobenius and is faithfully flat, and the third is free. (d) The completed base change functor α̂^* : D_{comp}(A) → D_{comp}(B) on derived (p,d)-complete objects is conservative and has finite (p,d)-complete Tor amplitude. (e) For every p-completely smooth A/(d)-algebra R with p-completed base change R_B, α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B} and α̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,(d)) is an oriented prism with A/(d) p-torsion-free; then p is a nonzerodivisor on A and (p,d) is a regular sequence.
- The Frobenius hypothesis is the corrected one of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E13: only the flatness of A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) is used, and this is what Example 3.4 provides for the universal oriented prism; the printed hypothesis 'the Frobenius on A/p is flat' is stronger than what is proved there.
- α is the Frobenius-twisted canonical map; the canonical map A → B itself is not a map of prisms to (B,(p)), since the image of d is not divisible by p.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a): by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39 with the regular element d of A/p), A{φ(d)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope of (d), discrete and p-torsion-free; φ(d) = p·u with u a unit by PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity (Lemma 2.24), because φ(d) is distinguished and divisible by p. Since d^p ∈ (p, φ(d)), p-completeness implies (p,d)-completeness.
2. (b): α(d) = φ(d) = pu ∈ pB; α is a δ-map as a composite of δ-maps; (B,(p)) is a crystalline prism by PR.0/crystalline-prism.
3. (c): B/p is the PD envelope of (d) in A/p, free over A/(p,d^p) with basis the divided powers γ_{kp}(d) (CR.0); the composite A/p → B/p is induced by φ, which factors through A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p).
4. (d): by derived Nakayama conservativity and Tor amplitude are checked modulo p for d-completed base change along the three maps of (c): the first is a quotient by a regular element, the others are faithfully flat (DD.1).
5. (e): PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude applied to α, using (d).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2 and Theorem 6.3: the Hodge–Tate comparison over the universal oriented prism is reduced to the crystalline prism (D_0,(p)) by conservativity of α̂^*
- Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.2, proof: for a general oriented prism the pushout E = A ⊗̂_{A_0} D_0 and the base change of α are used
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.3 (§15): the same reduction to the crystalline case is used for the Nygaard filtration and Lη

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization` (constructor): The bounded crystalline prism (B,(p)), B = A{φ(d)/p}^∧, attached to an oriented prism (A,(d)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationCan` (data): The canonical δ-map A → B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationMap` (data): The map of prisms α : (A,(d)) → (B,(p)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationMap_apply` (simp): α(a) = can(φ_A(a)) for a ∈ A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_isCrystalline` (characterisation): The prism ideal of B is (p).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_frobenius_unit` (relation): can(φ_A(d)) = p·u for a unit u of B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallization_cohomology` (compatibility): For R p-completely smooth over A/(d) and R_B its base change, the base change map Δ_{R/A} → α_*Δ_{R_B/B} induces α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr1_crystallization_alpha_d` (computation): α(d) lies in pB.
- `pr1_crystallization_alpha_eq` (compatibility): α = can ∘ φ_A; in particular α(d) = can(d)^p + p·can(δ(d)).
- `pr1_crystallization_can_not_prism_map` (non-example): If A/(p,d) ≠ 0 then can(d) ∉ pB: the untwisted canonical map A → B does not carry (d) into (p), so it is not a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)).

*Acceptance.*
- For the universal oriented prism A_0 the ring D_0 = A_0{φ(d)/p}^∧ receives Z_p, and (Z_p,(p)) → (D_0,(p)) is a map of crystalline prisms.
- For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]],(E(u))) the construction gives the p-completed PD envelope of (E(u)), a ring of Breuil type, with α induced by φ.
- α(d) = φ(d) is p times a unit; the canonical image of d is not in pB.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/animated-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

### `PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line` — The Hodge–Tate comparison for the affine line and the vanishing of β(f)²

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R = A/I⟨X⟩ the p-adic completion of the polynomial ring in one variable. Then η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) and η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} are isomorphisms and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) = 0 for i > 1. Consequently (Lemma 4.10): for every bounded prism (A,I), every smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I and every local section f of O_X, the element β_I(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{X/A}){1} has square zero.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is an arbitrary bounded prism; no orientation and no torsion-freeness is assumed.
- Only the maps η^0 and η^1 of PR.1/bockstein-differential occur in the statement; the full map η^* is constructed afterwards (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map).
- The printed proof refers to Ω^1_{R/(A/d)} for a general prism; it is Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Choose η : R ⊕ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) inducing η^0 and η^1{−1} on cohomology, possible since both modules are finite free over R; it suffices that η is an isomorphism. The consequence follows by functoriality: f defines A/I⟨X⟩ → O_X(U), and β_I(X)² lies in H^2 = 0.
2. I = (p): this is PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p for S = A/p[X] in degrees 0 and 1.
3. Universal oriented prism (A_0,(d)): the base change α̂^* of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism is conservative and carries Δ̄_{R/A_0} to Δ̄_{R_{D_0}/D_0} and η to the corresponding map over the crystalline prism (D_0,(p)), which is an isomorphism by the previous step.
4. General oriented bounded prism (A,(d)): the orientation gives A_0 → A; with a : A_0 → D_0 the map α and E := A ⊗̂^L_{A_0} D_0, b : A → E, c : Z_p → E, the functor b̂^* is conservative on (p,d)-complete objects. Using the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of the affine line (PR.1/cech-alexander-complex, Remark 4.19) and Lemma 4.22 (b and c have finite complete Tor amplitude), b̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ ĉ^*Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p}, compatibly with the maps η; the claim reduces to the case A = Z_p already treated.
5. General bounded prism: there is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (A′,(d)) with A′ oriented (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness, Lemma 3.7 (4)); flat base change (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude) and faithful flatness reduce to the oriented case.

*Acceptance.*
- A = Z_p: Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p} has H^0 = F_p[X], H^1 = F_p[X]·β(X), nothing else.
- q-de Rham prism: for R = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨X⟩ over (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free of rank one over R.
- p = 2: β_I(f)² = 0 for every f, which graded commutativity alone does not give.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/universal-oriented-prism`.

### `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map` — The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a unique map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) of sheaves of commutative differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét which in degree 0 is the structure map η^0_X : O_X → H^0(Δ̄_{X/A}); in degree 1 it is η^1_X, f dg ↦ f β_I(g), and η^i(f_0 df_1 ∧ … ∧ df_i) = f_0 β_I(f_1) ⋯ β_I(f_i). It is O_X-linear in each degree, compatible with the O_X-module structures, functorial in X and compatible with maps of bounded prisms. Its construction depends functorially only on the commutative algebra object Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) together with the O_X-algebra structure on Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}. Here Ω^i is the p-completed module of differential forms.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism and X is smooth over A/I.
- The existence of η^* uses Lemma 4.10: β_I(f)² = 0 for every local section f of O_X. For p odd this follows from graded commutativity; for p = 2 it is deduced from the affine line (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line), by functoriality along A/I⟨T⟩ → O_X(U), T ↦ f.
- The universal property used is that of the de Rham complex: Ω^*_{R/k} is initial among graded-commutative differential graded k-algebras E with a k-algebra map R → E^0 such that squares of the elements d(r) vanish (completed form for p-completely smooth R).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By PR.1/bockstein-differential the target is a graded-commutative dg A/I-algebra with O_X → H^0 and with η^0 ⊕ η^1 compatible with d and β_I.
2. Lemma 4.10 (from PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line): β_I(f)² = 0. Hence the elements β_I(f) generate a strictly graded-commutative sub-dg-algebra, and the universal property of the de Rham complex (requested from DD.2, built on DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex) extends η^0 ⊕ η^1 uniquely to η^*.
3. Functoriality in X and in the prism follows from uniqueness; the sheaf version is obtained from the affine maps η^*_R by Zariski and étale gluing.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorems 4.11 and 6.3: the Hodge–Tate comparison is the statement that η^* is an isomorphism
- Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 4.15: the maps H^i(μ), i = 0, 1, of the cotangent complex comparison are identified with η^0, η^1
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (Construction 7.6): the derived Hodge–Tate comparison is the left Kan extension of η^* on the canonical filtration
- PerfectoidQuotients:Q1: exports the Hodge–Tate comparison for smooth algebras

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap` (data): The R-linear map η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}, for every i ≥ 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_one` (simp): η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_wedge` (relation): η^{i+j}_R(ω ∧ τ) = η^i_R(ω) ∪ η^j_R(τ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_d` (relation): η^{i+1}_R(dω) = β_I(η^i_R(ω)), for d the de Rham differential.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_eta0_cup_self` (relation): β_I(η^0_R(f)) ∪ β_I(η^0_R(f)) = 0 for every f ∈ R (Lemma 4.10).

*Unit tests.*
- `pr1_comparison_map_one_formula` (computation): η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `pr1_comparison_map_base` (degenerate): For R = A/I, η^0 : A/I → H^0(Δ̄_{(A/I)/A}) is bijective and Ω^i = 0 for i > 0.
- `pr1_comparison_map_square_zero` (characterisation): η^2_R(dg ∧ dg) = 0 = β_I(g) ∪ β_I(g), also for p = 2.

*Acceptance.*
- η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(g).
- For R = A/I the map is the identity of A/I in degree 0.
- For an étale map R → S the maps η^*_R and η^*_S are compatible with Ω^i_R ⊗_R S ≅ Ω^i_S and with PR.1/etale-localization.

### `PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison` — The Hodge–Tate comparison theorem ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Hodge–Tate comparison**.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) is an isomorphism of sheaves of differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét. In particular Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is a perfect complex with H^i(Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}{−i}, zero for i larger than the relative dimension. For X = Spf(R) affine: Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) as R-modules, for every i.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism; X is smooth over A/I (R p-completely smooth over A/I). Without smoothness the statement fails for site cohomology.
- The twist is {−i} = ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ −i}; there is no Frobenius twist in this comparison.
- Ω^i denotes p-completed differential forms, a finite locally free O_X-module.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The map is globally defined (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), so the statement is local: it suffices to prove that η^i_R is an isomorphism for every p-completely smooth R.
2. Both sides localise for the étale topology: Ω^i_R ⊗_R S = Ω^i_S and PR.1/etale-localization. Since X is Zariski-locally étale over a completed affine space, one may take R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩.
3. Choose η : ⊕_{i=0}^n Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) lifting the maps η^i{−i} (the modules are finite free) and prove it is an isomorphism exactly as in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line: for I = (p) by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p; for the universal oriented prism by PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism; for an oriented prism by the pushout E and the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩; in general by faithfully flat base change to an oriented prism.
4. Perfectness: Δ̄_{X/A} has finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, each finite locally free.

*Acceptance.*
- Smooth polynomial algebra: for R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free over R on the classes β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i, twisted by {−i}.
- Torus: R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} free over R on η^1(dX/X) = X^{−1}β_I(X).
- A_inf prism and R = O_C⟨X⟩: H^1(Δ̄) ≅ Ω^1_{R/O_C}{−1}, the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist of BMS1.

### `PR.1/prismatic-base-change` — Base change for prismatic cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) → (B,IB) be a map of bounded prisms, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, X_B := X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Spf(B/IB) and g : X_B → X the projection. Then (g^*Δ_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ_{X_B/B} in D(X_{B,ét}, B), the completion being derived (p,I)-adic, and (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B} with p-adic completion. For X = Spf(R): Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ Δ_{R ⊗̂_A B/B}. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated then RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ RΓ_Δ(X_B/B). Consequence (the φ_A-twisted crystalline comparison): for a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, base change along the map of prisms φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) gives φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), compatibly with Frobenius; for X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over A/p, RΓ_crys(X/A) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A.

*Hypotheses.*
- Both prisms are bounded; no flatness or Tor amplitude hypothesis on A → B.
- X is smooth over A/I. The statement for global sections requires X quasi-compact and quasi-separated: completed base change does not commute with infinite products. Theorem 1.8 (5) of the source omits this hypothesis (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E13); the sheaf statement, Corollary 4.12, needs no such hypothesis.
- φ_A : A → A is a map of prisms (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) only for crystalline prisms; for a general prism the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{X/A} is not the prismatic cohomology of a base change over (A,I).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By derived Nakayama (DD.1) it suffices to prove the statement modulo I: (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B}.
2. Both sides are perfect complexes with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i} by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, the base change map is compatible with the maps η^* (functoriality of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map in the prism), and completed differential forms commute with base change (DD.2).
3. Global sections: for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated RΓ is a finite limit of the affine values, and completed base change commutes with finite limits.
4. Consequence: apply the affine statement to φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) and PR.1/crystalline-comparison with I = (p), noting R ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}.

*Acceptance.*
- Crystalline base: for (Z_p,(p)) → (W(k),(p)), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}.
- For the map of prisms α = can∘φ : (A_inf, ker θ) → (A_crys,(p)) (Construction 6.1 with d = ξ) and X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over O_C: RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf) ⊗̂^L_{A_inf,α} A_crys ≃ RΓ_Δ(Y/A_crys) with Y = X ×_{Spf O_C} Spf(A_crys/p) = (X_{O_C/p})^{(1)}; by PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the PD ideal ker(A_crys → O_C/p) the right side is RΓ_crys(X_{O_C/p}/A_crys), the A_crys-comparison of BMS1.
- Non-example: for X an infinite disjoint union of copies of Spf(F_p) over (Z_p,(p)) and B = Z_p⟨x⟩, the map (∏ Z_p) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨x⟩ → ∏ Z_p⟨x⟩ is not surjective.

### `PR.1/de-rham-comparison` — The de Rham comparison (W(A/I) p-torsion-free) ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **de Rham comparison**.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism such that the ring of p-typical Witt vectors W(A/I) is p-torsion-free, and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Then there is a natural isomorphism Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, A/I), where A/I is an A-algebra through A → A → A/I, the first map being φ_A, the completion is p-adic, and the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex. More precisely, for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R there is a functorial isomorphism Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) of commutative algebra objects of D(W(A/I)), where ψ : A → W(A/I) is the composite of the δ-map A → W(A/I) lifting A → A/I with the Witt vector Frobenius, and the crystalline cohomology is relative to the PD ideal ker(W(A/I) → A/(I,p)); reducing along W(A/I) → A/I gives the first isomorphism. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, RΓ_dR(X/(A/I)) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism and W(A/I) is p-torsion-free. This holds if A/I is p-torsion-free, or if I = (p) and A/p is reduced. This is the hypothesis of Theorem 6.4 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27).
- The statement for every bounded prism, without the hypothesis on W(A/I), is Corollary 15.4 of the source; it is deduced from the Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius and is the node PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general. It is not asserted here.
- The reduction is along the Frobenius-twisted map A → A/I. The untwisted reduction Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is Hodge–Tate cohomology, whose cohomology sheaves are Ω^i{−i} with the Bockstein as differential; the two are different objects.
- The proof of Theorem 6.4 is read with the correction of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E14: ψ carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reduce to the affine case by functoriality. The kernel J of W(A/I) → A/I → A/(I,p) is a PD ideal, and RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) ⊗̂^L_{W(A/I)} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}, because R is a p-completely smooth lift of R/p over the PD thickening W(A/I) → A/I (crystalline cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of a smooth lift, with base change; requested from CR.2).
2. The map A → A/I lifts uniquely to a δ-map w : A → W(A/I) (PR.0/delta-ring-category: W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor). It carries I into V W(A/I), so ψ = F ∘ w carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I). As W(A/I) is p-torsion-free and p-complete, (W(A/I),(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism (PR.0/crystalline-prism) and ψ : (A,I) → (W(A/I),(p)) is a map of bounded prisms.
3. PR.1/prismatic-base-change along ψ: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} with R′ := R ⊗̂_{A/I,ψ} W(A/I)/p.
4. PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the crystalline prism W(A/I), the PD ideal J and the smooth W(A/I)/J = A/(I,p)-algebra R/p: its Frobenius twist (R/p)^{(1)} is R′, since A/(I,p) → W(A/I)/p is induced by the Witt vector Frobenius. Hence Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)).
5. The composite A → W(A/I) → A/I of ψ with the projection is a ↦ φ_A(a) mod I (zeroth Witt component of F(w(a))), which gives the stated twist.

*Acceptance.*
- A = Z_p[[u]], I = (E(u)), A/I = O_K p-torsion-free: Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_{A,φ} O_K ≃ Ω^*_{X/O_K}.
- A = W(k), I = (p), k perfect: Δ_{R/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R/k}; with the Cartier isomorphism this is consistent with Δ̄_{R/W(k)} having cohomology Ω^i_{R/k}.
- A hypothesis check: W(F_p[x]/(x²)) has p-torsion, and for A a p-torsion-free δ-lift of F_p[x]/(x²) the theorem does not apply; the statement is then PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius_verschiebung`.

- BS22-v4, Theorem 6.4, proof: “lifts the de Rham complex” (The crystalline cohomology over W(A/I) lifts the de Rham complex.)

### `PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness` — Perfectness of prismatic cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme over Spf(A/I). Then RΓ_Δ(X/A) is a perfect complex of A-modules, and RΓ(X_ét, Δ̄_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is a perfect complex of A/I-modules with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are RΓ(X, Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i], 0 ≤ i ≤ dim(X/(A/I)). In particular RΓ_Δ(X/A) has Tor amplitude in [0, 2 dim], and its formation commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism; A/I need not be noetherian.
- X is proper and smooth over Spf(A/I): quasi-compact, separated, of finite relative dimension, with X ⊗ Z/p^n proper and smooth over A/(I,p^n) for all n.
- Perfectness is asserted for the complex of global sections, not for the individual cohomology modules H^i_Δ(X/A), which need not be finitely presented or flat.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is perfect with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i}; the canonical filtration gives the filtration of RΓ(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) with the stated graded pieces.
2. For X proper and smooth over the p-complete ring A/I of bounded p^∞-torsion, RΓ(X, E) is a perfect complex of A/I-modules for every vector bundle E, and commutes with base change (finiteness for proper flat finitely presented morphisms without noetherian hypotheses, passed to the p-adic limit; requested from DD.5, with formal schemes from SF.4).
3. RΓ_Δ(X/A) is derived (p,I)-complete, A is classically (p,I)-complete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness (1)) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is perfect over A/I; a derived I-complete complex over an I-adically complete ring whose reduction modulo I is perfect is perfect (requested from DD.1).
4. Base change: PR.1/prismatic-base-change for the quasi-compact and separated X; for perfect complexes the completed and the ordinary derived tensor product agree.

*Acceptance.*
- X = P^1 over A/I: RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≃ A ⊕ A{−1}[−2] as a complex, of rank 2.
- X an abelian formal scheme of dimension g: RΓ_Δ(X/A) is perfect of amplitude [0,2g] with H^1 of rank 2g after base change to a field.
- For X affine of positive dimension (not proper), RΓ_Δ(X/A) is not perfect: H^0(Δ̄) = O(X) is not finitely generated over A/I.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

- BS22-v4, Theorem 1.8, final sentence: “is a perfect complex of” (Perfectness over A for proper X.)

### `PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic` — p-torsion-freeness of H^0 for p-completely syntomic algebras

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion-free, and let S be a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra: S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, S/p ≅ S ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p, and (A/I)/p → S/p is syntomic. Then H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is p-torsion-free. Under the identification of site cohomology with derived prismatic cohomology for such S (PrismaticCohomology:PR.2), this is the statement that H^0(Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion-free.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a bounded prism and A is p-torsion-free.
- S is p-completely syntomic over A/I in the sense of Anschütz–Le Bras, footnote to Lemma 5.1.6.
- The proof planned here is complete when the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero, which holds whenever A/p has bounded I^∞-torsion ((A/d^n)[p] ≅ (A/p)[d^n] with transition maps multiplication by d): every crystalline prism, every prism with (p,d) regular (Breuil–Kisin, q-de Rham), every perfect prism (A/p is reduced; this is the case A = A_inf(R), R any perfectoid ring, used by the source) and every noetherian A. For an arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded prism the step 'a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module is p-torsion-free' is asserted in the source by calling the module p-completely flat over A; this is recorded as a gap of the packet and as source issue PrismaticCohomology/E14.
- The identification with derived prismatic cohomology uses descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and belongs to PR.2; this node is about the site.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Čech–Alexander complex: since S is p-completely syntomic, the kernel of a presentation is (ind-)Zariski-locally generated by I and a sequence completely regular relative to A, so PR.1/cech-alexander-complex applies and gives a weakly initial object C^0 of (S/A)_Δ with C^0 derived (p,I)-complete and (p,I)-completely flat over A (PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (1)).
2. H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is the equaliser of C^0 ⇉ C^1 (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), a subring of C^0; so it suffices that C^0 is p-torsion-free.
3. For a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module B over the p-torsion-free bounded prism A: B is discrete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness), B[p] = H^{−1}(B ⊗^L_A A/p), and by derived I-completeness and complete flatness B[p] ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A (A/I^n)[p], with transition maps induced by A/I^{n+1} → A/I^n. If the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero the limit vanishes. For I = (p) this is the source's argument: B is p-completely flat over Z_p, hence p-torsion-free.

*Acceptance.*
- A = A_inf, S = O_C⟨x⟩/(x^n − p)-type syntomic algebras, and the application of the source: S the ring of a finite locally free group scheme over a quasisyntomic base.
- A = Z_p, S = F_p: H^0 = Z_p is p-torsion-free while H^0 of Ō_Δ is F_p; the statement is about O_Δ.
- If A has p-torsion the statement fails already for S = A/I, where H^0 = A.

### `PR.1/perfect-prism-initial` — A perfect prism is initial among prisms over its reduction

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let (A,I) be a perfect prism with associated perfectoid ring R = A/I. For every prism (B,J), every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J). Equivalently, the category of prisms (B,J) with a map R → B/J is the category of prisms under (A,I): (R)_Δ = (R/A)_Δ, with (A,I) as initial object in the algebraic language. The converse fails: for a prism (A,I) and a perfect prism (B,J) there may be several maps (A,I) → (B,J) inducing the same map A/I → B/J.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A,I) is a perfect prism, so A = W(A/p) with A/p perfect, and A/I is a perfectoid ring (PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings).
- (B,J) is an arbitrary prism, not necessarily bounded; B may have p-torsion, so compatibility with Frobenius lifts does not by itself give a δ-map.
- The absolute prismatic site (R)_Δ as a site is defined in PrismaticCohomology:PR.5; the statement here is about maps of prisms only.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The p-completed cotangent complex of A over Z_p vanishes because A = W(perfect ring) (DD.0), and B is derived (p,J)-complete (it is a prism) while B/J is derived p-complete; by deformation theory along the (p,J)-adic tower Hom(A,B) ≃ Hom(A,B/J) ≃ Hom(A,B/(J,p)). So A → A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a ring map α : A → B, compatible with the Frobenius lifts, and α(I) ⊂ J.
2. α is a δ-map: since φ_A is bijective, α factors uniquely through B^{perf} := lim_φ B; B^{perf} is a perfect δ-ring, hence p-torsion-free (PR.0/perfect-delta-rings, Lemma 2.28), so the φ-equivariant map A → B^{perf} is a δ-map, and B^{perf} → B is a δ-map.
3. Uniqueness as a map of prisms follows from uniqueness as a ring map.

*Acceptance.*
- (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)): every prism (B,J) with p ∈ J, that is every crystalline prism, receives exactly one map from (Z_p,(p)).
- (A,I) = (A_inf, ker θ): a ring map O_C → B/J determines the map A_inf → B.
- Failure of the converse: for the Breuil–Kisin prism (Z_p[[u]],(u − p)) and the perfect prism (A_inf(O_C), ker θ), the maps u ↦ [p^♭] attached to the different compatible systems p^♭ of p-power roots of p are distinct maps of prisms inducing the same map Z_p → O_C.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-delta-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-category`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.2/qrsp-prism`, `PR.2/perfection-comparison`, `PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`, `PR.5/relative-site-comparison`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Lemma 4.8 (in Remark 4.7) and its proof: “of commutative rings lifts uniquely to a map” (The node is Lemma 4.8 with the remark following its proof.)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Site/Basic`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Site`.

### `PR.1/acceptance-computations` — Acceptance computations: polynomial algebra, étale chart, crystalline base, Frobenius twist

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/acceptance-computations` · application · part PR.0.

(1) Smooth polynomial algebra. For a bounded prism (A,I) and R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, Δ_{R/A} is computed by the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is the free R-module on the products β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i; so H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} is the exterior algebra over R on β_I(X_1),…,β_I(X_n) with differential determined by β_I(X_j^m) = m X_j^{m−1} β_I(X_j). (2) Étale chart. For a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}){i} ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/I)} is free over S on the same classes, and Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S. (3) Crystalline base. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and R = F_p[X], Δ_{R/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[X]/Z_p) is the de Rham complex Z_p⟨X⟩ → Z_p⟨X⟩dX: H^0 = Z_p and H^1 is the cokernel of d, X^m ↦ mX^{m−1}dX; its reduction modulo p, which is Δ̄_{R/Z_p}, has cohomology F_p[X^p] in degree 0 and F_p[X^p]·X^{p−1}dX in degree 1, with β_p(X) the class of X^{p−1}dX. (4) Nontrivial Frobenius-twisted coefficient map. For A = W(k) with k = F_{p²} and R̃ = k[X,Y]/(Y² − X³ − aX − b) an affine elliptic curve whose j-invariant is not in F_p (p ≥ 5), the algebras R̃ and R̃^{(1)} = R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob} k are not isomorphic over k, and Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)) while φ_A^*Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)): the comparison holds only after the scalar extension along φ_A, which is not the identity on W(k). Likewise Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R̃/k}, whereas the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{R̃/W(k)} = Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k)} k has cohomology modules Ω^i_{R̃/k} and is the de Rham complex of the Frobenius untwist R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob^{−1}} k, a curve not isomorphic to R̃.

*Hypotheses.*
- (1), (2): any bounded prism. (3): the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)). (4): k = F_{p²}, p ≥ 5, a, b ∈ k with j-invariant outside F_p.
- In (3) the twist is invisible because F_p[X]^{(1)} = F_p[X] over F_p; (4) is chosen so that the twist changes the algebra.
- In (4) the two W(k)-module structures on RΓ_crys differ by φ; the complexes are abstractly isomorphic as complexes of abelian groups since φ is an automorphism of W(k).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison for the polynomial ring, with the complex of PR.1/cech-alexander-complex (Remark 4.19) and the Leibniz rule of PR.1/bockstein-differential.
2. (2): PR.1/etale-localization and (1).
3. (3): PR.1/crystalline-comparison with A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[X] = R^{(1)}, the de Rham computation of crystalline cohomology of the affine line (CR.2), and the identification of β_p in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p.
4. (4): PR.1/crystalline-comparison for I = (p) over W(k), PR.1/prismatic-base-change along φ_A and PR.1/de-rham-comparison (W(k) is p-torsion-free and k is reduced); R̃^{(1)} is the curve with coefficients a^p, b^p, of j-invariant j^p ≠ j.

*Acceptance.*
- Each of the four computations is a test of the corresponding comparison theorem with a wrong twist: (1) fails with the twist {i} in place of {−i} for a non-orientable prism, (3) fails if β is omitted, (4) fails without φ_A.
- The torus R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ is an étale chart of the affine line and gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} = R·η^1(dX/X).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/etale-localization`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/de-rham-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/bockstein-differential`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

*Sources.*

- BS22-v4, Example 1.9 (1): “prismatic cohomology gives a canonical Frobenius descent of crystalline cohomology” (The crystalline example and the meaning of the Frobenius twist in (3) and (4).)

<a id="layer-pr2"></a>

# Layer PR.2. Derived extension, semiperfectoid inputs and descent

Layer PR.2 extends prismatic cohomology from smooth algebras to all derived p-complete animated A/I-algebras and computes it on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings, after Bhatt–Scholze §§7–8 and Anschütz–Le Bras §3 and Appendix A. It has 29 nodes.

Derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{R/A} is the derived (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of the smooth theory (Construction 7.6), with its conjugate filtration and the derived Hodge–Tate comparison gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ ∧^i L_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i]^∧. Anschütz–Le Bras add the first conjugate piece as a cotangent complex over the prism and the link between splitting it and lifting modulo I². Étale descent, base change, colimit preservation and the Künneth formulas follow. The comparison maps to prisms and to site cohomology agree with the site theory for smooth algebras and in the discrete case (Lemma 7.7, which uses PR.0's pullback square for W_2). The quasiregular semiperfectoid calculation (Proposition 7.10) proves that Δ_S is discrete and initial, and the layer identifies it with A_crys in characteristic p, with three acceptance examples (a regular semiperfectoid quotient, a singular quasiregular semiperfectoid algebra, a derived input with nonzero higher homotopy). Quasisyntomic covers lift to the prismatic site, and quasisyntomic descent and unfolding follow. The derived crystalline comparison was corrected by the review: it concerns derived crystalline cohomology, defined by Kan extension. It is not the p-completed derived de Rham complex over W(k), which already differs for S = k. A gap records that no stage states BMS2 8.13–8.14. The layer ends with the perfection of derived prismatic cohomology and perfectoidization (Definition 8.2 to Corollary 8.14) and the descent of finite projective modules along faithfully flat maps of prisms.

Animated rings come from EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5, the cotangent complex from DD.0, derived completion from DD.1, the quasisyntomic site and quasiregular semiperfectoid rings from DD.5. The universal prisms of semiperfectoid rings and André's flatness lemma stay with PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q3, which build on this layer. The arc-topology inputs of §8 are gaps. Three nodes keep an open point of the review (missing API items of the derived functor, of the conjugate filtration and of the perfection). The planets are derived prismatic cohomology, the conjugate filtration, the derived Hodge–Tate comparison, the prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, quasisyntomic descent and perfectoidization.

*Coverage of `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2`: planned.* The remaining items are listed in the Coverage section at the end.

### `PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology` — Derived prismatic cohomology ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Derived prismatic cohomology**.

Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let Poly_{A/I} be the category of p-completed polynomial algebras (A/I)⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩, n ≥ 0, and Sm_{A/I} the category of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Let CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) be the ∞-category of commutative algebra objects E of D_comp(A) equipped with a map of commutative algebras φ_E : E → φ_{A,*}E. PR.1 gives a functor Sm_{A/I} → CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)), R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R). Derived prismatic cohomology is its left Kan extension Δ_{−/A} to the ∞-category of derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras, with colimits in the target derived (p, I)-completed. Equivalently Δ_{−/A} is the unique functor on derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras that preserves sifted colimits and restricts to PR.1's functor on Poly_{A/I}; for a simplicial resolution P_• → R by objects of Poly_{A/I} (or by p-completely ind-smooth algebras) one has Δ_{R/A} ≃ (colim_{[n] ∈ Δ^op} Δ_{P_n/A})^∧, independently of the resolution. Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology is Δ̄_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, a derived p-complete commutative algebra in D(R). The functor carries: (1) the unit A → Δ_{R/A}, with Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A; (2) the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}; (3) the φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}, natural in R. For R in Sm_{A/I} the value is the site cohomology of PR.1 (node derived-agrees-with-site). Δ_{R/A} is an invariant of the animated ring R and not of π_0(R) alone (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).

*Hypotheses.*
- p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
- D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0.
- A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
- PR.1's functor is used as a functor of ∞-categories; its coherence in R is supplied by the functorial Čech–Alexander complexes.
- The left Kan extension from Sm_{A/I} and the one from Poly_{A/I} agree; this is part of the statement and is proved through the Hodge–Tate comparison (BS22 Construction 7.6 (1)).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Coherent source functor: the functorial Čech–Alexander complex (PR.1) makes R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R) a functor from Sm_{A/I} to cosimplicial derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras, hence to CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) after totalisation.
2. Animation: derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras are the derived p-complete objects (DD.1) of the animation of finitely generated polynomial A/I-algebras (E5:animation). By the universal property of animation (HTT 5.5.8.15) and the left Kan extension theorem of E3, the functor P ↦ Δ_{P^∧/A} on polynomial algebras extends uniquely to a sifted-colimit-preserving functor with values in D_comp(A); it inverts derived p-completion maps because its reduction modulo I has p-completed graded pieces, so it is defined on derived p-complete inputs.
3. Agreement of the two extensions: on Sm_{A/I} the complex Δ̄_{R/A} has the finite filtration τ^{≤i} with graded pieces Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] (PR.1, Hodge–Tate comparison), and R ↦ (Ω^i_{R/(A/I)})^∧ is left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I} (DD.0). By derived Nakayama for I (DD.1) the functor Δ_{−/A} on Sm_{A/I} is itself left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I}; hence the value on Sm_{A/I} is unchanged.
4. Structure maps: the unit, R → Δ̄_{R/A} and φ_R are the left Kan extensions of the corresponding natural transformations of PR.1; reduction modulo I commutes with the colimits because A/I is a perfect A-module (I is invertible).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 7.7, Example 7.9, Proposition 7.10: its discreteness on complete intersections and on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings produces prisms, among them the initial prism Δ_S
- BS22 Definition 8.2; PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q4: the perfection of Δ_{S/A} defines the perfectoidization S_perfd
- PrismaticCohomology PR.3 and PR.4 (BS22 §12, Theorem 9.1): the Nygaard filtration lives on Δ_S and its descent; the étale comparison is a statement about Δ_{S/A} for every p-complete S
- ALB23 §§3–4: prismatic Dieudonné theory evaluates Δ on quasisyntomic rings and uses base change and Künneth
- RefinedTraceMethods RT.6: the graded pieces of the motivic filtration on TC^- are compared with Nygaard-completed Δ

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.cohomology` (constructor): The object Δ_{R/A} of D(A) attached to a simplicial commutative A/I-algebra R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.map` (functoriality): A map R → S of simplicial A/I-algebras induces Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.map_id` (functoriality): The identity of R induces the identity of Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.map_comp` (functoriality): The map induced by a composite is the composite of the induced maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.frobenius` (data): The Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.frobenius_naturality` (compatibility): For f : R → S one has φ_S ∘ Δ(f) = φ_{A,*}(Δ(f)) ∘ φ_R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.hodgeTate` (constructor): Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, as an object of D(A/I).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.unit` (data): The unit map A → Δ_{R/A} in D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Derived.constIso` (compatibility): For a discrete A/I-algebra R, the value on the constant simplicial algebra R is the shared carrier Δ_{R/A} of PR.1 and PR.2; for p-completely smooth R this is the cohomology of the prismatic site.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr2_derived_base_ring` (degenerate): Δ_{(A/I)/A} is A, in degree 0.
- `pr2_derived_const_agrees` (compatibility): The value of the simplicial functor on a constant simplicial algebra R is isomorphic to Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr2_derived_product` (computation): Δ_{(A/I × A/I)/A} is A × A, in degree 0.
- `pr2_derived_not_pi0_invariant` (non-example): When A/I ≠ 0 there is a simplicial A/I-algebra R with H^{−1}(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≠ 0; so Δ̄_{R/A} is not the Hodge–Tate cohomology of the site of π_0(R), which lies in D^{≥0}.
- `pr2_derived_frobenius_natural_id` (characterisation): The map induced by the identity commutes with Frobenius: φ_R ∘ Δ(id) = φ_{A,*}(Δ(id)) ∘ φ_R.

*Acceptance.*
- Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A with φ = φ_A, and Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} = A/I.
- For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ the value is PR.1's complex: H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R, H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) = Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1} free of rank 1, and no other cohomology.
- For R = A/I × A/I (p-completely étale over A/I) the value is A × A.
- For a discrete p-complete R, two polynomial simplicial resolutions give canonically equivalent values.
- A non-discrete input is computed in node derived-input-higher-homotopy.
