### `PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples` — Breuil–Kisin twists over the q-de Rham prism and over crystalline prisms

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples` · application · part PR.0.

(1) Let (A, I) = (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) be the q-de Rham prism. It is transversal with I_r = ([p^r]_q), [p^r]_q = (q^{p^r} − 1)/(q − 1), and [p^{r+1}]_q = [p]_{q^{p^r}} [p^r]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r². There is a unique e_A ∈ A{1} whose image in I_r/I_r² is the class of [p^r]_q for every r; A{1} is the free A-module on e_A, and φ_{A{1}}(e_A) = [p]_q^{−1} e_A. (2) For a map of prisms f : (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) → (B, J), the image e_B of e_A generates B{1} and φ_{B{1}}(λ e_B) = φ_B(λ) f([p]_q)^{−1} e_B; e_B depends on f and not only on (B, J). (3) For a crystalline prism (B, (p)) the map q ↦ 1 gives a canonical generator e_B of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e_B) = e_B/p; hence (B{n}, φ_{B{n}}) ≅ (B, p^{−n} φ_B) for all n ∈ Z, and the twisted divided Frobenius of PR.3/divided-frobenius is φ/p^i. (4) For an oriented prism (B, (d)) and a generator e of B{1}, φ_{B{1}}(e) = u d^{−1} e for a unit u; replacing e by v e replaces u by φ(v) v^{−1} u.

*Hypotheses.*
- The q-de Rham prism is PR.0/q-de-rham-prism: φ(q) = q^p, δ(q) = 0.
- Bhatt–Lurie characterise e_A by (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p); the node uses the equivalent description by the classes of [p^r]_q, which is the one their proof establishes, so that no logarithm is needed.
- BL22 Remark 2.6.2 and Notation 2.6.3 write the target of the Frobenius as I^{−1}{1}; by Notation 2.5.4 this is A{1} ⊗_A I^{−1}, the module written I^{−1}A{1} in Remark 2.5.9.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): I_r is generated by φ^s([p]_q) = [p]_{q^{p^s}}, s < r, whose product is [p^r]_q; q^{p^r} ≡ 1 modulo I_r gives [p]_{q^{p^r}} ≡ p modulo I_r, hence the congruence modulo I_r². The compatible system defines e_A by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, and it generates because its image generates each I_r/I_r².
2. Frobenius: φ_A([p^r]_q) = [p^r]_{q^p} = [p^{r+1}]_q/[p]_q, which under φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1}I_{r+1} is [p]_q^{−1} times the class of [p^{r+1}]_q (BL22 Remark 2.6.2 obtains the same formula from φ(log_Δ) = log_Δ).
3. (2), (3): functoriality of the twist and of its Frobenius (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (2), (5)); for a crystalline prism q ↦ 1 is a map of prisms with [p]_q ↦ p (BL22 Example 2.6.4).
4. (4): B{1} is free by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (4) and φ_B^*(B{1}) ≅ d^{−1} B{1}.

*Acceptance.*
- Crystalline prism acceptance example of the stage: for (Z_p, (p)), Z_p{n} = Z_p · e^n with φ(e^n) = p^{−n} e^n.
- Under reduction modulo I the generator e_A maps to the class of [p]_q in I/I².
- The two generators of the twist of the coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself differ by a unit that is not 1, which is why e_B depends on f.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Proposition 2.6.1 and its proof, Remark 2.6.2: “Then there is a unique element” (part (1), with the generator described by its images as in the proof)
- BL22, Notation 2.6.3 and Example 2.6.4: “supplies a canonical generator” (parts (2) and (3))

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/BKTwist/Examples`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.BKTwist`.

### `PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra` — Large quasisyntomic algebras over A/I

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra` · definition · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and Ā = A/I. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra is a derived p-complete Ā-algebra S that is p-completely flat over Ā and whose cotangent complex L_{S/Ā} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]; such an S is classically p-complete. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra S is large if there is a surjection Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞} | t ∈ T⟩ → S for some set T; equivalently, S/pS is generated as an Ā-algebra by the images of elements of S that admit compatible systems of p-power roots in S. For a large quasisyntomic S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} vanishes after p-completion, so L_{S/Ā}[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and every (∧^i L_{S/Ā})[−i]^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module. Large quasisyntomic algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site of Ā: every quasisyntomic Ā-algebra has a quasisyntomic cover by a large one, and the terms of the Čech nerve of such a cover are large. The standard examples are Ā⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with (f_1, …, f_m) p-completely regular relative to Ā.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a bounded prism; Ā has bounded p^∞-torsion.
- Quasisyntomic algebras, covers and the site are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5 (BMS2 §4) over the base Ā.
- Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the p-adic completion of the perfected polynomial ring Ā[X_t^{1/p^∞}].
- The second formulation is the one of Bhatt–Lurie (S/pS generated by the images of Ā and of (S/pS)^♭); for p-complete S the two agree because compatible systems of p-power roots lift uniquely from S/pS to S.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Equivalence: a surjection from Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ exhibits generators with compatible roots; conversely generators x_t of S/p with compatible roots in S define Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S, surjective modulo p and hence surjective by p-completeness. The map S^♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} S → (S/p)^♭ is bijective for p-complete S.
2. Ω^1: if x = y^p then dx = p y^{p−1} dy, so Ω^1_{S/Ā}/p is generated by zero; with the Tor amplitude condition this gives p-complete flatness of L_{S/Ā}[−1] and of its divided and exterior powers (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).
3. Basis: for quasisyntomic S choose generators and adjoin compatible p-power roots, S → S ⊗̂_{Ā⟨X_t⟩} Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩, a quasisyntomic cover with large target (BS22, the paragraph after Definition 15.1; BMS2 Lemma 4.28).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 15.2: the rings on which Δ_{S/A} is discrete and the relative Nygaard filtration is defined by Frobenius divisibility
- BS22 Theorem 15.3 and BL22 Proposition 5.1.1: a basis of the quasisyntomic site on which sheaves are defined and from which they are right Kan extended
- PR.5 (Bhatt–Lurie §5.5): the same class of rings supports the absolute Nygaard filtration by descent

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge` (constructor): The predicate on an Ā-algebra S: S/pS is generated over Ā by images of elements with compatible p-power roots in S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.HasCompatibleRoots` (data): x ∈ S admits a sequence x = x_0, x_1, x_2, … with x_{n+1}^p = x_n.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_iff_exists_family` (characterisation): S is large iff there is a family (x_t) of elements with compatible p-power roots such that every s ∈ S is congruent modulo p to an element of the Ā-subalgebra generated by the x_t.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.of_surjective` (functoriality): If S is large and S → S′ is a surjective map of Ā-algebras then S′ is large.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.kaehler_eq_smul` (other): For large S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} = p · Ω^1_{S/Ā}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_bar` (example): Ā is a large Ā-algebra.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr3_large_base` (degenerate): Ā is large over itself.
- `pr3_large_generated_by_roots` (characterisation): If S is generated as an Ā-algebra by elements with compatible p-power roots, then S is large; this covers Ā[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X).
- `pr3_large_kaehler` (compatibility): For large S every Kähler differential of S over Ā is p times another one.
- `pr3_large_not_polynomial` (non-example): If p is not a unit of Ā, the polynomial ring Ā[X] is not large.

*Acceptance.*
- Ā itself is large (T empty).
- For a perfect prism, a quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebra that is quasisyntomic over Ā is large; large algebras replace quasiregular semiperfectoid rings when the base prism is not perfect.
- Ā⟨X⟩ is not large: dX is not divisible by p in Ω^1.

*Depends on:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`.

*Sources.*

- BL22, proof of Proposition 5.1.1, first paragraph: “can be identified with a” (the reformulation through (R/pR)^♭ and the discreteness of the prismatic complex on this class)

### `PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic` — Relative Nygaard filtration of a large quasisyntomic algebra (BS22 Theorem 15.2)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and S a large quasisyntomic A/I-algebra. (1) The derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{S/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra; (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is the initial object of the relative prismatic site (S/A)_Δ. Let Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A (the Frobenius twist, a discrete (p, I)-completely flat A-algebra) and φ_{S/A} : Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} the relative Frobenius, an A-algebra map. Put Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = {x ∈ Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} : φ_{S/A}(x) ∈ I^i Δ_{S/A}}. (2) φ_{S/A} induces an injection gr^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ̄_{S/A}{i} = I^iΔ_{S/A}/I^{i+1}Δ_{S/A} whose image is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}, for every i ≥ 0. (3) The formation of Fil^i_N commutes with base change in A: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) and S_B the p-completion of S ⊗_A B, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ⊗̂_A B ≅ Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a bounded prism; S is large and quasisyntomic over A/I (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra).
- The filtration lives on the Frobenius twist Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{S/A}, not on Δ_{S/A}: the relative Frobenius is A-linear only as a map out of the twist. For a perfect prism φ_A is an isomorphism and Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^* Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A}.
- The conjugate filtration is the one of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison relative to A/I; on large S its pieces are discrete, p-completely flat S-modules.
- Completed tensor products are derived (p, I)-completed; on completely flat modules over a bounded prism they are classical completions (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): by the derived Hodge–Tate comparison the graded pieces of the conjugate filtration of Δ̄_{S/A} are (∧^i L_{S/(A/I)})[−i]^∧{−i}, discrete and p-completely flat over S, so Δ_{S/A} is discrete and (p, I)-completely flat; initiality follows from PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site (BS22 Lemma 7.7) once a functorial idempotent endomorphism of Δ_{S/A} is shown to be the identity, as in the proof of PR.2/qrsp-prism (BS22 Proposition 7.10).
2. (3): if (2) holds for S over A, the base change of Fil^•_N to B is a filtration of Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B} satisfying (2), and a filtration by ideals satisfying (2) is the Nygaard filtration by the induction of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (1).
3. (2), reduction: by descent to smooth algebras and left Kan extension it suffices to treat S = (A/I)⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m); by PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent (BS22 Proposition 7.11) a flat base change in A gives compatible p-power roots of the f_j; the devissage of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid reduces to S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X).
4. (2), the key case over a general base: localise on A so that I = (d) (PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators), base change from the universal oriented prism, whose Frobenius is faithfully flat (PR.0/free-delta-ring), so its perfection A → A_∞ is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (PR.0/prism-perfection); over the perfect prism A_∞ the statement is PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces, and it descends along A → A_∞ because on the Čech nerve the filtration is the base change from A_∞ by (3).

*Acceptance.*
- S = A/I: Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = A, φ_{S/A} = id, Fil^i_N = I^i and gr^i = I^i/I^{i+1} = (A/I){i} = Fil_i^conj Δ̄{i} (BL22 Example 5.1.4).
- S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X) over the q-de Rham prism: the base change to the perfection is the key case of PR.3/nygaard-key-case.
- i = 0: gr^0_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ≅ S.

### `PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration` — Relative Nygaard filtration on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Relative Nygaard filtration**.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I. For an animated commutative Ā-algebra R write φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = Δ^{(1)}_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A for the Frobenius twist of derived prismatic cohomology and φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} for the relative Frobenius, a map of commutative algebra objects of the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. The relative Nygaard filtration is a decreasing filtration Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, an object of the I-complete filtered derived category DF(A), with a refinement Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^• ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} of φ_{R/A} to a map of filtered objects, constructed in three steps. (a) For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal {x : φ_{R/A}(x) ∈ I^iΔ_{R/A}} of PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b) For R quasisyntomic over Ā it is the right Kan extension of (a) along the inclusion of large algebras, equivalently the quasisyntomic unfolding: each R ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf and Fil^0_N = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. For X = Spf R affine and smooth over Ā this reads RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, Δ_{−/A}) and Fil^i_N RΓ_Δ(X/A)^{(1)} = RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}); for a smooth formal Ā-scheme X the filtrations on affine opens glue to a filtered object Fil^•_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} of D(X_ét, A). (c) For all animated R it is the (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of its restriction to finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras; on quasisyntomic algebras this agrees with (b). Characterisation (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1): the pair (Fil^•_N, Fil^•(φ)), functorial in R, is determined up to essentially unique isomorphism by: (1) each R ↦ Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} commutes with sifted colimits; (2) for R a finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebra, gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A}{n} is an isomorphism on H^m for m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 for m > n. Properties: gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0, so the filtration is N-indexed; it is multiplicative (a commutative algebra object of DF(A) refining φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), giving in particular v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^•_N → Fil^{•+1}_N whose composite with Fil^{•+1}_N → Fil^•_N is induced by I ⊂ A; for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^•_N φ_B^*Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R)/B}; for R = Ā, Fil^n_N = I^n ⊂ A; for a perfect prism, Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = φ_A^*(Fil^•_N Δ_{R/A}) with the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is an animated commutative Ā-algebra (derived prismatic cohomology depends only on the derived p-completion of R).
- The filtration is on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. It is not a filtration of Δ_{R/A} unless φ_A is an isomorphism.
- DF(A) is the filtered derived category of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the I-adic filtration I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A} is Z-indexed, with i-th term I^{⊗ i} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} for all i ∈ Z (negative powers are powers of the dual), as in BMS2 Proposition 5.8 and Bhatt–Lurie. Since gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0 the filtered Frobenius factors through its truncation to i ≥ 0, and for p-completely smooth R (Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}) the Beilinson connective covers of the two filtrations agree.
- BL22 Proposition 5.1.1 (1) prints the target of R ↦ Fil^n_N as the complete derived category of Ā; the objects are A-complexes (for R = Ā they are the ideals I^n), so the target is the (p, I)-complete derived category of A (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E34).
- Bhatt–Lurie's and Bhatt–Scholze's constructions agree wherever both apply: BL22 defines the filtration on large algebras by the formula of BS22 Theorem 15.2 and extends it by the same Kan extensions.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a) is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b): large algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra); R ↦ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} and R ↦ I^•Δ_{R/A} satisfy quasisyntomic descent (BL22 Lemma 5.1.7, from the conjugate filtration and flat descent for exterior powers of the cotangent complex, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5; PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent), hence are right Kan extended from large algebras, and so is the filtered Frobenius. For smooth X, BS22 Theorem 15.3 states the same definition on X_qsyn.
2. (c): by induction on n, R ↦ Fil^n_N on quasisyntomic algebras is left Kan extended from polynomial algebras, because gr^n_N ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} is (PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2) on large algebras, extended by descent); then extend to animated rings by the universal property of animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
3. Uniqueness: a second pair satisfying (1), (2) is, on large algebras, an honest filtration by subgroups equal to the Frobenius-divisibility ideals, by induction on n using the fibre sequence Fil′^{n+1} → Fil′^n → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}; the resulting comparison map is an isomorphism on polynomial algebras by (2), hence in general by (1) (BL22, proof of Proposition 5.1.1).
4. Multiplicativity, the map v and change of prism are checked on large algebras, where they are statements about ideals (φ(xy) = φ(x)φ(y); PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (3)), and extended by the Kan extensions (BL22 Remarks 5.1.8–5.1.10).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16): the filtered Frobenius out of this filtration factors through Lη_I and identifies φ_A^*Δ with Lη_IΔ
- BS22 Proposition 15.7 and BMS2 §11: its completion for the Breuil–Kisin prism is π_0 TP(−/S[u]; Z_p)
- Bhatt–Lurie §§5.2–5.5 and PR.5: the absolute Nygaard filtration is glued from the relative one over the Cartier–Witt stack and the Hodge filtration
- PR.6 (BS22 Theorem 17.2) and BMS2 Proposition 9.10: under AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ the filtration is the décalage filtration of AΩ ≃ Lη_ξ φ_* AΩ
- PR.8 (logarithmic Nygaard filtration): the log variant is modelled on this construction

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.frobeniusTwist` (constructor): The object φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} of D(A) for a prism (A, I) and an A/I-algebra R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeFrobenius` (data): The A-linear relative Frobenius φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil` (constructor): The filtered object i ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, a functor from (N, ≥) to D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilZeroIso` (simp): Fil^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relGr` (data): The graded piece gr^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relGr_triangle` (structure): There is a distinguished triangle Fil^{i+1}_N → Fil^i_N → gr^i_N → Fil^{i+1}_N[1].
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilMap` (functoriality): A map R → R′ of A/I-algebras induces a natural transformation Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R′/A}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_bar` (example): For R = A/I: Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal I^i of A placed in degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_large` (compatibility): For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0 (it is the ideal of Frobenius-divisible elements).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilBaseChange` (compatibility): For a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) with completed base change functor B ⊗̂^L_A −: B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^i_N φ_B^*Δ_{R_B/B}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr3_rel_fil_zero` (degenerate): Fil^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr3_rel_fil_base` (computation): For R = A/I and all i: Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^i in degree 0.
- `pr3_rel_gr_zero_base` (computation): For R = A/I: gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ A/I in degree 0.
- `pr3_rel_fil_needs_twist` (non-example): The Nygaard ideal Fil^1_N A = φ_A^{-1}(I) of the base prism is not I in general: for the q-de Rham prism it is (q − 1), while the relative filtration of R = A/I on φ_A^*Δ = A is I = ([p]_q).

*Acceptance.*
- R = Ā: φ_A^*Δ = A and Fil^n_N = I^n.
- Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)), k a perfect field, and R smooth over k: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and Fil^•_N is the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology; in coordinates it is p^{max(i−•, 0)} Ω^• (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates).
- Perfect prism: agreement with PR.3/nygaard-filtration after applying φ_A^*.
- Change of prism along the q-de Rham prism → its perfection recovers the key case.

### `PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces` — Graded pieces of the relative Nygaard filtration

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) For every n ≥ 0 the map gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^n/I^{n+1} ⊗^L_A Δ_{R/A} = Δ̄_{R/A}{n} factors through an isomorphism gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}, functorial in R; gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0. (2) gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ R̂, the derived p-completion of R. (3) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth over Ā (for example X = Spf R affine smooth), then gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ τ^{≤ n} Δ̄_{R/A}{n}: H^m(gr^n_N) ≅ Ω̂^m_{R/Ā}{n − m} for 0 ≤ m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 otherwise. (4) gr^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}[−1]^∧, the shifted p-completed cotangent complex of R over A. (5) For every R the filtered object Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure of DF(A): gr^n_N lies in D^{≤ n} for all n.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; the conjugate filtration and the twist {n} = ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} are those of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison.
- The isomorphism in (1) is A-linear: the semilinearity of the perfectoid statement PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces has been absorbed into the Frobenius twist.
- (4) is BS22 Remark 15.6, which prints L_{X/A} ≃ gr^1_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} without the shift and cites Theorem 1.16 (2) for (3) (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E26); the node states the corrected form.
- The Beilinson t-structure is requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 (BMS2 Definition 5.3).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) on large quasisyntomic algebras is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2); both sides are right Kan extended from large algebras on quasisyntomic ones and left Kan extended from polynomial algebras in general (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; the conjugate filtration commutes with sifted colimits), which gives the functorial isomorphism for all R (BL22 Remark 5.1.2 and the proof of Proposition 5.1.1).
2. (2): Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ R̂ (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison). (3): for p-completely smooth R the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration and H^m(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≅ Ω̂^m{−m} (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison); this is BS22 Theorem 15.3, second display, obtained there by descent from Theorem 15.2 (2).
3. (4): combine (1) for n = 1 with PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent (Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]^∧).
4. (5): Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A} has graded pieces (∧^j L_{R/Ā})[−j]^∧, j ≤ n, which lie in D^{≤ j} ⊂ D^{≤ n}.

*Acceptance.*
- R = Ā: gr^n = I^n/I^{n+1} = Ā{n}.
- R = Ā⟨T⟩: gr^n_N has H^0 = R{n} and, for n ≥ 1, H^1 = Ω̂^1_{R/Ā}{n−1}.
- R large quasisyntomic: gr^n_N is the discrete module Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}.
- Comparison with the Hodge–Tate side: the associated graded of the Nygaard filtration is the conjugate (Hodge–Tate) filtration, twisted; comparison with the de Rham side is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`, `PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit`, `PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates`, `PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`, `PR.5/absolute-frobenius`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16 (3)) and Theorem 15.2 (2): “Then there are natural isomorphisms” (part (3) for affine smooth X; part (1) on large algebras)
- BL22, Remarks 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 5.1.5: “we deduce the following stronger version of” (parts (1), (2), (3), (5) for animated Ā-algebras)
- BS22-v4, Remark 15.6: “there is a canonical identification” (part (4), with the shift corrected)

### `PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation` — The Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius (BS22 Theorem 15.3) ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Lη factorisation of Frobenius**.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, X = Spf R, Δ = Δ_{R/A} = RΓ_Δ(X/A). (1) The filtered Frobenius Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ → I^• ⊗ Δ factors uniquely through the connective cover τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ) for the Beilinson t-structure, whose underlying complex is Lη_I Δ. On underlying complexes this gives a canonical map φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} such that the relative Frobenius factors as φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the second map being the canonical one (it exists because Δ lies in D^{≥0} and H^0(Δ) is I-torsion-free). (2) φ̃ is an isomorphism. (3) The filtered map Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A}) is an isomorphism of filtered objects: Fil^•(φ) exhibits the Nygaard filtration as the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration. For an I-torsion-free complex K^• representing Δ, Fil^i_N corresponds under φ̃ to the subcomplex I^iK^• ∩ η_I K^• of η_I K^•. In particular lim_i Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = 0. (4) φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects, compatible with base change in (A, I) and with étale localisation on R; for a smooth formal A/I-scheme X it globalises to an isomorphism φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A).

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. No orientation of I and no hypothesis on W(A/I) is made.
- Lη_I is the derived décalage functor of AInfCohomology:AI.1 for the invertible ideal I ⊂ A (on the ringed topos (X_ét, A) in the global statement); it is not exact, and the statement is one about objects and maps in D(A).
- The Beilinson t-structure, τ^{≤0}_B, and the identification of Lη_I K with the underlying complex of τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ K) (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 and Proposition 5.8) are requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 and AInfCohomology:AI.1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (3), gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄{i} ∈ D^{≤i}, so Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ is Beilinson connective and the filtered Frobenius factors uniquely through τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ); its underlying complex is Lη_IΔ (BMS2 Proposition 5.8). Since Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}, the graded pieces of τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ) vanish in negative degrees, so the cover is N-indexed and its map to I^0Δ = Δ is the map Lη_IΔ → Δ of BMS1 Lemma 6.10.
2. (2): by derived Nakayama it suffices to check modulo I. Lη_IΔ ⊗^L_A A/I is the Bockstein complex (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I) (AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction, BMS1 Proposition 6.12), which is Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} by the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison). Both sides commute with base change in A and with étale localisation; reduce to a polynomial algebra, then by base change to an oriented prism, to the universal oriented prism, to a crystalline prism (BS22 Construction 6.1, as in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison) and to A = Z_p, where the claim is the crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and the Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map).
3. (3): the filtered map is an isomorphism on every gr^i, by (1) of PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and gr^i τ^{≤0}_B = τ^{≤i} gr^i. Its fibre is therefore a constant filtered object, equal to the fibre of φ̃ in filtration degree 0, which vanishes by (2). The subcomplex description is the filtration G^i = I^iK^• ∩ η_IK^• in the proof of BMS2 Proposition 5.8, and lim_i G^i = lim_i I^iΔ = 0.
4. (4): τ^{≤0}_B is lax symmetric monoidal because the Beilinson t-structure is compatible with the tensor product (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (1)); base change and étale localisation follow from PR.1/prismatic-base-change, PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration (change of prism) and flat base change for Lη (AInfCohomology:AI.1).

*Acceptance.*
- R = A/I: φ_A^*Δ = A = Lη_I A and φ̃ is the identity.
- Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)): the statement is the Berthelot–Ogus isomorphism φ : RΓ_crys ≅ Lη_p RΓ_crys, with the Nygaard filtration on the source and the décalage filtration on the target (BMS2 Proposition 8.5 and its corollary).
- Cohomology: H^i(φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ≅ (H^i(Δ_{R/A})/H^i(Δ_{R/A})[I]) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} (AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology).
- Consumers: PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general, PR.3/image-of-frobenius, PR.6 (AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ carries the décalage filtration to the Nygaard filtration), PR.8.

### `PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general` — De Rham comparison for every bounded prism (BS22 Corollary 15.4)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) For any bounded prism (A, I) and any smooth formal A/I-scheme X there is a canonical isomorphism of commutative algebra objects (E_∞-algebras) in D(X_ét, A/I): Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A/I ≅ Ω^•_{X/(A/I)}, the p-completed de Rham complex. No hypothesis on W(A/I) is needed. (2) For R p-completely smooth over A/I the isomorphism φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≅ Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} is the composite of φ̃ ⊗ A/I (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), the Bockstein reduction Lη_IΔ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≃ (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I), and the Hodge–Tate comparison (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I) ≅ (Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)}, d). (3) (Derived form, Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.2.5) For every animated commutative A/I-algebra R there is a natural isomorphism A/I ⊗^L_A φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} with the p-completed derived de Rham complex, the left Kan extension of (2) from polynomial algebras.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a bounded prism; X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, not necessarily affine or proper.
- The scalar extension is along φ_A followed by A → A/I and is derived (p, I)-completed; it is not the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{X/A}, whose cohomology is the Hodge–Tate cohomology.
- BS22 Corollary 15.4 prints the right-hand side as Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}; it is Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E1).
- PR.1/de-rham-comparison is the same statement under the hypothesis that W(A/I) is p-torsion-free (BS22 Theorem 6.4), proved without Lη. The sources do not compare the two isomorphisms when both are defined, and the node does not assert that they coincide (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27).
- Bhatt–Lurie prove (3) through the Hodge–Tate divisor of the Cartier–Witt stack; the plan uses the Bhatt–Scholze route, which needs nothing from PR.5.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (2): reduce φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ ≅ Lη_IΔ modulo I and apply AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction (BMS1 Proposition 6.12): Lη_IΔ ⊗^L A/I is represented by the complex with terms H^i(Δ̄){i} and the Bockstein differential β_I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map is by construction a map of differential graded algebras (Ω̂^•, d) → (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I), an isomorphism by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison.
2. Multiplicativity: φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)); the Bockstein reduction is multiplicative (BMS1 Lemma 6.13 and the remark before it, requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1; equivalently H^0_B is symmetric monoidal on Beilinson-connective objects, BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (3)).
3. (1): the affine isomorphisms are functorial for étale maps and Lη_I, the Bockstein complex and the de Rham complex are compatible with étale localisation, so they glue on X_ét (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)).
4. (3): both sides commute with sifted colimits in R (the left side by PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology, the right side by definition of derived de Rham cohomology, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), and (2) for polynomial algebras is natural; left Kan extend (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3).

*Acceptance.*
- Crystalline prism: reduces modulo p the crystalline comparison φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A).
- The q-de Rham prism: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂_{A, φ} A/([p]_q) is de Rham cohomology over Z_p[ζ_p]; here A/I = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free, so PR.1/de-rham-comparison also applies.
- A prism where Theorem 6.4 does not apply: a crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p non-reduced has p-torsion in W(A/p); the present node still applies.
- R = A/I: both sides are A/I.

### `PR.3/image-of-frobenius` — The image of Frobenius on prismatic cohomology (BS22 Corollary 15.5)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/image-of-frobenius` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth formal A/I-scheme. For every i ≥ 0 there is a natural map V_i : τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) such that φ ∘ V_i is the natural map τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} induced by I^{⊗ i} → A, and V_i ∘ (φ ⊗ 1) : τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} is the natural map. In particular V_i induces V_i : H^i_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}), an inverse of φ up to I^{⊗ i}; when I = (d), V_i φ = φ V_i = d^i on H^i. For X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A)) and the linearised Frobenius φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A) → RΓ_Δ(X/A) becomes an isomorphism after inverting I.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) bounded prism; X smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} = Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A as a sheaf on X_ét.
- BS22 Corollary 15.5 prints the induced map as H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} → H^i_Δ(X/A); source and target are interchanged (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E25). The node states the corrected direction, which is that of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6).
- The identification H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^*RΓ_Δ(X/A)) uses that completed base change commutes with the finite limits computing RΓ on a quasi-compact quasi-separated X; the sheaf-level statement needs no such hypothesis.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} and φ = (Lη_IΔ → Δ) ∘ φ̃.
2. BMS1 Lemma 6.9 (requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1) gives natural transformations I^{⊗ m} ⊗ τ^{≤ m} → τ^{≤ m} Lη_I and, on objects with I-torsion-free H^n, τ^{≥ n} Lη_I → I^{⊗ n} ⊗ τ^{≥ n}, whose composites in both orders on τ^{[n, m]} are the natural inclusions. Take n = 0, m = i and K = Δ_{X/A}, which lies in D^{≥0} with I-torsion-free H^0; define V_i as φ̃^{-1} composed with the first transformation.
3. H^i(X_ét, τ^{≤ i}K) → H^i(X_ét, K) is an isomorphism for every K, which gives the statement on H^i; after inverting I the maps φ and V_i are mutually inverse up to the unit d^i locally.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: V_0 φ = φ V_0 = 1 on τ^{≤0}, so φ : H^0(Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) → H^0(Δ_{X/A}) is an isomorphism.
- Crystalline prism: V_i is the classical operator with V_i φ = φ V_i = p^i on H^i_crys (Berthelot–Ogus).
- X = P^1 and i = 2: φ on H^2_Δ(P^1/A) = A{−1} is divisible by exactly I, consistent with φ_{A{−1}} : A{−1} → I ⊗ A{−1}.
- Consumer: finiteness and isogeny statements for prismatic cohomology (BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6)); PR.7 uses the isogeny property of Frobenius on prismatic F-crystals of geometric origin.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-truncations`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/derived-decalage`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Corollary 15.5 and its proof: “Another application is the following result on the image of” (the statement, with the direction of the induced map on H^i corrected)
- BS22-v4, Theorem 1.8 (6): “becomes an isomorphism after inverting” (the consequence for the linearised Frobenius and the direction of V_i)
- BMS1, Lemma 6.9: “The next lemma bounds how far” (the two natural transformations and their composites)

### `PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison` — Comparison of the Nygaard filtration with the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) (Bockstein and de Rham complex) Let β : H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) → H^{n+1}(gr^{n+1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) be the boundary map of gr^{n+1}_N → Fil^n_N/Fil^{n+2}_N → gr^n_N. Then (⊕_n H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), β) is a commutative differential graded algebra and there is a unique isomorphism of commutative differential graded algebras θ onto the p-completed de Rham complex (Ω̂^•_{R/Ā}, d) that in degree 0 is the isomorphism H^0(gr^0_N) ≅ H^0(R̂). (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects of DF(A), Fil^•(γ_R) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, to the p-completed derived de Rham complex with its Hodge filtration, determined by functoriality in R and by gr^0(γ_R) being the isomorphism gr^0_N ≅ R̂ ≅ gr^0_Hodge. (3) There is a functorial fibre sequence in DF(A): I ⊗^L_A Fil^{•−1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, the first map being the multiplication v of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration and the second Fil^•(γ_R). In filtration degree 0 it is the de Rham comparison PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3). (4) Consequently Ā ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}; and if the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over Ā then v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^n_N → Fil^{n+1}_N is an isomorphism for n ≥ d, so Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗_A Fil^d_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} for n ≥ d.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; dR^∧_{R/Ā} and its Hodge filtration are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2, p-completed; for p-completely smooth R they are the p-completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration.
- In (1) the de Rham complex is that of π_0(R) relative to Ā, and Ω̂^n is H^0 of the derived p-completion of Ω^n_{π_0(R)/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie's convention; it need not be p-adically separated and agrees with the classical completion when Ω^n has bounded p^∞-torsion).
- In the proof of BL22 Corollary 5.2.8 the Hodge–Tate comparison is printed gr_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n} ≃ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[n]; the shift is [−n] (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E35).
- The fibre sequence compares three filtrations at once: on graded pieces it reads Fil_{n−1}^conj Δ̄{n} → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} → gr_n^conj Δ̄{n} ≅ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[−n].

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): H^n(gr^n_N) ≅ H^n(Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}) ≅ Ω̂^n_{R/Ā} by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and the connectivity of the conjugate filtration; the Bockstein is identified with d on polynomial algebras through the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), hence in general; uniqueness because the de Rham complex is generated in degree 0 (BL22 Proposition 5.2.2).
2. (2): left Kan extend from polynomial algebras, where Fil^•_Hodge is the object (Ω̂^{≥ •}, d) of the heart of the Beilinson t-structure and Fil^•_N is Beilinson connective (PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (5)), so maps Fil^•_N → Fil^•_Hodge are maps of complexes H^0_B(Fil^•_N) = (⊕ H^n(gr^n_N), β) → (Ω̂^•, d); take θ (BL22 Proposition 5.2.3).
3. (3): the composite Fil^•(γ) ∘ v is canonically null because I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N lies in DF^{≤ −1} and the target in the heart, on polynomial algebras; the induced map from the cofibre of v to Fil^•_Hodge is an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 0 by PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3) and on graded pieces by the Hodge–Tate comparison, hence in all degrees by induction (BL22 Corollary 5.2.8).
4. (4): take limits in (3) (BL22 Corollary 5.2.9); for smooth R of dimension ≤ d, Fil^{n}_Hodge = Ω̂^{≥ n} vanishes for n > d (BL22 Corollary 5.2.15).

*Acceptance.*
- R = Ā: the sequence is I ⊗ I^{n−1} → I^n → 0 for n ≥ 1 and I ⊗ A → A → Ā for n = 0.
- Crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R regular Noetherian over F_p: the sequence is p · N^{n−1}WΩ → N^nWΩ → Ω^{≥ n}, the defining property of Nygaard's filtration on the de Rham–Witt complex.
- R p-completely smooth of dimension d: the Nygaard filtration is I-adic from degree d on.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

- BL22, Corollaries 5.2.8, 5.2.9, 5.2.15: “admits a refinement, which describes the Hodge filtration on derived de Rham cohomology:” (parts (3), (4))

### `PR.3/nygaard-completion` — Nygaard completion ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Nygaard completion**.

(a) For a prism (B, J) the Nygaard completion is the ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B (inverse limit along the surjections B/Fil^{i+1}_N → B/Fil^i_N), with the canonical map c : B → B̂ and the filtration Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B). Then ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B; B̂/Fil^i_N B̂ = B/Fil^i_N B; gr^i_N B̂ = gr^i_N B; and B̂ is complete for its filtration. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ̂_S denotes the Nygaard completion of Δ_S; Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N Δ̂_S ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces). (b) Frobenius. Assume J = (d) (then B is d-adically complete). Since φ(Fil^n_N B) ⊂ d^n B, φ induces a ring map φ̂ : B̂ → lim_n B/d^n B = B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ; the Frobenius of B̂ is c ∘ φ̂, so it factors through B. Likewise the divided Frobenius extends to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ → B with d^i φ_i = φ̂ on Fil^i_N B̂, and with twists to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ ⊗_B B{i} → B̂{i}. (c) Filtered objects. For a filtered object Fil^• of DF(A) with underlying object M = Fil^0 (N-indexed), the completion is M̂ = lim_i M/Fil^i with Fil^i M̂ = lim_{j ≥ i} Fil^i/Fil^j; M → M̂ is an isomorphism if and only if lim_i Fil^i = 0, and then M is called Nygaard-complete. This defines the Nygaard completions of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration) and of Δ_{S/A} over a perfectoid base (PR.3/nygaard-filtration); for a tower of surjections of discrete modules the derived limit is the limit, so (a) is a special case. (d) On quasisyntomic algebras over a perfectoid ring R, S ↦ Fil^•_N Δ̂_{S/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf of complete filtered objects, the unfolding of (a) from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. The map Δ → Δ̂ is not an isomorphism in general; PR.3/nygaard-completeness states when it is, and PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example gives a ring S for which Δ_S → Δ̂_S is injective and not surjective.

*Hypotheses.*
- (B, J) is a prism; in (b) J is principal, which holds for the initial prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring.
- Completion means completion with respect to the Nygaard filtration only; no (p, J)-adic completion is applied, and by BS22 Lemma 13.2 (2) none is needed for Δ_S (PR.3/bms2-comparison).
- Statement (b) is not printed in the sources in this form; it is immediate from the definition of the filtration and is recorded because the syntomic complexes of PR.4 need φ_i on the completion without passing through topological Hochschild homology.
- Δ and Δ̂ are distinct objects: no statement of the stage identifies them outside the cases listed in PR.3/nygaard-completeness.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a): the inverse limit of rings along surjections; the kernel of B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is the limit of Fil^i_N/Fil^j_N, the transition maps are surjective, so B̂ → B/Fil^i_N is surjective and the quotients and graded pieces are unchanged; completeness of B̂ is the standard statement for limits of towers.
2. (b): a prism is derived J-complete and d is a nonzerodivisor, so B is classically d-adically complete. For x ∈ Fil^i_N B̂ represented by x_n ∈ Fil^i_N B with x_{n+1} − x_n ∈ Fil^n_N B, the elements φ_i(x_n) satisfy φ_i(x_{n+1}) − φ_i(x_n) ∈ d^{n−i}B and converge d-adically; the limit is φ_i(x). Twists: tensor with the invertible module B{i} (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)).
3. (c): completion of filtered objects (BMS2 Lemma 5.2 (2), requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1): F̂(i) = F(i)/F(∞), and gr^i is unchanged.
4. (d): each gr^i_N is a quasisyntomic sheaf (PR.3/nygaard-filtration (c)); a limit of sheaves is a sheaf.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 13.1: Δ̂_S is identified with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) of BMS2 (proved in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 from PR.3/bms2-comparison)
- BS22 §14 and PR.4: Z_p(n)(S) = fib(φ_n − 1 : Fil^n_N Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n})
- BS22 Proposition 15.7: the Nygaard completion of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖} is π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p)
- Bhatt–Lurie §5.8 and PR.5: the Nygaard-completed absolute prismatic complex and its comparison with the Hodge-completed derived de Rham complex

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completion` (constructor): The ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B, realised as the subring of compatible families in ∏_i B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.mem_completion_iff` (characterisation): A family (x_i) lies in B̂ iff x_j maps to x_i under B/Fil^j_N → B/Fil^i_N for all i ≤ j.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.toCompletion` (data): The canonical ring map c : B → B̂.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.toCompletion_apply` (simp): The i-th component of c(x) is the class of x in B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.ker_toCompletion` (characterisation): ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionProj` (projection): The ring map B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionProj_surjective` (other): B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is surjective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFil` (data): The ideal Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFrobenius` (data): For J = (d) and B d-adically complete, the ring map φ̂ : B̂ → B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.completionFrobenius_toCompletion` (simp): φ̂(c(x)) = φ(x).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard.IsNygaardComplete` (constructor): The predicate that c : B → B̂ is bijective.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr3_completion_perfect` (compatibility): For a perfect prism (B, (d)) with B classically (p, d)-adically complete, c : B → B̂ is bijective.
- `pr3_completion_quotient` (characterisation): B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is surjective with kernel Fil^i_N B̂, and c^{-1}(Fil^i_N B̂) = Fil^i_N B.
- `pr3_completion_frobenius` (compatibility): φ̂ ∘ c = φ: the Frobenius of the completion restricts to φ on B.
- `pr3_completion_not_surjective` (non-example): It is false that c is surjective for every prism: for the prism of F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) the element Σ_m Y^m/m! of B̂ is not in the image.

*Acceptance.*
- S perfectoid: Δ̂_S = A_inf(S) (PR.3/nygaard-completeness (2)).
- S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): Δ̂_S is strictly larger than Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example).
- φ̂ ∘ c = φ and the Frobenius of Δ̂_S has image in the image of Δ_S.
- Export: Δ̂_S with its filtration, Frobenius and divided Frobenius is the object that RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 compares with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), and the object from which PR.4 builds Z_p(n).

### `PR.3/nygaard-completeness` — Completeness of the Nygaard filtration: exact statements

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completeness` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) (Criterion) For a prism (B, J): c : B → B̂ is injective iff ∩_i Fil^i_N B = 0, and bijective iff moreover lim^1_i Fil^i_N B = 0; for a filtered object, M → M̂ is an isomorphism iff lim_i Fil^i = 0. (2) (Perfectoid rings) If S is perfectoid then Δ_S = A_inf(S) is Nygaard-complete: Fil^i_N = (e^i) with e = φ^{-1}(d), and A_inf(S) is e-adically complete. (3) (Relative criterion, Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.2.10) For a bounded prism (A, I) and an animated A/I-algebra R: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete if and only if the p-completed derived de Rham complex dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete (lim_m Fil^m_Hodge = 0). (4) (Smooth case, Corollary 5.2.11) If R is p-completely flat over A/I and R/pR is a filtered colimit of smooth (A/I)/p-algebras, in particular if R is p-completely smooth, then φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete; if R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d then moreover Fil^n_N = I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗ Fil^d_N for n ≥ d. (5) (Perfect base) For a perfect prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra S: Δ_{S/A} is Nygaard-complete for the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration iff dR^∧_{S/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete. In particular Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S for S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example). (6) (Exhaustiveness) The Nygaard filtration is exhaustive in the trivial sense Fil^0_N = Δ; the non-trivial exhaustiveness statement is PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit.

*Hypotheses.*
- Completeness always refers to the Nygaard filtration; all objects are already derived (p, I)-complete.
- In (3), (4) the filtration is the relative one on the Frobenius twist; in (2), (5) the base prism is perfect and the filtration is on Δ itself.
- Hodge-completeness of derived de Rham cohomology is a property owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; for p-completely smooth R the Hodge filtration is the finite stupid filtration.
- BL22 Remark 5.8.4 prints Fil^n ≃ I^{n−d} Fil^{n−d}; the correct right-hand side is I^{n−d} ⊗ Fil^d (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E36); (4) states the relative form.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): the Milnor sequence for the tower Fil^i_N B: 0 → lim Fil^i → B → lim B/Fil^i → lim^1 Fil^i → 0.
2. (2): φ is bijective, so Fil^i_N = φ^{-1}(d^i A) = (e^i) (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp); A_inf(S) is classically (p, d)-complete, e^p ≡ d modulo p, so it is derived e-complete and e-adically separated, hence e-adically complete.
3. (3): PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) gives A/I ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge; lim_m Fil^m_N is derived I-complete, so it vanishes iff its reduction does. (4): for such R the Hodge filtration of dR^∧ is the stupid filtration of the p-completed de Rham complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), which is complete; the last assertion is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4); for smooth R completeness also follows from PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3).
4. (5): for a perfect prism φ_A^* is an equivalence carrying Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} to Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{S/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration); apply (3).

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p, (p)), S = F_p: Δ = Z_p, Fil^i = (p^i), complete.
- R = A/I⟨T⟩: complete, with Fil^n_N = I^{n−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N for n ≥ 1.
- S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): dR^∧_{S/F_p} is the divided power algebra with its divided power filtration, which is not complete; correspondingly Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S.
- The statement of BS22 Theorem 13.1 involves Δ̂_S and not Δ_S for exactly this reason.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.5/absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Corollaries 5.2.9, 5.2.10, 5.2.11: “is Hodge-complete (that is, the limit” (parts (3), (4))
- BL22, Example 5.8.1 and Proposition 5.8.2: “is not Nygaard-complete.” (the failure of completeness for a quasiregular semiperfect ring, part (5))
- BS22-v4, the warning after Definition 12.1: “We warn the reader that in general the Nygaard filtration is not separated.” (the caution behind (1))

### `PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit` — Prismatic cohomology as the completed colimit of the Nygaard pieces

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R an animated commutative A/I-algebra. The maps v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^m_N → Fil^{m+1}_N of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration give a diagram φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−2} ⊗ Fil^2_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → ⋯, and the maps I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m(φ) : I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} are compatible with it. (1) The induced map from the (p, I)-completed colimit of this diagram to Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism: the relative Frobenius exhibits Δ_{R/A} as the completed union of the twisted Nygaard pieces. (2) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d, the diagram is constant from m = d on and Fil^m(φ) : Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{⊗ m} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every m ≥ d. (3) Consequently for X smooth over A/I of dimension ≤ d and i ≥ d, RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) bounded prism; R animated A/I-algebra; I^{−m} is the dual of I^{⊗ m}.
- The colimit is formed in the (p, I)-complete derived category of A.
- BS22 states (3) for the Nygaard-completed sheaf; by PR.3/nygaard-completeness (4) completion changes nothing for smooth X.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Both sides of (1) commute with filtered (indeed sifted) colimits in R, so R may be taken a polynomial algebra in d variables.
2. By PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) the diagram is constant for m ≥ d. It remains to see that Fil^d(φ) : Fil^d_N → I^d ⊗ Δ is an isomorphism; by derived Nakayama and the same result it suffices that gr^d(φ) : gr^d_N → Δ̄{d} is one.
3. By PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces, gr^d(φ) is the inclusion Fil_d^conj Δ̄{d} → Δ̄{d}, an isomorphism because gr_n^conj Δ̄ ≅ (∧^n L)[−n]^∧{−n} vanishes for n > d and the conjugate filtration is exhaustive (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison).
4. (3): apply (2) on affines and glue (BS22, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7).

*Acceptance.*
- R = A/I (d = 0): Fil^m_N = I^m and I^{−m} ⊗ I^m = A = Δ for all m.
- Perfect prism and S perfectoid: e^{−m}(e^m) = A_inf(S).
- After inverting I the relative Frobenius φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}[1/I] → Δ_{R/A}[1/I] is an isomorphism for smooth R, in agreement with PR.3/image-of-frobenius.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.5/absolute-frobenius`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Corollary 5.2.16 and its proof: “Then the relative Frobenius map exhibits” (parts (1), (2))
- BL22, Corollary 5.2.15: “is an isomorphism for” (the constancy of the diagram for smooth algebras)
- BS22-v4, §15.2, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7: “as both are complete for compatible filtrations” (part (3), stated there for the completed sheaf)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Nygaard/Hodge`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Nygaard`.

### `PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example` — A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring whose prism is not Nygaard-complete

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example` · application · part PR.0.

Let S_0 = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, with perfect base prism (Z_p, (p)). (1) Δ_{S_0} = Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in Z_p[Y^{1/p^∞}], with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; it is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!. (2) Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the p-completion of ⊕_i p^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!; equivalently it is generated by the elements p^a · Y^b/b! · Y^ε with a + b ≥ n, b ∈ N, 0 ≤ ε < 1. (3) ∩_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} = 0, and Δ̂_{S_0} is the set of families (a_i)_{i ∈ N[1/p]} of p-adic integers, written Σ a_i Y^i/⌊i⌋!, such that for every n only finitely many i with ⌊i⌋ < n have a_i ∉ p^{n−⌊i⌋}Z_p; Δ_{S_0} is the subset of families with a_i → 0 p-adically. (4) The element exp(Y) = Σ_{m ≥ 0} Y^m/m! lies in Δ̂_{S_0} and not in Δ_{S_0}. Hence c : Δ_{S_0} → Δ̂_{S_0} is injective and not surjective, and lim^1_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} ≠ 0. (5) The same holds for the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ of PR.3/nygaard-key-case, with Σ_m Y^m/[m]_q! ∈ Δ̂_S ∖ Δ_S. By contrast Δ_S = Δ̂_S for S perfectoid.

*Hypotheses.*
- S_0 is the reduction of the key case along Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p; the description (1), (2) is that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case at q = 1.
- Bhatt–Lurie state the example for k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) in the coordinates of A_crys, which differ from the present ones by the Frobenius twist of Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.4.3 (x corresponds to Y); the filtration is the ideal generated by p^a x^b/b! with a + b ≥ m.
- The example concerns the prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring as defined in PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp; no absolute prismatic cohomology is used.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): Δ_{S_0} is the prismatic envelope Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧ (PR.2/qrsp-prism), which is the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Corollary 2.39) since Y^p = φ(Y); its basis is the standard one (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0).
2. (2): S → S_0 is relatively perfect over the map of perfectoid rings Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p, so by PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (3) the Nygaard filtration is the base change of that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (e) along q ↦ 1, where [p]_{q^{1/p}} ↦ p and [n]_q! ↦ n!. It agrees with BL22 Proposition 5.3.6.
3. (3): Fil^n_N is graded and its degree i part is p^{max(n−⌊i⌋,0)}Z_p, with zero intersection over n; Δ/Fil^n = ⊕_{⌊i⌋<n} Z/p^{n−⌊i⌋}, and the limit over n is the stated set of families.
4. (4): for exp(Y) the family is a_m = 1 for m ∈ N and 0 otherwise; for each n only the indices m < n are non-zero modulo Fil^n, and a_m does not tend to 0. (5): the same argument with [p]_{q^{1/p}}-adic separatedness of A; the perfectoid case is PR.3/nygaard-completeness (2).

*Acceptance.*
- Acceptance example of the stage: a case where Δ and its Nygaard completion visibly differ.
- Δ_{S_0}/Fil^1_N = ⊕_{i<1} F_p Y^i ≅ S_0.
- gr^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the F_p-span of the classes of p^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/⌊i⌋! for ⌊i⌋ ≤ n, a free S_0-module of rank n + 1, matching Fil_n^conj of the divided power algebra.
- The partial sums Σ_{m<n} Y^m/m! are a Cauchy sequence for the Nygaard topology with no limit in Δ_{S_0}.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-key-case`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-completion`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

### `PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates` — The Nygaard filtration in coordinates (de Rham and q-de Rham models)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, (d)) be a perfect prism, d′ = φ_A(d), and R a p-completely smooth A/d-algebra. Let M^• be a cochain complex of A-modules in degrees ≥ 0 whose terms are d-torsion-free, d′-torsion-free and d-adically complete, with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M of complexes, and an isomorphism M^• ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in D(A) carrying φ_M to the Frobenius. Assume (a) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ d′^n M^n for all n, and (b) for all n the map M^n/dM^n → H^n(M^•/d′M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, is bijective. Then the subcomplexes N^iM^• = d^{max(i − •, 0)} M^• (in degree n: d^{max(i−n,0)}M^n), with φ_M : N^iM^• → d′^iM^•, represent the relative Nygaard filtration and its filtered Frobenius: there is a unique isomorphism N^•M^• ≅ Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in DF(A) compatible with the maps to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}. If moreover φ_M/d′^n : M^n/d → M^n/d′ is injective for all n, then N^iM^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ d′^i M^n}. Instances. (i) (BMS2 Proposition 8.7) A = W(k) with k a perfect field, d = d′ = p, R smooth over k, Ã a p-completely smooth lift of R with a Frobenius lift, M^• the p-completed de Rham complex of Ã over W(k): the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology is p^{max(i − •, 0)} Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)}. (ii) (BMS2 Remark 9.11) A = A_inf(O_C), d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ = [p]_q with q = [ε], R with a framing, M^• the framed q-de Rham complex q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf} with φ(T_j) = T_j^p: the Nygaard filtration is ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf}.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, (d)) is a perfect prism; under Δ_{R/A} = (φ_A)_* φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} the ideal I^i Δ corresponds to d′^i M, which is why d′ appears in (a) and d in the conclusion.
- Hypothesis (b) is the Cartier isomorphism in the model M: in (i) it is the inverse Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3), in (ii) its q-analogue.
- In instance (ii) the identification of the framed q-de Rham complex with φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} (through AΩ) and hypothesis (b) are supplied by PR.6, which applies this node; the present stage proves the criterion and instance (i).
- BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 is taken with q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E37).
- BMS2 prove (i) through the de Rham–Witt complex; the plan derives it from the Lη_I factorisation, which needs no de Rham–Witt theory.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. N^iM^• is a subcomplex and φ_M(N^iM^n) ⊂ d′^{max(i−n,0)+n}M^n ⊂ d′^iM^n by (a), so φ_M is a filtered map from N^•M^• to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A} refining the relative Frobenius.
2. gr^i N is ⊕_{n ≤ i} (M^n/d)[−n] with zero differential, so N^• is Beilinson connective; it is complete because each M^n is d-adically complete and d-torsion-free. On H^n of gr^i (n ≤ i) the map to gr^i of the I-adic filtration is x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, bijective by (b).
3. By the criterion for connective covers (BL22, the remark characterising Beilinson connective covers; BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (2)), N^• is the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}; so is Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} by PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3). Connective covers are unique.
4. (i): M ≅ RΓ_crys(R/W(k)) ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} compatibly with Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2, PR.1/crystalline-comparison); φ̃ is divisible by p^n on n-forms, and (b) is the Cartier isomorphism. (ii): φ(d_q log T_j) = ξ̃ d_q log T_j gives (a).

*Acceptance.*
- R = k[T], Ã = W(k)⟨T⟩, φ̃(T) = T^p: Fil^i_N is p^iW(k)⟨T⟩ → p^{i−1}W(k)⟨T⟩dT for i ≥ 1; modulo p · Fil^{i−1}_N this is Ω^{≥ i}, as in PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison.
- i = 1: Fil^1_N = (pÃ → Ω^1 → ⋯), the kernel of Ω^•_{Ã} → R.
- Routed item PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/098 is instance (ii); its q-de Rham input is PR.6's.
- The filtration depends on the Frobenius lift only up to filtered quasi-isomorphism.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`.

### `PR.3/bms2-comparison` — The prismatic half of the comparison with BMS2 (BS22 Lemma 13.2 and Theorem 13.1)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/bms2-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_S, (d)). (1) (BS22 Lemma 13.2 (1)) δ(Fil^i_N Δ_S) ⊂ Fil^{pi}_N Δ_S + (d, p)^{i−1} Δ_S for all i ≥ 1. (2) (Lemma 13.2 (2)) The completion of Δ_S for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S agrees with its completion for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S + (d, p)^j Δ_S; this follows because every gr^i_N Δ_S is classically (d, p)-adically complete. (3) Hence the δ-structure of Δ_S extends uniquely to a continuous δ-structure on the Nygaard completion Δ̂_S, functorially in S; its Frobenius is the Frobenius c ∘ φ̂ of PR.3/nygaard-completion, it maps Fil^i_N Δ̂_S into d^i Δ̂_S, and (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) satisfies Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} via φ/d^i. (4) (Recognition in the key case) Let R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ with prism (A, ([p]_q)) and S = R⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X). Let D be a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat A-algebra with an endomorphism φ_D over φ_A and an A-algebra map A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ → D commuting with the Frobenius lifts (φ(Y^{1/p^n}) = Y^{1/p^{n−1}}), such that the image of Y^p lies in [p]_q D. Then there is a unique map Δ_S → D of A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras commuting with φ, and it is an isomorphism if and only if it is one after derived reduction modulo (p, [p]_q). Export. These statements, with PR.3/nygaard-key-case, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces and PR.3/nygaard-completion, are the prismatic input of BS22 Theorem 13.1: the identification of (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), its cyclotomic Frobenius and the Nygaard filtration of BMS2, and likewise BS22 Proposition 15.7 for π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p) and the Nygaard completion of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}. Those identifications are proved in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6, which imports this node; they are not asserted here.

*Hypotheses.*
- S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; d is the image of a generator of ker θ for a perfectoid ring mapping to S.
- The node contains no statement about topological Hochschild homology and has no trace-theoretic prerequisite. In the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1 the inputs from BMS2 (the non-completed theory of Construction 7.12 with its Nygaard filtration, the Hodge–Tate comparison from the Segal conjecture, Corollary 9.12, and the characteristic p comparison, Theorem 8.17) belong to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6; the steps planned here are the lemma, the extension of the δ-structure, and the construction of the comparison map from the q-divided power structure.
- The interface entry for this node described it as the identification with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p); the stage edge PR.3 → RT.6 makes RT.6 the owner of that identification, and the node is sharpened accordingly.
- In (1) the case i = 1 is empty of content: (d, p)^0 Δ_S = Δ_S.

1. (1): choose a surjection S′ = R⟨X_a^{1/p^∞}, Y_b^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_a) → S inducing a surjection on cotangent complexes, hence on Δ and on every Fil^i_N (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces); reduce to S′, absorb the Y_b into R, pass to finitely many X_a by filtered colimits and to one variable by the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (5)), using that the claim is stable under products: for x ∈ Fil^j_N, y ∈ Fil^k_N the formula δ(xy) = x^pδ(y) + y^pδ(x) + pδ(x)δ(y) and φ = x^p + pδ(x) give δ(xy) ∈ Fil^{p(j+k)}_N + (d, p)^{j+k−1}.
2. In one variable (PR.3/nygaard-key-case) the filtration is generated multiplicatively by [p]_{q^{1/p}} ∈ Fil^1_N, where the claim is empty, and by Y^i/[i]_q! ∈ Fil^i_N, where δ of the element is homogeneous of degree pi and every homogeneous element of degree pi lies in Fil^{pi}_N.
3. (2): gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} semilinearly (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces), and Fil_i Δ̄_S is derived p-complete and p-completely flat over S, hence classically p-adically complete; φ(d) is a unit multiple of p modulo d. (3): by (1), δ is continuous for the topology of (2), so it extends to the completion (the extension of a δ-structure to a completion as in PR.0/delta-classical-completion); the remaining assertions are PR.3/nygaard-completion.
4. (4): BS22 Lemma 12.5 (PR.3/nygaard-key-case (b)) applied to D and x = Y gives Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ D, and the basis of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (d) gives the map, unique because D is [n]_q-torsion-free; both sides are derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, so derived Nakayama applies.

# Layer PR.4. Étale comparison and p-adic Tate twists

Layer PR.4 proves the étale comparison and builds the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), after Bhatt–Scholze §§9, 11 and 14, BMS2 §§7–8 and 10, Bhatt–Lurie §§7–8 and Bhatt–Mathew. It has 30 nodes, and its coverage is **partial**.

Frobenius fixed points are derived: M^{φ=1} is the fibre of φ − 1 (Lemma 9.2), and it commutes with completed colimits. The étale comparison is proved first for perfectoid rings (Artin–Schreier–Witt and tilting) and then for every p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring, with derived prismatic cohomology, in both forms of Theorem 9.1. Coefficient compatibility, passage to Z_p and the variant of Remark 9.3 without inverting d follow, with the smooth case Theorem 1.8 (4) and the étale cohomological dimension of the generic fibre of a perfectoid ring (Theorem 11.1). Z_p(n)(S) is the fibre of φ_n − can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} on the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology with its Breuil–Kisin twist; PR.4 defines only these fibres and imports the Nygaard filtration from PR.3 and PR.5 and the twists from PR.3 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28). The syntomic part covers: syntomic complexes of quasisyntomic rings, animated rings and formal schemes; the prismatic logarithm; weights n ≤ 1; the Tate twists of perfectoid rings (Theorem 9.4; formula (9.3) corrected by the review to generators adapted to a trivialisation of the twist); Picard groups of perfectoid rings (Corollary 9.7, for perfectoid R only); discreteness and p-torsion-freeness of Z_p(n) (Theorem 14.1); connectivity and left Kan extension; and, in characteristic p, logarithmic forms and the logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparison. Over O_C the layer proves the vanishing above degree i, the nearby-cycles comparison of BMS2 Theorem 10.1 (through PR.6's AΩ comparison, with no trace-theoretic input), and the étale comparison morphism and syntomic cohomology of schemes (Bhatt–Lurie §8). It also records the warning that syntomic cohomology is not étale cohomology of the generic fibre in every degree.

The coverage is partial because the stage text asks for an étale comparison over a general base prism ("the specified perfected-site or scalar-extension version"), and no node states one; the review asks the orchestrator whether the target is wanted. The arc-topology inputs are gaps, the nearby-cycles morphism is requested from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0 and H1, and the Fontaine–Messing form is proposed for a downstream owner (Structural proposals). Three nodes keep an open point (the multiplicative structure of Z_p(n), the exact sequence of Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc–Soulé in the log de Rham–Witt comparison, and the form of part (4) of the syntomic étale comparison). The planets are the étale comparison theorem, the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), the discreteness of the Tate twists, the logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparison, syntomic complexes as truncated nearby cycles, and the étale comparison for syntomic cohomology.

*Coverage of `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4`: partial.* The remaining items are listed in the Coverage section at the end.

### `PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points` — Derived Frobenius fixed points of a φ-module

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points` · construction · part PR.0.

Let Λ be a commutative ring (Λ = F_p, Z/p^n or Z_p in this stage), B a commutative Λ-algebra and σ a Λ-linear ring endomorphism of B (the Frobenius when B is an F_p-algebra; φ_A when B = A/p^n for a prism (A, (d))). The ∞-category D(B[F]) has as objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M ∈ D(B) and φ_M : M → σ_*M a map in D(B), that is, a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M; it is the lax equaliser of the identity and σ_* on D(B), and a morphism is a map f : M → N with a chosen homotopy φ_N f ≃ σ_*(f) φ_M. The derived Frobenius fixed points are M^{φ=1} := fib(φ_M − 1 : M → M) ∈ D(Λ), the fibre being formed after restriction of scalars to Λ. For t ∈ B such that σ(t) becomes a unit of B[1/t] (for example σ(t) = t^p, or σ(t) ≡ t^p modulo a nilpotent ideal), φ_M extends uniquely to a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M[1/t] = M ⊗^L_B B[1/t], and (M[1/t])^{φ=1} denotes its fixed points. For a Z_p-linear φ-module M one writes (M/p^n)^{φ=1} for the fixed points of M ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n. For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → coker(φ_M − 1 on H^{i−1}(M)) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ_M − 1 on H^i(M)) → 0; in particular H^0(M^{φ=1}) is in general not the group of φ-fixed vectors of H^0(M), and H^1(M^{φ=1}) can be non-zero for M concentrated in degree 0.

*Hypotheses.*
- Λ lies in the σ-fixed subring of B, so that φ_M − 1 is Λ-linear; it is not B-linear.
- The fibre is taken in D(Λ) (or D(Z)); M^{φ=1} carries no B-module structure.
- For (M[1/t])^{φ=1} the image of σ(t) in B[1/t] is a unit; this holds for B = A/p^n, t = d, since φ(d) ≡ d^p mod p.
- As a model in the pinned library a φ-module is a cochain complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism, and the fibre is the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Define D(B[F]) as in the statement of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.2 and the functor (M, φ_M) ↦ fib(φ_M − 1) to D(Λ); in the library model the fibre is the mapping cone of φ − 1 shifted by −1, an object of the derived category through the localisation functor.
2. The long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle M^{φ=1} → M → M gives the short exact sequences 0 → coker(φ − 1 | H^{i−1}) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ − 1 | H^i) → 0.
3. Extension to M[1/t]: σ extends uniquely to B[1/t] because σ(t) is a unit there, and φ_M ⊗ σ is the required endomorphism of M ⊗^L_B B[1/t]; for σ(t) = t^p this is the colimit of φ_M along M → M → … with transition maps t.
4. Exactness: (−)^{φ=1} is a finite limit, hence commutes with all limits, with shifts and with ⊗^L_Λ Λ' for Λ → Λ' of finite Tor-dimension data used here (Z_p → Z/p^n, Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}); it commutes with filtered colimits in D(B), and Lemma 9.2 treats completed colimits.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 and Theorem 1.8(4): the right-hand side (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} of the étale comparison
- Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.2 and the proof of Theorem 9.1: fixed points are compared along completed colimits and along Δ → Δ_perf
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 11.1: RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) is obtained by applying (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} to a fibre of perfected prismatic complexes
- Bhatt–Lurie Example 8.1.3 and Theorem 8.1.9: Artin–Schreier: RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p) is the fixed points of Frobenius on R
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 (étale realisation of Laurent F-crystals): the local system is the fixed points of φ on the Laurent crystal

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.FrobeniusModule` (structure): A φ-module over Λ: a complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism; the model of an object of D(B[F]) after restriction to Λ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints` (constructor): M^{φ=1} = fib(φ_M − 1), as the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1, an object of D(Λ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsι` (projection): The canonical map M^{φ=1} → M, whose composite with φ_M − 1 is zero.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsMap` (functoriality): A map of φ-modules induces a map of fixed points; quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isGE` (characterisation): If M is concentrated in degrees ≥ a then so is M^{φ=1}; if M is in degrees ≤ b then M^{φ=1} is in degrees ≤ b + 1.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isZero_of_isIso` (characterisation): M^{φ=1} = 0 if and only if φ_M − 1 is an isomorphism in D(Λ).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.invert` (constructor): The φ-module M[1/t] for t with σ(t) = t^p·u, u a unit after inverting t: the colimit of M along multiplication by t with the induced endomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale.reduce` (compatibility): The φ-module M/p^n = cone(p^n : M → M) and the transition maps M/p^n → M/p^{n−1}; (M/p^n)^{φ=1} ≃ M^{φ=1} ⊗^L Z/p^n.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr4_fixed_points_fp_h1` (computation): For Λ = F_p, M = F_p in degree 0, φ = id: H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ F_p (and H^0 ≅ F_p).
- `pr4_fixed_points_zero_map` (degenerate): If φ_M = 0 then M^{φ=1} = 0.
- `pr4_fixed_points_identity` (computation): If φ_M = id then M^{φ=1} ≅ M ⊕ M[−1]; in particular H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ H^1(M) ⊕ H^0(M).
- `pr4_fixed_points_not_fixed_vectors` (non-example): For M = F_p[x] in degree 0 with its Frobenius, H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≠ 0 although M is discrete: the class of x is not of the form f^p − f.

*Acceptance.*
- For M = F_p in degree 0 with φ = id: H^0(M^{φ=1}) = F_p and H^1(M^{φ=1}) = F_p.
- For M an algebraic closure of F_p with its Frobenius: M^{φ=1} = F_p in degree 0 (Artin–Schreier equations are solvable).
- For M = F_p[x] with its Frobenius: H^1(M^{φ=1}) = coker(F − 1) ≠ 0, the group H^1_ét(A^1_{F_p}, F_p).
- If φ_M is topologically nilpotent for a complete filtration of M then M^{φ=1} = 0.

*Sources.*

### `PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits` — Frobenius fixed points commute with completed colimits

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let B be an F_p-algebra with an element t ∈ B, with its Frobenius σ, and let D_comp(B[F]) ⊂ D(B[F]) be the full subcategory of pairs (M, φ_M) with M derived t-complete. Then the functors D_comp(B[F]) → D(F_p), M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}, commute with colimits. Explicitly, for a diagram (M_i, φ_i) in D_comp(B[F]) with colimit colim M_i in D(B) and derived t-completion (colim M_i)^∧ (the colimit in D_comp(B[F])), the maps colim (M_i)^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧)^{φ=1} and colim (M_i[1/t])^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧[1/t])^{φ=1} are isomorphisms. The proof shows N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} for every N ∈ D_comp(B[F]).

*Hypotheses.*
- B is an F_p-algebra and φ_M is semilinear over the Frobenius of B, so φ(t) = t^p.
- t is an arbitrary element; derived t-completeness is required of every M_i and the target colimit is the completed one.
- The colimits are indexed by arbitrary small diagrams.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The fibre F of colim M_i → (colim M_i)^∧ is uniquely t-divisible, so F ≃ F[1/t] and it suffices to prove F^{φ=1} = 0, that is, the statement for M ↦ M^{φ=1} (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Lemma 9.2).
2. For N ∈ D(B[F]) the quotient N/t carries an induced φ because φ(t) = t^p ∈ tB. If N is derived t-complete, the fibre of N → N/t is complete for the t-adic filtration and φ is topologically nilpotent on it since φ(t) = t^p ∈ t^2 B; hence its fixed points vanish and N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1}.
3. Both functors in D_comp(B[F]) → D(B[F]) → D(F_p), N ↦ N/t ↦ (N/t)^{φ=1}, commute with all colimits (reduction modulo t kills the difference between a colimit and its completion; fixed points are a finite limit in a stable category).

*Acceptance.*
- For B = F_p[t] and the completed direct sum of copies of F_p[[t]] indexed by a set J: the fixed points are the direct sum over J of F_p ⊕ F_p[−1].
- For a derived p-complete simplicial algebra S over a perfectoid ring: (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1} ≃ (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1}, the step used in Theorem 9.1.
- Without derived t-completeness of the terms the statement N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} fails: N = B[1/t] has N/t = 0.
