### `PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt` — The étale comparison for perfectoid rings (Artin–Schreier–Witt and tilting)

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let S be a perfectoid ring, (A_inf(S), (d)) its perfect prism and S^♭ its tilt; write d also for the image of d in S^♭ = A_inf(S)/p. For every perfect prism (A, (d)) with a map A/d → S one has Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n = W_n(S^♭[1/d]). For n ≥ 1: (1) (Artin–Schreier–Witt) RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n) ≃ fib(F − 1 : W_n(S^♭[1/d]) → W_n(S^♭[1/d])) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}; (2) (tilting) there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n). Hence RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}, naturally in the perfectoid ring S.

*Hypotheses.*
- S is a perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (integral perfectoid; p-torsion and characteristic p are allowed).
- If p = 0 in S both sides vanish: S[1/p] = 0 and d maps to 0 in S^♭.
- Étale cohomology is that of the schemes Spec(S[1/p]) and Spec(S^♭[1/d]), not of adic spectra; the adic spectra enter only through Huber's comparison.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Δ_{S/A} is discrete and equal to the initial prism A_inf(S) of S (PR.2/qrsp-prism applied to the perfectoid ring S, and PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); reducing modulo p^n and inverting d gives W_n(S^♭)[1/[d]] = W_n(S^♭[1/d]) because S^♭ is perfect.
2. Artin–Schreier–Witt: on the étale site of an F_p-scheme the sequence 0 → Z/p^n → W_n(O) → W_n(O) → 0 with second map F − 1 is exact and W_n(O) has no higher cohomology on affines (requested from SF.2); this gives (1) (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Theorem 9.1, first approach).
3. Tilting: RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p])) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spa(S[1/p], S)) and the same for (S^♭[1/d], S^♭) by Huber's comparison [Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, Corollary 3.2.2] (H1:henselian), and the two adic spaces have equivalent étale sites by the tilting equivalence [Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 1.11] (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
4. Naturality in S of all three identifications gives a natural isomorphism on the category of perfectoid rings, as needed to finish the proof of Theorem 9.1 arc-locally.

*Acceptance.*
- S = O_C, C complete algebraically closed: both sides are Z/p^n in degree 0 (W_n(C^♭)^{F=1} = Z/p^n and F − 1 is surjective).
- S a perfect F_p-algebra: both sides are 0.
- S = Z_p^cycl (the p-completion of Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]): H^1 of the right-hand side is coker(F − 1) on W_n of the tilt of the cyclotomic field, the group Hom_cont(Gal, Z/p^n).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/ainf-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/qrsp-prism`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:TruncatedWittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`.

### `PR.4/etale-comparison` — The étale comparison theorem for arbitrary p-adic formal schemes ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Étale comparison theorem**.

Let R be a perfectoid ring, (A, (d)) the perfect prism with A/d = R, and X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R. Let Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) be the derived prismatic cohomology of X relative to A (PR.2; the étale sheafification of S ↦ Δ_{S/A} on affine opens Spf S), with its Frobenius. Let X_η := X ×_{Spf R} Spa(R[1/p], R) be the adic generic fibre and μ : X_{η,ét} → X_ét the nearby-cycles map. Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} in D(X_ét, Z/p^n). In particular, for X = Spf S affine, RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. The fixed points are the derived ones of PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points. The identification is natural in X and in (R, A), and for X = Spf S with S perfectoid it is the isomorphism of PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is perfectoid and (A, (d)) is its perfect prism; a generator d of the prism ideal is fixed (it exists, the prism being perfect).
- X is any p-adic formal scheme over Spf R: no smoothness, no finite-type, flatness or regularity hypothesis, and no restriction on singularities; this corrects the stage text, which restricted the comparison to smooth formal schemes (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/6).
- Δ_{X/A} is the derived (animated) prismatic cohomology of PR.2, not the cohomology of the prismatic site of a singular X.
- (−)[1/d] and /p^n are applied before taking fixed points; no completion is applied after inverting d.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Let F(S) = RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) and G(S) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} on affine formal schemes over Spf R. F is an arc_p-sheaf [Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, Corollary 6.17] and is arc_p-locally concentrated in degree 0 (products of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, BS22 Remark 8.9), so F is the arc_p-sheafification of H^0(F); lifting clopen decompositions through arc_p-equivalences gives H^0(F) → H^0_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) and hence F → RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n).
2. G(S) → (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} is an isomorphism: reduce to n = 1, where Δ_{S/A,perf}/p is the d-completed colimit of Δ_{S/A}/p along φ_S and each φ_S induces an equivalence on ((−)[1/d])^{φ=1}; apply PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits.
3. G is an arc-sheaf because S ↦ S_perfd is (BS22 Corollary 8.11), and an arc_p-sheaf because G(S × S') = G(S) when pS' = 0: Δ_{S'/A,perf} = W(S'_perf) (BS22 Example 8.3) and (d) = (p) there, so W(S'_perf)/p^n[1/d] = 0.
4. The map Z/p^n → G extends uniquely to RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) → G; composing gives F → G, a map of arc_p-sheaves. It is an isomorphism arc-locally, where S may be taken perfectoid and the claim is PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt (alternatively on products of absolutely integrally closed valuation rings of rank ≤ 1).
5. Globalise: the étale sheafification of S ↦ RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) on X_ét is Rμ_* Z/p^n by Huber's comparison between Spec(S[1/p]) and Spa(S[1/p], S) (H1:henselian), and that of G is (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}.

*Acceptance.*
- X = Spf O_C: both sides are Z/p^n.
- X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ (formal torus): after a choice of ε, H^1 of both sides is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers (Kummer theory; C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is a principal ideal domain); it contains the class of T, of order p^n, and is not finitely generated, since units 1 + aT with |a| < 1 close to 1 are not p-th powers.
- A singular input, S = O_C⟨x, y⟩/(xy): the statement holds with the derived Δ_{S/A}; no smoothness is used.
- X of characteristic p: both sides vanish.
- For S perfectoid the map is the Artin–Schreier–Witt/tilting isomorphism.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

- BS22-v4, Section 9, first sentence: “of the generic fibre from prismatic cohomology for arbitrary rings” (the source states the generality (arbitrary rings) that the stage text had narrowed)

### `PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients` — Coefficient compatibility and passage to Z_p in the étale comparison

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients` · theorem · part PR.0.

In the situation of PR.4/etale-comparison write c_n : Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. (1) For n ≥ 1 the square formed by c_n, c_{n−1}, the map Rμ_* Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^{n−1} induced by reduction and the map of fixed points induced by Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^{n−1} commutes; likewise for the maps induced by multiplication p : Z/p^{n−1} → Z/p^n, and c_n ⊗^L_{Z/p^n} Z/p^{n−1} = c_{n−1}. (2) The c_n are maps of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n). (3) Passing to derived limits, Rμ_* Z_p := R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ ((Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}, where (−)^∧_p is derived p-completion; for X = Spf S, R lim_n RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_{S/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}. The limit is the derived limit of complexes; its cohomology sits in Milnor sequences with lim and lim^1 of the groups H^i(−, Z/p^n).

*Hypotheses.*
- Same hypotheses as PR.4/etale-comparison: R perfectoid, X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R.
- Z_p-coefficients on the generic fibre mean the derived limit of the Z/p^n-cohomology (equivalently pro-étale cohomology of the constant sheaf lim Z/p^n); they are not étale cohomology of a constant sheaf Z_p.
- The p-completion in (3) is applied after inverting d; (Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p is in general not Δ_{X/A}[1/d].

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. The comparison F_n → G_n of Theorem 9.1 is the unique map of arc_p-sheaves of Z/p^n-modules extending the unit Z/p^n → G_n; functoriality of this characterisation in the coefficient ring gives the commutative squares of (1) (the source states the identification as canonical for each n; the squares follow from the uniqueness in its proof).
2. Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n := Δ_{X/A}[1/d] ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n, so reduction of coefficients is base change and fixed points, a finite limit, commute with it; multiplicativity (2) holds because both sides are sheaves of commutative algebras and the comparison is the unit-preserving map of such (BS22 Theorem 1.8(4) states it for commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n)).
3. (3): R lim_n (M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (R lim_n M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (M^∧_p)^{φ=1} for M = Δ_{X/A}[1/d], since fibres commute with limits and R lim_n M ⊗^L Z/p^n is the derived p-completion (DD.1); Rμ_* commutes with R lim.
4. The identification of R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n with pro-étale nearby cycles of the sheaf lim Z/p^n uses repleteness of the pro-étale topos (E2).

*Acceptance.*
- X = Spf O_C: Z_p ≃ (W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, and the square for n → n − 1 is reduction Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}.
- Finite level: for the formal torus the Kummer class of T at level n maps to the Kummer class of T at level n − 1 on both sides.
- For S = Z_p^cycl the lim^1 term vanishes and H^1 = Hom_cont(Gal, Z_p).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Theorem 9.1 (the identification is canonical, for each n ≥ 0) and proof of Theorem 9.4 (the sheaves G_n with Z_p-coefficients): “extends uniquely to a comparison map” (the compatibility in n is not printed as a statement; it follows from the uniqueness of the comparison map in the proof, and the Z_p-form is the one used in Theorem 9.4)
- BL22, Section 8.1, first paragraph: “denote the inverse limit” (the convention that Z_p-étale cohomology is the inverse limit of the Z/p^k-cohomology formed in the derived category)

### `PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d` — The variant of the étale comparison without inverting p or d

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and X a p-adic formal scheme over R. Then for all n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}/p^n)^{φ=1} of objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n), where Z/p^n is the constant étale sheaf on X. For X = Spf S affine: RΓ_ét(Spf S, Z/p^n) = RΓ_ét(Spec(S/p), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}/p^n)^{φ=1}, and R lim_n gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ (Δ_{S/A})^{φ=1} = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A}). The map Δ_{X/A}/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n induces on fixed points the adjunction map Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^n of PR.4/etale-comparison.

*Hypotheses.*
- Same generality as Theorem 9.1: X arbitrary over a perfectoid ring R.
- No element is inverted; the right-hand side is in general not concentrated in degree 0 on global sections, since H^1_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) can be non-zero.
- The source leaves the proof to the reader (the remark is quoted in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E17 for a wording slip: read 'a p-adic formal R-scheme'); the proof route below supplies it.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. For a p-complete R-algebra S the absolute prismatic complex of S agrees with the relative one, Δ_S ≃ Δ_{S/A}, compatibly with Frobenius (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 4.4.12; PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A).
2. Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 8.1.9 (the weight-0 case of PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_syn(Spf S, Z_p) = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_S → Δ_S); its proof reduces modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗^L Δ is de Rham cohomology and φ − 1 is an automorphism of the Hodge-filtration piece Fil^1 because Frobenius vanishes on differential forms of positive degree.
3. Reduce modulo p^n; Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change for the henselian pair (S, pS) identifies RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) with RΓ_ét(Spec S/p, Z/p^n), the étale cohomology of Spf S; sheafify on X_ét.
4. Compatibility with Theorem 9.1: both comparison maps are unit-preserving maps of étale sheaves of commutative algebras, and the square with Δ/p^n → Δ[1/d]/p^n commutes by the uniqueness used in Theorem 9.1 (checked arc_p-locally on O_C, as in Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 8.3.7).

*Acceptance.*
- S = O_C: Z/p^n ≃ (A_inf/p^n)^{φ=1} = W_n(O_C^♭)^{F=1}, and F − 1 is surjective on W_n(O_C^♭).
- S = Z_p^cycl: H^1 of both sides is H^1_ét(Spec F_p, Z/p^n) = Z/p^n, since the residue field of S is F_p.
- S an F_p-algebra over a perfect ring R: Δ_{S/A}/p is derived de Rham cohomology up to Frobenius twist and the statement is the Artin–Schreier sequence.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

### `PR.4/etale-comparison-smooth` — The étale comparison for smooth formal schemes (Theorem 1.8(4))

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-smooth` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, with generic fibre X_η over Q_p as a (pre-)adic space and RΓ_Δ(X/A) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.1). Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) ≅ (RΓ_Δ(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} of commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n). It is the corollary of PR.4/etale-comparison obtained by taking RΓ(X_ét, −) and using that for smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with site cohomology.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a perfect prism, so I = (d) is principal and A/I is perfectoid; perfectness is part of the hypothesis of Theorem 1.8(4).
- X is smooth over A/I; smoothness is needed only to identify the derived Δ_{X/A} with the site-theoretic RΓ_Δ(X/A), not for the comparison itself.
- X is qcqs for the global statement, so that inverting d and reducing modulo p^n commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Apply RΓ(X_ét, −) to Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} (PR.4/etale-comparison): the left side is RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) by definition of μ.
2. For smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site), so RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A); fixed points, /p^n and (for qcqs X) [1/d] commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).
3. Multiplicativity is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients (2).

*Acceptance.*
- X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over (A_inf, ker θ): H^1_ét(X_η, μ_{p^n}) is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers, and the class of T corresponds to a φ-fixed class in H^1 of RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf)/p^n[1/d].
- X proper smooth over O_C: with PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness, RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n) is the fixed points of φ on a perfect complex over A_inf/p^n[1/d] = W_n(C^♭).
- The statement for singular X is PR.4/etale-comparison, not this node.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`.

### `PR.4/perfectoid-etale-cohomological-dimension` — Étale cohomological dimension of the generic fibre of a perfectoid ring

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/perfectoid-etale-cohomological-dimension` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let R be a perfectoid ring corresponding to a perfect prism (A, I). The F_p-étale cohomological dimension of the scheme X = Spec(R[1/p]) is ≤ 1: for every étale sheaf F of F_p-modules on X one has H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 1.

*Hypotheses.*
- X is the spectrum, not the adic spectrum, of R[1/p]; the statement is false for general sheaves on the adic spectrum.
- F is an arbitrary étale F_p-sheaf on the scheme X (a filtered colimit of Zariski-constructible sheaves).
- The bound concerns F_p-coefficients (hence p-power torsion sheaves by dévissage); nothing is claimed for ℓ ≠ p.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reduce to F = j_! L with j : U → X the inclusion of a quasi-compact open of a constructible closed subset and L an F_p-local system of constant rank; by the method of the trace [Stacks, Tag 03SH] pass to a finite étale cover V → U of degree prime to p on which L is a successive extension of constant sheaves F_p.
2. Lift V → U to a finitely presented finite map Spec(S) → Spec(R), put Y = Spec(S[1/p]) and let J ⊂ S be a finitely generated ideal cutting out the complement of V; dévissage reduces to RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) ∈ D^{≤1}.
3. By the étale comparison (PR.4/etale-comparison) for Spec(S) and Spec(S/J), RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) is (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} applied to the fibre of Δ_{S/A,perf} → Δ_{(S/J)/A,perf}; fixed points raise the cohomological amplitude by at most one, so it suffices that this fibre is connective, which can be checked after base change to A/I, that is, for S_perfd → (S/J)_perfd.
4. Both S_perfd and (S/J)_perfd are discrete perfectoid rings because R → S is integral (BS22 Theorem 10.11), (S/J)_perfd ≃ (S_perfd/J S_perfd)_perfd by the universal property (PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), and S_perfd/J → (S_perfd/J)_perfd is surjective by BS22 Theorem 7.4 (PerfectoidQuotients:Q4).

*Acceptance.*
- R = O_C: X = Spec C has cohomological dimension 0 ≤ 1.
- R = Z_p^cycl: X is the spectrum of the completed cyclotomic field, whose absolute Galois group has p-cohomological dimension ≤ 1; H^1_ét(X, F_p) = Hom_cont(Gal, F_p) is non-zero, so the bound 1 is attained.
- R a perfect F_p-algebra: X is empty and the statement is vacuous.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Theorem 11.1 and its proof: “is the spectrum, not the adic spectrum, of” (statement with the warning about adic spectra, and the printed proof)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Etale/CohomologicalDimension`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Etale`.

### `PR.4/syntomic-complex` — Syntomic complexes Z_p(n) on quasisyntomic rings ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Syntomic complexes Z_p(n)**.

Let S be a quasisyntomic ring (p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{S/Z_p} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]) and n an integer. Let Δ̂_S{n} be the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology of S with its n-th Breuil–Kisin twist, with Nygaard filtration N^{≥•}Δ̂_S{n}, obtained by quasisyntomic descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (PR.3). Let can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} be the canonical map and φ_n : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} the divided Frobenius; when S is an algebra over a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and the twist is trivialised, φ_n is the restriction of φ/d^n to N^{≥n}Δ̂_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ̂_S}. The n-th syntomic complex is Z_p(n)(S) := fib(φ_n − can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}) ∈ D(Z_p), a derived p-complete complex, and Z/p^r(n)(S) := Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L_Z Z/p^r. The functor S ↦ Z_p(n)(S) is a sheaf of complexes on the quasisyntomic site. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} are discrete, Z_p(n)(S) is the two-term complex N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} in degrees 0 and 1, H^0 = {x ∈ N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} : φ_n(x) = x} and H^1 = coker(φ_n − can). For a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I), choose a generator e of A{1} and let d be the generator of I with φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (for a Z_p^cycl-algebra: d = [p]_q with e = e_A; in characteristic p: d = p). Then Z_p(n)(R) ≃ (φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A) with differential φ/d^n − 1. Another choice e' = ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v) and the complexes are identified by multiplication by v^n. For a generator d' = ud not of this form the two-term complex is in general not quasi-isomorphic to Z_p(n)(R) (R = Z_p^cycl, d' = u[p]_q with u ∈ Z_p^×, u^n ≢ 1 mod p: H^0 = 0 instead of Z_p).

*Hypotheses.*
- S is quasisyntomic; the construction is functorial for all maps of quasisyntomic rings and satisfies quasisyntomic descent.
- The complex is defined by the formula of BMS2 §7.4 and Theorem 1.12(5) as a fibre of prismatic data; it is not defined as a graded piece of TC (that identification belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6). The first display of BMS2 §7.4 prints gr^n TC for gr^i TC, registered as PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E5.
- Sign convention: BMS2 writes hofib(φ − can), Bhatt–Scholze write fib(1 − φ_n); the two fibres are canonically isomorphic.
- The divided Frobenius is a map between different objects (source N^{≥n}, target the whole twisted complex), so Z_p(n) is not an instance of fixed points of an endomorphism for n ≥ 1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. On quasiregular semiperfectoid S: Δ_S is the initial prism (PR.2/qrsp-prism), N^{≥n}Δ_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ_S} (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp), the completion Δ̂_S and its filtration are PR.3/nygaard-completion, the twist is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist and φ_n is PR.3/divided-frobenius; define the two-term complex.
2. Unfold to all quasisyntomic rings by quasisyntomic descent (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent, PR.3/nygaard-filtration; the quasisyntomic site and its basis of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are DD.5): each of N^{≥n}Δ̂{n}, Δ̂{n} is a sheaf, and a fibre of sheaves is a sheaf.
3. Perfectoid case: for R perfectoid Δ̂_R = A_inf(R) = A is Nygaard complete with N^{≥n}A = φ^{−1}(d)^n A, giving formula (9.3) of Bhatt–Scholze; the generator d is the one determined by a generator e of A{1} through φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)); replacing e by ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v), and multiplication by v^n identifies the two complexes.
4. p-completeness: both terms are derived p-complete, hence so is the fibre; Z/p^r(n) is the derived reduction.

*Uses.*

- Bhatt–Scholze Theorems 9.4 and 14.1: Z_p(n)(R) for perfectoid R is compared with étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p]; Z_p(n) is shown discrete and p-torsion-free as a quasisyntomic sheaf
- BMS2 Corollary 8.21 and Theorem 10.1: pushforward to the étale site gives logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves in characteristic p and truncated nearby cycles over O_C
- Bhatt–Lurie Sections 7.4 and 8; Bhatt–Mathew: the same complexes for animated rings and schemes, with first Chern class and étale comparison
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 and arithmetic consumers (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §0.6.1): the defining fibre sequence Z_p(n) → N^{≥n}Δ̂{n} → Δ̂{n} is the syntomic triangle

### `PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes` — Syntomic cohomology of animated rings and bounded p-adic formal schemes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes` · construction · part PR.0.

For an animated commutative ring R and an integer n let Δ_R{n} be the absolute prismatic complex with Breuil–Kisin twist and Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} its absolute Nygaard filtration (PR.5), with ι : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the canonical map and φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the Frobenius. Define RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) := fib(φ{n} − ι) in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p). Then: (a) R → R^∧_p induces an isomorphism on RΓ_syn(Spf −, Z_p(n)); (b) the map to the Nygaard-completed version fib(φ̂{n} − ι̂ : Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ̂_R{n}) is an isomorphism (Proposition 7.4.6); so for R quasisyntomic RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = Z_p(n)(R) of PR.4/syntomic-complex; (c) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) satisfies p-complete fpqc descent (7.4.7); (d) it commutes with sifted colimits, hence is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras (7.4.8); (e) RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → Tot RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}), Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 (7.4.10) and RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≃ lim_m RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L Z/p^m), Z_p(n)) (7.4.11). For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛, RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) := lim over maps Spec(A) → 𝔛 of RΓ_syn(Spf A, Z_p(n)); it agrees with the affine definition on Spf R, satisfies étale descent, and sits in the fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} with second map φ{n} − ι.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is any animated commutative ring; p-completeness is not assumed, and is harmless by (a).
- The construction uses the absolute prismatic cohomology and absolute Nygaard filtration of PR.5 and the twists of PR.3; PR.4 owns only the fibre (ownership fixed by red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28).
- 𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme: locally Spf R with R p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion.
- n is any integer; the complex vanishes for n < 0 (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition and (a): Bhatt–Lurie Construction 7.4.1 and Warning 7.4.2; absolute prismatic complexes and the Nygaard filtration are invariant under p-completion (PR.5).
2. (b): the Frobenius factors as Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ_R{n} (BL Remark 5.7.10), and the 3 × 3 diagram of BL Proposition 7.4.6 has pullback squares in the upper left and lower right, so the two fibres agree; on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings the absolute filtration is {x : φ(x) ∈ Δ^{[n]}} (BL Corollary 5.6.3) and Theorem 5.6.2 identifies it with the Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism, giving agreement with PR.4/syntomic-complex.
3. (c), (d): descent and sifted colimits for the Nygaard-completed filtered complexes (BL Remark 5.8.6); for (d) reduce modulo p, where for m > n the Frobenius maps F_p ⊗ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} into Δ_R^{[pm−n]}{n} ⊂ Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n}, so φ{n} − 1 is an isomorphism on a deep enough step of a complete filtration and F(R) is the fibre of a map between quotients that commute with sifted colimits (BL Proposition 7.4.8).
4. (e) from the corresponding statements for Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} (BL Proposition 5.5.24, Corollary 5.5.25).
5. Globalisation: BL Variant 7.4.12, using (e) for agreement on affines and (c) for étale descent.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie Sections 7.5 and 8: target of the syntomic first Chern class and source of the étale comparison morphism
- Bhatt–Lurie Construction 8.4.1: the p-adic corner of the pullback square defining syntomic cohomology of schemes
- Bhatt–Mathew Example 1.4 and Section 5: the restriction of Z/p^n(i)_X to the p-adic completion
- Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł §0.6.1 (routed item in-syntomic): the fibre sequence RΓ_syn → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ{n} → RΓ_Δ{n} is the syntomic triangle in prismatic form
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: syntomic cohomology of Spf O_K and its Frobenius-fixed description

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.AbsoluteDatum` (structure): The imported data of an animated ring in weight n: Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} and Δ_R{n} as p-complete complexes with ι and φ{n} (owner PR.5), viewed as a Nygaard datum.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology` (constructor): RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = fib(φ{n} − ι).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology_completion` (compatibility): The map to the fibre formed with the Nygaard-completed datum is an isomorphism (BL Proposition 7.4.6).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomology_eq_syntomicComplex` (compatibility): For R quasisyntomic, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≅ Z_p(n)(R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomologyFormal` (constructor): RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) for a bounded p-adic formal scheme, the limit over affines mapping to 𝔛.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicTriangle` (relation): The fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_trivial_ring` (degenerate): For the zero datum (the ring Z[1/p], whose p-completion vanishes) RΓ_syn = 0.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_qrsp_two_term` (computation): For a datum with both terms discrete, RΓ_syn has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_completed_agrees` (compatibility): If the completion maps on Fil^n and on Δ{n} are isomorphisms, the completed and uncompleted syntomic complexes are isomorphic.
- `pr4_syntomic_cohomology_not_hodge` (non-example): Replacing the Nygaard filtration by the datum with ι = 0 changes the answer: fib(φ{n}) ≠ fib(φ{n} − ι) already for the perfectoid datum of O_C in weight 0, where the first is 0 and the second has H^0 = Z_p.

*Acceptance.*
- For R quasiregular semiperfectoid the complex is the two-term complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex.
- For R a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra it is Fil^n_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R), x ↦ φ(x)/p^n − x (BL Example 7.4.4).
- RΓ_syn(Spf Z[1/p], Z_p(n)) = 0, since the p-completion of Z[1/p] is 0.
- For 𝔛 = Spf R the limit definition returns RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).

### `PR.4/prismatic-logarithm` — The prismatic logarithm

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a prism with Breuil–Kisin twist A{1} (PR.3) and (1 + I)_{rk=1} := {u ∈ 1 + I : δ(u) = 0} the group of rank-one units congruent to 1 modulo I. If (A, I) is transversal, A{1} = lim_r I_r/I_r^2 with I_r = I φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^{r−1})^*(I) and transition maps division by p, and for u ∈ (1 + I)_{rk=1} the element log_Δ(u) ∈ A{1} is the unique element with image u^{p^r} − 1 in I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}^2 for all r ≥ 0. For a general prism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} is the unique function compatible with every map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) from a transversal prism. It is a group homomorphism, natural in the prism, satisfies φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u), and log_Δ(u) ≡ (u − 1 mod I^2) under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2. For Ā = A/I the Tate module T_p(Ā^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(Ā), x ↦ x^p) maps to (1 + I)_{rk=1} by ρ_0 (lift x ∈ Ā^{♭×} uniquely to A^{♭×} and apply ♯), and the composite log_Δ : T_p(Ā^×) → A{1} is also called the prismatic logarithm. For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)) there is a unique generator e_A of A{1} with (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p). For a crystalline prism (A, (p)) and u with φ(u) = u^p, u^p ≡ 1 mod p: log_Δ(u^p) = log(u) e_A with log(u) = Σ_{n>0} (−1)^{n−1}(u − 1)^n/n.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is a prism; for the Tate-module form A/I is its reduction. Transversal means A/I is p-torsion-free (so (p, I) is regular locally).
- Rank one means δ(u) = 0, equivalently φ(u) = u^p when A is p-torsion-free.
- The construction is algebraic; no K-theory or cyclotomic trace enters (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5 describes the earlier trace-theoretic construction of the comparison for Z_p(1), which this replaces).
- Ownership: the twist A{1} is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist; the logarithm is planned here because its consumers are the Tate twists of this stage.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Transversal case (BL Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2): u^{p^r} ≡ 1 mod I_{r+1} because u^{p^r} = φ^s(u^{p^{r−s}}), and division by p carries the class of u^{p^r} − 1 to that of u^{p^{r−1}} − 1, since x^p − 1 ≡ p(x − 1) mod I_r^2 for x = u^{p^{r−1}}; additivity because (u^{p^r} − 1)(v^{p^r} − 1) ∈ I_{r+1}^2 (Proposition 2.3.3).
2. General prisms (BL Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, Remark 2.5.17): every prism receives a map from a transversal prism through which given rank-one units lift (Lemmas 2.5.13, 2.5.15), and A{1} is the limit of the twists of transversal prisms over A (Proposition 2.5.1); define log_Δ by compatibility and deduce additivity, functoriality, Frobenius invariance (2.5.18) and the normalisation modulo I (2.5.19).
3. Tate modules (BL Notation 2.7.1, Propositions 2.7.2, 2.7.3, Construction 2.7.4): A^{♭×} → (A/I)^{♭×} is an isomorphism because the groups I^n/I^{n+1} are p-complete, and ♯ of an element of A^♭ has rank one.
4. Examples: q-de Rham prism (BL Proposition 2.6.1: [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q mod I_r^2 and (q − 1)[p^r]_q = q^{p^r} − 1) and crystalline prisms (BL Corollary 2.6.12), proved directly: for a crystalline prism I_r = (p^r), A{1} = lim (p^r)/(p^{2r}) with e_A the class of p^r, and u − 1 has divided powers because φ(u) = u^p ≡ 1 mod p; hence u^{p^m} = exp(p^m log u) ≡ 1 + p^m log(u) modulo p^{2m}, the terms p^{km}(log u)^k/k! for k ≥ 2 being divisible by p^{2m}; so the class of (u^p)^{p^r} − 1 in (p^{r+1})/(p^{2r+2}) is log(u)·p^{r+1}, that is log_Δ(u^p) = log(u)e_A. This avoids the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie Notation 7.5.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6: defines the syntomic first Chern class T_p(R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings
- Bhatt–Lurie Lemma 8.3.2, Proposition 8.3.3, Theorem 8.5.1: multiplication by log_Δ(ε) relates syntomic complexes of consecutive weights and is inverted to reach étale cohomology
- Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4 (through Remark 9.5): gives the comparison map α_1 : Z_p(1)(R) → RΓ(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) without the cyclotomic trace
- Bhatt–Mathew Section 1.1: the bottom map of the fibre square defining Z/p^n(i) of a ring comes from the prismatic logarithm

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.rankOneUnits` (data): The subgroup (1 + I)_{rk=1} of A^× of units u ≡ 1 mod I with δ(u) = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog` (constructor): The group homomorphism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_frobenius` (relation): φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_map` (functoriality): For a map of prisms f : (B, J) → (A, I): f{1}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(f(u)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_mod` (characterisation): log_Δ(u) reduces to the class of u − 1 under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.tateModule` (data): T_p(R^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(R), x ↦ x^p), the kernel of ♯ : R^{♭×} → R^×.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.tateLog` (constructor): The composite T_p((A/I)^×) → (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr4_prismatic_log_one` (degenerate): log_Δ(1) = 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_q_de_rham` (computation): In the q-de Rham prism, log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A for a generator e_A of A{1}; in particular log_Δ(q^p) ≠ 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_mul` (characterisation): log_Δ(u v) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v) and log_Δ(u^p) = p log_Δ(u).
- `pr4_prismatic_log_not_all_units` (non-example): In the q-de Rham prism the unit 1 + [p]_q lies in 1 + I but has δ ≠ 0, so it is not a rank-one unit and lies outside the domain of log_Δ.

*Acceptance.*
- q-de Rham prism: log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A with e_A a generator of A{1}.
- Perfected q-de Rham prism: for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ T_p((A/I)^×), ρ_0(ε) = q^p and log_Δ(ε) = (q − 1) e_A.
- log_Δ(1) = 0 and log_Δ(uv) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v).
- log_Δ is not defined on units of rank ≠ 1: for u ∈ 1 + I with δ(u) ≠ 0 the classes u^{p^r} − 1 need not lie in I_{r+1}.

- BL22, Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2, Proposition 2.3.3 (transversal case); Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, 2.5.18, 2.5.19 and Remark 2.5.17 (general prisms): “Then there is a unique function” (construction of the logarithm on rank-one units, with its additivity, functoriality, Frobenius invariance and normalisation)

### `PR.4/syntomic-low-weights` — Syntomic complexes in weights n < 0, n = 0 and n = 1

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) For n > 0, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(−n)) = 0. (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects α_R : RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p), characterised by functoriality in R, and it is an isomorphism when R is p-complete; here RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = lim_k RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p^k). If moreover R is a p-complete ring with x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, then RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ring of continuous Z_p-valued functions on Spec R. (3) There is a canonical map c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), functorial in R and given, for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, in degree 0 by T_p(R^×) → T_p(Δ̄_R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), the second map being the prismatic logarithm; for R p-complete the induced map RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) from the p-completion is an isomorphism. (4) Consequently, for a quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1], and the natural map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Z_p(1)(R), where Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] and (−)^∧ is derived p-completion, is an isomorphism on H^i for i ≤ 1 and injective on H^2; it is an isomorphism if and only if (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0, which holds for perfectoid R and fails for R = F_p(t) (H^2 of the target is T_p Br(R) ≠ 0). This corrects Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6, which asserts the isomorphism for every quasisyntomic ring; Z_p(1) is, locally for the quasisyntomic topology, the sheaf R ↦ T_p(R^×) = lim_n μ_{p^n}(R) in degree 0; and for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R the sequence 0 → T_p(R^×) → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 (maps log[·] and φ/p − 1) is exact.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (1); p-complete in the isomorphism statements of (2) and (3); quasisyntomic in (4).
- Étale cohomology with Z_p-coefficients is the derived inverse limit of Z/p^k-cohomology; G_m-cohomology is étale (for (4), flat cohomology gives the same τ^{≤1}).
- These statements replace BMS2 Propositions 7.16 and 7.17, whose proofs use K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow; the proofs planned here are Bhatt–Lurie's and use no K-theory, TC or trace (requirement of the BMS2 route).
- In (2) the comparison is with étale cohomology of Spec R (equivalently of Spec R/p), not of the generic fibre Spec R[1/p].

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) (BL Corollary 7.4.9): by sifted colimits and descent reduce to R quasiregular semiperfectoid, where with a generator e of A{−n}, φ{−n}(e) = λe with λ ∈ I^n, the complex is A → A, x ↦ x − λφ(x), whose differential has the convergent inverse x ↦ x + λφ(x) + λφ(λ)φ^2(x) + ⋯.
2. (2) (BL Proposition 8.1.8, Theorem 8.1.9, Corollary 8.1.10): α_R exists by the universal property of RΓ_ét(Spec −, Z_p) among étale sheaves of algebras; by derived descent modulo p (7.4.10 and Gabber's affine proper base change) reduce to animated F_p-algebras, by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗ Δ_R ≃ dR_{R/F_p} and φ − 1 is an automorphism of Fil^1_Hodge = (Ω^{≥1}, d) since Frobenius vanishes on it; the remaining map is the Artin–Schreier isomorphism.
3. (3) (BL Theorem 7.1.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6): construct c_1^syn on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings from PR.4/prismatic-logarithm (its image is φ{1}-fixed and lies in Fil^1_N) and extend by descent and Kan extension; to prove the isomorphism reduce modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then to quasisyntomic F_p-algebras, where it is the crystalline first Chern class isomorphism (BL Theorem 7.3.5), proved from the logarithm sequence 0 → (1 + J)^× → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 for quasiregular semiperfect R; surjectivity of φ/p − 1 there is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective with i = 1.
4. (4) (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6): Pic(−) is a quasisyntomic sheaf locally concentrated in degree −1 (rings without non-trivial line bundles form a basis), units are p-divisible locally, so the sheaf of complexes associated with R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is locally T_p(R^×), which is Z_p(1) by (3); the presheaf R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is itself not a sheaf of complexes, and the comparison map has cofibre (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧[−1] ∈ D^{≥2}. For perfectoid R this cofibre vanishes because Z_p(1)(R) ∈ D^{[0,1]} (PR.4/syntomic-complex). The exact sequence is BL Example 7.4.5.

*Acceptance.*
- Z_p(0)(O_C) = Z_p in degree 0; Z_p(0)(F_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec F_p, Z_p) has H^1 = Z_p.
- Z_p(1)(O_C) = T_p(O_C^×) = Z_p(1) in degree 0, since O_C^× is p-divisible and Pic(O_C) = 0.
- Z_p(1)(Z_p) has H^1 = (Z_p^×)^∧ = 1 + pZ_p for p odd and H^0 = T_p(Z_p^×) = 0.
- Z_p(−1)(R) = 0 for every R.

### `PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction` — The divided Frobenius contracts deep Nygaard levels modulo p

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and A a p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebra; fix i ≥ 0. For every integer m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), both φ_i and the canonical map preserve N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p functorially in A, and φ_i − 1 : N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p → N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p is an equivalence; more precisely φ_i maps N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p into N^{≥m+1}Δ̂_A{i}/p. Consequently Z/p(i)(A) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) → (Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p)), and, for quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebras S, Z_p(i)(S) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S) computed without Nygaard completion and without twists.

*Hypotheses.*
- C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0; over O_C the Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised.
- A is p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic over O_C; by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion the endomorphism φ_i of N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p and the equivalence extend to every quasisyntomic O_C-algebra.
- m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), which is the condition p(m − i) ≥ m + 1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By quasisyntomic descent assume A quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free; then all N^kΔ̂_A/p are discrete, so N^{≥k}Δ̂_A/p is discrete and ξ-torsion-free, and φ_i is induced by ξ̃^{−i}φ on Δ̂_A[1/ξ̃], ξ̃ = φ(ξ) (BMS2 proof of Lemma 7.22).
2. φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A) ⊂ ξ̃^{m−i}Δ̂_A for m ≥ i; modulo p, ξ̃ ≡ ξ^p, so φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A/p) ⊂ ξ^{p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p ⊂ N^{≥p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p because ξ^kΔ̂_A ⊂ N^{≥k}Δ̂_A.
3. For p(m − i) ≥ m + 1 this gives φ_i(N^{≥m}/p) ⊂ N^{≥m+1}/p: φ_i is topologically nilpotent for the complete Nygaard filtration, so φ_i − 1 is an automorphism.
4. The consequences follow by comparing the fibres of φ_i − 1 on N^{≥i} → Δ̂ and on the quotients by N^{≥m}; for the uncompleted form use that the divided Frobenius of the completion factors through Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-completion (b)): the cofibres of Fil^i_N Δ_S → N^{≥i}Δ̂_S and of Δ_S → Δ̂_S agree, φ_i induces 0 between them and the canonical map the identity, so the two fibres of φ_i − 1 agree (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6); this holds for every quasiregular semiperfectoid ring.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: every m ≥ 1 works when p ≥ 2, and φ maps N^{≥m}/p into N^{≥pm}/p.
- i = 1, p = 2: m ≥ 3; i = 1, p odd: m ≥ 2.
- A = O_C, i = 1: N^{≥m}A_inf/p = ξ^m O_C^♭ and φ_1(ξ^m x) = ξ^{p(m−1)} x^p, which lies in ξ^{m+1}O_C^♭ exactly when p(m − 1) ≥ m + 1.

- BS22-v4, Proof of Theorem 14.1, first paragraph: “the Breuil-Kisin twists and the Nygaard completion may be ignored whilst calculating” (the consequence for quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebras used in the proof of discreteness)

### `PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits` — Z/p^r(i) commutes with filtered colimits

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits` · theorem · part PR.0.

For all i ≥ 0 and r ≥ 1 the sheaf Z/p^r(i) = Z_p(i)/p^r commutes with filtered colimits in the category QSyn of quasisyntomic rings: for a filtered diagram (A_j) of quasisyntomic rings whose p-completed colimit A is quasisyntomic, colim_j Z/p^r(i)(A_j) → Z/p^r(i)(A) is an isomorphism.

*Hypotheses.*
- Colimits of rings are p-completed colimits; the statement is about the reduction modulo p^r, not about Z_p(i) itself.
- The proof planned is the direct proof of BMS2 through Lemma 7.22; the first printed proof, through K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, is not used (no trace input may enter PR.4).
- i ≥ 0; for i < 0 both sides vanish.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Induct on r to reduce to r = 1, using the fibre sequences Z/p^{r−1}(i) → Z/p^r(i) → Z/p(i).
2. Fix C = Q_p^cycl completed; by quasisyntomic descent along A → A ⊗̂ O_C and its Čech nerve (functorial quasisyntomic covers) assume the A_j are O_C-algebras.
3. For p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebras, PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction lets one compute Z/p(i)(A) modulo N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p for m large, and (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) is a finite extension of Nygaard graded pieces, which commute with filtered colimits (they are built from wedge powers of the cotangent complex, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces).
4. For arbitrary quasisyntomic O_C-algebras define φ_i on N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion; φ_i − 1 is still an equivalence and the same argument applies (BMS2, direct proof of Proposition 7.21). The statement for all animated rings is BL Proposition 7.4.8.

*Acceptance.*
- O_C = colim of the rings of integers of finite extensions, p-completed: Z/p^r(i)(O_C) is the colimit of the complexes of the p-completed finite levels.
- A filtered colimit of perfectoid rings: Z/p^r(i) of the p-completed colimit is the colimit, as used in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4.
- The statement fails for Z_p(i) without reduction: Z_p(0) of a filtered colimit is p-complete, the colimit of Z_p(0) need not be.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`, `PR.4/syntomic-connectivity`.

*Sources.*
- BMS2, Proposition 7.21, direct proof: “is more elementary and self-contained, relying ultimately on the contracting property of the Frobenius in characteristic” (statement of the proposition and its second (direct) proof, the one planned)
- BL22, Proposition 7.4.8: “commutes with sifted colimits (and is therefore a left Kan extension of its restriction to the category” (the stronger statement for all animated rings, by the same contraction argument)

### `PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid` — p-adic Tate twists of perfectoid rings and étale cohomology of the generic fibre

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let R be a perfectoid ring. For every integer n ≥ 1 there is a canonical identification Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), where the right-hand side is the derived limit over k of RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}). For n = 0 there are canonical identifications Z_p(0)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec((R/p)_perf), Z_p). The identifications are multiplicative in n, natural in R, and for n = 1 the map is the Kummer map T_p-completion of units: on a p-complete, p-torsion-free rank-one valuation ring V with algebraically closed fraction field C it is T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)). Moreover, as presheaves on perfectoid rings both sides are, p-completely arc-locally, concentrated in degree 0 and p-torsion-free, and the multiplication Z_p(1)^{⊗̂n} → Z_p(n) exhibits the target as the p-complete arc-sheafification of the source.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is an arbitrary perfectoid ring; for n ≥ 1 both sides vanish on rings of characteristic p.
- For n ≥ 1 the comparison is with the generic fibre Spec R[1/p]; for n = 0 with Spec R, equivalently with the special fibre. The two cases are different statements.
- The comparison map for n = 1 is constructed from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), not from the cyclotomic trace; with this input the proof is purely algebraic (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5).
- Two slips in the printed proof are in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E18: (∗_b) concerns (G_1/p)^{⊗n} → G_n/p, and 'stacks' reads 'stalks'.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. n = 0: PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d and R lim give Z_p(0)(R) = fib(φ − 1 on A_inf(R)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p); Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change passes to R/p and then to its perfection.
2. Over Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebras, with q = [ε], d = [p]_q, μ = q − 1: multiplication by μ^{−n} gives α'_n : F_n(R)/p = (d^{n/p}R^♭ → R^♭, φ/d^n − 1) → G_n(R)/p = (R^♭[1/d] → R^♭[1/d], φ − 1), where G_n/p is identified by PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt; α'_n is the colimit of maps homotopic to isomorphisms induced by φ, hence a quasi-isomorphism, and is multiplicative in n.
3. (∗): F_n and G_n are p-complete arc-sheaves on perfectoid rings (arc-descent, BS22 §8.2 and Bhatt–Mathew), arc-locally discrete and p-torsion-free, and F_1^{⊗̂n} → F_n, G_1^{⊗̂n} → G_n are arc-sheafifications: checked for G_n/p on products of p-complete valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, using that G_n(−)/p turns p-completed filtered colimits into filtered colimits (Fujiwara–Gabber) and that stalks are absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.
4. Construct α_1 : F_1 → G_1 from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} and Kummer theory; it is an isomorphism because, arc-locally on V as in the statement, T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) is an isomorphism (C^×/V^× is uniquely p-divisible) and T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)) is an isomorphism (H^1(Spec C, G_m) = 0). By (∗), α_1 induces a multiplicative system of isomorphisms α_n.

*Acceptance.*
- R = O_C: Z_p(n)(O_C) ≃ Z_p(n) in degree 0, a free Z_p-module of rank one, for every n ≥ 0.
- R perfect of characteristic p and n ≥ 1: Z_p(n)(R) = 0; for n = 0, Z_p(0)(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = W(R)^{F=1} derived.
- R = Z_p^cycl: H^1(Z_p(n)(R)) = H^1(Gal of the completed cyclotomic field, Z_p(n)), non-zero.
- Finite level: Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}(C), and the maps for k → k − 1 are the reduction maps.

### `PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible` — Picard groups of perfectoid rings are uniquely p-divisible

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible` · application · part PR.0.

For a perfectoid ring R the groups Pic(R) and Pic(R[1/p]) are uniquely p-divisible. Moreover the canonical map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] of p-completed Picard groupoids is an isomorphism, compatible with Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) (PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid) and the Kummer map Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)).

*Hypotheses.*
- R is any perfectoid ring.
- Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] denotes the Picard groupoid as an object of D(Z); Pic(R) with roman type is its H^0, the Picard group.
- Cohomology of G_m is computed in the flat topology (equivalently étale).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Pic(R) ≅ Pic(A_inf(R)) ≅ Pic(R^♭) by deformation theory along the (p, d)-adically complete ring A_inf(R), and the Picard group of a perfect ring is uniquely p-divisible (Frobenius is an automorphism inducing multiplication by p).
2. In the square with a : Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (valid for perfectoid R: Z_p(1)(R) = RΓ(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1, so (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0), c : Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)), b the canonical map and d the Kummer map, commutativity is checked by p-complete arc-descent on R = O_C; d[1] is the p-completion of τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m) → RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m), hence injective on cohomology, so b and d are isomorphisms.
3. Reduce b modulo p: H^0 gives Pic(R[1/p])/p ≅ Pic(R)/p = 0, and H^{−1} with the Bockstein sequences gives a surjection Pic(R)[p] → Pic(R[1/p])[p], whose source is 0.

*Acceptance.*
- R = O_C: Pic(O_C) = 0 and Pic(C) = 0.
- R perfect of characteristic p: R[1/p] = 0 and Pic(R) is uniquely p-divisible because Frobenius acts as an automorphism and as multiplication by p.
- Consequence used in Theorem 14.1: H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^×.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `mathlib:CommRing.Pic`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.4/tate-twist-discreteness`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Corollary 9.7 and its proof: “as any perfect ring has a uniquely” (statement and proof; the two inputs are Theorem 9.4 and Lemma 9.6)

### `PR.4/tate-twist-discreteness` — Z_p(n) is discrete and p-torsion-free ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twist-discreteness` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Discreteness of the Tate twists Z_p(n)**.

For each n ≥ 0 the sheaf of complexes Z_p(n) on the quasisyntomic site is discrete and p-torsion-free: for every quasisyntomic ring S, H^0(Z_p(n)(−)) is a sheaf of p-torsion-free abelian groups, and every class in H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) vanishes on some quasisyntomic cover S → S' (so the quasisyntomic sheafification of H^1(Z_p(n)(−)) is 0, and H^i(Z_p(n)(−)) = 0 locally for i ≠ 0). Hence Z_p(n)(S) = RΓ(S_qsyn, H^0(Z_p(n))) is the cohomology of a sheaf of p-torsion-free groups. Two lemmas of the proof: (Lemma 14.4) for a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra R, R' = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R'/(X_1, …, X_r), the map Z_p(n)(R') → Z_p(n)(S) is surjective on H^1; (Lemma 14.5) for a perfectoid ring R and a surjection S' → S of quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras such that the p-completion of L_{S'/R} → L_{S/R} is surjective on H^{−1}, the map Δ_{S'} → Δ_S is surjective.

*Hypotheses.*
- The statement is local: discreteness means vanishing of H^1 after quasisyntomic sheafification; Z_p(n)(S) itself can have H^1 ≠ 0 (already Z_p(0)(F_p)).
- n ≥ 0; for n < 0 the sheaf is 0.
- This is Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2. Its K-theoretic consequences, Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 of Bhatt–Scholze (evenness of K(−; Z_p) locally and for regular quotients), need K(−; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(−; Z_p) on henselian pairs and belong to the proposed roadmap RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs; they are not planned here.
- In the printed proof 'C/Q' reads 'C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed' (register PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E30).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. p-torsion-freeness of H^0: for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ_S is a d-torsion-free δ-ring; if x ∈ H^0 has px = 0 then φ(x) = 0, so d^n x = d^n φ_n(x) = φ(x) = 0 and x = 0 (BMS2 Remark 7.20; by PR.3/nygaard-completion (b) a class of H^0 is the image of an element of Fil^n_N Δ_S, so the argument takes place in the δ-ring Δ_S). It remains to prove (∗)_S: every α ∈ H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) dies on a quasisyntomic cover, for S quasiregular semiperfectoid over O_C, where Z_p(n)(S) = fib(1 − φ_n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ_S) (PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction).
2. Perfectoid S = R: for n = 0 use PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid and Artin–Schreier covers; for n > 0 reduce to n = 1 by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid, where H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^× (PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible), and André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3) gives a cover R → R' with (R')^× p-divisible.
3. S_0 = R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩/(x_i): Lemma 14.4 reduces (∗)_{S_0} to the perfectoid ring R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩. Proof of 14.4: with A = A_inf(R), D = Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R'){X_i^p/[p]_q}^∧ has a completed N[1/p]^r-grading with basis X^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!, Fil^n_N D is described termwise by powers of [p]_{q^{1/p}}, φ_n − 1 is surjective on the part of total integral degree ≥ n + 1 (φ_n is contracting there), φ_n divides degrees by p on the rest, and in degrees with all i_j < 1 the map A_inf(R') → D is bijective.
4. General S = R'/I: by André's lemma assume generators x_t of I have compatible p-power roots, map S' = (R'[x_t^{1/p^∞}]/(x_t))^∧ onto S; the map on p-completed cotangent complexes is surjective on H^{−1}, so Δ_{S'} → Δ_S and then H^1(Z_p(n)(S')) → H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) are surjective (Lemma 14.5, from the Hodge–Tate comparison PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison); filter the index set by finite subsets to reduce to S_0.

*Acceptance.*
- n = 0: Z_p(0) is the constant sheaf lim Z/p^r, and H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) = Z_p dies on the cover F_p → algebraic closure.
- n = 1: Z_p(1) = T_p G_m, and a class in H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) = (R^×)^∧ dies after adjoining p-power roots of units.
- S = O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X): H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) is a quotient of H^1(Z_p(n)(O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩)) by Lemma 14.4.
- In characteristic p the statement is PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p.

### `PR.4/syntomic-connectivity` — Connectivity, rigidity and left Kan extension of syntomic complexes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-connectivity` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let i ≥ 0. (1) The functor R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(i)) on animated rings commutes with sifted colimits and is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras; on quasisyntomic rings Z_p(i) is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras. (2) For every quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i+1}(Z_p). (3) (Rigidity) For a henselian pair (R, I) with R and R/I p-complete, fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤ i}(Z_p). (4) For a p-complete ring R, H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) ≅ coker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R/p} → Ω^i_{R/p}/dΩ^{i−1}_{R/p}); it vanishes when R is w-strictly local, in particular strictly henselian local. (5) Consequently, for every scheme X the étale sheaf of complexes Z/p^n(i)_X obtained by restricting syntomic cohomology (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes) to the small étale site lies in D^{[0, i]}(X_ét, Z/p^n), and Z/p^n(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i} for R strictly henselian local.

*Hypotheses.*
- Statements (2)–(4) are Theorems 5.1, 5.2 and Corollary 5.43 of Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, as used by Bhatt–Mathew (routed item PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-23/009).
- In (3) both R and R/I are p-complete and (R, I) is henselian.
- The printed proofs of (2)–(4) describe Nygaard graded pieces as gr^n THH and use THH of graded rings; no trace-theoretic object may enter PR.4, so the plan replaces each such description by its prismatic counterpart and records the remaining step as a gap.
- (5) uses that the generic-fibre part of Z/p^n(i)_X is μ_{p^n}^{⊗i} in degree 0 and that stalks at characteristic-p points are computed on strictly henselian local rings by PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): BL Proposition 7.4.8 (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes (d)); AMMN Theorem 5.1(2).
2. (2): the cofibre of N^{≥i+1}Δ_R{i} → N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} is N^iΔ_R{i} ∈ D^{≤ i} (BL Proposition 5.5.19, from the fibre sequence for Nygaard graded pieces of Remark 5.5.8; PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration); modulo p, can and φ_i on N^{≥i+1}Δ_R{i}/p respect the I-adic filtrations and φ_i is zero on graded pieces, so by the connectivity lemma fib(can − φ_i) ∈ D^{≤ i+1} (AMMN Lemma 5.34, Proposition 5.35), first for p-complete polynomial algebras and then by (1).
3. (3): continuity Z_p(i)(R) ≃ lim_s Z_p(i)(R/I^s) for noetherian F-finite I-adically complete R, Néron–Popescu and left Kan extension reduce to trivial square-zero extensions A ⊕ N of p-completed polynomial algebras, where the internal grading by the weight of N and 'Frobenius multiplies the grading by p' give pro-nilpotence (AMMN Propositions 5.36, 5.38, 5.41; Bhatt–Mathew Remark 3.8 for the gradings in prismatic terms).
4. (4): by (3) reduce to F_p-algebras and then to ind-smooth ones, where F_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_R → Ω^i_R/dΩ^{i−1}_R)[−i] by PR.4/log-de-rham-witt-comparison reduced modulo p and the sequence 0 → Ω^i_log → Ω^i → Ω^i/dΩ^{i−1} → 0.
5. (5): combine (2), (4), the fibre square of PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes and Bhatt–Mathew §1.2.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: Z/p^n(0)_X = Z/p^n in degree 0.
- i = 1: Z/p^n(1)_X = fib(p^n : G_m → G_m) on X_ét, in degrees [0, 1].
- R = Z_p, i = 1: Z_p(1)(Z_p) = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1] ∈ D^{≤ 2}; the fibre to Z_p(1)(F_p) = 0 is in D^{≤ 1}.
- R strictly henselian local: H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) = 0.

### `PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius` — Logarithmic forms as fixed points of the divided Frobenius on the de Rham–Witt complex

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and X a smooth k-scheme, with de Rham–Witt complex WΩ^•_X and Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X ⊂ WΩ^•_X, the subcomplex p^{i−1}VW(O_X) → p^{i−2}VWΩ^1_X → ⋯ → VWΩ^{i−1}_X → WΩ^i_X → WΩ^{i+1}_X → ⋯, on which the Frobenius φ is uniquely divisible by p^i; write φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X. Let W_rΩ^i_{X,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^i_X be the image of dlog[·] : G_m^{⊗i} → W_rΩ^i_X and WΩ^i_{X,log} = lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}, as pro-étale sheaves. Then for every i ≥ 0 the sequence of complexes of pro-étale sheaves 0 → WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] → N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X → 0, with second map φ_i − 1, is exact in each degree, and WΩ^i_{X,log} = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}.

*Hypotheses.*
- k is a perfect field of characteristic p and X is smooth over k.
- Exactness is degreewise and holds for sheaves on the pro-étale site of X; surjectivity of F − 1 in degree i holds only locally.
- The objects N^{≥i}WΩ and WΩ_log are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4; this node is the statement about φ_i − 1 that the syntomic comparison needs (link CR.4 → PR.4).
- In the printed proof the boundary case reads 'i = n − 1'; it is n = i − 1 (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E7).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Degrees n > i: φ_i − 1 = p^{n−i}F − 1 on WΩ^n_A, an isomorphism because p^{n−i}F is p-adically contracting and WΩ^n_A is p-adically complete.
2. Degrees n < i: N^{≥i}WΩ^n_A = p^{i−1−n}V WΩ^n_A and (φ_i − 1) ∘ p^{i−1−n}V = 1 − p^{i−1−n}V on WΩ^n_A (using FV = p and φ = p^n F), an isomorphism by p-adic completeness, and by V-adic completeness in the boundary case n = i − 1.
3. Degree n = i: φ_i − 1 = F − 1 on WΩ^i_X; the sequence of pro-sheaves 0 → {W_nΩ^i_{X,log}} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → 0 with F − 1 is exact on X_ét [Illusie, Complexe de de Rham–Witt et cohomologie cristalline, Théorème I.5.7.2]; passing to the inverse limit gives exactness on the pro-étale site and WΩ^i_log = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_log.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: 0 → Z_p → W(O_X) → W(O_X) → 0 with F − 1, the Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence on the pro-étale site.
- i = 1, X = G_m: dlog[T] ∈ WΩ^1 is fixed by F, since F(dlog[T]) = dlog[T].
- X = Spec k, i ≥ 1: N^{≥i}W(k) = p^{i−1}VW(k) = p^iW(k) and (φ_i − 1)(p^i x) = F(x) − p^i x is bijective onto W(k), so WΩ^i_{k,log} = 0 and the cokernel vanishes.

### `PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective` — Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 on the Nygaard pieces of Â_crys

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, A_crys(S) the p-completed divided power envelope of W(S^♭) → S, with Frobenius φ, Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^i A_crys(S)}, Nygaard completion Â_crys(S) and divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S). (1) For every i > 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S) is surjective. (2) For every i ≥ 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(−) → Â_crys(−) is surjective as a map of sheaves on the site of quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras with the quasisyntomic topology.

*Hypotheses.*
- S is quasiregular semiperfect: Frobenius is surjective on S and L_{S/F_p} is a flat S-module placed in degree −1.
- In (1) i > 0 is necessary: for i = 0 and S = F_p the map φ − 1 on Z_p is zero.
- The inputs on A_crys(S) are BMS2 Theorem 8.14 (p-torsion-freeness; φ_i mod p identifies N^iA_crys(S) with Fil_i^conj(A_crys(S)/p); the image of N^{≥i} modulo p is the divided power filtration Fil^i_pd, the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology), owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): by p-completeness it suffices to prove surjectivity modulo p. On N^{≥i+1}Â_crys(S), φ_i is divisible by p, so φ_i − 1 is minus the canonical map and its image modulo p contains the image Fil^{i+1}_pd of N^{≥i+1} (Theorem 8.14(4)).
2. On pN^{≥i−1}Â_crys(S), φ_i − 1 agrees modulo p with φ_{i−1}, whose image modulo p is Fil^conj_{i−1}(Â_crys(S)/p) (Theorem 8.14(2)).
3. For j ≥ 1, Fil^conj_{j−1} + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p, since Fil^conj_{j−1} is generated by divided power monomials of total degree < pj and Fil^{pj}_pd by those of degree ≥ pj; with j = i and pi ≥ i + 1 this gives (1).
4. (2): for i = 0, part (1)'s argument shows the image of φ − 1 modulo p contains Fil^1_pd, and Â_crys(S) → S composed with φ − 1 is surjective on a tower of Artin–Schreier covers, which is a quasisyntomic cover; conclude by p-adic completeness.

*Acceptance.*
- S perfect, i ≥ 1: A_crys(S) = W(S), N^{≥i} = p^iW(S), φ_i − 1 = (F − p^i)/p^i, surjective because F is bijective and p^iF^{−1} is contracting.
- S = F_p, i = 0: φ − 1 = 0 on Z_p is not surjective, but becomes surjective on W of an algebraic closure.
- S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), i = 1: the class of the divided power γ_p(x) is hit, since it lies in Fil^p_pd.

*Depends on:* `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-filtration`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p`.

*Sources.*
- BMS2, Lemma 8.19 and its proof: “is surjective as a map of sheaves on” (statement and proof; the identity Fil_{j−1}^conj + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p is checked from the definitions of the two filtrations)

### `PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p` — Syntomic complexes of quasiregular semiperfect rings

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra. There is a φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ_S ≅ A_crys(S) identifying the Nygaard filtration of Δ_S with N^{≥•}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^• A_crys(S)}, and Z_p(i)(S) is represented by the two-term complex N^{≥i}A_crys(S) → A_crys(S), x ↦ φ(x)/p^i − x (equivalently by its Nygaard-completed version). For i > 0 the complex Z_p(i)(S) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the p-torsion-free group A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}. For i = 0, H^0(Z_p(0)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=1} is p-torsion-free and H^1(Z_p(0)(S)) = coker(φ − 1) vanishes after sheafification on quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras. In particular Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2 holds in characteristic p. By quasisyntomic descent, for every quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a fibre sequence RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i)) → Fil^i_N RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) with second map φ/p^i − 1, and after inverting p, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i))[1/p] ≃ fib(φ − p^i on RΓ_crys(X/Z_p)[1/p]).

*Hypotheses.*
- S is a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra; X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme.
- Δ̂_S and its Nygaard filtration are identified with Â_crys(S) through the prismatic crystalline comparison and the Nygaard theory of PR.1–PR.3 (Bhatt–Lurie Example 7.4.4; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2), not through BMS2 Theorem 8.17, which is a statement about TC^− owned by RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.
- The printed Proposition 8.20 asserts concentration in degree 0 for all i ≥ 0 and every S; for i = 0 this holds only after sheafification (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E41: Z_p(0)(F_p) has H^1 = Z_p). The statement above is the corrected one.
- The exact sequence 0 → π_{2i}TC → π_{2i}TC^− → π_{2i}TP → 0 of the same passage belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.
- The filtration on crystalline cohomology is the Nygaard filtration, not the Hodge filtration; after inverting p it becomes trivial.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Identify (Δ_S, φ, Fil_N) with (A_crys(S), φ, N^{≥•}): Δ_S, the initial prism of S, is a crystalline prism, and the crystalline comparison identifies it φ-equivariantly with the p-completed divided power envelope A_crys(S) of W(S^♭) → S (PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys (2), PR.2/qrsp-prism, CR.0; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2); both Nygaard filtrations are defined by divisibility of φ by powers of the generator p (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp).
2. Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 for i > 0 on the completed complex is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (1); p-torsion-freeness of N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) follows from that of A_crys(S) (BMS2 Theorem 8.14(1), DD.4) and the definition of the Nygaard filtration.
3. The map α from ker(φ_i − 1) on N^{≥i}A_crys(S) to the kernel on the completion is an isomorphism: the Frobenius of A_crys(S) factors through the Nygaard completion, which gives β : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → A_crys(S) with β ∘ α = φ_i and α ∘ β = φ_i; so α(x) = 0 and φ_i(x) = x give x = β(α(x)) = 0, and for y in the completed kernel x = β(y) maps to y and satisfies φ(x) = p^i x. The uncompleted kernel is A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i} by definition of the filtration.
4. i = 0: PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (2). Globalisation: quasisyntomic descent for crystalline cohomology and its Nygaard filtration (BL Theorem 4.6.1, Notation 5.3.2, Proposition 5.3.6) and PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes; Fil^i_N ⊗ Q is everything since p^i lies in Fil^i_N.

*Acceptance.*
- S perfect: Z_p(i)(S) = W(S)^{F=p^i} = 0 for i > 0, and Z_p(0)(S) = fib(F − 1 on W(S)).
- S = O_C/p: H^0(Z_p(i)(S)) = A_crys^{φ=p^i} contains t^i for t = log[ε], since φ(t) = pt; after inverting p these are the graded pieces of the ring of the Fargues–Fontaine curve.
- S = F_p, i = 0: H^1 = Z_p ≠ 0, the counterexample to the uncorrected statement.
- i = 1: A_crys(S)^{φ=p} ≅ T_p(S^×) via x ↦ log[x] (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).

### `PR.4/log-de-rham-witt-comparison` — Syntomic complexes of smooth algebras in characteristic p are logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/log-de-rham-witt-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparison**.

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A a smooth k-algebra and X = Spec A. Let λ : qSyn_A^op → X_proét be the natural map from the (opposite of the) quasisyntomic site of A to the pro-étale site of X. Then for all i ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] of sheaves of complexes on X_proét. Reducing modulo p^r: Rλ_* Z/p^r(i) ≃ W_rΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] on X_ét.

*Hypotheses.*
- k is a perfect field of characteristic p and A is smooth over k (Theorem 1.15(1) of BMS2 and Corollary 8.21).
- The statement is on the pro-étale site of X because the coefficients are p-adic; WΩ^i_log is the inverse limit sheaf.
- The source deduces it from the description of gr^i TC^− and gr^i TP; the plan uses instead the identification of Rλ_* of the Nygaard-filtered prismatic sheaves with the Nygaard-filtered de Rham–Witt complex, which needs no trace-theoretic input.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Rλ_* of S ↦ (Δ_S, Fil^•_N, φ) on qSyn_A is the étale-local Nygaard-filtered absolute prismatic complex of A, which is (WΩ^•_X, N^{≥•}WΩ^•_X, φ): crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison, BL Theorem 4.6.1), the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham–Witt complex (CR.4), and the match of filtrations for regular F_p-algebras (BL Proposition 5.3.8; equivalently BMS2 Theorem 8.14(3) with quasisyntomic descent, DD.4).
2. N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X is complete for the Nygaard filtration, so the Nygaard completion changes nothing and Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X) as pro-étale sheaves of complexes.
3. PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius identifies this fibre with WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i].
4. Modulo p^r: WΩ^i_log/p^r = W_rΩ^i_log because WΩ^i_log = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_log with surjective transition maps and p-torsion-free limit.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: Rλ_* Z_p(0) = Z_p, the constant pro-étale sheaf lim Z/p^r.
- i = 1: Rλ_* Z_p(1) = WΩ^1_log[−1], matching the classical fact that the pushforward of μ_{p^n} from the flat site is W_nΩ^1_log[−1].
- A = k: Z_p(i)(k) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
- A = k[T^{±1}], i = 1: dlog[T] is a non-zero section of WΩ^1_log.

### `PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf` — Syntomic complexes of smooth formal schemes over O_C vanish above degree i

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C) with ξ a generator of ker θ, ξ̃ = φ(ξ), and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C. On 𝔛_ét the syntomic sheaf Z/p^n(i) = Z_p(i)/p^n is identified with hofib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}AΩ_𝔛{i} → AΩ_𝔛{i})/p^n, where AΩ_𝔛 is the A_inf-cohomology sheaf with its Nygaard filtration. Then this complex is concentrated in degrees ≤ i, and the natural map τ^{≤i} hofib(τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n) → hofib(N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i})/p^n (both fibres of φ_i − 1) is an equivalence of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét. In coordinates: for 𝔛 = Spf A with a framing O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → A (the p-completion of an étale map) and the induced deformation Ã over A_inf, AΩ_A = q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, N^{≥i}AΩ_A = ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, φ(d_q log T_a) = ξ̃ d_q log T_a and φ_i = ξ̃^{−i}φ.

*Hypotheses.*
- C is algebraically closed and complete (the hypothesis of Theorem 1.15(2); Section 10 itself uses the notation μ, ξ of Section 9 and does not restate it).
- 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C; the framing exists étale-locally.
- The identification of Z/p^n(i) on 𝔛_ét with the AΩ-fibre uses AΩ ≃ φ^*Δ (PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison) and the match of the Nygaard filtration with the Lη_ξ filtration (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation); the printed text cites BMS2 Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.11, obtained there through TC, which the plan does not use.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Restrict Z_p(i) to 𝔛_ét (BMS2 Remark 10.4: a quasisyntomic sheaf gives an étale sheaf on 𝔛) and identify N^{≥i}Δ̂{i} → Δ̂{i} with N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i}: PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison, PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, and PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A_inf.
2. Reduce to n = 1 and to a framed affine; write the complex as ξ̃^{−i}φ − 1 : ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^• → q-Ω^• on the basis d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_j}, on which φ acts by ξ̃^j (PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison and AI.4 for the coordinate description).
3. Degree j > i: the map is ξ̃^{j−i}φ − 1 on Ã/p, an automorphism with inverse −Σ_{r≥0} ξ̃_r^{j−i}φ^r, ξ̃_r = ξ̃φ(ξ̃)⋯φ^{r−1}(ξ̃). Degree j = i: the map is φ − 1 on Ã/p, étale-locally surjective by Artin–Schreier covers, the étale sites of 𝔛, Spf Ã/p and Spec A/p being equivalent.
4. Hence the fibre has no cohomology above degree i and is unchanged by truncating source and target at degree i.

*Acceptance.*
- i = 0: the complex is fib(φ − 1 on Ã/p^n) étale-locally, namely Z/p^n in degree 0.
- 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i) = Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0 for all i.
- 𝔛 the formal torus of dimension 1 and i = 0: the degree-1 term contributes nothing, since ξ̃φ − 1 is invertible on Ã/p.
- The basis elements d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_i} of degree i are fixed by φ_i.

### `PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition` — The condition (As) for Rν_* A_inf,X modulo p^n

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition` · lemma · part PR.0.

Setting: A is a p-power-torsion ring in a topos with an automorphism φ, and μ, ξ ∈ A are non-zero-divisors with μ = ξ φ^{−1}(μ); put ξ_r = ξ φ^{−1}(ξ) ⋯ φ^{1−r}(ξ), so μ = ξ_r φ^{−r}(μ). Let C ∈ D^{≥0}(A) with H^0(C) μ-torsion-free and a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism φ : C ≃ C. Condition (As): 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : C/μ^j C → C/μ^j C is a quasi-isomorphism for all i ≥ j ≥ 0. Claim: for a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf O_C with generic fibre X and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét, (As) holds for A = A_inf/p^n and C = Rν_* A_inf,X/p^n. More precisely 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} is an automorphism of the pro-étale sheaf A_inf,X/(p^n, μ^j) for i ≥ j ≥ 0, and 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : A_inf,X/p^n → A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i).

*Hypotheses.*
- C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ) (the standing notation of BMS2 Section 9).
- i ≥ j ≥ 0 in (As); for j = 0 the condition is empty.
- In the printed remark 'g − μ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' reads 'g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E10); the node uses the corrected computation.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reduce to n = 1 by dévissage, where A_inf,X/(p, μ^j) = Ô_X^{♭+}/μ^j.
2. Injectivity: if f ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} and f − ξ^i φ^{−1}(f) ∈ μ^j Ô_X^{♭+}, then g = f/μ^j satisfies g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g) ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} because ξ^i φ^{−1}(μ)^j = ξ^{i−j}μ^j; with h = φ^{−1}(g) this says h^p − ξ^{i−j}h ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}, so h is integral over Ô_X^{♭+}, which is integrally closed in Ô_X^♭; hence g ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}.
3. Surjectivity on Ô_X^{♭+}: by integral closedness it reduces to surjectivity of 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} on Ô_X^♭, i.e. to solving h^p − ξ^i h = f pro-étale locally; ξ is a unit of Ô_X^♭, so this is an Artin–Schreier-type finite étale equation, solvable pro-étale locally by the tilting equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
4. Kernel on A_inf,X/p^n: μ^i is fixed by ξ^i φ^{−1} since ξ φ^{−1}(μ) = μ, and the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n[1/μ] = W_n(Ô_X^♭) is Z/p^n.

*Acceptance.*
- i = j = 0: empty; i = j = 1: 1 − ξφ^{−1} is bijective on Ô_X^{♭+}/μ.
- X = Spa(C, O_C): 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} is surjective on O_C^♭ with kernel F_p · μ^i modulo p.
- The kernel Z/p^n · μ^i is identified with Z/p^n(i) by ε^{⊗i} ↦ μ^i for the chosen ε (over C every Tate twist is trivialised by ε); the identification is canonical only after twisting A_inf by {i}.
