### `PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points` — Fixed points of ξ^i φ^{−1} are unchanged under Lη_μ in degrees ≤ i

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points` · lemma · part PR.0.

In the abstract setting of PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition assume (As). (Lemma 10.7) For i ≥ 0 and j ≥ 1: (1) the endomorphism 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1} of H^i(C)/μ^j H^i(C) is injective for ℓ = 0 and an automorphism for ℓ > 0; (2) the endomorphism 1 − ξ^ℓ φ^{−1} of H^i(C)[μ^j] is surjective for ℓ = 0 and an automorphism for ℓ > 0; (3) the endomorphism 1 − ξ^ℓ φ^{−1} of H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ] is an automorphism for ℓ ≥ 0. (Lemma 10.8) Define ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C as the composite τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C ≃ τ^{≤i}Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C → τ^{≤i}Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C = τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C (first map φ^{−1}, second map multiplication by ξ^i). Then the canonical map ι : τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C → C commutes with 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} and induces a quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C) → τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on C).

*Hypotheses.*
- A is p-power torsion, so p is nilpotent on C and 1 − p·(anything) is an automorphism of C.
- (As) holds; H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free; φ : C ≃ C is a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism.
- The décalage functor Lη and the identities H^j(Lη_μ C) ≅ H^j(C)/H^j(C)[μ] and Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} = Lη_μ are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1), (2): the fibre sequence C → C → C/μ^jC (first map μ^j) is compatible with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}; so is the Bockstein sequence 0 → H^i(C)/μ^j → H^i(C/μ^j) → H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j] → 0, whose middle operator is an automorphism by (As). This gives injectivity on the left and surjectivity on the right.
2. For ℓ > 0 it remains to prove injectivity of 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} on H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j]; induct on j through 0 → H[μ] → H[μ^j] → H[μ^{j−1}] to j = 1, where ξ^ℓφ^{−1} is the restriction of pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} because ξ ≡ p modulo φ^{−1}(μ), and 1 − pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} is an automorphism.
3. (3): multiplication by μ embeds H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ] into H^i(C)[μ^{j−1}] compatibly with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} and 1 − ξ^{ℓ+1}φ^{−1}; injectivity from (2) on the right, surjectivity from (2) on the left.
4. Lemma 10.8: for 0 < j ≤ i the map ι sits in the exact sequence 0 → H^j(C)[μ] → H^j(C)[μ^j] → H^j(Lη_μ C) → H^j(C) → H^j(C)/μ^j → 0 (AI.1/decalage-cohomology), compatible with 1 − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1} on the first two terms and 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on the others; by Lemma 10.7 the operator is an automorphism of the kernel and cokernel of ι for j < i, an automorphism of the kernel and injective on the cokernel for j = i, which gives the claim by a nine-term diagram of fibre sequences.

*Acceptance.*
- j = 0 in Lemma 10.8: H^0(Lη_μ C) = H^0(C) because H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free.
- i = 0: both truncated fibres are the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on H^0(C).
- For C = Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n the lemma compares fixed points on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n and on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n.

### `PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison` — Syntomic complexes as truncated p-adic nearby cycles ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Syntomic complexes as truncated nearby cycles**.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C with generic fibre X; let ψ : X_ét → 𝔛_ét be the map of sites. Then for all i ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1 there is a natural equivalence Z/p^n(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét, compatible in n; on the left Z/p^n(i) is the syntomic sheaf Z_p(i)/p^n restricted to 𝔛_ét, on the right the usual Tate twist on X. Passing to the inverse limit over n gives Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z_p(i) on the pro-étale site of 𝔛. Consequently the nearby cycle sheaves R^iψ_* Z/p^n are flat over Z/p^n.

*Hypotheses.*
- C is algebraically closed and complete over Q_p (BMS2 Theorem 1.15(2)); 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C. No properness is assumed.
- The comparison is with the truncation τ^{≤i}, not with all of Rψ_*: Z/p^n(i) → Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) is an isomorphism exactly when R^jψ_* Z/p^n = 0 for j > i.
- X is a rigid space, Rψ_* is the nearby-cycles functor of the formal scheme (owner ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology); no theory of nearby cycles beyond the definition is used.
- The AΩ input is PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison; no TC enters.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf, Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i} hofib(φ_i − 1 : τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n).
2. φ_i identifies τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ with τ^{≤i}AΩ (the Nygaard filtration is the Lη_ξ-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), turning the fibre into τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n), with AΩ = Lη_μ Rν_*A_inf,X (AI.3).
3. By PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points and PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition this equals τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n).
4. On X_proét the map 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i), so the fibre is τ^{≤i}Rν_*Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i}Rψ_*Z/p^n(i). All identifications are compatible with reduction n → n − 1; flatness of R^iψ_*Z/p^n follows from compatibility in n (BMS2 Remark 10.3).

*Acceptance.*
- 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i)(O_C) ≃ Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0, agreeing with PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid.
- 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i = 1: H^1 of both sides contains the Kummer class of T, which is non-zero in R^1ψ_*μ_{p^n}.
- i = 0: Z/p^n ≃ τ^{≤0}Rψ_*Z/p^n = ψ_*Z/p^n.
- Compatibility in n: the squares with Z/p^n(i) → Z/p^{n−1}(i) commute.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation`, `AInfCohomology:AI.3`, `AInfCohomology:AI.4`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

### `PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison` — The étale comparison morphism for syntomic cohomology ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **Étale comparison for syntomic cohomology**.

(1) For every p-complete animated commutative ring R there is a canonical map of graded commutative ring objects of D(Z), ⊕_n γ{n} : ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in R and by γ{1} ∘ c_1^syn ≃ c_1^ét, where c_1^ét : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) is the étale first Chern class. (2) γ{0} is the composite of α_R^{−1} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) with restriction to Spec R[1/p]. (3) For a perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebra R with Ext^i_{Z_p^cyc}(F_p, R) = 0 for all i and x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, the map H^0_ét(Spf R, Z_p)[log_Δ(ε)] → ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism of graded rings; in particular each RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is concentrated in degree 0. This applies to O_C for C algebraically closed and spherically complete of mixed characteristic. (4) For an animated Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra R with ε ∈ H^0_syn(Spec R, Z_p(1)) the class of (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …), the map (⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)))[1/ε] → ⊕_n RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) becomes an isomorphism after p-completion; for R p-complete, RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p) is the p-completed colimit of RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) → ⋯ along multiplication by ε.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is a p-complete animated ring in (1), (2); a perfectoid algebra over Z_p^cyc, the p-completion of Z[q^{1/p^∞}]/([p]_q), in (3); an animated Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra in (4).
- γ{n} is in general not an isomorphism, and no range of degrees in which it is one is asserted here: the isomorphism statements are (4) after inverting ε, PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid for perfectoid rings and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for smooth formal schemes over O_C. Bhatt–Lurie Section 8 proves no range of degrees in which γ{n} is an isomorphism.
- (4) is a reformulation of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 over the perfectoid base Z_p^cyc and depends on it.
- In the Bhatt–Lurie text the remark after Theorem 8.1.9 cites the wrong theorem and Remark 8.5.4 misprints a target (source issues PrismaticCohomology/E43, E44).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Let 𝒞 be the perfectoid rings admitting a map from Z_p^cyc satisfying the two conditions of (3); 𝒞 contains products of O_{C_i} with C_i algebraically closed and spherically complete, hence is a basis for the arc_p-topology, and R ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is right Kan extended from 𝒞 [Bhatt–Mathew, Corollary 6.17]. So γ and the homotopy with c_1 need only be built on 𝒞.
2. (3): for perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebras multiplication by log_Δ(ε) : Z_p(n − 1) → Z_p(n) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 2 (its cofibre is 1 − φ^{−1} on (q − 1)^{−n}A/(q − 1)^{1−n}A, where φ^{−1} is divisible by p^{n−1}), and for n = 1 under the Ext-vanishing condition (BL Lemma 8.3.2); with PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (weights ≤ 0) this gives the polynomial ring.
3. (1), (2): on 𝒞 both graded rings are discrete in degree 0 after truncation, and there is a unique graded ring map extending restriction in weight 0 and sending log_Δ(ε) to the Kummer class ρ(ε); it sends log_Δ(u) to ρ(u) for all u ∈ T_p(R^×), checked pointwise on Spec R[1/p] by reduction to O_C, where T_p(O_C^×) is free on ε; hence independence of choices and functoriality (BL proofs of Theorem 8.3.1 and Proposition 8.3.7).
4. (4): reduce to R p-complete over Z_p^cyc = A/I with (A, I) the perfected q-de Rham prism; colim_n Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → colim_n Δ_R{n} along log_Δ(q^p) is an isomorphism after p-completion (BL Proposition 8.5.3), so colim_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = fib(φ − 1 on A[1/(q − 1)] ⊗̂ Δ_R) = (Δ_{R/A}[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, which is RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p) by PR.4/etale-comparison and PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients; the composite with the map from (1) is the identity, checked arc_p-locally.

*Acceptance.*
- R = O_C with C algebraically closed and spherically complete: ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)] and γ sends log_Δ(ε) to the generator ρ(ε) of Z_p(1)(C); γ{n} is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 and 0 → Z_p(n)(C) for n < 0.
- R = Z_p, n = 1: γ{1} on H^1 is the inclusion of the p-completion of Z_p^× into that of Q_p^×, with cokernel Z_p; not an isomorphism.
- R an F_p-algebra: the target vanishes, and (4) says that ε acts nilpotently up to p-completion: colim along ε of RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is 0.
- n = 0: γ{0} is restriction RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/prismatic-logarithm`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism-perfection`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra`.

*Sources.*

### `PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes` — Syntomic cohomology of schemes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes` · construction · part PR.0.

For an animated commutative ring R with p-completion R̂ and an integer n, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is the pullback in D̂(Z_p) of RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)) ← RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)), the first map being γ{n} of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison; the projection to RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is again called the étale comparison morphism γ{n}. Properties: (a) if R is p-complete then RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (b) if p is invertible in R then γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p(n)); (c) with j : Spec R[1/p] → Spec R there is a fibre sequence RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (d) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) satisfies fpqc descent, hence extends to schemes, formal schemes and algebraic stacks X by RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = lim over Spec R → X; (e) it is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras and commutes with filtered colimits; it does not commute with sifted colimits; (f) RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(0)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) canonically; (g) c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(1)) exhibits the target as the p-completion of the source. For a scheme X, Z/p^k(n)_X ∈ D(X_ét, Z/p^k) denotes the restriction of RΓ_syn(−, Z_p(n))/p^k to the small étale site.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is any animated commutative ring; the étale site and étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] depend only on π_0(R).
- The pullback is formed in the p-complete derived ∞-category; all four corners are p-complete.
- Étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] with twisted coefficients, j_!, Gabber's affine proper base change and formal glueing for étale cohomology are imported (SF.2 and the arc-descent gap).
- In the printed proof of Proposition 8.4.10 the last colimit is indexed by ℰ where ℰ' is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E45).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition and (a), (b): BL Construction 8.4.1 and Remark 8.4.2; for (a) the right vertical map of the square is an isomorphism, for (b) both lower corners vanish.
2. (c): formal glueing gives a pullback square for RΓ_ét(−, j_!Z_p(n)) along R → R̂ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 6.4], and RΓ_ét(Spec R̂, j_!Z_p(n)) = 0 by Gabber's affine proper base change; so RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) is the fibre of RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p]) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p]) (BL Remark 8.4.4).
3. (d): the first term of (c) satisfies arc-descent [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.4] and the third p-complete fpqc descent (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); (e): the third term commutes with sifted colimits, and F(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) commutes with filtered colimits and is invariant under henselian surjections (Gabber), which gives left Kan extension from smooth Z-algebras by a cofinality argument (BL Proposition 8.4.10, Corollary 8.4.11, Warning 8.4.12).
4. (f), (g): arithmetic fracture squares for RΓ_ét(−, Z_p) and RΓ_ét(−, G_m)^∧ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.13; Česnavičius–Scholze] reduce to the p-complete case (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) and the case p invertible (BL Propositions 8.4.13, 8.4.14).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 8.5.1 and Variant 8.5.5: the source of the localisation to the generic fibre: inverting ε gives étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p]
- Bhatt–Mathew Notation 1.1, Theorem 1.8: the sheaves Z/p^n(i)_X on the small étale site and their comparison with truncated nearby cycles
- PR.4/syntomic-connectivity: the bound Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D^{[0,i]} is a statement about these sheaves
- Bhatt–Lurie Remark 8.4.3 (Selmer K-theory): graded pieces of the motivic filtration; consumed by trace-theoretic roadmaps, not proved here

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.SchemeDatum` (structure): The imported cospan of an animated ring in weight n: RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)), RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)), RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) with γ{n} and restriction (owners: this stage and SF.2).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCohomologyScheme` (constructor): RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)), the pullback of the cospan.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.etaleComparison` (projection): γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.toFormal` (projection): The map RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.toFormal_isIso_of_complete` (compatibility): If the restriction map of the cospan is an isomorphism (R p-complete), the map to the formal syntomic complex is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.etaleComparison_isIso_of_invertible` (compatibility): If the two p-adic corners vanish (p invertible in R), γ{n} is an isomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic.pullback_condition` (relation): The square commutes: γ{n} on Spf R̂ after the map to the formal complex equals restriction after γ{n}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_invertible` (degenerate): For a cospan with zero p-adic corners, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_complete` (compatibility): For a cospan whose restriction map is the identity, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_zero` (computation): For the zero cospan (the zero ring) RΓ_syn = 0.
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_not_product` (non-example): RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is not the direct sum of the formal and the étale corner: for the cospan with all three objects M ≠ 0 and both maps the identity the pullback is M, not M ⊕ M.

*Acceptance.*
- RΓ_syn(Spec Q, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Q, Z_p(n)).
- RΓ_syn(Spec Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1].
- RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) for n < 0.
- For X proper over a p-henselian ring with bounded p-power torsion, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn of its p-adic completion.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.4/syntomic-connectivity`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Construction 8.4.1, Remarks 8.4.2 and 8.4.4, Proposition 8.4.6, Variant 8.4.7: “to produce a refinement of Construction” (definition by the pullback square, the two degenerate cases, the fibre sequence and fpqc descent)
- BL22, Proposition 8.4.10, Corollary 8.4.11, Warning 8.4.12, Propositions 8.4.13 and 8.4.14: “does not commute with sifted colimits (and is therefore not a left Kan extension of its restriction to finitely generated polynomial algebras over” (left Kan extension from smooth Z-algebras, filtered colimits, the failure for sifted colimits, weights 0 and 1)
- BM23, Notation 1.1: “obtained by restricting the syntomic complexes” (the étale sheaves Z/p^n(i)_X of Bhatt–Mathew are the restrictions of these complexes)

### `PR.4/syntomic-not-generic-fibre-etale` — Syntomic cohomology is not étale cohomology of the generic fibre in all degrees

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-not-generic-fibre-etale` · application · part PR.0.

The étale comparison morphism γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is not an isomorphism in general, and the φ = 1 statement of PR.4/etale-comparison does not extend to the divided-Frobenius fibres Z_p(n). Instances: (1) R = Z_p, n = 1: H^1 of the source is the p-completion of Z_p^× and H^1 of the target the p-completion of Q_p^×; γ{1} is injective on H^1 with cokernel Z_p, generated by the Kummer class of p. (2) R an F_p-algebra: the target is 0 for every n, while RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≠ 0 for R ≠ 0, and for R = O_C/p the group H^0(Z_p(n)(R)) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is non-zero for all n ≥ 0. (3) For 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_C the sheaf Z/p^k(n) on 𝔛_ét is the truncation τ^{≤n}Rψ_*Z/p^k(n), so Z/p^k(n) → Rψ_*Z/p^k(n) is an isomorphism if and only if R^jψ_*Z/p^k = 0 for all j > n. (4) For a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme X (for example regular and flat over Z) with j : X[1/p] → X, Bhatt–Mathew prove that Z/p^k(n)_X → τ^{≤n}Rj_*μ_{p^k}^{⊗n} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in degrees < n and injective in degree n with image generated by symbols from O_X^×; instance (1) is the case X = Spec Z_p, n = 1. What does hold for all p-complete R is the isomorphism after inverting ε and p-completing (PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (4)) and, for the fixed points of φ itself, PR.4/etale-comparison.

*Hypotheses.*
- The warning concerns the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), built from the Nygaard filtration and the divided Frobenius; it does not concern the φ = 1 statement of Theorem 9.1, which holds for every p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring.
- (4) is quoted from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8 as the general shape of the discrepancy; its proof (F-smoothness, Bloch–Kato) is outside this stage and is not a prerequisite of any node.
- In (1) p is odd for the explicit description 1 + pZ_p of the completed units; the statement about the cokernel holds for all p.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): by PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (3), RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Z_p, G_m)^∧[−1] = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1], and RΓ_ét(Spec Q_p, Z_p(1)) has H^1 = lim Q_p^×/(Q_p^×)^{p^k} by Kummer theory; γ{1} is induced by Z_p^× ⊂ Q_p^× by the characterisation of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, and Q_p^×/Z_p^× = Z.
2. (2): R[1/p] = 0; PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (2) and PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p give the non-vanishing; t = log[ε] ∈ A_crys(O_C/p) satisfies φ(t) = pt.
3. (3) is a reformulation of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison. (4) is the statement of Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8.

*Acceptance.*
- The cokernel of γ{1} on H^1 for R = Z_p is Z_p, not 0.
- For R = F_p: RΓ_syn(Spf F_p, Z_p) has H^0 = H^1 = Z_p while Spec F_p[1/p] is empty.
- For R = O_C: γ{n} is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 0, so the discrepancy is invisible on the basis of the arc_p-topology.
- A statement 'Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) for every quasisyntomic R' is false by (1).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-low-weights`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/etale-comparison`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

*Sources.*
- BM23, Theorem 1.8 and the paragraph after it: “is obtained by modifying the truncated” (the precise relation between Z/p^n(i)_X and truncated nearby cycles for F-smooth schemes, quoted as the shape of the discrepancy)
- BL22, Section 8, introduction: “into a single invariant” (étale cohomology of the generic fibre and syntomic cohomology of the formal completion are different invariants, amalgamated in Construction 8.4.1)
- BMS2, Theorem 10.1: “There is a natural equivalence” (only the truncation τ^{≤i} of the nearby cycles is syntomic cohomology)

*Proposed location:* module `TauCeti/Prismatic/Syntomic/EtaleComparison`, namespace `TauCeti.Prismatic.Syntomic`.

### `PR.4/tate-twists-acceptance-examples` — Acceptance examples: O_C, the formal torus, finite levels and the maps n → n − 1

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.4/tate-twists-acceptance-examples` · application · part PR.0.

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε^{1/p}] with ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, d = [p]_q a generator of ker(A_inf → O_C) and μ = q − 1, so φ(μ) = dμ. (1) For every n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(O_C) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals Z_p · μ^n ⊂ φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf, the kernel of φ/d^n − 1; it is identified with H^0(Spec C, Z_p(n)) = T_p(C^×)^{⊗n}. (2) At finite level Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = Z/p^k · μ^n = μ_{p^k}(C)^{⊗n}, and the maps induced by k → k − 1 are the reduction maps, compatible with those of étale cohomology; likewise in PR.4/etale-comparison the isomorphisms Z/p^k ≃ (A_inf[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1} = W_k(C^♭)^{F=1} commute with reduction. (3) For the formal torus 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ with S = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^k) ≃ (Δ_{S/A_inf}[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1}, and on 𝔛_ét, Z/p^k(0) = Z/p^k and Z/p^k(1) ≃ τ^{≤1}Rψ_*μ_{p^k}, whose H^1 contains the Kummer class of T, a non-zero section of R^1ψ_*μ_{p^k}. (4) For C spherically complete, ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)].

*Hypotheses.*
- C is complete and algebraically closed; in (4) also spherically complete.
- The normalisation q = [ε^{1/p}] makes [p]_q a generator of the kernel of θ, as in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4.
- These are instances of earlier nodes, collected as the acceptance tests the stage names; nothing new is proved.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): Z_p(n)(O_C) = fib(φ/d^n − 1 : φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf → A_inf) (PR.4/syntomic-complex); μ^n lies in the kernel because φ(μ^n) = d^nμ^n; by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid the complex is RΓ(Spec C, Z_p(n)), free of rank one in degree 0, and multiplication by μ^{−n} is the comparison used in that proof.
2. (2): reduce (1) modulo p^k; compatibility in k is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients and the compatibility in n of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison.
3. (3): PR.4/etale-comparison for S and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for 𝔛; T has no p-th root in the strict henselisations of 𝔛 at points of the special fibre after inverting p, these local rings being normal, so its Kummer class is non-zero.
4. (4): PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (3).

*Acceptance.*
- φ(μ) = dμ, hence φ(μ^n)/d^n = μ^n.
- Z/p^k(n)(O_C) → Z/p^{k−1}(n)(O_C) is surjective with kernel p^{k−1}Z/p^k · μ^n.
- The Kummer class of T in H^1_ét(Spec C⟨T^{±1}⟩, μ_{p^k}) has order p^k.
- Z_p(n)(O_C) ≠ 0 for every n ≥ 0, whereas Z_p(n)(O_C/p) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is much larger: reduction modulo p changes syntomic cohomology.

<a id="layer-pr5"></a>

# Layer PR.5. Absolute prismatics and geometric coefficient packages

Layer PR.5 treats absolute prismatic cohomology and the Cartier–Witt stack, after Bhatt–Lurie §§3–5 and Bhatt–Scholze's F-crystal paper §2. It has 28 nodes.

The absolute prismatic site X_Δ of a p-adic formal scheme X is the opposite of the category of triples (A, I, u), with (A, I) a bounded prism and u : Spf(A/I) → X (Definition 2.3 of the F-crystal paper), with the flat topology of finite (p, I)-completely faithfully flat families. Bhatt–Lurie's stack-theoretic form starts from generalized Cartier divisors and Cartier–Witt divisors. It builds the Cartier–Witt stack WCart with its quotient presentation [WCart_0/W^×], the point ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart of a prism, fibre products of prisms over WCart and the flatness of ρ_A. Quasi-coherent and perfect complexes on WCart are identified with prismatic crystals. The Hodge–Tate divisor is identified with BG_m^♯; complexes on it are classified by the Sen operator. The layer also gives the Frobenius of WCart and the Frobenius pullback square. Absolute prismatic cohomology is the cohomology of the prismatic sheaf on WCart, compared with relative prismatic complexes and the relative site, with absolute-versus-relative comparisons, descent and continuity, and the cohomology of the absolute site. Then come absolute Hodge–Tate cohomology and the diffracted Hodge complex, the crystalline comparison in characteristic p, the absolute de Rham comparison and the de Rham point, the absolute Nygaard filtration with its graded pieces, de Rham specialisation, descent and completeness, its form over a perfect prism, and the Frobenius φ{n}.

Stacks and quasi-coherent complexes on them are requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1 and LanglandsParameterStacks LP1; their suppliers do not state descent for groups of infinite type (the review's questions to the orchestrator). Breuil–Kisin twists are PR.3's and syntomic complexes PR.4's (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28). Six nodes keep an open point: functoriality of the absolute site, a principalisation step that belongs in `PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor`, two statements that use the absolute Frobenius before `PR.5/absolute-frobenius` constructs it, and the API of the absolute Nygaard filtration and of Remark 5.7.10. The planets are the absolute prismatic site, the Cartier–Witt stack, the Hodge–Tate divisor, the Sen operator, absolute prismatic cohomology and the absolute Nygaard filtration.

*Coverage of `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5`: planned.* The remaining items are listed in the Coverage section at the end.

### `PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site` — The absolute prismatic site of a p-adic formal scheme ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site` · definition · part PR.0 · planet **Absolute prismatic site**.

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. The absolute prismatic site X_Δ is the opposite of the category whose objects are triples (A, I, u), with (A, I) a bounded prism and u : Spf(A/I) → X a morphism of p-adic formal schemes (A/I carries the p-adic topology), and whose morphisms (A, I, u) → (B, J, v) are the maps of prisms f : (A, I) → (B, J) with u ∘ Spf(f mod I) = v. The flat topology on X_Δ is generated by the finite families {(A, I, u) → (A_s, I_s, u_s)}_s of maps of prisms over X for which A → ∏_s A_s is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat. The structure sheaf is O_Δ(A, I, u) = A, with its δ-structure and Frobenius φ; the prism-ideal sheaf (the ideal sheaf of the Hodge–Tate divisor) is I_Δ(A, I, u) = I ⊂ A; the reduced structure sheaf is Ō_Δ(A, I, u) = A/I = O_Δ/I_Δ. For all integers m, n the presheaf (A, I, u) ↦ I^m ⊗_A A{n} is a sheaf with values in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p), and RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(X){n} denotes the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u). Comparison with relative sites: if X lies over Spf(A/I) for a bounded prism (A, I), the relative site (X/A)_Δ is the category of objects (B, J, v) of X_Δ together with a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) such that v lies over Spf(B/J) → Spf(A/I); the forgetful functor (X/A)_Δ → X_Δ carries covers to covers and O_Δ, I_Δ, Ō_Δ to the relative sheaves. If (A, I) is a perfect prism this functor is an equivalence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ.

*Hypotheses.*
- X is a p-adic formal scheme; Bhatt–Lurie assume in addition that X is bounded (locally Spf of a p-complete ring with bounded p-power torsion) wherever the site computes cohomology.
- Every prism in the site is bounded; the convention is that of Bhatt–Scholze (the site is the opposite category), while Bhatt–Lurie write (X)_Δ for the category of triples itself and put the topology on its opposite.
- Register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E5: for a semiperfectoid ring the category having an initial object consists of all prisms, not only bounded ones; the absolute site here always uses bounded prisms.
- Complete flatness and the complete derived category are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Category: triples (A, I, u) with the maps of prisms of PR.0/prism-category compatible with the structure maps; composition and identities are those of prisms (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Definition 2.3; Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 4.4.27).
2. Topology and sheaves: covers are tested on underlying prisms, so O_Δ and Ō_Δ are sheaves with vanishing higher Čech cohomology by PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (Bhatt–Scholze, Corollary 3.12); I_Δ = I is a sheaf because I ⊗_A B = IB for a map of prisms (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal); I^m{n} is a sheaf by completely faithfully flat descent for invertible modules and the base-change compatibility of the twists A{n} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.4.28).
3. Relative comparison: unwind Bhatt–Lurie Definition 4.1.1 against Definition 4.4.27; for a perfect prism every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) (the lemma inside Bhatt–Scholze Remark 4.7), which gives the equivalence.
4. Repleteness of the topos Shv(X_Δ), so that derived limits behave well: Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Remark 2.4, with the replete topoi of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 4.4.30: absolute prismatic cohomology of a p-quasisyntomic formal scheme is the cohomology of this site with coefficients in I^m{n}
- Bhatt–Lurie, Remark after Proposition 3.3.5: quasi-coherent complexes on the Cartier–Witt stack are crystals of complete complexes on (Spf Z_p)_Δ
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7 (prismatic F-crystals): vector bundles and perfect complexes over O_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ] on X_Δ are the crystals of that layer
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 (syntomic complexes): the sheaves I_Δ^m{n} are the coefficients of the absolute theory from which Z_p(n) is built

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj` (structure): An object of (Spf R)_Δ: a ring A with a prism structure (A, I), boundedness of A/I, and a ring map R → A/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.Hom` (structure): A morphism (A, I, u) → (B, J, v): a map of prisms whose reduction carries u to v.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.ofPrism` (constructor): The tautological object (A, I, id) of (Spf A/I)_Δ attached to a bounded prism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.idealSheaf` (data): The value I of the prism-ideal sheaf I_Δ on an object; the quotient of the structure sheaf by it is the reduced sheaf.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.RelativeObj` (compatibility): An object of the relative site (R/A)_Δ is an object of (Spf R)_Δ with a map of prisms from (A, I) compatible with the structure maps.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.existsUnique_hom_of_perfect` (universal-property): For a perfect prism (A, I), every object of (Spf A/I)_Δ receives a unique morphism from (A, I, id); hence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ for X over A/I.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_site_perfect_initial` (characterisation): For a perfect prism (A, I) the object (A, I, id) admits a morphism to every object of (Spf A/I)_Δ.
- `pr5_site_char_p_crystalline` (computation): If R has characteristic p then every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ has I = (p).
- `pr5_site_structure_map_matters` (non-example): A prism endomorphism of (A, I) that does not induce the identity on A/I is not a morphism of the object (A, I, id) of (Spf A/I)_Δ: the site is not the category of all bounded prisms.

*Acceptance.*
- For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R the site (Spf R)_Δ has a final object, the prism (Δ_R, I) of PR.2/qrsp-prism (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.5; Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.4.29).
- For X = Spf(O_K), K a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field, the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) and the A_inf-prism of O_C are objects of X_Δ that cover the final object (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.6).
- For an F_p-algebra R every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ is crystalline: I = (p).

### `PR.5/generalized-cartier-divisor` — Generalized Cartier divisors and the stack Cart

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/generalized-cartier-divisor` · definition · part PR.0.

Let R be a commutative ring. A generalized Cartier divisor of Spec R is a pair (I, α) with I an invertible R-module and α : I → R an R-linear map. Cart(R) is the groupoid whose objects are these pairs and whose morphisms (I, α) → (I′, α′) are the R-linear isomorphisms ρ : I → I′ with α = α′ ∘ ρ. A ring map f : R → S induces the pullback functor Cart(R) → Cart(S), (I, α) ↦ (S ⊗_R I, S ⊗ α). The pair is a Cartier divisor exactly when α is injective; the Cartier divisors form a full subgroupoid with only identity automorphisms. The functor R ↦ Cart(R) is a stack for the fpqc topology, equivalent to the quotient stack [A^1/G_m]: the divisor of an element f ∈ R is (R, f·), and (R, f·) ≅ (R, g·) exactly when g = u f for a unit u.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is any commutative ring; for a scheme X the definition is the same with an invertible O_X-module.
- Injectivity of α is not preserved by pullback: this is the reason for the generalized notion.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition and groupoid structure: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.1.1, with invertible modules as in Mathlib (Module.Invertible).
2. Cartier divisors as the objects with α injective, and full faithfulness of D ↦ (O(−D), ι): Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.2. Pullback: Remark 3.1.3.
3. Stack property and the identification with [A^1/G_m]: effective fpqc descent for modules and for module maps (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1), and Zariski-local triviality of invertible modules, which makes A^1 → Cart, f ↦ (R, f·), a G_m-torsor over Cart (quotient stacks of LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.1.4: a Cartier–Witt divisor is a generalized Cartier divisor of Spec W(R) with two conditions
- Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.6 and Definition 3.4.1: the map μ : WCart → Cart = [A^1/G_m] whose fibre over [0/G_m] is the Hodge–Tate divisor
- Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.4: the pullback of the Cartier divisor (I ⊂ A) of a prism along a δ-map A → W(R) is a generalized Cartier divisor

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor` (structure): A pair (I, α): an invertible R-module I with an R-linear map α : I → R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.Iso` (structure): A morphism of Cart(R): a linear equivalence ρ : I ≃ I′ with α′ ∘ ρ = α.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofElement` (constructor): The principal divisor (R, f·) of an element f ∈ R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofIdeal` (constructor): The Cartier divisor (I, inclusion) of an invertible ideal I ⊂ R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.baseChange` (functoriality): Pullback along a ring map f : R → S: (I, α) ↦ (S ⊗_R I, S ⊗ α).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.IsCartier` (characterisation): α is injective; equivalently (I, α) comes from a Cartier divisor of Spec R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofElement_iso_iff` (characterisation): (R, f·) and (R, g·) are isomorphic in Cart(R) if and only if g = u f for a unit u of R.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_cartier_zero_not_cartier` (non-example): For a nonzero ring R the generalized Cartier divisor (R, 0) is not a Cartier divisor.
- `pr5_cartier_unit_trivial` (degenerate): For a unit u, (R, u·) is isomorphic to (R, 1·): the empty divisor.
- `pr5_cartier_base_change_loses_injectivity` (computation): (Z, p·) is a Cartier divisor and its pullback to F_p is not.
- `pr5_cartier_automorphisms` (characterisation): The automorphisms of (R, f·) are the units u with u f = f; for f a nonzerodivisor only u = 1.

*Acceptance.*
- The element 0 gives the generalized Cartier divisor (R, 0) with automorphism group R^×: the point of [A^1/G_m] with stabiliser G_m.
- The divisor (Z, p·) is a Cartier divisor of Spec Z whose pullback to Spec F_p is (F_p, 0), which is not a Cartier divisor.

*Depends on:* `mathlib:Module.Invertible`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor`, `PR.5/cartier-witt-stack`, `PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Definition 3.1.1, Remarks 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 and the paragraph after them: “are generalized Cartier divisors” (the definition of the groupoid Cart(R), its pullback functors, and its identification with the quotient stack of the affine line by the multiplicative group)

### `PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor` — Cartier–Witt divisors

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-divisor` · definition · part PR.0.

Let R be a commutative ring in which p is nilpotent and let W(R) be its ring of p-typical Witt vectors, with its δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius F. A Cartier–Witt divisor of R is a generalized Cartier divisor (I, α) of Spec W(R) such that (a) the image of I → W(R) → R (α followed by the restriction x ↦ x_0) is a nilpotent ideal of R, and (b) the image of I → W(R) → W(R) (α followed by δ) generates the unit ideal of W(R). WCart(R) is the full subgroupoid of Cart(W(R)) on these objects, and WCart(R) = ∅ when p is not nilpotent in R. In Witt coordinates x = (x_0, x_1, …) one has δ(x)_0 = x_1, and an element of W(R) with invertible x_0 is a unit when p is nilpotent in R; hence (a) and (b) together are equivalent to: every α(y)_0 is nilpotent, and the elements α(y)_1, y ∈ I, generate the unit ideal of R. A divisor is principalized when I = W(R); then α is multiplication by f = α(1), and (W(R), f·) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if f lies in WCart_0(R) = {f ∈ W(R) : f_0 nilpotent, f_1 a unit}, the set of distinguished Witt vectors (equivalently f = Σ V^n[a_n] with a_0 nilpotent and a_1 a unit). For an invertible ideal I ⊂ W(R), the inclusion (I, ι) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if (W(R), I) is a prism and the images of p and I in R are nilpotent.

*Hypotheses.*
- p is nilpotent in R; by convention there is no Cartier–Witt divisor otherwise.
- The δ-structure on W(R) is the canonical one (natural in R, with Frobenius F); when W(R) has p-torsion it is not determined by F alone.
- Condition (a) is stated for the ideal image; since I is finitely generated it is equivalent to the nilpotence of each element α(y)_0.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.1.4, on the generalized Cartier divisors of the previous node and the Witt vectors of Mathlib (WittVector, with constantCoeff for restriction).
2. Coordinate form of (b): the identity δ(x)_0 = x_1 holds in the universal case Z[x_0, x_1, …], where W is p-torsion-free and the ghost components give w_0(F x − x^p) = p x_1; it follows for all R by naturality of δ (PR.0/delta-ring-category). The kernel V W(R) of W(R) → R lies in the Jacobson radical when p is nilpotent in R, so an ideal of W(R) is the unit ideal exactly when its image in R is.
3. Principalized divisors and WCart_0: Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.1 and Remark 3.2.2; the Teichmüller expansion f = Σ V^n[a_n] holds in every ring with a_n = f_n the Witt coordinates.
4. Relation with prisms: Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.5, using PR.0/prism and PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators (I is locally generated by a distinguished element exactly when δ(I) generates the unit ideal modulo the radical).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.7: the groupoids WCart(R) are the R-points of the Cartier–Witt stack
- Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.4: a prism (A, I) and a map A → R give the Cartier–Witt divisor W(R) ⊗_A I → W(R)
- Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.3.1: a quasi-coherent complex on WCart assigns a complex of R-modules to every Cartier–Witt divisor of R
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: crystals on the absolute prismatic site of Spf Z_p are tested on Cartier–Witt divisors

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.IsCartierWitt` (characterisation): The predicate on a generalized Cartier divisor (I, α) of W(R): p is nilpotent in R, every α(y)_0 is nilpotent, and the α(y)_1 generate the unit ideal of R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor` (structure): A generalized Cartier divisor of W(R) satisfying IsCartierWitt: an object of WCart(R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.IsDistinguishedWitt` (characterisation): f ∈ WCart_0(R): f_0 is nilpotent and f_1 is a unit.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor.ofWitt` (constructor): The principalized Cartier–Witt divisor (W(R), f·) of a distinguished Witt vector f over a ring in which p is nilpotent.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.isCartierWitt_ofElement_iff` (characterisation): (W(R), f·) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if p is nilpotent in R and f ∈ WCart_0(R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.coeff_zero_delta` (relation): For the canonical δ-structure on W(R): δ(x)_0 = x_1; this turns condition (b) of the source into the coordinate condition of IsCartierWitt.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_cw_p_distinguished` (computation): p ∈ W(Z/p^{n+1}) lies in WCart_0: its coordinates begin (p, 1 − p^{p−1}).
- `pr5_cw_verschiebung_one` (computation): V(1) ∈ W(R) lies in WCart_0(R): its coordinates are (0, 1, 0, …).
- `pr5_cw_one_not_distinguished` (non-example): Over a nonzero ring, 1 ∈ W(R) is not distinguished: condition (a) fails.
- `pr5_cw_teichmuller_not_distinguished` (non-example): Over a nonzero ring, no Teichmüller element [a] is distinguished: condition (b) fails.
- `pr5_cw_empty_of_p_not_nilpotent` (degenerate): If p is not nilpotent in R then R has no Cartier–Witt divisor.

*Acceptance.*
- p ∈ W(Z/p^n) is a distinguished Witt vector: p = (p, 1 − p^{p−1}, …); it defines the de Rham point.
- V(1) ∈ W(R) is a distinguished Witt vector for every R; it defines the point η of the Hodge–Tate divisor.
- A Teichmüller element [a] is never distinguished over a nonzero ring (its coordinate x_1 is 0), and a unit of W(R) is never distinguished.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/generalized-cartier-divisor`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/prism`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/distinguished-element`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.constantCoeff`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`, `mathlib:WittVector.verschiebung`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.5/cartier-witt-stack`, `PR.5/wcart-quotient-presentation`, `PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart`, `PR.5/wcart-frobenius`.

*Sources.*

- BL22, Construction 3.2.1 and Remark 3.2.2: “this determines an action of the affine group scheme” (the set of distinguished Witt vectors, principalized divisors and the action of the units of W(R))

### `PR.5/cartier-witt-stack` — The Cartier–Witt stack WCart ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/cartier-witt-stack` · construction · part PR.0 · planet **Cartier–Witt stack**.

A ring map f : R → S induces W(f) : W(R) → W(S), and pullback along W(f) carries Cartier–Witt divisors of R to Cartier–Witt divisors of S, giving a functor f^* : WCart(R) → WCart(S), (I, α) ↦ (W(S) ⊗_{W(R)} I, W(S) ⊗ α), with coherent isomorphisms (g f)^* ≅ g^* f^*. The Cartier–Witt stack WCart is the resulting functor from commutative rings to groupoids (empty on rings in which p is not nilpotent, so WCart lives over Spf Z_p). It satisfies descent for the fpqc topology: for a faithfully flat map R → S, WCart(R) is equivalent to the groupoid of descent data in WCart(S) relative to S ⊗_R S and S ⊗_R S ⊗_R S. Restriction along W(R) → R gives a morphism of stacks μ : WCart → Cart = [A^1/G_m], (I, α) ↦ (R ⊗_{W(R)} I, R ⊗ α), which factors through [Â^1/G_m] (the formal completion of A^1 at 0): the image of μ(I, α) is a nil ideal, so μ(I, α) is never a Cartier divisor unless R = 0. WCart is not a formal scheme: its points have nontrivial automorphisms.

*Hypotheses.*
- Rings are ordinary commutative rings; WCart(R) is empty unless p is nilpotent in R.
- Corrected direction (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E53): the functor induced by f : R → S goes from WCart(R) to WCart(S); Bhatt–Lurie Remark 3.1.7 prints the opposite direction, and Warning 3.1.8 uses the correct one.
- The fpqc descent is asserted in the source without proof (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E55); W(R) → W(S) is in general not flat for a flat map R → S, so the proof below does not use flat descent along it.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Pullback: W(f) is a δ-map with W(f)(x)_i = f(x_i) (Mathlib WittVector.map), so conditions (a) and (b) in coordinate form are preserved; the pseudofunctor structure is that of Cart applied to W (previous nodes).
2. Descent for morphisms: Zariski-locally on R two divisors are principalized (next node), and isomorphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) are the units u of W(R) with g = u f; S ↦ W(S)^× and S ↦ W(S) are representable by affine schemes, hence fpqc sheaves.
3. Descent for objects: write the groupoid of invertible W(R)-modules as the limit over n of the groupoids for W_n(R); the kernel of W_{n+1}(R)^× → W_n(R)^× has a finite filtration (by powers of p) whose graded pieces are quasi-coherent on flat R-algebras, so its Čech H^1 and H^2 for a faithfully flat cover vanish (Amitsur exactness, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1); induction on n starting from fpqc descent for invertible R-modules gives effectivity, and the map α descends as a morphism.
4. The morphism μ and its factorisation through the formal affine line: Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.6. Stack formalism (2-category of fpqc stacks, morphisms of stacks): LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.2.3: WCart is presented as the quotient of the formal scheme of distinguished Witt vectors by the units of W
- Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.3.1: D(WCart) is the limit of D(R) over the category of points of this stack
- Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.4.1: relative prismatic cohomology over all bounded prisms assembles to a sheaf on this stack
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 and PR.7: syntomic complexes and prismatic F-crystals are built from sheaves on WCart and its Hodge–Tate divisor

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor.groupoid` (instance): WCart(R) is a groupoid: morphisms are the isomorphisms of the underlying generalized Cartier divisors.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.pullback` (functoriality): For f : R → S the functor f^* : WCart(R) → WCart(S) of base change along W(f).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.pullbackComp` (functoriality): The coherence isomorphism g^* ∘ f^* ≅ (g ∘ f)^*.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.toCart` (data): μ : WCart(R) → Cart(R), base change along the restriction W(R) → R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.toCart_not_isCartier` (characterisation): For a nonzero ring R, μ(I, α) is never a Cartier divisor.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.pullback_faithful` (characterisation): For a faithfully flat map f the functor f^* is faithful: the separatedness half of fpqc descent.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_wcart_hom_principal` (characterisation): Morphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) in WCart(R) correspond to the units u of W(R) with g = u f.
- `pr5_wcart_zero_ring` (degenerate): Over the zero ring any two Cartier–Witt divisors are uniquely isomorphic.
- `pr5_wcart_pullback_principal` (compatibility): f^*(W(R), x·) ≅ (W(S), W(f)(x)·) for a distinguished Witt vector x.
- `pr5_wcart_nontrivial_automorphism` (non-example): Over the dual numbers F_p[ε]/(ε²) the divisor (W, V(1)·) has an automorphism different from the identity: WCart is not a functor to sets.

*Acceptance.*
- WCart(F_p) contains the point (W(F_p), p·) = (Z_p, p·) and every point of WCart(F_p) is isomorphic to it; its automorphism group is trivial, while over F_p[ε]/(ε²) the point (W, V(1)·) has the non-trivial automorphism 1 + [ε].
- The pullback of (W(Z/p²), p·) along Z/p² → F_p is (W(F_p), p·).
- μ carries the point (W(R), V(1)·) to (R, 0), the generalized Cartier divisor with automorphism group R^×.

### `PR.5/wcart-quotient-presentation` — Presentation of WCart as the quotient [WCart_0 / W^×]

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-quotient-presentation` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let WCart_0 be the functor R ↦ WCart_0(R) of distinguished Witt vectors; it is represented by the affine formal scheme Spf(A^0), A^0 the (p, a_0)-adic completion of Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, a_3, …]. Let W^× be the affine group scheme R ↦ W(R)^×; it acts on WCart_0 by multiplication. The morphism WCart_0 → WCart, f ↦ (W(R), f·), exhibits WCart as the quotient stack [WCart_0 / W^×], the quotient being formed in the 2-category of stacks for the Zariski topology on Spec R. Explicitly: (i) every Cartier–Witt divisor of R is, Zariski-locally on Spec R, isomorphic to a principalized one; (ii) for f, g ∈ WCart_0(R) the isomorphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) are the units u ∈ W(R)^× with g = u f, so WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 ≅ WCart_0 × W^×. Since WCart is an fpqc stack, the same morphism exhibits it as the fpqc quotient, and Spf(A^0) → WCart is a surjection for the Zariski topology whose (n+1)-fold fibre power is Spf(A^0) × (W^×)^n.

*Hypotheses.*
- The quotient is formed for the Zariski topology, as in the source; its agreement with the fpqc quotient uses the fpqc descent of the previous node.
- W^× is a flat affine group scheme over Z that is not of finite type; WCart_0 is a formal scheme, a functor on rings in which p is nilpotent.
- Carriers imported: quotient stacks and their universal property from LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1, effective descent from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1; what those stages do not state is recorded in the requests.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. By the description of morphisms between principalized divisors (cartier-witt-divisor), the map WCart_0 → WCart is W^×-equivariant and induces a fully faithful map from the prestack quotient; it remains to show Zariski-local essential surjectivity (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.2.3 and Remark 3.2.2).
2. (I, α) is in the essential image if and only if I ≅ W(R). Since p is nilpotent in R the kernel of W(R) → R lies in the Jacobson radical and W(R) is complete along it, so an invertible W(R)-module I is trivial if and only if R ⊗_{W(R)} I is trivial.
3. R ⊗_{W(R)} I is an invertible R-module, hence trivial on a Zariski cover Spec R[1/g_i]; pulling (I, α) back to R[1/g_i] gives principalized divisors.
4. Representability of WCart_0 by Spf(A^0): a Witt vector is its sequence of coordinates, f_0 nilpotent and f_1 invertible (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.1).

*Acceptance.*
- Over a local ring R in which p is nilpotent every Cartier–Witt divisor is principalized, and WCart(R) is the action groupoid of W(R)^× on WCart_0(R).
- The fibre product WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 is the formal scheme WCart_0 × W^×, with the two projections f and u f.
- Red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/29: the stack-theoretic inputs of this statement are imported from LP1 and SF.1 and are not rebuilt here.

### `PR.5/transversal-prism-coproducts` — Transversal prisms and coproducts of prisms

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/transversal-prism-coproducts` · theorem · part PR.0.

Transversal prisms (A/I is p-torsion-free) and their approximation property are those of PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/transversal-prism and PR.3/transversal-approximation: (1) for every prism (A, I) there is a transversal prism (B, J) with a map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I). This node adds the statements about coproducts. (2) Coproducts: if (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is bounded, the coproduct (C, K) = (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists in the category of prisms, and (B, J) → (C, K) is flat (B/J → C/K is p-completely flat); if both are transversal, so is the coproduct. (3) If moreover A ≠ 0, then (B, J) → (C, K) is faithfully flat. (4) For every prism (A, I) the category of transversal prisms mapping to (A, I) is sifted; in particular a limit over all bounded prisms may be computed over transversal prisms, or over all prisms. (5) A bounded prism (A, I) is transversal if and only if (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists and is flat over (B, J) for every bounded prism (B, J), if and only if this holds for one nonzero transversal prism (B, J).

*Hypotheses.*
- Prisms are those of PR.0/prism (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)A).
- (2) needs (A, I) transversal and (B, J) bounded; existence of coproducts without these hypotheses requires animated prisms and is not claimed.
- Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are defined by p-complete (faithful) flatness of A/I → B/J (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): choose a smooth Z-algebra B_0 with an invertible module J_0 inducing I, pass to Sym_{B_0}(J_0), take the free p-complete δ-ring on it (flat over it by a lifting argument through W_n) and complete to a prism (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 2.4.1 with Lemmas 2.4.2 and 2.4.3 and Proposition 2.1.10).
2. (2): étale-locally I = (d); let C_0 be the (p, J)-completion of A ⊗_Z B; d is (p, J)-completely regular relative to B because A/d is flat over Z; the prismatic envelope of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes gives the universal prism (C, JC) with d ∈ JC, flat over (B, J), and PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal identifies it as the coproduct (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 2.4.5, Corollary 2.4.7).
3. (3): test faithful flatness on points of Spec B/(p, J) by mapping both prisms to (W(k), (p)) for a perfect field k (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 2.4.9).
4. (4) and (5): nonempty with pairwise coproducts implies sifted (Corollary 2.4.8); (5) is Corollary 2.4.10, using that flatness over a transversal prism preserves and faithfully flat descent reflects transversality (Remark 2.4.4).

*Acceptance.*
- The q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) and the universal oriented prism (A^0, (a_0)) are nonzero transversal prisms; a crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A ≠ 0 is not transversal.
- The coproduct of a transversal prism (A, I) with (Z_p, (p)) is the universal crystalline prism A{p/I}^∧ over (A, I).

### `PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart` — The point ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart of a prism

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (A, I) be a prism and f : A → R a ring map. f lifts uniquely to a δ-map f̃ : A → W(R). Put f̃^*(I) = W(R) ⊗_A I and let α : f̃^*(I) → W(R) be induced by the inclusion I ⊂ A. The pair (f̃^*(I), α) is a generalized Cartier divisor of W(R), and it is a Cartier–Witt divisor of R exactly when the image of I + (p) in R consists of nilpotent elements. This defines a morphism of stacks ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart, where Spf(A) is the formal scheme of the (p, I)-adic topology, functorial in the prism: for a map of prisms h : (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism ρ_B ≅ ρ_A ∘ Spf(h). Composing with μ gives the Cartier divisor I ⊂ A pulled back along f. Special cases: (i) the de Rham point ρ_dR = ρ_{Z_p} : Spf(Z_p) → WCart of the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)), which is R ↦ (W(R), p·); more generally ρ_A(f) ≅ (W(R), p·) for a crystalline prism; (ii) the universal oriented prism (A^0, I^0): A^0 = Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, …]^∧_{(p, a_0)} with the δ-structure induced by the Witt vector Frobenius on WCart_0 = Spf(A^0) and I^0 = (a_0); it is a transversal prism, maps of prisms (A^0, I^0) → (B, J) correspond bijectively to generators of J via h ↦ h(a_0), and ρ_{A^0} is the atlas WCart_0 → WCart.

*Hypotheses.*
- (A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only where D(Spf A) is identified with complete complexes.
- The δ-lift f̃ exists because W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor from δ-rings (PR.0/delta-ring-category).
- The condition for a Cartier–Witt divisor is that f is continuous for the (p, I)-adic topology on A and the discrete topology on R.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. δ-lift: the adjunction δ-rings ⇄ rings with right adjoint W gives f̃ with f̃(a)_0 = f(a) (PR.0/delta-ring-category).
2. Conditions (a) and (b): the image of f̃^*(I) in R is f(I)R; and p ∈ I + φ(I)A (PR.0/prism) with δ-compatibility of f̃ shows that δ(f̃(I)) generates the unit ideal of W(R) once f(I) and f(p) are nilpotent (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.4).
3. Functoriality: for a map of prisms h, J = IB (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) gives W(R) ⊗_B J ≅ W(R) ⊗_A I compatibly with the maps to W(R).
4. The prism (A^0, I^0): the Witt vector Frobenius preserves WCart_0 and lifts Frobenius modulo p, and A^0 is p-torsion-free, so it defines a δ-structure; φ(a_0) = a_0^p + p a_1, so δ(a_0) = a_1 is invertible and a_0 is distinguished; the universal property is Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.2.7, and the identification with the atlas is Example 3.2.5.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.3.5: pullback along the points ρ_A identifies quasi-coherent complexes on WCart with prismatic crystals
- Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.4.1 and Proposition 4.4.8: ρ_A^* of the prismatic cohomology sheaf is relative prismatic cohomology over (A, I)
- Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.6.6 and Proposition 5.4.8: the de Rham point is the image of the Hodge–Tate divisor under Frobenius and implements the de Rham comparison
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.7: evaluation of an F-crystal at the Breuil–Kisin prism is pullback along ρ of that prism

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint` (constructor): For a prism (A, I) and f : A → R with f(I + (p)) nilpotent, the Cartier–Witt divisor ρ_A(f) = (W(R) ⊗_A I → W(R)).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint_comp` (functoriality): g^* ρ_A(f) ≅ ρ_A(g ∘ f) for a ring map g : R → S.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint_map` (functoriality): ρ_A(f ∘ h) ≅ ρ_B(f) for a map of prisms h : (A, I) → (B, J) and f : B → R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.exists_universalOrientedPrism` (universal-property): There is a prism (A^0, (a_0)) such that maps of prisms (A^0, (a_0)) → (B, J) correspond bijectively to generators d of J by h ↦ h(a_0).

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_point_crystalline_is_p` (computation): For a crystalline prism the point ρ_A(f) is isomorphic to the principalized divisor (W(R), p·).
- `pr5_point_orientable_principal` (characterisation): If I is principal then ρ_A(f) is isomorphic to a principalized divisor.
- `pr5_point_to_cart` (compatibility): μ(ρ_A(f)) is isomorphic in Cart(R) to the pullback along f of the Cartier divisor (I ⊂ A).

*Acceptance.*
- For the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R = Z/p^n the point is (W(Z/p^n), p·).
- For an oriented prism (A, (d)) the point ρ_A(f) is the principalized divisor (W(R), f̃(d)·).
- μ(ρ_A(f)) is the generalized Cartier divisor (R ⊗_A I → R) of Spec R.

### `PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms` — Fibre products of prisms over WCart and flatness of ρ_A

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms` · theorem · part PR.0.

(1) Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and (B, J) a transversal prism, with coproduct (C, K) in the category of prisms. Then the square formed by Spf(C) → Spf(A), Spf(C) → Spf(B), ρ_A and ρ_B is a pullback square of stacks: Spf(A) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(C). (2) For every prism (B, J) the morphism ρ_B : Spf(B) → WCart is affine: for every ring R and every Cartier–Witt divisor of R, Spf(B) ×_{WCart} Spec(R) is an affine R-scheme. (3) A bounded prism (B, J) is transversal if and only if ρ_B is flat; if (B, J) is transversal and B ≠ 0 then ρ_B is faithfully flat. In particular for the universal oriented prism the (n+1)-fold fibre power of Spf(A^0) over WCart is Spf(A^n), where (A^n, I^n) is the coproduct of n+1 copies of (A^0, I^0); (A^•, I^•) is a cosimplicial transversal prism, the Čech nerve of the atlas.

*Hypotheses.*
- (1): (A, I) bounded and (B, J) transversal; the roles are not symmetric in the source and the coproduct exists by transversal-prism-coproducts.
- (3): (B, J) bounded.
- Corrected misprints of the proof (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E56): the fibre product computed there is Spf(A^0) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(B) × W^×, and the bijection is with the invertible elements of the test prism.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Reduce (1) Zariski-locally to I = (d_A), J = (d_B); factor through the universal oriented prism (A^0, I^0) → (A, I), a_0 ↦ d_A; the left square Spf(C) = Spf(A) ×_{Spf(A^0)} Spf(C^0) is a pullback because (B, J) → (C^0, K^0) is flat (transversal-prism-coproducts).
2. For the right square use the quotient presentation: Spf(A^0) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(B) × W^× = Spf(B′) with B′ the (p, J)-completion of the free δ-B-algebra on a unit u; maps of prisms (A^0, I^0) → (B″, JB″) over (B, J) correspond to units of B″ by h ↦ h(a_0)/d_B, so (B′, JB′) is the coproduct (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.2.8).
3. (2): replace (B, J) by a transversal prism mapping to it, localise on Spec R so that the divisor is principalized, and apply (1) with (A^0, I^0) (Corollary 3.2.9).
4. (3): by the quotient presentation flatness of ρ_B is flatness of Spf(B) ×_{WCart} Spf(A^0) = Spf(C) over Spf(A^0); use (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) faithfully flat over each factor when the other is transversal and nonzero, and descent of transversality (Corollary 3.2.10).

*Acceptance.*
- Spf(Z_p) ×_{WCart} Spf(A) = Spf(A{p/I}^∧) for a transversal prism (A, I): the universal crystalline prism over (A, I).
- ρ_dR : Spf(Z_p) → WCart is affine and not flat (the crystalline prism is not transversal); the atlas ρ_{A^0} and the q-de Rham point are faithfully flat.

### `PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart` — Quasi-coherent and perfect complexes on WCart

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart` · construction · part PR.0.

For a commutative ring R let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules, a symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category, functorial in R by derived base change. D(WCart) is the limit of the categories D(R) over the category of points of WCart, whose objects are pairs (R, (I, α)) with (I, α) a Cartier–Witt divisor of R and whose morphisms are ring maps with an isomorphism of pulled-back divisors. Its objects are the quasi-coherent complexes on WCart: such an E assigns to every Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R a complex E_α ∈ D(R), compatibly with base change. Perf(WCart) ⊂ D(WCart) is the full subcategory of the E with every E_α perfect; these are the dualizable objects. The structure sheaf O_WCart is the unit object, (R, α) ↦ R. The Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf I ∈ D(WCart) is (R, (I, α)) ↦ R ⊗_{W(R)} I, an invertible object with a morphism I → O_WCart induced by α; I^m denotes its m-th tensor power for m ∈ Z. For a bounded prism (A, I) pullback along ρ_A is a symmetric monoidal exact functor ρ_A^* : D(WCart) → D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A), where D̂(A) ⊂ D(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete complexes; ρ_A^* O_WCart = A and ρ_A^* I = I. Since ρ_A is affine, ρ_A^* has a right adjoint ρ_{A*} : D̂(A) → D(WCart) satisfying base change and the projection formula. The functor D(Z) → D(WCart), M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart, has a right adjoint RΓ(WCart, −) : D(WCart) → D(Z), the global sections functor; it takes values in D̂(Z_p).

*Hypotheses.*
- The limit is a limit of ∞-categories; it is not the limit of the triangulated homotopy categories.
- D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A) uses that the prism (A, I) is bounded.
- WCart is a stack over Spf Z_p, so every R in the index category has p nilpotent.
- In the suggested Lean section these categories and functors are a structure of carriers; Mathlib has no derived category of a stack.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Definition as a limit: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.3.1, an instance of the functor X ↦ D(X) on stacks of LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1, with the stable ∞-categories and limits of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract and E0.
2. Unit and Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf: Bhatt–Lurie, Examples 3.3.3 and 3.3.4; invertibility of I is objectwise invertibility of R ⊗_{W(R)} I.
3. Pullback to a bounded prism and the identification D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A): the paragraph before Proposition 3.3.5, with derived completion from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; pushforward along the affine morphism ρ_A (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms) with base change and projection formula from LP1.
4. Global sections: the right adjoint exists because M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart preserves colimits between presentable categories; its values are p-complete because p is nilpotent on every point (Bhatt–Lurie, Corollary 3.3.11).

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.3.5: the target of the comparison with prismatic crystals
- Bhatt–Lurie, Constructions 4.4.1 and 4.4.10: the prismatic cohomology sheaf is an object of D(WCart) and absolute prismatic cohomology is its global sections
- Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 5.5.3: the absolute Nygaard filtration is a pullback of global sections of filtered objects of D(WCart)
- PrismaticCohomology:PR.4 and PR.7: syntomic complexes and F-crystals use RΓ(WCart, −), F^* and Perf(WCart)

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.Carriers` (structure): The data of D(WCart) and D(WCart^HT) as symmetric monoidal categories with the functors ι^*, ι_*, F^*, RΓ, ρ_A^*, ρ_{A*}, η^*, ρ_dR^* and the objects I^m and O{n}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.carriers` (data): The carriers constructed by this node and its successors on the Cartier–Witt stack.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.Carriers.prismPullback` (functoriality): ρ_A^* : D(WCart) → D(A) for a prism (A, I), with values in derived (p, I)-complete complexes.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.Carriers.globalSections` (data): RΓ(WCart, −) : D(WCart) → D(Z_p), right adjoint of M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.Carriers.idealPow` (data): The invertible objects I^m, m ∈ Z, with I^0 = O_WCart and I^1 the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.prismPullback_unit` (simp): ρ_A^* O_WCart ≅ A.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.prismPullback_ideal` (simp): ρ_A^* I ≅ I, the prism ideal regarded as a complex in degree 0.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_qcoh_pullback_unit` (compatibility): ρ_A^* of the unit object is A in degree 0.
- `pr5_qcoh_ideal_pow_zero` (degenerate): I^0 is isomorphic to the unit object O_WCart.
- `pr5_qcoh_ideal_not_trivial` (non-example): The Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf I is not isomorphic to O_WCart.

*Acceptance.*

- For the de Rham point, ρ_dR^* E ∈ D̂(Z_p) is the de Rham specialisation E_dR of Bhatt–Lurie Notation 5.4.4.

### `PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart` — Quasi-coherent complexes on WCart are prismatic crystals

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart` · theorem · part PR.0.

The pullback functors ρ_A^* induce an equivalence of symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories D(WCart) → lim_{(A, I)} D̂(A), the limit being indexed by the category of all bounded prisms with transition functors M ↦ B ⊗̂^L_A M (derived (p, J)-completed base change). The limit is unchanged if the index category is enlarged to all prisms or restricted to transversal prisms. Equivalently, with (A^•, I^•) the cosimplicial prism of coproducts of the universal oriented prism, pullback along ρ_{A^•} gives an equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•). Passing to dualizable objects, Perf(WCart) ≃ lim_{(A, I)} Perf(A). Hence D(WCart) is the ∞-category of crystals of (p, I_Δ)-complete complexes on the absolute prismatic site ((Spf Z_p)_Δ, O_Δ), and Perf(WCart) is the category of perfect complexes on it. Consequences: (1) the Breuil–Kisin twists (A, I) ↦ A{n} define invertible objects O_WCart{n} ∈ D(WCart) with ρ_A^* O_WCart{n} = A{n}, and E{n} denotes E ⊗ O_WCart{n}; (2) under D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•) the global sections functor is M^• ↦ Tot(M^•) ∈ D̂(Z_p).

*Hypotheses.*
- The index category is that of bounded prisms; boundedness identifies D̂(A) with D(Spf A) (Bhatt–Lurie, Warning 3.3.6).
- D̂(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects of D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).
- The equivalence is one of ∞-categories; the Lean section records only the joint conservativity of the functors ρ_A^*.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Tot description (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 3.3.10): Spf(A^0) → WCart is a Zariski surjection (wcart-quotient-presentation) whose Čech nerve is Spf(A^•) (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms); cohomological descent for the Zariski topology gives D(WCart) ≃ Tot D(Spf A^•) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•), each A^n being transversal, hence bounded.
2. Reduce the limit over bounded prisms to the prisms with principal ideal by (p, I)-completely faithfully flat descent for D̂ (DD.1), using that every prism is Zariski-locally oriented (PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators).
3. The functor Δ → {oriented bounded prisms}, [n] ↦ A^n, is cofinal: every oriented prism receives a map from (A^0, I^0), and the A^n are the coproducts (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Proposition 3.3.5).
4. Enlarging or restricting the index category: the category of transversal prisms over a given prism is sifted (transversal-prism-coproducts; Warning 3.3.6). Perfect complexes: dualizable objects of a limit of symmetric monoidal categories are the families of dualizable objects, and a (p, I)-complete dualizable object of D̂(A) is a perfect complex; on the site side this is Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Proposition 2.7.
5. Twists: the functoriality A{n} ⊗_A B ≅ B{n} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist makes (A, I) ↦ A{n} an object of the limit (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 3.3.8); global sections: Corollary 3.3.11.

*Acceptance.*
- A morphism of D(WCart) is an isomorphism as soon as its pullback to every bounded prism is; it suffices to test on one nonzero transversal prism, for example the q-de Rham prism.
- The rule (A, I) ↦ Δ_{(A/I ⊗^L R)/A} with its base-change isomorphisms defines an object of D(WCart): the prismatic cohomology sheaf.
- The rule (A, I) ↦ A/I is ι_* O_{WCart^HT}, and (A, I) ↦ I is the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-quotient-presentation`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/transversal-prism-coproducts`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/prism-point-of-wcart`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/absolute-prismatic-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/limits-colimits-and-slices`, `LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.5/sen-operator`, `PR.5/wcart-frobenius`, `PR.5/frobenius-pullback-square`, `PR.5/absolute-prismatic-cohomology`, `PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison`, `PR.5/absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology`, `PR.5/absolute-de-rham-comparison`, `PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration`, `PR.7/mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails`.

*Sources.*
- BL22, Proposition 3.3.5 with its proof, Warning 3.3.6 and Remark 3.3.7: “where the limit is indexed by the category of all bounded prisms” (the equivalence between quasi-coherent complexes on the Cartier–Witt stack and compatible families of complete complexes over all bounded prisms)
- BL22, Lemma 3.3.10 and Example 3.3.8: “determines an equivalence of” (the description by the cosimplicial prism and the Breuil–Kisin line bundle)
- BS23-FCRYS, Proposition 2.7: “A similar assertion holds true with” (perfect complexes on the absolute prismatic site are compatible families of perfect complexes over the prisms of the site)

### `PR.5/divided-power-multiplicative-group` — The group scheme G_m^♯ and the Frobenius kernel of W^×

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.5/divided-power-multiplicative-group` · construction · part PR.0.

Let O(G_m) = Z[t^{±1}]. O(G_m^♯) is the subring of Q[t^{±1}] generated by t^{−1} and the divided powers (t−1)^n/n!, n ≥ 0; it is the divided power envelope of the ideal (t−1) ⊂ Z[t^{±1}]. G_m^♯ = Spec O(G_m^♯), with β : G_m^♯ → G_m induced by the inclusion; β is an isomorphism over Q and there is a unique group structure on G_m^♯ making β a homomorphism (the comultiplication t ↦ t ⊗ t preserves O(G_m^♯)). For a torsion-free ring R, β(R) is injective with image the units u such that n! divides (u−1)^n for all n; in particular G_m^♯(Z_p) = 1 + pZ_p. Let W^×[F] be the kernel of the Witt vector Frobenius F : W^× → W^×, an affine group scheme over Z. Then: (1) F : W → W and F : W^× → W^× are faithfully flat, so W^×[F] is flat over Z; (2) the map W^×[F] → G_m, u ↦ u_0, lifts uniquely to an isomorphism of group schemes W^×[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_m^♯ × Spec Z_(p). Variant: with G_a^♯ = Spec Z[x^n/n! : n ≥ 1] and W[F] = ker(F : W → W), the map W[F] → G_a lifts uniquely to an isomorphism W[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_a^♯ × Spec Z_(p).

*Hypotheses.*
- The isomorphism (2) holds after localisation at p, not over Z: W^×[F] becomes G_m over Z[1/p], while G_m^♯ becomes G_m only over Q, having divided powers at every prime ℓ.
- G_m^♯(R) → R^× is neither injective nor surjective for general R; G_m^♯(F_p) is trivial.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Divided power envelope and group structure: Bhatt–Lurie, Notation 3.4.9 and Remark 3.4.10, with the envelopes of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0; the comultiplication formula c((t−1)^n/n!) = Σ_{a+b=n} t^a (t−1)^b/b! ⊗ (t−1)^a/a!.
2. Faithful flatness of F on W = Spec Z[a_0, a_1, …]: the ring is torsion-free; after inverting p, ghost coordinates give a polynomial ring on which F shifts the variables; modulo p, F is a_i ↦ a_i^p (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.4.7, Corollary 3.4.8).
3. Let S = O(W^×[F])_(p), flat over Z_(p), with the δ-structure of the Witt Frobenius and φ(t) = 1; then t − 1 is killed by φ and has divided powers in S (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), giving ν : O(G_m^♯)_(p) → S.
4. ν is an isomorphism over Q (ghost components split W^× over Z[1/p]) and a homomorphism of group schemes by flatness; modulo p it carries the F_p-basis of monomials (t−1)^{e_0} α(t−1)^{e_1} ⋯ with α(x) = −x^p/p, 0 ≤ e_i < p, to the basis a^{e_0} δ(a)^{e_1} ⋯ of S/p = F_p[a, δ(a), …]/(a^p, δ(a)^p, …) (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 3.4.11). The additive variant is Variant 3.4.12.

*Uses.*
- Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 3.4.13: the automorphism group of the point η of the Hodge–Tate divisor, so that WCart^HT is its classifying stack
- Bhatt–Lurie, Theorem 3.5.8: representations of G_m^♯ on p-complete complexes are complexes with a Sen operator
- Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 4.2.8: faithful flatness of F on W^× gives derived descent for prismatic cohomology along F_p ⊗^L −

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.gmSharpRing` (data): The coordinate ring O(G_m^♯) as a subring of the Laurent polynomials over Q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp` (data): The functor of points R ↦ G_m^♯(R) = Hom(O(G_m^♯), R).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.group` (instance): The group structure on G_m^♯(R) for which β is a homomorphism.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.toUnits` (projection): β(R) : G_m^♯(R) → R^×, the image of t.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.toUnits_injective` (characterisation): For a torsion-free ring R the map β(R) is injective.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.WCart.gmSharpEquivFrobeniusKernel` (equivalence): For a ring R in which every integer prime to p is invertible: G_m^♯(R) ≅ {u ∈ W(R)^× : F(u) = 1}, compatibly with u ↦ u_0.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr5_gmsharp_padic_points` (computation): The image of G_m^♯(Z_p) → Z_p^× is 1 + pZ_p.
- `pr5_gmsharp_rational` (compatibility): For a Q-algebra R the map G_m^♯(R) → R^× is bijective.
- `pr5_gmsharp_fp_trivial` (non-example): G_m^♯(F_p) has exactly one element, so β is not an isomorphism: G_m^♯ ≠ G_m.

*Acceptance.*
- G_m^♯(Z_p) = 1 + pZ_p for every prime p, including p = 2.
- Over a Q-algebra R, G_m^♯(R) = R^×.
- In the language of δ-rings: the free δ-Z_(p)-algebra on an invertible element x with φ(x) = 1 is O(G_m^♯)_(p).

*Depends on:* `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category`, `mathlib:WittVector.frobenius`, `mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-pd-envelope`.

- BL22, Proposition 3.4.7, Corollary 3.4.8 and Lemma 3.4.11: “lifts uniquely to an isomorphism” (faithful flatness of the Witt vector Frobenius and the identification of its kernel on units with the divided power multiplicative group after localisation at p)
