### `PR.6/q-pd-pair` — q-PD pairs ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair` · definition · part PR.0 · planet **q-PD pair**.

A q-PD pair is a δ-pair (D, I) (a δ-ring D with an ideal I ⊂ D) with a map of δ-pairs (A, (q−1)) → (D, I), A = Z_p[[q−1]] with δ(q) = 0 (so D is a δ-A-algebra and q − 1 ∈ I), such that D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and the following three conditions hold. (1) φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D (so γ is defined on I) and γ(I) ⊂ I. (2) The pair (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism over (A, ([p]_q)): D is [p]_q-torsion-free and D/([p]_q) has bounded p^∞-torsion. (3) The ring D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free and has finite (p,[p]_q)-complete Tor-amplitude over D; equivalently finite p-complete Tor-amplitude, because [p]_q ≡ p mod (q−1). The map D → D/I is called a q-PD thickening and I a q-PD ideal. Being a q-PD pair is a property of a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)), not extra structure. Morphisms of q-PD pairs are maps of δ-pairs over (A, (q−1)): δ-ring maps D → D′ sending q to q and I into I′. A δ-PD pair is a q-PD pair with q − 1 = 0 in D; δ-PD pairs form a full subcategory. Conditions (2) and (3) hold when D is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A, and when q = 1 in D and D is p-torsion-free and p-complete. By (2) and PR.0's Lemma 3.7, D is classically (p,[p]_q)-adically complete.

*Hypotheses.*
- The source's phrase 'derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-pair (D, I)' is read as: both D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete. Remark 16.3 (a) and the proof of Corollary 16.8 confirm that completeness of the ideal is part of the definition.
- Condition (3) is a technical condition; condition (2) could be weakened to D being [p]_q-torsion-free. The source works with bounded prisms and so does this node.
- The conditions γ(I) ⊂ I, q − 1 ∈ I and the p-torsion-freeness of D/(q−1) are part of Definition 16.2 and are easily overlooked.
- Derived completeness, complete flatness and complete Tor-amplitude are DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1's notions.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. State the data (D, I, the δ-A-algebra structure) and the conditions; by (1) and (2) the operation γ of q-divided-power-operation is defined on I.
2. Classical completeness: (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism by (2), so D is classically (p,[p]_q)-complete by PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7).
3. The two standard sources of (2) and (3) (text after Definition 16.2): if D is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A then D/[p]_q is p-completely flat over Z_p[ζ_p] and D/(q−1) = D ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is p-completely flat over Z_p with Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; if q = 1 in D and D is p-torsion-free then [p]_q = p and D/(q−1) = D.
4. Morphisms compose and the identity is a morphism, so q-PD pairs form a category; δ-PD pairs are the full subcategory on the pairs with q = 1.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Definition 16.12: the objects of the q-crystalline site are q-PD pairs over the base pair
- BS22 Lemma 16.10 and Theorem 16.17: q-PD envelopes are universal maps to q-PD pairs; invariance compares two q-PD ideals on one δ-ring
- BS22 Notation 17.1: the pair (A_inf, (ξ)) is the base of the comparison with AΩ
- HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the local q-crystalline site, whose base is the q-PD pair (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1))

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair` (structure): A q-PD pair on a commutative ring D: a δ-structure, an element q with δ(q) = 0, an ideal I ∋ q−1, with conditions (1), (2), the p-torsion-freeness of D/(q−1) and classical (p,[p]_q)-completeness of D. The derived completeness of I and the Tor-amplitude part of (3) are DD.1's notions.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.Hom` (structure): A morphism of q-PD pairs: a ring map commuting with δ, sending q to q and I into I′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.prism` (projection): The bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)) of a q-PD pair.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.prism_I` (simp): The ideal of that prism is the principal ideal generated by [p]_q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.IsDeltaPD` (characterisation): A q-PD pair is a δ-PD pair when q = 1 in D.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.frobenius_mem` (relation): φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D for x ∈ I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.gamma_mem` (relation): γ(x) ∈ I for x ∈ I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.QPDPair.isAdicComplete` (compatibility): D is (p,[p]_q)-adically complete in Mathlib's sense (IsAdicComplete); under condition (2) this is equivalent to derived completeness of D.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_qpd_pair_initial` (computation): There is a q-PD pair on Z_p[[X]] with q = 1 + X and I = (X).
- `pr6_qpd_pair_classical` (compatibility): There is a q-PD pair on Z_p with q = 1 and I = (p): the classical PD pair (Z_p, (p)).
- `pr6_qpd_pair_zero_ideal` (degenerate): There is a q-PD pair on Z_p with q = 1 and I = 0.
- `pr6_qpd_pair_p_not_mem` (non-example): No q-PD pair on Z_p[[X]] with q = 1 + X has p ∈ I.
- `pr6_qpd_pair_sub_one_frobenius` (characterisation): In every q-PD pair, φ(q−1) = [p]_q·(q−1).

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is a q-PD pair, and it is initial (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals).
- (A_inf, (ξ)) with ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) is a q-PD pair (ainf-q-pd-pair).
- (Z_p, (p)) with q = 1 is a δ-PD pair; (Z_p[[q−1]], (p, q−1)) is not a q-PD pair, since φ(p) = p ∉ [p]_q Z_p[[q−1]].

### `PR.6/delta-pd-pairs` — δ-PD pairs and reduction modulo q − 1

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/delta-pd-pairs` · comparison · part PR.0.

(a) (Remark 16.3.) Let D be a δ-ring, regarded as an A-algebra through q ↦ 1, and I ⊂ D an ideal. Then (D, I) is a δ-PD pair if and only if (i) D is p-torsion-free and both D and I are p-adically complete, and (ii) I admits divided powers: x^n/n! ∈ I for every x ∈ I and n > 0. (b) (Remark 16.4.) If (D, I) is a q-PD pair then (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is a δ-PD pair, and (D, I) ↦ (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is left adjoint to the inclusion of δ-PD pairs into q-PD pairs. (c) (Example 16.9 (3).) For a p-torsion-free p-complete δ-ring D with a p-complete ideal I, (D, I) is a δ-PD pair exactly when every x ∈ I has all its divided powers x^n/n! in I. In particular a δ-PD pair is a p-adically complete PD pair in the sense of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0 whose ring is p-torsion-free and carries a δ-structure.

*Hypotheses.*
- In (a) the source prints 'I ⊂ A'; the ideal lies in D (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
- In (c) the source prints 'admits all divided powers in D'; the divided powers must lie in I, as Remark 16.3 (b) says (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- The divided powers are unique because D is p-torsion-free: γ_n(x) = x^n/n!.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (⇐ of (a)) With q = 1 one has [p]_q = p and γ(x) = x^p/p, which lies in I by (ii); D is p-torsion-free and p-complete, so (D, (p)) is a bounded prism, and D/(q−1) = D gives (3).
2. (⇒ of (a)) Completeness and torsion-freeness in (i) are conditions (2), (3) and the completeness in the definition. For (ii): condition (1) gives x^p/p ∈ I; as (p−1)! is a unit, x^p/p! ∈ I; for n < p, x^n/n! is a unit multiple of x^n; the general case follows by induction from γ_{kp}(x) = u·γ_k(γ_p(x)) with u a p-adic unit (the composition rule of divided powers, Mathlib's DividedPowers.dpow_comp and CR.0).
3. (b) Conditions (2), (3) make D/(q−1) p-torsion-free and p-complete; the image of I satisfies x^p/p ∈ Ī by (1) reduced modulo q−1, and it is p-complete as the image of a derived complete module; apply (a). Adjunction: a map of q-PD pairs to a δ-PD pair kills q − 1, so it factors uniquely through the reduction.
4. (c) is (a) for the given D.

*Acceptance.*
- (Z_p, (p)) is a δ-PD pair; (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) reduces to (Z_p, 0).
- (A_inf, (ξ)) reduces to (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)), so ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1).
- For D the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on t over Z_p with δ(t) = 0, the ideal tD is not a q-PD ideal although every element of tD has all divided powers in D: t^p/p ∉ tD.

### `PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties` — Homological properties of q-PD pairs

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair. (1) D is derived f-complete for every f ∈ I. (2) The functor M ↦ M ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) of (p,[p]_q)-completed base change along D → D/(q−1) is conservative on derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes. (3) This functor commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes in D^{≥0}. (4) Let I_0 ⊂ D be an ideal containing q − 1 such that (D, I_0) satisfies conditions (1)–(3) of q-pd-pair, with D derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and I_0 not assumed derived complete, and let I′ ⊂ D be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal generated by I_0, that is, the image of I_0^∧ → D. Then (D, I′) is a q-PD pair. (5) Let D → D′ be a (p,[p]_q)-completely flat map of δ-A-algebras with D′ derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, and let I′ be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal of D′ generated by I. Then (D′, I′) is a q-PD pair.

*Hypotheses.*
- (3): the source prints 'cosimplicial (p,[p]_q)-complexes'; the complexes are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- (4): the source states it for a q-PD pair (D, I); since the ideal of a q-PD pair is already derived complete that statement is empty, and the proof of (5) and of Theorem 16.17 apply (4) to an ideal that is not known to be complete. The node states the form that the printed proof of (4) proves (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E63).
- Completed base change, conservativity (derived Nakayama) and Tor-amplitude are DD.1's.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1) For f ∈ I, φ(f) = f^p + pδ(f) ∈ [p]_q D, so f^p ∈ (p, [p]_q); derived (p,[p]_q)-completeness gives derived f^p-completeness, hence derived f-completeness.
2. (2) It suffices that base change to D/(q−1, p) is conservative. If M ⊗^L_D D/(q−1, p) = 0 then M ⊗^L_D Kos(D; [p]_q, q−1) = 0, because this Koszul complex has at most two nonzero cohomology groups, each a D/(q−1, p)-module; then M = 0 by derived Nakayama (DD.1).
3. (3) Condition (3) of q-pd-pair gives finite complete Tor-amplitude of D → D/(q−1); a completed base change of finite complete Tor-amplitude commutes with totalisations in D^{≥0} (BS22 Lemma 4.22, a statement of DD.1).
4. (4) φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is derived complete, so φ(I′) ⊂ [p]_q D. As q − 1 ∈ I_0, I′ is the preimage of its image in D/(q−1), and that image is the p-complete ideal generated by the image of I_0 (derived completion preserves surjections). This reduces γ(I′) ⊂ I′ to q = 1, where it is the p-adic continuity of divided powers in a p-torsion-free ring (delta-pd-pairs).
5. (5) Condition (1) for (D′, I′): the generators of I·D′ satisfy it by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation, then apply (4) to I_0 = I·D′. Condition (2): PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7). Condition (3): the p-completed base change of D → D′ along D → D/(q−1) is p-completely flat with p-torsion-free source, so it is discrete and p-torsion-free and equals D′/(q−1); D′ → D′/(q−1) is the completed base change of D → D/(q−1), so it has finite p-complete Tor-amplitude.

*Acceptance.*
- For (D, I) = (A_inf, (ξ)): A_inf is derived ξ-complete, and a derived (p, ξ)-complete complex M with M ⊗^L A_inf/(q−1) = 0 is zero.
- For D = Z_p[[q−1]] → D′ = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T⟩ (completed polynomial ring, δ(T) = 0): (D′, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair.
- (2) fails without completeness: for D = Z_p[[q−1]], M = D[1/(q−1)] has zero base change and is not zero.

### `PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals` — Higher q-divided powers and the smallest and largest q-PD ideals

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals` · theorem · part PR.0.

(a) (Existence of higher q-divided powers, Lemma 16.7.) Let D be a δ-A-algebra and let f, z ∈ D satisfy [p]_q·z = φ(f). Then φ(z − δ(f)) ∈ [p]_q D. In particular, if D is [p]_q-torsion-free, the ideal N(D) = φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is stable under γ: if γ(x) is defined then so is γ(γ(x)). (b) (Corollary 16.8.) Let D be a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-A-algebra satisfying conditions (2) and (3) of q-pd-pair. Then (q−1)D is the smallest q-PD ideal of D and N(D) is the largest q-PD ideal of D. (c) (Example 16.9 (1).) The pair (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair and is the initial object of the category of q-PD pairs; more generally (D, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair for every derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-A-algebra D.

*Hypotheses.*
- (a) is stated for every δ-A-algebra, with no torsion-freeness, flatness or completeness. The source states it for [p]_q-torsion-free D and proves it by reduction to a universal case whose flatness is taken from Proposition 3.13; that proposition concerns the completed envelope, so the printed argument covers derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D, which is all the source uses (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E61). The proof steps give a direct argument.
- (b): the source prints 'A-algebra'; a δ-A-algebra is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
- A q-PD ideal of D is an ideal I such that (D, I) is a q-PD pair.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a), direct argument: apply δ to [p]_q·z = φ(f) and use δ∘φ = φ∘δ and the product formula for δ: φ(δ(f)) = δ(z)·φ([p]_q) + z^p·δ([p]_q). With φ([p]_q) = [p]_q^p + pδ([p]_q) this gives φ(z) − φ(δ(f)) = (1 − δ([p]_q))·φ(z) − δ(z)·[p]_q^p, which lies in [p]_q D by fact (iv) of q-divided-power-operation.
2. (a), the source's route: in the universal case A{f, φ(f)/[p]_q}, flat over A by PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (Proposition 3.13), φ([p]_q) = p is a nonzerodivisor modulo [p]_q, and φ²(f) = φ(f)^p + pφ(δ(f)) ≡ pφ(δ(f)) modulo [p]_q.
3. (b), smallest: (q−1)D is derived complete as the image of multiplication by q − 1 on D. φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q, and γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1); pδ(q−1) = (q^p − 1) − (q−1)^p = (q−1)([p]_q − (q−1)^{p−1}) and D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free, so δ(q−1) ∈ (q−1). Fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation extends this to the ideal. Every q-PD ideal contains q − 1 by definition.
4. (b), largest: N(D) is the limit of D →φ φ_*D ← φ_*D (multiplication by [p]_q), hence derived complete; it is stable under γ by (a); every q-PD ideal lies in N(D) by condition (1).
5. (c) A satisfies (2) and (3), so (b) applies; it is initial because a q-PD pair is by definition a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)). The same argument applies to completely flat D.

*Acceptance.*
- In A = Z_p[[q−1]] one has N(A) = (q−1)A, so (q−1) is the only q-PD ideal of A.
- In Z_p with q = 1: the smallest q-PD ideal is 0 and the largest is N(Z_p) = pZ_p.
- In A_inf: N(A_inf) = φ^{-1}(φ(ξ)A_inf) = (ξ), so (q−1) is the smallest and (ξ) the largest q-PD ideal of A_inf.

### `PR.6/ainf-q-pd-pair` — The q-PD pair (A_inf, (ξ))

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-q-pd-pair` · lemma · part PR.0.

(a) (Example 16.9 (2).) Let A_∞ be the (p,[p]_q)-completed perfection of A = Z_p[[q−1]] (PR.0's perfection of the q-de Rham prism) and ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) ∈ A_∞. Then (A_∞, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair. (b) (Notation 17.1.) Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a compatible system (ζ_{p^n})_n of primitive p-power roots of 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ and A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = W(O_C^♭). Then q := [ε] has δ(q) = 0, so A_inf is a perfect δ-A-algebra; it is (p, q−1)-completely flat over A, hence flat over A; the element ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}] generates the kernel of Fontaine's map θ : A_inf → O_C; and (A_inf, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair whose q-PD thickening is θ : A_inf → A_inf/(ξ) ≅ O_C. Moreover [p]_q = φ(ξ) =: ξ̃ generates the kernel of θ̃ := θ∘φ^{-1}, the prism (A_inf, ([p]_q)) is the image of the perfect prism (A_inf, (ξ)) under the automorphism φ, and q − 1 = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.

*Hypotheses.*
- C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of 1; the system (ζ_{p^n}) is fixed. The ideals (q−1) and (ξ) do not depend on the choice.
- A_inf, θ and the element [ε] are owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; the perfect prism (A_inf, ker θ) by PR.0.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Conditions (2) and (3): A_∞ and A_inf are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A (A_∞ is a completed colimit along the flat Frobenius of A; for A_inf, (p, q−1) is a regular sequence and A_inf/(p, q−1) = O_C^♭/(ε−1) is flat over F_p), so the remark after Definition 16.2 applies; flatness over the noetherian ring A follows from complete flatness and derived completeness (the implication quoted in Notation 17.1; DD.1).
2. Condition (1) on the generator: φ(ξ) = [p]_q, so γ(ξ) = 1 − δ(ξ), and one needs δ(ξ) ≡ 1 modulo ξ. As p is a nonzerodivisor modulo ξ it suffices that φ(ξ) ≡ p modulo ξ; and φ(ξ) = [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q−1), while ξ divides q − 1 because q − 1 = φ^{-1}((q−1)[p]_q) = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.
3. By fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation the conditions hold on the ideal (ξ), which is derived complete (principal, generated by a nonzerodivisor of a derived complete ring) and contains q − 1.
4. (b): q = [ε] is a Teichmüller element, so δ(q) = 0 (PR.0, Q0:integral-algebra); θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0 and ξ is distinguished, so it generates ker θ (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). The statements about ξ̃ and θ̃ follow by applying φ.

*Acceptance.*
- γ(ξ) = 1 − δ(ξ) ∈ (ξ).
- The reduction (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)) is a δ-PD pair: ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1).
- (A_inf, (q−1)) is also a q-PD pair, with A_inf/(q−1) a p-torsion-free lift of O_C modulo the divided power ideal (ξ); q-pd-thickening-invariance compares the two.

### `PR.6/q-pd-envelope` — q-PD envelopes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair, P a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-D-algebra and x_1, …, x_r ∈ P a sequence that is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D; let J = (I, x_1, …, x_r) ⊂ P. (1) The derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial δ-P-algebra E := P{φ(x_1)/[p]_q, …, φ(x_r)/[p]_q}^∧ obtained by freely adjoining the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; in particular it is discrete and [p]_q-torsion-free. (2) Let K ⊂ E be the minimal derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal containing the image of J and stable under γ. Then P/J → E/K is an isomorphism, (E, K) is a q-PD pair, and (P, J) → (E, K) is the universal map of δ-pairs from (P, J) to a q-PD pair: every map of δ-pairs (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair factors uniquely through (E, K). One writes D_{J,q}(P) := E and calls (D_{J,q}(P), K) the q-PD envelope of (P, J); it depends only on the ideal J, not on the generators. (3) Extension used by the Čech–Alexander construction: the same statements hold when J is, Zariski locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a sequence as above, and when (P, J) is a filtered colimit (completed) of such pairs.

*Hypotheses.*
- (D, I) is a q-PD pair; P is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the sequence is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D (DD.1's notion, BS22 Definition 2.42).
- The source does not state that P is derived complete. Without it E/K is the derived p-completion of P/J, so the isomorphism P/J ≅ E/K needs it (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- Part (3) is not stated in Lemma 16.10, but Construction 16.13 and Remark 16.16 apply the lemma to such ideals (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E64).
- Free adjunction of elements to simplicial δ-rings is PR.0's animated-delta-rings.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Let Ẽ be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial commutative δ-P-algebra freely adjoining φ(x_i)/[p]_q. Complete flatness of Ẽ over D may be checked after derived base change along D → D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties); there [p]_q = p and the claim is BS22 Corollary 2.44 with Lemma 2.43 (PR.0), the sequence φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p being p-completely regular relative to D/(q−1). So Ẽ is discrete, equal to E, and [p]_q-torsion-free (PR.0, Lemma 3.7).
2. The map E → P/J: E/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) along (x_1, …, x_r) (PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), which maps to P/(q−1, x_1, …, x_r) → P/J. Let K′ be the kernel of E → P/J; it is the preimage of the kernel K̄′ of E/(q−1) → P/J, and K̄′ has divided powers.
3. (E, K′) is a q-PD pair: put K″ = K′ ∩ φ^{-1}([p]_q E). γ(K″) ⊂ K″, because γ(f) ∈ φ^{-1}([p]_q E) by smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (a), and γ(f) reduces to f^p/p ∈ K̄′. K″ is the preimage of its image in E/(q−1), since x + (q−1)y ∈ K″ for x ∈ K″. It contains (I, x_1, …, x_r). By BS22 Lemma 16.11 (CR.0: the ideal of a PD envelope is the smallest ideal containing the generators and stable under f ↦ f^p/p) one gets K″ = K′ = K.
4. Universality: for a map of δ-pairs g : (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair, g(φ(x_i)) ∈ [p]_q E′; as E′ is [p]_q-torsion-free and derived complete, g extends uniquely to a δ-map E → E′; the preimage of K′ is a derived complete γ-stable ideal containing J, so it contains K.
5. (3): Zariski gluing by the flat-localisation property of envelopes (PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (3)) together with q-pd-homological-properties (5); filtered colimits by the universal property, the envelope being the completed colimit of the envelopes.

*Uses.*

- BS22 Construction 16.20 and Lemma 16.21: the framed q-de Rham complex lives on D_{J,q}(P), to which the automorphisms γ_s extend

- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap` (data): The canonical ring map P → D_{J,q}(P).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopePair` (structure): The q-PD pair (D_{J,q}(P), K); its δ-structure extends that of P and its element q is the image of q.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap_delta` (compatibility): P → D_{J,q}(P) commutes with δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelope_frobenius_mem` (relation): φ(x_i) ∈ [p]_q·D_{J,q}(P) for every i.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeMap_mem` (relation): The image of J = (I, x_1, …, x_r) lies in K.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeQuotientEquiv` (characterisation): P/J ≅ D_{J,q}(P)/K.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift` (universal-property): A δ-ring map g from P to the ring of a q-PD pair (E′, K′) with g(q) = q and g(J) ⊂ K′ extends to a ring map D_{J,q}(P) → E′.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_comp` (universal-property): The extension restricts to g on P.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.envelopeLift_unique` (universal-property): Two δ-ring maps out of D_{J,q}(P) into the ring of a q-PD pair that agree on P are equal.

### `PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change` — q-PD envelopes: base change, PD envelopes and prismatic envelopes

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change` · theorem · part PR.0.

In the situation of q-pd-envelope: (a) (Lemma 16.10 (3).) The functor (P, J) ↦ (D_{J,q}(P), K) commutes with (p,[p]_q)-completed derived base change along maps (D, I) → (D′, I′) of q-PD pairs: D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D′ ≅ D_{J′,q}(P′) for P′ = P ⊗̂^L_D D′ and J′ = (I′, x_1, …, x_r). (b) In particular D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) = D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of the ideal J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1), relative to the PD pair (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)), and K/(q−1) is its PD ideal. (c) (Lemma 16.11.) Let B be a p-torsion-free Z_p-algebra and I ⊂ B an ideal generated by a sequence that is regular modulo p; let (D_I(B), J) be the PD envelope of (B, I). Then J is the smallest ideal of D_I(B) that contains I·D_I(B) and is stable under f ↦ f^p/p. (d) (Relation to prismatic envelopes.) D_{J,q}(P) is the prismatic envelope of PR.0, over the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)), of the δ-pair (P, ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r))); when q = 1 in D this is the identification of P{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ with the p-completed PD envelope of (x_1, …, x_r) (BS22 Corollary 2.39).

*Hypotheses.*
- (b): the source prints 'is the pd-envelope'; the p-completed PD envelope is meant, as in its proof and in Remark 16.16 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- (c): the source says 'an ideal I that is regular modulo p'; the node reads it as generated by a sequence regular modulo p.
- (d) is not printed as a statement; it is the content of the first step of the proof of Lemma 16.10 and of the reference to Proposition 3.13 in the proof of Lemma 16.7.
- PD envelopes and their ideals are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (a) E is the free derived complete δ-P-algebra on the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q, and complete regularity relative to the base is stable under base change, so the construction commutes with completed base change; K′ is identified by the universal property.
2. (b) Take D′ = D/(q−1) with the δ-PD pair of delta-pd-pairs (b). Then [p]_q = p and P̄{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope by PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Lemma 2.38, Corollary 2.39), with its PD structure compatible with that of I·D/(q−1) (CR.0).
3. (c) The regularity hypothesis makes D_I(B) p-torsion-free; the description of J is the standard generation of the PD ideal by divided powers of generators, in which γ_n for general n is a unit multiple of iterates of γ_p and ordinary powers (CR.0; the source cites the Stacks project, Tag 07GS).
4. (d) Modulo (p, [p]_q) one has φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p, and (x_1^p, …, x_r^p) is completely regular relative to D when (x_1, …, x_r) is (the remark after BS22 Lemma 2.43); apply PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes to the ideal ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r)).

*Acceptance.*
- For D = Z_p[[q−1]], P = D⟨X⟩, J = (q−1, X): D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on X over Z_p.
- For D with q = 1: D_{J,q}(P) is the p-completed PD envelope D_J(P)^∧ and K its PD ideal.
- Base change of the envelope of (Z_p[[q−1]]⟨x⟩, (q−1, x)) along the map of q-PD pairs (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) → (A_inf, (ξ)) is the envelope of (A_inf⟨x⟩, (ξ, x)).

### `PR.6/q-crystalline-site` — The q-crystalline site and q-crystalline cohomology ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site` · definition · part PR.0 · planet **q-crystalline cohomology**.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. The q-crystalline site of R relative to D, written (R/D)_{q-crys}, is the opposite of the category of q-PD thickenings of R relative to D: its objects are q-PD pairs (E, J) over (D, I) together with a D/I-algebra map R → E/J, and its morphisms are maps of q-PD pairs over (D, I) compatible with the maps from R. The category carries the indiscrete topology, so every presheaf is a sheaf. The structure presheaf O_{q-crys} sends (E, J) to E; it takes values in δ-D-algebras. The q-crystalline cohomology of R relative to D is qΩ_{R/D} := RΓ((R/D)_{q-crys}, O_{q-crys}), the derived limit of the rings E over all q-PD thickenings; it is a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete commutative algebra object of D(D), equipped with the φ_D-semilinear endomorphism φ_{R/D} induced by the Frobenius lifts of the δ-rings E. It is functorial in R and in the base pair (D, I).

*Hypotheses.*
- (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I: derived p-complete with R ⊗^L_{D/I} (D/I)/p smooth over (D/I)/p.
- The source prints 'valued in δ-B-algebras'; δ-D-algebras is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
- The objects only carry a map R → E/J; it need not be an isomorphism.
- The category is not small; the cohomology is computed by a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve (q-crystalline-cech-alexander), which is how the derived limit is given a meaning.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Objects, morphisms and the topology are as stated; with the indiscrete topology the cohomology of a presheaf is its derived limit over the opposite category.
2. O_{q-crys} is a presheaf of δ-D-algebras, so its derived global sections are a commutative algebra object of D(D) with an endomorphism induced by the Frobenii φ_E, semilinear over φ_D.
3. Completeness: each E is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and derived complete objects are closed under limits (DD.1).
4. Functoriality: a map R → R′ over D/I induces (R′/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} by composing structure maps; a map of q-PD pairs (D, I) → (D′, I′) acts by restriction of the base.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorems 16.14, 16.17, 16.18 and 16.22: qΩ_{R/D} is the object compared with crystalline, prismatic and q-de Rham cohomology
- BS22 Theorem 17.2: qΩ_{R/A_inf} is the intermediary between AΩ_R and φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf}
- HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the local q-crystalline site and glues the p-complete theories over all primes
- AInfCohomology:AI.7 and CohomologyComparisons:CP.1: import the comparison with AΩ that is built from qΩ_{R/A_inf}

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening` (structure): An object of (R/D)_{q-crys}: a ring E with a q-PD pair, a morphism of q-PD pairs from (D, I) and a ring map R → E/J compatible with D/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening.Hom` (structure): A morphism of q-PD thickenings: a morphism of q-PD pairs commuting with the maps from D and from R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.Thickening.base` (example): The thickening (D, I) of R = D/I, the initial object of the site of D/I.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineCohomology` (constructor): qΩ_{R/D} as an object of the derived category of D-modules.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineFrobenius` (data): φ_{R/D} : qΩ_{R/D} → φ_{D,*} qΩ_{R/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineEval` (projection): For every q-PD thickening (E, J) of R the canonical map qΩ_{R/D} → E in D(D).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineMap` (functoriality): For a D/I-algebra map R → R′ the induced map qΩ_{R/D} → qΩ_{R′/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.qCrystallineBaseIso` (example): qΩ_{(D/I)/D} ≅ D, the complex with D in degree 0.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_qcrys_base` (degenerate): For R = D/I the evaluation map at the thickening (D, I) is an isomorphism qΩ_{(D/I)/D} ≅ D.
- `pr6_qcrys_eval_natural` (characterisation): Evaluation maps are compatible with morphisms of thickenings: for a morphism (E, J) → (E′, J′) the evaluation at E′ factors through the evaluation at E.
- `pr6_qcrys_map_id` (compatibility): The map induced by the identity of R is the identity of qΩ_{R/D}.
- `pr6_qcrys_not_structure_ring` (non-example): Evaluation at a thickening is not an isomorphism in general: over D = Z_p[[q−1]] there are R and a thickening, namely R = Z_p⟨T⟩ and (D⟨T⟩, (q−1)), for which qΩ_{R/D} → D⟨T⟩ is not an isomorphism.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = D/I the pair (D, I) is the initial q-PD thickening, so qΩ_{(D/I)/D} = D with φ_{R/D} = φ_D.
- For D with q = 1 the site consists of p-complete PD thickenings carrying δ-structures and qΩ_{R/D} is crystalline cohomology (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison).
- For D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R = Z_p⟨T⟩: H^0(qΩ_{R/D}) = D, so qΩ_{R/D} is not the value D⟨T⟩ of the structure presheaf on the thickening (D⟨T⟩, (q−1)).

### `PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander` — Čech–Alexander complexes for q-crystalline cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander` · construction · part PR.0.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. Choose a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete polynomial D-algebra P with a D-algebra surjection P → R with kernel J_0. Let F be the free derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-D-algebra on P and J = (J_0F)^∧ the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal of F generated by J_0. Let P^• and F^• be the (completed) Čech nerves of D → P and D → F; F^• is the free derived complete δ-D-algebra on P^•. Let J_0^• ⊂ P^• be the kernel of P^• → P → R and J^• = (J_0^•F^•)^∧. Then: (1) R ≅ P^•/J_0^• → F^•/J^• is the derived p-completed Čech nerve of R → F/J. (2) The q-PD envelopes D_{J^•,q}(F^•) → F^•/J^•, with kernels K^•, form a cosimplicial object (D_{J^•,q}(F^•), K^•) of (R/D)_{q-crys}, which is the Čech nerve of its 0-th term D_{J,q}(F). (3) D_{J,q}(F) is weakly initial: every q-PD thickening of R receives a map from it. (4) Hence qΩ_{R/D} ≃ lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(F^•), the totalisation of a cosimplicial δ-D-algebra whose terms are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the Frobenius φ_{R/D} is induced by the Frobenii of the terms. (5) (Small variant, Remark 16.16.) For a (p,[p]_q)-completely smooth (or ind-smooth) δ-D-algebra P with a D-algebra surjection P → R, for instance a (p, I)-completely smooth lift of R with a δ-structure, let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P and J^• = ker(P^• → R); then lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ≃ qΩ_{R/D} as well.

*Hypotheses.*
- The kernel of each augmentation P^n → P → R is generated by I and, locally on Spec(P), by a filtered colimit of ideals generated by completely regular sequences relative to D; the envelopes exist by part (3) of q-pd-envelope.
- The choice of P → R may be made functorial in R (the polynomial algebra on the set R), giving a strictly functorial complex.
- In (5) the weak initiality is replaced by the comparison with crystalline cohomology.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): push out P^• → F^• along P^• → P and then along P → R.
2. (2): the construction carrying a surjection (P → R) to the thickening D_{J,q}(F) takes tensor products of the input to coproducts in the site (universal properties of the free δ-algebra and of the q-PD envelope), so the cosimplicial object is a Čech nerve; this is the argument of BS22 Constructions 4.17–4.18 (PR.1's cech-alexander-complex).
3. (3): given a thickening (E, J_E), lift R → E/J_E to a D-algebra map P → E (P is a completed polynomial algebra and E is derived complete), extend uniquely to a δ-map F → E, note that J maps into J_E, and apply the universal property of q-pd-envelope.
4. (4): Čech theory for a weakly final object of a presheaf topos (the argument of the Stacks project, Tag 07JM, as used in PR.1; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2).
5. (5): run the proof of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison with D_{J^•,q}(P^•): modulo q − 1 it is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope, which computes crystalline cohomology because D_{J^0}(P^0) is weakly initial among PD thickenings (CR.2); then use conservativity of reduction modulo q − 1 (q-pd-homological-properties (2), (3)).

*Uses.*
- BS22 proofs of Theorems 16.14, 16.17 and 16.18: all three comparisons are proved on this cosimplicial ring
- BS22 proof of Theorem 16.22: the small variant for the Čech nerve of a framed algebra is row 0 of the bicomplex
- HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: the explicit model of the local q-crystalline cohomology that the global gluing uses

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex of D-modules attached to the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) of a presentation P → R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderIso` (characterisation): The image of that complex in D(D) is isomorphic to qΩ_{R/D}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderZero` (data): The weakly initial thickening D_{J,q}(F) of R, the term of degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderZero_weaklyInitial` (universal-property): Every q-PD thickening of R receives a morphism from the term of degree 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderSmallComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex attached to the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(P^•) of a δ-D-algebra P with a surjection onto R (Remark 16.16).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.cechAlexanderSmallIso` (characterisation): For a completely (ind-)smooth δ-presentation the small complex also represents qΩ_{R/D}.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_cech_alexander_independent` (characterisation): The complexes of two presentations of R have isomorphic images in D(D).
- `pr6_cech_alexander_weakly_initial_base` (compatibility): The thickening (D, I) of D/I receives a morphism from the term of degree 0 of every presentation of D/I.
- `pr6_cech_alexander_base_presentation` (degenerate): For R = D/I and the presentation P = D the complex represents D in degree 0.
- `pr6_cech_alexander_not_cech_nerve` (non-example): The Čech nerve P^• of D → P without envelopes does not compute qΩ_{R/D}: for a faithfully flat P its totalisation is D in degree 0, while over Z_p[[q−1]] there is R (namely Z_p⟨T⟩) with qΩ_{R/D} not isomorphic to D in degree 0.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = D/I and P = D the cosimplicial ring is constant with value D.
- For D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R = Z_p⟨T⟩ and P = D⟨T⟩ (small variant): the term of degree 1 is D⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧.
- Two choices of presentation give canonically isomorphic objects of D(D).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/free-delta-ring`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/cech-alexander-complex`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

### `PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison` — q-crystalline and crystalline cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. There is a canonical identification qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) of commutative algebra objects of D(D/(q−1)), where the right side is the crystalline cohomology of Spf(R) relative to the p-adic PD thickening D/(q−1) → D/I, whose ideal I·D/(q−1) has divided powers by delta-pd-pairs. Consequences (Remark 16.15 (1)): a map of derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-complexes is an isomorphism if and only if its completed base change to D/(q−1) is; hence R ↦ qΩ_{R/D} is a sheaf for the Zariski topology on p-completely smooth D/I-algebras, and defines a Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of commutative algebras on every smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I, whose reduction modulo q − 1 is the pushforward of the crystalline structure sheaf.

*Hypotheses.*
- (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I.
- The source prints 'q Ω_D' in the proof; qΩ_{R/D} is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
- Crystalline cohomology over a p-adic PD base and its computation by PD envelopes are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2 and CR.0.
- The ringed q-crystalline site of a non-affine formal scheme (Remark 16.15 (2)) is not developed in the source and is not used.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Compute qΩ_{R/D} by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) of q-crystalline-cech-alexander.
2. The completed base change − ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) commutes with the totalisation (q-pd-homological-properties (3)), so the left side is computed by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1).
3. By q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) this is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of J^•/(q−1) ⊂ F^•/(q−1), a Čech–Alexander complex computing RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) (CR.2).
4. Sheaf property: D is derived (q−1)-complete (q-pd-homological-properties (1)), so derived Nakayama reduces isomorphy to D/(q−1); combine with Zariski descent for crystalline cohomology (CR.2).

*Acceptance.*
- D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D Z_p ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), the p-completed de Rham complex of R; so qΩ_{R/D} is a q-deformation of de Rham cohomology.
- D with q = 1: the statement is the identity, qΩ_{R/D} = RΓ_crys(R/D).
- D = A_inf, I = (ξ): qΩ_{R/A_inf} ⊗̂^L A_inf/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(A_inf/(q−1))).

### `PR.6/q-pd-thickening-invariance` — Invariance under q-PD thickenings of the base

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-thickening-invariance` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (D, J) → (D, I) be a morphism of q-PD pairs that is the identity on the underlying δ-ring, so J ⊂ I are two q-PD ideals of D (for example J = (q−1)). Let R be a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra and R̃ a p-completely smooth D/J-algebra lifting R along D/J → D/I. Then there is a canonical identification qΩ_{R̃/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}, the first taken relative to (D, J) and the second relative to (D, I). It is induced by the functor (R̃/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} sending a thickening (E, K) with R̃ → E/K to (E, K_I), where K_I is the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal of E generated by K and I·E, with the induced map R = R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I → E/K_I; this functor does not change the underlying δ-D-algebra.

*Hypotheses.*
- Both (D, J) and (D, I) are q-PD pairs on the same δ-ring; R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I ≅ R.
- The printed proof writes 'E → E/K ≃ R̃' for an object of the site; objects only carry a map R̃ → E/K, and the functor is defined on all of them as stated here (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- The identification is compatible with Frobenius and multiplication, since it is induced by a functor of sites that is the identity on structure rings.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (E, K + I·E) satisfies condition (1) of q-pd-pair: it holds on K and on the image of I, hence on the ideal they generate by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation; the derived complete ideal K_I it generates is then a q-PD ideal by q-pd-homological-properties (4).
2. The functor is the identity on the rings E, so it induces a map qΩ_{R̃/D} → qΩ_{R/D} of commutative algebras compatible with Frobenius.
3. Take a presentation P → R̃ and compose with R̃ → R. By inspection of the proof of q-pd-envelope the q-PD envelopes of the two kernels in F^• are the same rings, since the envelope ring only adjoins φ(x_i)/[p]_q for the regular sequence and does not depend on the base ideal; so the Čech–Alexander complex computing qΩ_{R̃/D} also computes qΩ_{R/D}.

*Acceptance.*
- D = A_inf, J = (q−1) ⊂ I = (ξ): for R̃ p-completely smooth over A_inf/(q−1) lifting R over O_C, qΩ_{R̃/A_inf} ≃ qΩ_{R/A_inf}.
- For q = 1 this is the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base.
- For J = I and R̃ = R the identification is the identity.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`.

*Used in this roadmap by:* `PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison`.

*Sources.*
- BS22-v4, Theorem 16.17: “that is the identity on underlying” (the statement)
- BS22-v4, Theorem 16.17, proof: “It now follows by inspection of the proof of Lemma” (the functor of sites and the comparison of Čech–Alexander complexes)

### `PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison` — q-crystalline and prismatic cohomology ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **q-crystalline and prismatic cohomology**.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{D/I, φ_D} D/([p]_q) be the p-completed base change of R along the map D/I → D/([p]_q) induced by φ_D (it exists because φ_D(I) ⊂ [p]_q D); it is a p-completely smooth D/([p]_q)-algebra. Let Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} be the prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)} relative to the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)). Then there is a canonical isomorphism α : Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}. The map α is induced by the functor (R/D)_{q-crys} → (R^{(1)}/D)_Δ sending (E, J) to the prism (E, ([p]_q)) with the map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) obtained by linearising R → E/J → E/([p]_q), the second map being induced by φ_E. By construction α is a map of commutative algebra objects of D(D), compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms and natural in R and in (D, I).

*Hypotheses.*
- (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I.
- The Frobenius twist R^{(1)} is part of the statement: R itself is not an algebra over D/([p]_q) unless q = 1.
- The printed proof writes 'E → E/J ≅ R'; objects carry only a map R → E/J, which suffices (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- The printed proof identifies the source and the target of α modulo q − 1 with crystalline cohomology and does not say that the reduction of α is that identification; step 5 supplies this (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E66).
- The reduction to I = (q−1) uses a lift of R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra, which the source uses implicitly.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Construction of α: for (E, J) in the site, φ_E(J) ⊂ [p]_q E, so φ_E induces a φ_D-linear map R → E/J → E/([p]_q), hence a D-linear map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) and an object of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} over (D, ([p]_q)); evaluating the prismatic structure sheaf gives α.
2. Reduction to I = (q−1): lift R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra R̃ (the kernel of D/(q−1) → D/I consists of elements f with f^p ∈ p·D/(q−1), so smooth algebras lift; DD.1) and apply q-pd-thickening-invariance; R̃^{(1)} = R^{(1)} because φ_D factors through D/I.
3. It suffices to prove that α is an isomorphism after (p,[p]_q)-completed base change to D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties (2)).
4. D → D/(q−1) is a map of bounded prisms (D, ([p]_q)) → (D/(q−1), (p)); by PR.1's prismatic-base-change, Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ Δ_{R̄^{(1)}/(D/(q−1))} = φ^*Δ_{R̄/(D/(q−1))} with R̄ = R/p; by PR.1's crystalline-comparison this is RΓ_crys(R̄/(D/(q−1))) = RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))), which is qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) by q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.
5. The reduction of α is this composite: both α and the comparison map of PR.1's crystalline-comparison (general case of BS22 Theorem 5.2) are induced by sending a (q-)PD thickening E, whose ideal is carried by φ into the prism ideal, to the prism E; the equality is checked on the Čech–Alexander complexes of q-crystalline-cech-alexander and their reductions.

*Acceptance.*
- D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p] and Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}.
- D = A_inf, I = (ξ): R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A_inf, φ} A_inf and Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_inf} = φ^*Δ_{R/A_inf}, the prismatic cohomology relative to (A_inf, (ξ)) pulled back along φ.
- q = 1: the statement is the crystalline comparison of PR.1 for the PD ideal I.
- R = D/I: both sides are D and α is the identity.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-thickening-invariance`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-cech-alexander`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-homological-properties`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-site`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/prismatic-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/crystalline-prism`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

### `PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum` — Framed D-algebras and framed q-PD data

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum` · definition · part PR.0.

Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]] and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. A framed D-algebra is a pair (P, S) of a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-algebra P and a set S with elements X_s ∈ P (s ∈ S) such that the framing □ : D[X_s : s ∈ S]^∧ → P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-étale; then P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-smooth over D. This is the (p, q−1)-complete case, over the base ring D with its element q, of the framed algebras of QWittVectors:QW.6, and the following are imported from QW.6, not constructed here: the pairwise commuting D-algebra automorphisms γ_s of P, determined by γ_s(X_s) = qX_s, γ_s(X_t) = X_t for t ≠ s and γ_s ≡ id modulo (q−1)X_s; the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s}(f) = (γ_s(f) − f)/((q−1)X_s); the twisted Leibniz rule; the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D}, the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s}; and its reduction modulo q − 1 to the de Rham complex. PR.6 adds: (i) the unique δ-D-algebra structures on D[S]^∧ and on P with δ(X_s) = 0 for all s, compatible along □, for which every γ_s is a δ-D-algebra automorphism; (ii) P is flat over A, so (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on P; (iii) a framed q-PD datum is a triple (P, S, J) where (P, S) is a framed D-algebra and J ⊂ P is the kernel of a D-algebra surjection P → R. A morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′) is a D-algebra map P → P′ together with an injective map S → S′, s ↦ s′, such that X_s ↦ X_{s′}, carrying J into J′.

*Hypotheses.*
- D is flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]]: the standing assumption of BS22 §16.3.
- The source writes 'p-completely ind-smooth' and 'p-completely ind-étale'. The unique extension of γ_s uses that (q−1)X_s is topologically nilpotent, which holds for the (p, q−1)-adic topology and fails for the p-adic one; the conditions are therefore (p,[p]_q)-complete ones, as the source itself writes in Remark 16.16 and at the end of Construction 16.20 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E65).
- Ownership (RT-AREA-etale/28): framed algebras, γ_s, ∇_{q,s}, the twisted Leibniz rule, the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex and its reduction modulo q − 1 belong to QWittVectors:QW.6 in the general form over an I-completely étale framing, I = (q−1) or (p, q−1). This node imports the (p, q−1)-complete case and adds only (i)–(iii).
- A morphism of framed q-PD data is injective on coordinates (the map S → S′ with X_s ↦ X_{s′} is injective); it need not be étale. Without injectivity the map does not commute with the q-derivatives: for D⟨X_0,X_1⟩ → D⟨X⟩, ∇_q(X_0X_1) ↦ 2X dX but ∇_q(X²) = (1+q)X dX.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Import from QW.6 the framed algebra (P, S) with its automorphisms and q-derivatives, for the base ring D, the element q and the ideal (p, q−1): the automorphism of D[S]^∧ scaling X_s by q is congruent to the identity modulo the topologically nilpotent element (q−1)X_s, so it extends uniquely along the completely ind-étale framing (Construction 16.19).
2. (i) D[S] has the δ-D-algebra structure with δ(X_s) = 0, that is φ(X_s) = X_s^p; it extends uniquely to the completion and along the completely ind-étale map □ (BS22 Lemma 2.18; equivalently, P being p-torsion-free, the framed Frobenius lift of QW.6 gives a δ-structure by PR.0's torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence). γ_s is a δ-map on D[S]^∧ because δ(qX_s) = 0, and on P by uniqueness of the extension.
3. (ii) P is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D and derived complete, D is flat over the noetherian ring A, so P is flat over A (DD.1); hence q − 1 and X_s are nonzerodivisors on P.
4. (iii) The kernel J of P → R is, locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a filtered colimit of completely regular sequences relative to D, so q-pd-envelope (3) applies to (P, J).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Lemma 16.21 and Construction 16.20: the automorphisms γ_s are extended to the q-PD envelope of J and their Koszul complex is formed
- BS22 Theorem 16.22: the framed q-PD datum is the input of the q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison
- BS22 proof of Theorem 17.2: the formal tori P_Σ over A_inf with coordinates indexed by finite sets of units are framed q-PD data
- QWittVectors:QW.6 and HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: QW.6 owns the framed algebra and its q-derivatives; HQ.1 imports them from QW.6 and the q-PD part from this stage

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra` (structure): A framed D-algebra with its imported structure: coordinates X_s, automorphisms γ_s, q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} (owner QWittVectors:QW.6) and the δ-structure with δ(X_s) = 0. The complete ind-étaleness of the framing is DD.1's and QW.6's notion.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.delta_coord` (relation): δ(X_s) = 0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.gamma_coord_self` (relation): γ_s(X_s) = q·X_s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.gamma_coord_of_ne` (relation): γ_s(X_t) = X_t for t ≠ s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.gamma_comm` (relation): γ_s γ_t = γ_t γ_s.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.gamma_delta` (compatibility): γ_s commutes with δ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.sub_one_mul_coord_mul_nabla` (characterisation): (q−1)·X_s·∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum` (structure): A framed q-PD datum (P, S, J): a framed D-algebra and an ideal J of P, the kernel of a surjection onto R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.Hom` (structure): A morphism of framed q-PD data: a D-algebra map carrying coordinates to coordinates and J into J′.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_framed_nabla_coord_pow` (computation): If (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor then ∇_{q,s}(X_s^{n+1}) = [n+1]_q·X_s^n, with [n+1]_q = Σ_{i≤n} q^i.
- `pr6_framed_nabla_const` (degenerate): If (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor then ∇_{q,s} vanishes on the image of D.
- `pr6_framed_gamma_frobenius` (compatibility): γ_s commutes with the Frobenius lift φ of the δ-structure.
- `pr6_framed_two_framings_gamma` (non-example): If two framed structures on the same P with one coordinate have X′ = X + 1, then γ′(X) = qX + (q−1); so the automorphism depends on the framing and is not determined by P.

*Acceptance.*
- One polynomial coordinate: P = D⟨X⟩, S = {X}: γ(X^n) = q^n X^n and ∇_q(X^n) = [n]_q X^{n−1}.
- A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩ with γ(X^n) = q^n X^n for n ∈ Z and logarithmic q-derivative (γ − 1)/(q−1).
- Two framings: on D⟨T⟩ the coordinates T and T + 1 give automorphisms with γ^{T}(T) = qT and γ^{T+1}(T) = qT + (q−1).
- S = ∅ and P = D: the framed q-PD datum (D, ∅, I) of R = D/I.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-pair`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`, `QWittVectors:QW.6`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

### `PR.6/gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope` — Extension of the automorphisms γ_s to the q-PD envelope

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope` · lemma · part PR.0.

Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum (so D is flat over A). For each s ∈ S the automorphism γ_s of P extends uniquely to an automorphism of the q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P) that is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. The extensions are δ-D-algebra automorphisms and commute pairwise; (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on D_{J,q}(P), so the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} := (γ_s − 1)/((q−1)X_s) are defined on D_{J,q}(P) and commute; and they lift the derivations ∂/∂X_s of the p-completed PD envelope D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) of P/(q−1) → R.

*Hypotheses.*
- (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A.
- This lemma and the resulting q-derivatives on D_{J,q}(P) are kept by PR.6 (RT-AREA-etale/28); the q-derivatives on P itself are QW.6's.
- The source prints 'as in Construction 16.10'; Lemma 16.10 is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. It suffices to extend γ_s to an endomorphism of D_{J,q}(P) congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s; such an endomorphism of a derived complete ring is an automorphism.
2. Consider P → P → D_{J,q}(P), the first map being γ_s. All rings are A-flat, so by the universal property of the envelope as a free δ-algebra (q-pd-envelope) it suffices that φ(γ_s(f)) ∈ [p]_q·D_{J,q}(P) for f ∈ J. Write γ_s(f) = f + (q−1)X_s·g with g ∈ P; then φ(γ_s(f)) = φ(f) + [p]_q·(q−1)·X_s^p·φ(g), using φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q and δ(X_s) = 0.
3. The same formula shows that the extension is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. Uniqueness and commutation: D_{J,q}(P) is topologically generated as a δ-P-algebra by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q, f ∈ J, and is [p]_q-torsion-free.
4. Lifting ∂/∂X_s: identify D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) with the p-completed PD envelope (q-pd-envelope-base-change (b)) and reduce to the statement on P/(q−1), which is QW.6's reduction modulo q − 1, by torsion-freeness and density.

*Acceptance.*
- P = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩, J = (q−1, X), z = φ(X)/[p]_q: γ(z) = q^p z = z + (q−1)X·X^{p−1}, so ∇_q(z) = X^{p−1}, lifting ∂/∂X(X^p/p) = X^{p−1}.
- For J = (q−1)P the envelope is P and the extension is γ_s itself.

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-pd-datum`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-pd-envelope-base-change`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-divided-power-operation`, `QWittVectors:QW.6`.

### `PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex` — The q-de Rham complex of a framed q-PD datum

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex` · construction · part PR.0.

Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A. Its q-de Rham complex is the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∇_{q,s} (s ∈ S) of the q-PD envelope: qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} := (D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^1_{P/D} → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^2_{P/D} → …), where Ω^1_{P/D} is the completed direct sum of the P·dX_s and ∇_q(f) = Σ_s ∇_{q,s}(f) dX_s; it is a cochain complex of D-modules, and an instance of the Koszul complex of commuting q-derivations of QWittVectors:QW.6, applied to the ring D_{J,q}(P) with the elements X_s and the automorphisms of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope. Properties. (a) If J = I·P with I = (q−1), then D_{J,q}(P) = P and the complex is the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D} of QW.6. (b) Functoriality: a morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′), which by definition is injective on coordinates, induces a morphism of complexes qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}; a D-algebra map identifying two coordinates (for instance a codegeneracy of the Čech nerve) does not. (c) Reduction: the complex modulo q − 1 is the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1). (d) Frobenius: ∇_{q,s}∘φ = [p]_q·X_s^{p−1}·φ∘∇_{q,s}, so the maps f·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} ↦ φ(f)·∏_j([p]_q X_{s_j}^{p−1})·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} form a φ_D-semilinear endomorphism of the complex. (e) Toric form: if the X_s are units of P the complex is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of the logarithmic q-derivatives X_s∇_{q,s} = (γ_s − 1)/(q−1), which is η_{(q−1)} applied to the Koszul complex of the endomorphisms γ_s − 1 (the décalage of AInfCohomology:AI.1 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes).

*Hypotheses.*
- (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum; D is flat over A.
- For infinite S the complex is the completed filtered colimit over finite subsets of S.
- (b): the source prints the last sentence of Construction 16.20 with the framing A[{X_s}] → P; the framing D[{X_s}] → P is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
- (d) is not printed in §16; it follows from φ∘γ_s = γ_s∘φ and φ((q−1)X_s) = [p]_q(q−1)X_s^p, and is what the Frobenius compatibility in Theorem 17.2 uses.
- The Koszul complex of commuting endomorphisms and the identification in (e) are AI.1's (BMS1 Definition 7.1, Lemma 7.9); the Koszul complex of q-derivations is QW.6's.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Extend the γ_s to D_{J,q}(P) and form the commuting q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} (gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope); take their Koszul complex (QW.6, AI.1).
2. (b): let α : D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J′,q}(P′) be induced by P → P′ and the universal property. For t ∈ S′ outside the image of S one has γ_t∘α = α: the identity holds on the étale coordinates X_s, hence on P by complete étaleness of the framing, and on the envelope because it is [p]_q-torsion-free and generated over P by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q. So α commutes with the q-derivatives indexed by S and is killed by the others.
3. (c): q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) and the last statement of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope.
4. (d): apply φ to (q−1)X_s∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f and cancel the nonzerodivisor (q−1)X_s. (e): X_s is a unit, so the Koszul complexes of ∇_{q,s} and X_s∇_{q,s} are isomorphic; then use η_f Kos(g_i) ≅ Kos(g_i/f) for f dividing all g_i (AI.1).

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 16.22: it is the explicit complex shown to compute qΩ_{R/D}
- BS22 proof of Theorem 17.2: for the tori P_Σ its toric form is η_{q−1} of the Koszul complex of γ_s − 1, which maps to the complex computing AΩ_R
- BMS2 Remark 9.11 (PR.3) and BMS2 §10 (PR.4): the Nygaard filtration and the syntomic complexes are computed in these coordinates, using φ(dlog_q X_s) = [p]_q dlog_q X_s from (d)
- HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.1: imports the framed complex from QW.6 and its comparison with qΩ from this stage

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelope` (constructor): The q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P) of a framed q-PD datum.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeMap` (data): The canonical map P → D_{J,q}(P).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeFramed` (structure): The extended structure on D_{J,q}(P): the images of the coordinates, the extended automorphisms γ_s, the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} and the δ-structure.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.envelopeFramed_gamma` (compatibility): The extended γ_s restricts to γ_s on P.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamComplex` (constructor): The cochain complex qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} of D-modules.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamMap` (functoriality): The morphism of complexes induced by a morphism of framed q-PD data.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedDatum.qDeRhamFrobenius` (data): The φ_D-semilinear endomorphism of (d).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.QCrys.FramedAlgebra.nabla_frobenius` (relation): ∇_{q,s}(φ(f)) = [p]_q·X_s^{p−1}·φ(∇_{q,s}(f)) on a framed algebra in which (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor and δ(q) = 0.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_qdr_polynomial_nabla` (computation): In the polynomial ring D[X] with the automorphism X ↦ qX: γ(X^{n+1}) − X^{n+1} = (q−1)·X·([n+1]_q·X^n).
- `pr6_qdr_at_q_one_derivative` (compatibility): The formula Σ_n a_n [n]_q X^{n−1} for the q-derivative on D[X] specialises at q = 1 to Mathlib's Polynomial.derivative.
- `pr6_qdr_no_coordinates` (degenerate): For S = ∅ all terms of the complex in nonzero degrees vanish: the complex is D_{J,q}(P) in degree 0.
- `pr6_qdr_two_framings_differ` (non-example): For two framed structures on P with one coordinate and X′ = X + 1, with (q−1)X and (q−1)X′ nonzerodivisors: ∇′(X²) = ∇(X²) + (q−1); so the complex depends on the framing as a complex.
- `pr6_qdr_leibniz` (characterisation): The twisted Leibniz rule ∇_{q,s}(fg) = f·∇_{q,s}(g) + γ_s(g)·∇_{q,s}(f) holds when (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor.

*Acceptance.*
- One polynomial coordinate: P = D⟨X⟩, J = (q−1)P with I = (q−1): the complex is D⟨X⟩ → D⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX; for D = Z_p[[q−1]] its H^0 is D and its H^1 is the completed direct sum of the D/[n]_q·X^{n−1}dX, n ≥ 1.
- A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩: the complex is D⟨X^{±1}⟩ → D⟨X^{±1}⟩ dlog X, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^n dlog X, with [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1) for n ∈ Z.
- S = ∅: the complex is D in degree 0.

### `PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison` — q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison ★

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison` · theorem · part PR.0 · planet **q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison**.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]], R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra and (P, S, J) a framed q-PD datum with P/J ≅ R. Then there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism qΩ_{R/D} ≃ qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}: the q-de Rham complex of the framed q-PD datum computes q-crystalline cohomology. The identification is natural for morphisms of framed q-PD data lying over maps R → R′, and it carries the Frobenius φ_{R/D} to the Frobenius of framed-q-de-rham-complex (d).

*Hypotheses.*
- (D, I) is a q-PD pair with D flat over A; (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum for R.
- The source states the quasi-isomorphism; naturality in the framed datum and the compatibility with Frobenius are visible in its proof (the bicomplex is functorial and carries the Frobenius) and are used in Theorem 17.2.
- For q = 1 this is the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham complex of a PD envelope, owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. Let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P; the coordinates S define coordinates S^n on P^n by coproducts, and J^n = ker(P^n → P → R) gives framed q-PD data (P^n, S^n, J^n). The coface maps are morphisms of framed q-PD data (injective on coordinates); the codegeneracies are not and do not commute with ∇_q. Apply framed-q-de-rham-complex to get complexes M^{n,*} = qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J^n,q}(P^n)} with maps of complexes for the cofaces; each row M^{•,i} = D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ⊗̂ Ω^i_{P^•/D} is a cosimplicial D-module. Form the double complex with horizontal differential the alternating sum of the cofaces. In a semi-cosimplicial module whose cofaces are all isomorphisms the cofaces of each level coincide, which is what step 4 uses.
2. Rows: for i > 0 the cosimplicial D-module M^{•,i} is homotopy equivalent to 0 as a cosimplicial module, by the standard argument for the crystalline case (Stacks project, Tag 07JP; CR.2).
3. Columns: every face map P^i → P^j induces a quasi-isomorphism M^{i,*} → M^{j,*}: modulo q − 1 this is the PD Poincaré lemma (framed-q-de-rham-complex (c); CR.2), and the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama gives the claim.
4. Therefore the complex attached to the cosimplicial module M^{•,0} is quasi-isomorphic to the column M^{0,*}. The former is the small Čech–Alexander complex of q-crystalline-cech-alexander (5) and computes qΩ_{R/D}; the latter is qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}.
5. Naturality and Frobenius: the bicomplex is functorial in the framed datum by framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) and carries the Frobenius of (d), which on row 0 is the Frobenius of the δ-rings D_{J^•,q}(P^•).

*Acceptance.*
- One polynomial coordinate: qΩ_{Z_p⟨X⟩/Z_p[[q−1]]} is computed by Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ → Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX.
- A torus over A_inf: qΩ_{O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩/A_inf} is computed by A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ dlog x, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n dlog x.
- Modulo q − 1 the quasi-isomorphism reduces to the statement that the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) → R computes RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))).

### `PR.6/change-of-framing` — Change of framing and the cocycle identity

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/change-of-framing` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let (P, S, J) and (P′, S′, J′) be two framed q-PD data for R; the case P = P′ with two coordinate systems is included. Put P″ = P ⊗̂_D P′ (derived (p,[p]_q)-completed), S″ = S ⊔ S′ and J″ = ker(P″ → R). Then (P″, S″, J″) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and the two morphisms of framed q-PD data induce quasi-isomorphisms qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□″}_{D_{J″,q}(P″)/D} ← qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}. The resulting isomorphism c_{□,□′} in D(D) equals the composite of the identifications of q-de-rham-comparison with qΩ_{R/D}. Consequently c_{□,□} = id and c_{□′,□″}∘c_{□,□′} = c_{□,□″} for three framed data (the cocycle identity); the isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius and with maps R → R′ covered by morphisms of framed data; the framed q-de Rham complex is independent of the framing up to canonical isomorphism in D(D); and on a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I the complexes of framed affine charts descend to the Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.

*Hypotheses.*
- Both data are framed q-PD data for the same R over the same q-PD pair, D flat over A.
- The complexes of two framings are different complexes; only their images in D(D), with Frobenius and multiplication, are identified.
- The statement is what the source calls independence 'up to canonical quasi-isomorphism' of the framing; it is deduced from Construction 16.20 and the proof of Theorem 16.22, where the same argument is applied to the face maps of the Čech nerve.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (P″, S″) is a framed D-algebra: the framing is the completed tensor product of the two framings; J″ is the kernel of the surjection P″ → R.
2. The maps P → P″ ← P′ are morphisms of framed q-PD data, so framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) gives the two maps of complexes.
3. They are quasi-isomorphisms: modulo q − 1 they are the comparison maps between the PD de Rham complexes of two embeddings of R and of their product, quasi-isomorphisms by the independence of the embedding in CR.2; the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama applies. This is the column argument of the proof of Theorem 16.22.
4. Agreement with q-de-rham-comparison: the bicomplex of that proof is functorial in the framed datum, so the two maps commute with the identifications with qΩ_{R/D}. The cocycle identity and c_{□,□} = id follow formally.
5. Descent: qΩ_{−/D} is a Zariski sheaf (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison) and the identifications are natural for localisation.

*Acceptance.*
- Two framings: R = Z_p⟨T⟩ over Z_p[[q−1]] with coordinates T and T + 1. The complexes differ, ∇^{T+1}(T²) − ∇^{T}(T²) = q − 1, and are identified through the datum on Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧ with coordinates T_0 and T_1 + 1.
- Three framings T, T + 1, T + 2 of Z_p⟨T⟩: the three isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle identity.
- Equal framings give the identity.

### `PR.6/q-de-rham-prismatic-comparison-zp` — The framed q-de Rham complex of a smooth Z_p-algebra and prismatic cohomology

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-prismatic-comparison-zp` · theorem · part PR.0.

Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the q-de Rham prism (A, ([p]_q)), and let R be a p-completely smooth Z_p-algebra with a p-completely étale framing □ : Z_p⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → R. Let P be the (p, q−1)-completely étale A⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩-algebra lifting R (so P/(q−1) = R), framed by T_1, …, T_d, and let qΩ_R^□ := qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} be its (p, q−1)-completed framed q-de Rham complex (QWittVectors:QW.6). Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p], the p-completed base change of R along Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p]. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in D(A), compatible with Frobenius, qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = RΓ_Δ(Spf(R^{(1)})/A). Consequently qΩ_R^□ is independent of the framing □ up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, is functorial in R as an object of D(A), and qΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is the p-completed de Rham complex of R over Z_p. Scope: this is a statement for one prime p over the (p, q−1)-complete base Z_p[[q−1]]; it does not produce a theory over Z[[q−1]] or over the Habiro ring. The gluing over all primes is owned by HabiroCohomologyFoundations HQ.1–HQ.2.

*Hypotheses.*
- R is p-completely smooth over Z_p with a p-completely étale framing; the prism is (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), not (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)).
- The base change to Z_p[ζ_p] is part of the statement: prismatic cohomology is taken of R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂ Z_p[ζ_p], not of R.
- The framed complex qΩ_R^□ itself is QW.6's object; this node proves its comparison.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (c)) and A is flat over itself. (P, {T_i}, (q−1)P) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and D_{J,q}(P) = P because (P, (q−1)P) is already a q-PD pair, P being completely flat over A; so its q-de Rham complex is qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} (framed-q-de-rham-complex (a)).
2. q-de-rham-comparison gives qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A}.
3. q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison with I = (q−1) gives qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}; here φ_A induces Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p], the structure map, so R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p].
4. Independence of □ and functoriality: change-of-framing. Reduction modulo q − 1: q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison and the identification of RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) with the de Rham complex of the smooth lift (CR.2).

*Acceptance.*
- One polynomial coordinate: R = Z_p⟨T⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T⟩ → A⟨T⟩dT), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^{n−1}dT. Modulo [p]_q the coefficient [n]_ζ is a unit for p ∤ n and 0 for p | n, so H^0 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩ and H^1 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩·T^{p−1}dT, which are R^{(1)} and Ω^1_{R^{(1)}/Z_p[ζ_p]} through T ↦ T^p, as the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} predicts.
- A torus: R = Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩ dlog T), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^n dlog T.
- Two framings T and T + 1 of Z_p⟨T⟩ give canonically isomorphic objects of D(A).

*Depends on:* `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/change-of-framing`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/framed-q-de-rham-complex`, `PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/q-de-rham-prism`, `QWittVectors:QW.6`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

- BS22-v4, §16, introduction: “gives an explicit complex computing prismatic cohomology in many cases” (the combination of Theorems 16.18 and 16.22 that proves it)

### `PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map` — The all-coordinates comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ

Node `PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison-map` · construction · part PR.0.

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C) with q = [ε] and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of ainf-q-pd-pair. Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra that is very small: R/p is generated over O_C/p by units, and R is small, that is, there are units x_1, …, x_n of R defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. Put S = R^× and let C_S be the filtered poset of finite subsets Σ ⊂ S such that A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ → R, x_s ↦ s, is surjective. For Σ ∈ C_S let P_Σ = A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ be the formal torus over A, with δ(x_s) = 0 and the automorphisms γ_s scaling x_s by q, and J_Σ = ker(P_Σ → R); (P_Σ, Σ, J_Σ) is a framed q-PD datum. (1) The q-side. qΩ_{R/A} is computed by the complex colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}_{s∈Σ}), which is functorial in the very small algebra R. (2) The AΩ-side. Let Δ_Σ = ∏_{s∈Σ} Z_p(1) and let R_{Σ,∞} be the p-completed integral closure of R in the pro-étale Δ_Σ-torsor over R[1/p] obtained by extracting all p-power roots of the x_s; R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid, and σ_s denotes the automorphism of A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) induced by the s-th basis vector of Δ_Σ. Then AΩ_R is computed by colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}_{s∈Σ}), and already by each term whose Σ contains units x_1, …, x_n defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. (3) The map. For each Σ ∈ C_S there is a unique map of δ-A-algebras μ_0 : D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) extending the δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}), x_s ↦ [(s, s^{1/p}, s^{1/p²}, …)]; it intertwines γ_s with σ_s and is compatible with enlarging Σ. It induces maps Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}) ≅ η_{q−1} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {γ_s − 1}) → η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}), and in the colimit over Σ the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R. It is a map of E_1-A-algebras (represented by differential graded algebras), natural in the very small algebra R and compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms. For a general p-completely smooth O_C-algebra, and for smooth formal O_C-schemes, μ is obtained by gluing, the very small affine opens being a basis.

*Hypotheses.*
- C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}; R is p-completely smooth over O_C and very small.
- The colimit in (2) is over C_S; the printed index set is a misprint registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E28.
- AΩ_R, the perfectoid rings R_{Σ,∞}, the identification of continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ with a Koszul complex and the statement that the complexes in (2) compute AΩ_R are owned by AInfCohomology AI.3 and AI.4 (BMS1 Lemma 7.3, Theorem 9.4 (iii), and the all-coordinates construction).
- Kos_c denotes the completed Koszul complex: for the q-derivatives it is the complex of framed-q-de-rham-complex.
- The source asserts that R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid for every Σ in C_S by a general reference, and notes that the subset of those Σ containing a framing is cofinal and suffices; for these the perfectoidness follows from almost purity (AI.3, AI.4). The plan uses this cofinal subset.
- The map is constructed without any choice of coordinates: all finite generating sets of units are used at once.

*Proof or construction outline.*
1. (1): q-de-rham-comparison for each Σ, the functoriality of framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) in Σ, and a filtered colimit.
2. (2): import from AI.3 and AI.4. Each Σ containing a framing gives a complex computing AΩ_R by BMS1 Theorem 9.4 (iii) and the enlargement criterion quoted in the source; the continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ is the Koszul complex by BMS1 Lemma 7.3 (AI.1).
3. (3), the map μ_0: let P_Σ → P_{Σ,∞} be the (p, ξ)-completed perfection (PR.0's prism-perfection). It is a perfect, completely flat δ-A-algebra, so P_{Σ,∞}/ξ is perfectoid, obtained from P_Σ/ξ by extracting p-power roots of the x_s, and P_{Σ,∞} ≅ A_inf(P_{Σ,∞}/ξ) (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). Composing with A_inf of the map to R_{Σ,∞} gives a δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) lying over R → R_{Σ,∞}. Since A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) → R_{Σ,∞} is a q-PD thickening (q-pd-homological-properties (5) applied to A → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞})), the universal property of q-pd-envelope extends it uniquely to μ_0.
4. Equivariance: σ_s∘μ_0 and μ_0∘γ_s are both the extension, by the universal property, of maps out of P_Σ that agree; so they coincide.
5. The Koszul map: the x_s are units, so the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s} is η_{q−1} of the Koszul complex of the γ_s − 1 (framed-q-de-rham-complex (e)); η_{q−1} is functorial for μ_0 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes (AI.1). Multiplicativity: both Koszul complexes are differential graded algebras and μ_0 is a ring map (BMS1 Lemmas 7.5 and 6.13; AI.1). Frobenius: μ_0 is a δ-map.

*Uses.*
- BS22 Theorem 17.2: μ_R is the map shown to be an isomorphism
- AInfCohomology:AI.7 and CohomologyComparisons:CP.1: import the comparison map and do not rebuild it
- PrismaticCohomology PR.4 (BMS2 §10): the syntomic complexes are rewritten through AΩ ≃ φ^*Δ, whose map is μ_R

*API.*
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.Chart` (structure): Imported data of a chart Σ (owners AInfCohomology AI.3 and AI.4): the ring A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}), its automorphisms σ_s and the map from the torus P_Σ.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.coordinateMap` (data): μ_0 : D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.coordinateMap_comp` (characterisation): μ_0 restricts on P_Σ to the given map of the chart.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.coordinateMap_gamma` (relation): μ_0∘γ_s = σ_s∘μ_0.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.AOmegaData` (structure): Imported data (owner AInfCohomology AI.3): the complex AΩ_R in D(A) and its Frobenius AΩ_R → φ_* AΩ_R.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.frobeniusPullback` (constructor): φ_A^* on D(A) for a perfect prism: restriction of scalars along φ^{-1}.
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.comparisonMap` (constructor): μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R in D(A).
- `TauCeti.Prismatic.AOmega.comparisonMap_frobenius` (compatibility): μ_R commutes with the Frobenius endomorphisms.

*Unit tests.*
- `pr6_mu_torus_coordinate` (computation): If the map of the chart sends the coordinate x_s to an element y, then μ_0(x_s) = y and σ_s(y) = q·y: for the torus, y = [x^♭] and σ([x^♭]) = [ε][x^♭].
- `pr6_mu_point` (degenerate): For R = O_C (no coordinates) qΩ_{O_C/A} ≅ A.
- `pr6_mu_frobenius_square` (compatibility): The square formed by μ_R and the two Frobenius maps commutes.
- `pr6_mu_needs_decalage` (non-example): Without η_{q−1} the target is wrong: if σ(y) = q′·y with q′^p = q and σ(q′) = q′, then (q−1)·y = (σ − 1)([p]_{q′}·y), so the class of y in the cokernel of σ − 1 is (q−1)-torsion; for the torus this class is nonzero, while AΩ has no such torsion.

*Acceptance.*
- A torus: R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩, Σ = {x}: J_Σ = (ξ), D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) = P_Σ = A⟨x^{±1}⟩, A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) = A⟨x^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and μ_0 is the inclusion; μ_R is the injective quasi-isomorphism of BMS1 Lemma 9.6.
- R = O_C, Σ = ∅: both complexes are A in degree 0 and μ_R is the identity.
- Enlarging Σ by a unit that is a product of the given ones changes neither side up to the canonical quasi-isomorphisms.
